Channelization results from the coupling of decompaction, fluid-pressure buildup, buoyancy-driven flow, and metasomatic reactions associated with infiltration of SiO$_2$-poor hydrous fluid and olivine formation. The resulting fluid-rich channels propagate upward and develop connected networks resembling natural vein systems. Our results demonstrate that reactive porosity waves in compositionally heterogeneous serpentinites provide a robust mechanism for focusing fluid flow and enhancing fluid extraction from dehydrating subducting slabs.

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

papers.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
papers.abstract: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. In this paper, we present FATCAT, the first physical fault-injection attacks capable of eliminating refusal in modern large language and vision-language models. Specifically, we present a non-invasive electromagnetic (EM) fault injection attack targeting GPU-accelerated Systems-on-Chip with physical access, requiring neither software execution privileges nor model-layer access. By leveraging an autonomous Radio Frequency (RF) side-channel trigger to synchronize EM faults to the prompt prefill phase, the attack corrupts safety-critical memory transactions across off-chip LPDDR5 DRAM and on-chip LPDDR physical interfaces without crashing the system while preserving model coherence. Evaluated on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and AGX Thor running Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B, localized physical faults reliably force models to fulfill restricted requests, demonstrating that model-level alignment provides no robust security guarantees without hardware-level fault tolerance. Finally, we demonstrate the physical-world consequences of this vulnerability on an active 6-DoF robotic manipulator controlled by a SmolVLA vision-language-action policy. Our attack silently corrupts the model forcing the arm into abrupt, hazardous lunges; in two instances the robotic arm attempted to pinch the paper author -- proving that hardware faults can directly translate into real physical harm.

papers.title: CrownFusion: 3D Dental Crown Generation Using Geometry Images and Latent Diffusion
papers.abstract: We introduce CrownFusion, a latent diffusion model to generate 3D dental crown designs from geometry images, a 2D-grid encoding of surface coordinates. Departing from traditional approaches that use point clouds, our "CrownImage" representation not only unlocks the full power of image-based generative architectures, but also preserves fine geometric detail by operating at far higher spatial resolutions than point clouds to alleviate smoothing artifacts in the 3D generation. Conditioned on jointly learned embeddings of the surrounding dentition, our probabilistic diffusion model produces anatomically plausible crowns with morphological variations tailored to individual patient cases. To accommodate multiple valid designs, we propose an occlusal fit metric based on proximity to the antagonist teeth. We evaluate our method through quantitative experiments and qualitative studies involving expert testimonials. We also release the FDI 16 Crown Dataset, comprising 11,513 annotated intra-oral scans, to support future research in dental CAD.

papers.title: Data-Driven Identification of Uncertainty Sets with Conformance Guarantees
papers.abstract: Formal verification and controller synthesis require accurate models. Conformance relations specify the required accuracy of a model such that properties established for the model carry over to the target system. Existing methods for establishing them from measured data are typically restricted to a single relation, a specific model class, or a downstream verification algorithm. We present ConfID, a unified framework that establishes reachset, trace, and simulation conformance with respect to measured traces by identifying uncertainty sets for a given, possibly nonlinear nominal model. Unmodeled effects are thus captured by nondeterminism rather than by refining the nominal dynamics. For all three conformance relations, the identification is a linear program that minimizes the size of the reachable sets; only its constraints depend on the relation. We further derive distribution-free bounds on the probability that the identified models are conformant for unseen behaviors. Experiments on simulated and real-world data evaluate the models identified for the three relations, confirm the guarantees, and show that these models cover unseen behaviors more reliably than baselines, with comparable or smaller sets.

papers.title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{WeaveVLA}, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context. A learned-query readout summarizes the updated graph representations into compact relational tokens, which condition the action expert alongside the original vision-language context. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages spatial structure preservation. We instantiate WeaveVLA on StarVLA-GR00T and $\pi_{0.5}$, achieving over 98\% average success on LIBERO with both backbones. On LIBERO-Plus, WeaveVLA improves success from 74.9\% to 82.0\% and from 85.7\% to 87.8\%, respectively, with additional improvements on CALVIN D$\rightarrow$D. On three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based variant improves average success from 55.6\% to 70.0\% under standard conditions and from 33.3\% to 53.3\% under OOD perturbations, surpassing the $\pi_{0.5}$ baseline in both settings.

papers.title: Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure for Subsurface Seepage Forecasting and Relief Placement
papers.abstract: Truncating a large heterogeneous diffusion model around a localized, threshold-activated outlet saves degrees of freedom but severs exterior feedback that governs when the outlet opens and how much it discharges. By separating forcing-driven background head from local withdrawal drawdown, Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure (SCBC) maps local physical descriptors to positive exchange coefficients at the cut boundary. Supervised on unforced donor-domain withdrawal responses, these coefficients yield a passivity-preserving reduced operator that generalizes across unseen forcing histories without refitting. We evaluate SCBC on flood-driven subsurface seepage beneath levee foundations against full-grid reference simulations (MODFLOW~6). Across three held-out foundation panels, a single frozen SCBC tree estimator reduced peak-discharge log RMSE by 26.1%, 30.9% and 42.6% relative to identical local patches using a shared boundary coefficient. We then test whether better screening forecasts improve constrained placement, minimizing peak landside toe head subject to a discharge capacity limit and a budget of three sequential full-grid checks. On a separate 36-foundation test using a coarser 30-state ring operator, a neural SCBC estimator improved discharge forecasts across candidates yet selected four over-capacity placements before checks, compared with one for a shared-coefficient ring, which recovered all 144 reference optima after three checks.

papers.title: Euler Characteristics of Perverse Sheaves on Complex Ball Quotients
papers.abstract: Let $X=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{B}^n$ be a finite-volume complex ball quotient with neat lattice. We prove that every nonzero algebraically constructible perverse sheaf on $X$ has positive Euler characteristic. More generally, we establish a criterion for strict positivity on smooth quasi-projective varieties whose logarithmic cotangent bundle is nef and admits an ample negative rational twist of the boundary divisor. For perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support, we give a lower bound in terms of the intrinsic geometry of $X$ for both proper and nonproper quotients. The bound depends on the systole of $X$ and tends to infinity with it. In particular, the minimum Euler characteristic among perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support tends to infinity as one passes to higher levels of any cofinal normal tower of finite covers. We also deduce lower bounds for the middle intersection Betti numbers of projective subvarieties and boundedness of supports with bounded middle intersection cohomology.

papers.title: Selection-aware inference of supernova kicks
papers.abstract: Observed compact objects (isolated or in binaries) used to infer natal kicks are selected by class membership, which depends on disruption, subsequent evolution, and discovery. Ignoring this selection can bias the inferred kicks. To demonstrate this bias in a comprehensive inference framework, we construct a differentiable model for key components of binary evolution, including correlated remnant-mass and kick prescriptions as well as survival probabilities. As initial conditions prior to the first SN, we use a fiducial COSMIC analysis. Using conventional statistical methods to assess bias due to omitted selection factors in a likelihood, we demonstrate this bias concretely. Reliable natal inference requires a forward prediction for both the observed properties and the probability of observing them. Our framework provides a novel method to enable robust neutron star population inference combining heterogeneous observations of multiple NS-pertinent observations.

papers.title: The Privacy Cost of Writing an Audit Receipt Before Its Context Is Known
papers.abstract: An audit recorder must permit exact recovery with a small private index before it knows which questions a future reader will ask. A recursion on question partitions generates the decision trees, their eventwise costs and the price equations. A common-optimal-tree criterion explains when reduction to a fractional cover preserves the result. On uniform binary linear event spaces with four private roles, if every quartet is split evenly by some bit, optimal identification probability at expected follow-up budget $b$ is $(1+b)/2$. Otherwise it is $\min(1/2+b/3,3/4)$. We characterize all priors attaining the latter curve in its rising regime and derive a closed-form compiler for three binary fields. For a population tilted by one pairwise parity we obtain the full budget curve and a single recorder attaining it. On eight negotiated TLS suites the aligned populations allow a 60 percent follow-up rate at a 70 percent identification ceiling. A pairwise correlation with unchanged marginal field frequencies reduces that maximum to 40 percent. Across 960 local TLS sessions, the recorder recovered every negotiated suite using two private bits per session.

papers.title: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
papers.abstract: We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.

papers.title: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
papers.abstract: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $\omega(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an \'{e}tale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

papers.title: Uniqueness and comparison for a singular parabolic equation with a concave nonlinearity
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for $\partial_t u-\Delta u=|x|^{-\gamma}u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, with $0 0$. The solution $U$ is radially symmetric and self-similar, it obeys {two-sided pointwise bounds by multiples of the same profile}, and it is the limit of the solutions with nontrivial data as the data decrease to zero. Finally, we show that $U$ describes the large-time behavior of every nontrivial solution. The proofs replace the singular Gronwall inequality used in earlier work by a quotient estimate which exploits the concavity of $s\mapsto s^q$ and requires no smallness condition.

papers.title: TideSand: Performance-Accurate Sandbox Multiplexing for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: We propose TideSand, a sandbox system that intelligently multiplexes resources for performance-sensitive LLM agents, such as auto research agents working on system measurement tasks. TideSand combines three key ideas: agent-aware scheduling, which schedules sandbox execution intelligently at the tool call level to avoid resource contention; speculative swapping, which offloads the memory of sandboxes waiting on inference and restores it before their next tool call; and selective rollback, which checkpoints selected sandboxes when contention occurs and restores them when machines are idle. We evaluate TideSand across six model-workload pairs on AlgoTune, Terminal-Bench 4.0, and Terminal-Bench Science. TideSand achieves 3.8-10x higher throughput than strict reservation while maintaining tool-call fidelity, or 7-44% higher fidelity than overcommit baselines at similar throughput. Moreover, TideSand reduces the evaluation error on Algotune by 19x through improved tool-call fidelity. We hope the work motivates future research to maintain tool call fidelity while keeping resource utilization high through statistical multiplexing.

papers.title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: An embodied agent built on a language model goes to work with the weights it was given and keeps them for life. To get better, it needs more training, or reflection, memory, search or prompts that cost every step and are lost when the task changes. Editing weights by reasoning, weight-space programming, could end this, but has stayed with models that only reason or relied on a far larger commercial model. We introduce the self-upgrading embodied agent, to our knowledge the first that learns from its own experience by upgrading its own weights on the job, between its tasks, with no training, no gradient, no reward model, no second model, no test-time scaling and no harness or prompt engineering. By day a 27B agent works in a household environment. At night it reads its record, finds many of its steps wasted on replies that reach the token limit before any action, traces the habit to one direction in its hidden states, and rewrites one tensor of its weights. An agent that rewrites itself must first never break itself, so it is its own examiner: it tests every change against its unchanged self on practice tasks and keeps only what holds. When an edit holds, the next day it is a better agent, at the same cost per step: over thousands of held-out episodes, 48 fresh seeds a task, its one kept edit makes it complete significantly more tasks, in fewer steps, with fewer wasted and fewer tokens. This self-improvement is multi-round, stable and continual: through the nights that follow, the upgrade holds, without collapse. Of four sizes of its family, only the 27B agent does this. From here on, an embodied agent need not keep training and inference apart: as it works, it gathers its own experience and upgrades itself, with no separate pre-training or post-training and no human intervention. We believe this opens lifelong continual learning for robots: stable, continual, recursive self-improvement.

papers.title: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
papers.abstract: We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.

papers.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
papers.abstract: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%. Our analysis reveals that effective interfaces reduce unnecessary decisions while preserving essential feedback, with their benefits shaped by agent behavior and physical uncertainty. We further uncover a verification gap, where agents frequently declare success despite observable failures, revealing the need for task-level verification beyond individual actions. Together, these findings establish RUI design as a critical factor in embodied agent reliability.

papers.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
papers.abstract: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. These results follow from a general expression, derived here, for the average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations, valid for generic multiqubit systems and system-environment coupling structures. The infidelity takes the form of a spectral overlap between the noise correlation matrix and a gate-dependent filter function, in which the coherent dynamics of the gate itself shapes the spectral window through which correlated fluctuations enter. The framework converts measured noise correlations into quantitative error budgets and provides a concrete design principle for selecting entangling operations in scalable quantum architectures.

papers.title: Attention Temperature Confounds Zero-Shot Context Extension
papers.abstract: A training-time attention change is usually judged for zero-shot context extension against a dense baseline beyond the training length at the default temperature, $\tau = 1$. The outcome depends on how miscalibrated the baseline is there: the share of perplexity it recovers when its logits are sharpened by one scalar. Under the standard recipe (fp32 master weights), an 8k-trained baseline is 8-15% miscalibrated at 30k in three seed-paired 365M twins; in one of them this makes the block-sparse-trained twin look 7% better, which calibration removes. In pure-bf16 training without master weights the miscalibration is several times larger: an AdamW step ($\beta_2 = 0.95$) on a gain initialised at 1.0 is below half the bf16 spacing at peak learning rates under $1.7\times10^{-3}$, so gains never move (22 checkpoints), the baseline is 37-58% miscalibrated, and block-sparse pretraining, attention dropout and ALiBi look 6-35% better. Calibrating one temperature per model and length removes all three advantages, leaves ALiBi 5% behind RoPE and keeps part of the gain of a positive control, NTK-aware scaling. Unfreezing the gains reverses the block-sparse advantage at 365M and removes 71-89% of it at 1.2B. We recommend reporting extension results at calibrated temperatures and checking that normalisation gains moved.

papers.title: Look Back, Draft Ahead: Corrective Prefix Attention for Parallel Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Parallel speculative decoders propose an entire token block at once, yet one early inconsistency can cause the target to reject its remaining suffix. We introduce Corrective Prefix Attention (CPA), which combines prefix-aware selection with autoregressive supervision to improve these parallel drafts. CPA lets each candidate attend to earlier choices within the block. Fixed candidate shortlists allow all pairwise interactions to be computed before selection, reducing the sequential walk to table lookups, accumulation and lightweight scoring rather than repeated neural evaluations. An auxiliary autoregressive loss trains the shared backbone on clean prefixes without adding an inference pass. Across eight math, code and dialogue benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B targets on Ascend NPUs, CPA commits 13--15\% more tokens per verification round than DSpark and 25--26\% more than DFlash. Its mean speedups reach $3.35\times$ and $3.37\times$ under greedy decoding and $2.86\times$ under sampling for both targets. Ablations support both components, while capacity sweeps demonstrate that greater acceptance alone does not guarantee faster decoding. These results motivate correcting parallel proposals with causal information while keeping sequential computation inexpensive.

papers.title: Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.

papers.title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains
papers.abstract: Software dependencies execute within the trust boundary of downstream applications, yet provenance, static analysis, and package-level behavioral approaches do not directly determine how a released artifact behaves for a specific program. We present Preflight, a program-scoped pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, iteratively synthesizes and validates function-level harnesses, executes resolved artifacts in a restricted environment, records behavioral fingerprints, and compares target behavior against prior versions when suitable baselines exist. We evaluate Preflight on four real software-supply-chain incidents under five application contexts, a 100-package benign corpus, and a controlled function-level versus import-only ablation. Preflight returns malicious verdicts in four incident contexts and a clean verdict in the LiteLLM client context, where the affected proxy-server path is not exercised. All 100 evaluated benign packages receive clean verdicts, with zero observed false positives. In a controlled ablation on Ultralytics and ctx, function-level harnesses expose malicious behavior in both incidents, whereas import-only probing exposes neither. Together, these results show that conditioning behavioral verification on the downstream program can expose security-relevant dependency behavior while remaining selective on benign workloads.

papers.title: Quantales Arising From Rings
papers.abstract: We study the quantale, or multiplicative lattice, of additive submonoids of an arbitrary ring, with particular focus on the question of which properties of the ring can be recovered from it. We show that this quantale, unlike the better-known quantale of ideals, captures significant information about the cardinality, characteristic, and center of the ring. Certain rings, such as non-prime finite fields, torsion-free rings, and those with characteristic 2, are completely determined by their submonoid quantales. We also discuss various other subobject quantales one can associate to a (semi)ring.

papers.title: CASPER: Discovering Spatially Resolved Causal Cell-Cell Communications
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics can reveal where ligands and receptors are expressed together. A harder question is whether exposure to a ligand changes pathway activity in nearby cells, since the same tissue environment can influence both ligand expression and pathway activity. We introduce CASPER, a Bayesian structural equation model that adjusts for receptor expression and represents the shared tissue environment with a Gaussian Markov random field. We show that the ligand-exposure effect is identifiable when the spatial covariance is known and distinguishable from independent noise, the coefficients are constant, and the structural errors are independent and homoskedastic. In simulations, CASPER reduced the bias seen in ordinary regression and in a regression that accounted for spatial dependence only in the outcome. We compared CASPER with CellPhoneDB in four public Xenium datasets. In ovarian cancer, CellPhoneDB found evidence of ligand--receptor expression enrichment for both IL6 and VEGFA. CASPER found greater support for a positive effect of fibroblast IL6 on the inflammatory-response score of ciliated epithelial cells than for an effect of fibroblast VEGFA on the angiogenesis score of endothelial cells. Code accompanies the Supplementary Materials and is available at https://github.com/nySTAT/casperCCC.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Memory as a Collider Observable
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic memory and charge correlators are measured by different detectors, sensitive to soft radiation and to hard charged tracks. We show that the Ward identity of large gauge symmetry relates these quantities as inclusive observables. For lepton pairs produced by an electromagnetic current, we compute all massless multipoint memory correlators and the massive two-point function, whose coincident limit gives the soft photon number. The correlators admit a celestial free-boson representation and remain finite at first radiative order, where recoil generates back-to-back Sudakov logarithms.

papers.title: Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime
papers.abstract: We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\cosh\tau - 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_\alpha(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_\alpha(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does not. A BTZ black hole with the same Hawking temperature reproduces the response to within about ten percent, and the remaining difference is set by the early/late mismatch. A Gaussian mass profile gives the same picture. The horizon radius and the surface gravity vanish at the critical smearing with exponents $1/2$ and $3/2$. At fixed mass the boundary stress tensor coincides with that of BTZ, but the $z^3$ Fefferman--Graham coefficient and the lengths of boundary-anchored geodesics do not.

papers.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Updating an LLM adapter should not require replaying the full interaction history of every active session. Yet reusing key-value (KV) cache entries computed under an earlier version mixes model versions, while full-history re-prefill becomes increasingly costly as histories and session fleets grow. We introduce LiveLora, a model-runtime co-design for exact final-block KV cache migration. Frozen lower decoder blocks and fixed K/V adapter down-projections preserve each token's base projections and low-rank coordinates across adapter versions. The runtime reconstructs candidate K/V, reevaluates the latest token through the final block, and commits the adapter, cache, and next-token logits together. We prove continuation equivalence to full-history re-prefill in exact arithmetic under the stated model assumptions. On Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, median paired publication speedups over full-history re-prefill average $68.98\times$ across five runs for 32 active sessions with 8K tokens each. Serving benchmarks show approximately 4.8% decoding overhead relative to native cached decoding. Compared with retained-boundary replay, compact retention gives a $3.42\times$ reduction in additional session storage at 8K, with similar measured publication-plus-decoding cost. LiveLora allows persistent LLM agents to adopt new adapter versions without replaying their full interaction histories.

papers.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
papers.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

papers.title: Self-similar Inequality Dynamics in Biased Competition for a Conserved Resource
papers.abstract: In many complex systems the redistribution of a conserved resource can generate strong inequality. Important examples are cities exchanging inhabitants, farms competing for farmland, or agents for wealth in saturated markets. Here we model such systems as agents competing for a fixed total resource, and show that coupling agent extinction to a bias favoring richer agents dynamically amplifies this inequality over time. Drawing on an analogy with emulsions, where droplets compete for a conserved quantity, we introduce a dynamical critical resource size that determines an agent's fate. Crucially, this threshold grows in time, continuously raising the bar for survival and further reinforcing inequality. Increasing the bias strength, we find a transition from a continuous resource concentration towards a winner-takes-all outcome. Furthermore, the case of continuous resource concentration is characterized by a self-similar dynamics accompanied by a power-law or exponential increase in inequality, quantified by the Gini coefficient. We derive these results analytically in a mean-field model and compare them to agent-based simulations, showing excellent agreement.

papers.title: Lincege.jl: LINked Cluster Expansions on a GEneral GEometry
papers.abstract: The numerical linked-cluster expansion (NLCE) is a powerful tool for studying properties of quantum lattice models directly in the thermodynamic limit. Here, we introduce Lincege.jl, a versatile, efficient, and easy-to-use package for generating the clusters needed to perform the NLCE on a general finite or infinite lattice. Lincege.jl takes as input only the Bravais lattice vectors, the basis information, and the expansion unit and uses a depth-first search to efficiently generate clusters, their lattice constants, and the sub-cluster information. It outputs final coefficients of the series, expressed in terms of the extensive properties of the clusters, in different orders. The package also contains tools for visualizing the lattice and the generated clusters as well as a classical Ising model solver that can be used as a template for interfacing Lincege.jl with solvers of other lattice models. This package can be installed using the Julia package manager and utilized with example scripts from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/rightleftspin/Lincege.jl. The online documentation, including examples, can be found at https://rightleftspin.github.io/Lincege.jl/stable/.

papers.title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech
papers.abstract: Speaking early turns a prediction into an irreversible public commitment. We introduce SayWhen, a test-time controller that selects a task-directed act shared across typed continuation plans and controls its release as speech. A persistent veto blocks playback when intervening transcripts invalidate the candidate. We define regret-free early speech (RFES) to measure supported pre-endpoint releases without scored incompatibility. On a 72-prefix branching diagnostic, the generated-plan frontier attains 6.0% RFES with zero observed mean regret, versus 8.2% RFES and 0.068 regret for Matched Top-One. Measured planner latency constrains this path; a deterministic retail schema attains 31.7% RFES, compared with 32.0% for the complete policy. In a separate 30-task $\tau$-Voice simulation, schema-derived candidates with cached text-to-speech (TTS) audio attain 21/30 task-level RFES. Eligible audio begins 1.51 seconds before the user-audio endpoint among the 22 tasks with early speech, or 1.11 seconds over all 30 tasks with zero for tasks without eligible early speech. Semantic veto and endpoint waiting each pass 16/30 tasks. Together, the studies demonstrate a controlled coverage-compatibility trade-off and schema-based pre-endpoint operation, making the supported public commitment an explicit unit of voice-agent control.

papers.title: Place-Based Policy from Space: Evidence from Italy's Inner Areas
papers.abstract: This paper evaluates a place-based policy, Italy's National Strategy for Inner Areas (SNAI), using satellite nighttime lights. Targeting structurally fragile and peripheral municipalities, SNAI invests in essential services and economic activities. Staggered difference-in-differences compares 941 funded municipalities with 3,112 eligible controls over 2011--2022. Funding is associated with an expansion of lit area and no detectable change in radiance per lit cell, suggesting that activity extends its footprint rather than intensifying in existing centres. The expansion holds across comparison groups and, descriptively, concentrates at intermediate funding per resident. Annual satellite data can complement slower and coarser statistics.

papers.title: NoveltyGate: Novelty, Not Error, Decides Which VLA Prefix Tokens to Compute Exactly
papers.abstract: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $\pi_{0.5}$ re-encode the camera images and the instruction with a 2B-parameter backbone at every control step, and the feed-forward layers of this prefix account for most of its compute. A natural way to save this compute is to send most tokens through a low-rank MLP and compute exactly only the tokens whose approximation error is large. We find that this intuition is wrong. Even a verifier that knows every token's exact error picks the wrong tokens, producing 1.3--1.7$\times$ larger action deviation than a simple test of whether a token's input is novel, that is, whether it falls outside the subspace seen during calibration. Large errors concentrate in tokens the policy relies on little, such as the third-person camera, while the novelty test favors the wrist camera, a view the action depends on heavily. We call this the error--reliance gap. Building on it, we propose NoveltyGate, a training-free method that routes each prefix token, once per layer and before any multiplication, to either a low-rank or the original MLP. Deciding once per layer instead of once per matrix product avoids moving wide intermediate tensors and keeps every shape static, so the whole prefix runs as a single CUDA graph. On LIBERO, NoveltyGate accelerates the $\pi_{0.5}$ prefix by up to 1.61$\times$, stays 2.7--2.9$\times$ closer to the original policy than channel pruning and low-rank compression at equal compute, and preserves closed-loop task success.

papers.title: Real2Worlds2Real: Scaling Self-Improving Agentic Real2Sim2Real for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Scaling robot manipulation learning remains challenging due to the high cost of collecting real-world interaction data. Real-to-Sim-to-Real (Real2Sim2Real) offers a promising route by enabling policy learning in simulation grounded in real-world observations, yet scaling this paradigm across diverse tasks and physical interactions remains difficult. We introduce Real2Worlds2Real, a self-improving agentic framework that integrates scalable simulation-world construction with policy development. Given limited visual observations and task descriptions, its tool-orchestration harness constructs faithful digital twins and expands them into diverse, physically executable digital cousins. The agent adaptively selects tools and revisits construction decisions, using visual and execution feedback to refine geometry and physical behavior. Building on these worlds, the agent orchestrates policy development by coordinating data generation, policy learning, and refinement based on task requirements and simulation rollout feedback. Across both stages, the agent distills validated procedures into reusable skills that guide subsequent tasks. Experiments demonstrate improved world fidelity and successful real-world policy transfer, with performance gains from increasing world diversity and interaction-data volume. Skill reuse further improves world-building efficiency and long-horizon task success.

papers.title: Localized Strain Tuning of Second-Harmonic Generation in MoS2 Monolayers and Bilayers
papers.abstract: We investigate the modulation of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in CVD-grown MoS2 monolayers and few-layer flakes through localized mechanical deformation applied by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip. MoS2 membranes suspended over microstructured Si3N4 substrates allow simultaneous measurements of force and SHG intensity during controlled approach and retraction cycles. Suspended regions exhibit enhanced SHG relative to substrate-supported regions, with pronounced suppression near the clamping boundaries. While the SHG response during compressive loading varies among individual membranes, adhesion-mediated pulling during retraction consistently reduces the SHG intensity until tip detachment, when the signal recovers. By correlating the optical modulation with the measured pull-off force and a phenomenological estimate of effective strain, we obtain a characteristic sensitivity of approximately 12% SHG modulation per 1% effective strain, with comparable behavior in monolayers and bilayers. These findings reveal adhesion-mediated mechanical deformation as a distinct and reversible mechanism for controlling nonlinear optical emission in atomically thin membranes.

papers.title: Leakage-Safe Auditing of Attribution-Driven Data Curation in Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: When can an attribution-derived anomaly justify changing a medical-imaging training set? We formulate attribution-driven curation as three separately testable claims: anomaly detection, harmfulness estimation, and intervention utility. We test the first and third using a patient-disjoint, identifier-preserving audit of a 3D convolutional classifier for computed tomography angiography aneurysm candidates. We identify 232 exactly zero-valued arrays among 1,201 positive patches, including 170 training positives, and invalidate a historical 321-patch attention-failure subgroup whose identifier-free records were joined to files by position. On the held-out test set, GradCAM++ spatial concentration is central for every candidate class, reversing the historical pattern. GradCAM++ and Integrated Gradients show negative rank-order agreement for positives, limiting method-independent anatomical interpretation. Across five paired training seeds, removing the 170 corrupted training positives yields AUC 0.9617 +/- 0.0044 versus 0.9652 +/- 0.0039 for full-data training (difference -0.0035; 95% CI -0.0082 to 0.0007). Excluding 34 raw-zero test positives widens rather than closes the gap, countering a blank-memorization explanation. Budget-matched random-removal controls suggest the result is not simply an effect of reducing training size. Input corruption does not necessarily imply that deletion improves generalization. Our framework makes leakage control, sample identity, and intervention testing explicit in attribution-driven medical-imaging data curation.

papers.title: Tradeoffs between objective outcomes and human enjoyment of work in human-AI task allocation
papers.abstract: For people, tasks at work are defined by more than their outcome: they are colored by the experience of engaging in that task. As AI systems become increasingly capable of performing human-level work they may be deployed to tasks that people find enjoyable while simultaneously creating comparatively more aversive tasks such as monitoring AI outputs. This creates a thorny tradeoff for managers: whether work should be assigned purely based on the expected performance of the workers in question, or also account for the subjective experience of the person potentially doing the task. Most economic accounts focus on expected utility calculations based on the former. Here, we assess how people balance objective outcomes and more subjective qualities like enjoyment. In a series of large-scale (N=800) behavioral studies in which people allocate tasks to either an AI or human worker we find that people's allocation decisions are best captured by a model that systematically balances relative objective performance with the human worker's expected enjoyment, weighting human experience higher when a task is framed as inducing less enjoyment and adjusting based on the stakes of the task. As AI also makes decisions about work allocation, we compare a set of LLMs. We find many models also deviate from purely objective decisions, particularly when the project stakes are low, but there is wide heterogeneity as to how much and in what manner they weigh enjoyment. These results raise questions about what role human experience may play in decisions around where and how to integrate AI into workplaces. Integration may be jagged across settings due to consideration not only of the relative capabilities of workers, but also the human experience of work, the valence of that experience (e.g., more strongly weighing aversion), the context (e.g., stakes), and who is making or guiding such choices (human or LLM).

papers.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity. Attending to all earlier loops also lets layers skip intermediate ones, so we restrict each layer to a residual window of the latest W loops, forcing every loop to build incrementally on recent ones. Across 6 pretrained LLMs from 3 model families and 9 benchmarks, LoopRes delivers significant and consistent gains: at 2x compute, it improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base by 29.1% over SFT, more than doubling the gain of the state-of-the-art baseline. The gains hold on larger models up to 30B and across all three families. More importantly, from 1.7B to 8B, LoopRes scales more steeply than SFT as compute grows, reaching a higher ceiling while needing less compute on long outputs. These results establish LoopRes as an effective looping approach, delivering both better performance and better test-time scaling.

papers.title: Quantum and classical transport in the underscreened Kondo lattice
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum effects in high-spin Kondo-lattice transport as resistivity approaches the classical spin-disorder limit. Using dynamical mean-field theory and the numerical renormalization group, we calculate resistivity, the Seebeck coefficient, and optical conductivity for the paramagnetic single-channel Kondo lattice away from half filling. At intermediate temperatures, the resistivity for large local spin $S$ approaches the double-exchange plateau. Thermopower retains a positive quantum excess even where resistivity is nearly classical. The excess arises from the transport kernel's particle-hole asymmetry. Even the full Kelvin approximation, often accurate for incoherent correlated metals, captures only part of it. Incomplete Kondo screening leaves residual moments and leads to singular Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures. For $S=1$, the apparent power-law resistivity is consistent with a $1/\ln^2(T_\rho/T)$ asymptote. Above the Kondo scale $T_K$, weak-coupling resistivity follows $1/\ln^2(T/T_K)$. Above the band and exchange scales, the charge susceptibility decreases as $1/T$, while the effective diffusion constant becomes nearly temperature independent, resulting in linear resistivity. A many-body coherent-potential approximation accounts for the spin dependence of the linear coefficient without adjustable parameters.

papers.title: A Systematic Method of GPU Verification on Subsystem Modelling
papers.abstract: ARM Fast Model is a software modelling system for simulating multiple systems IPs integrated in a subsystem. Fast Model allows customer to run whole software stack as early as system IPs' specification is just ready. In this paper, we talk about a systematic method to enable GPU modelling and make whole system software stacks executable for both CPU and GPU in the integrated modelling environment, and eventually the major GPU IP can be verified. With our solution, we can directly run commercial benchmarks like Antutu and GFX Bench in Android target system with underlying ARM Fast Model mobile subsystem support. This was unbelievable in the past due to 3D rendering simulation for GPU verification is very slow. We also introduce some special techniques to improve performance. Eventually the whole software stack can directly work on real hardware without any changes as soon as the first tape-out is ready.

papers.title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^\gamma y,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $\gamma\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a B\^ocher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincar\'e condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\log\rho$ term, $\rho=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $\rho^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.

papers.title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing
papers.abstract: Efficient vehicle routing is critical to logistics and transportation, yet solving large-scale capacitated vehicle routing problems (CVRP) remains computationally challenging due to their combinatorial complexity. One approach to solve large-scale vehicle routing optimization is to identify promising subproblems and then optimize them using solvers. In this paper, we propose a framework of automatic heuristic design (AHD) in which a large language model (LLM) autonomously refines heuristics for selecting subproblems, enabling effective optimization of large-scale CVRP instances. Compared to prior approaches that train task-specific neural networks to select among heuristically constructed subproblems, our method discovers generalizable, interpretable LLM-generated heuristics to directly construct subproblems. Experiments show that our approach achieves comparable in-distribution performance while outperforming neural network-based policies on out-of-distribution instances with large-scale problems.

papers.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
papers.abstract: LLM quantization reduces storage but often degrades predictive fidelity at low bit rates. We propose a training-free, CDF-free, Gaussian-CLT-motivated progressive residual-sign quantization framework that uses randomized orthogonal mixing to promote Gaussian-like residual distributions and improve sign based reconstruction of Transformer weights. Each stage independently normalizes residuals and analytically calibrates reconstruction, progressively recovering quantization errors. The framework enables flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs without learned codebooks, empirical CDFs, or trellis optimization. We evaluate GPT-2 Large and Llama-3-8B across attention and MLP projections. At five residual stages, joint quantization preserves near-baseline predictive fidelity, achieving perplexities of 32.16 and 12.73, compared with full-precision values of 29.89 and 11.07, respectively. Ablations further demonstrate that orthogonal mixing substantially improves reconstruction over identity-based sign coding, while activation-aware scaling improves output fidelity and reduced-precision statistics lower storage overhead with negligible perplexity degradation. Comparisons with conventional quantizers establish the method's progressive fidelity recovery and characterize its storage-quality and runtime trade-offs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of orthogonally mixed residual-sign coding for flexible, training-free Transformer weight compression.

papers.title: MAASAI: A Tool-Augmented Multi-Agent System for Astronomical Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Modern astronomical workflows require the coordinated use of specialised software, scientific archives, heterogeneous data, and domain-specific knowledge. Advances in large language models and multimodal foundation models enable natural-language interaction with scientific data and tools. Realising this potential requires integrating these models with established scientific capabilities. We present MAASAI (Multi-agent Astronomy Assistant for Scientific Analysis and Inference), a modular multi-agent system combining foundation-model reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge, and specialised astronomical tools within a graph-based execution framework. MAASAI coordinates request preparation, planning, execution, and response synthesis via specialised workers. Its architecture supports native and external applications, artefact and provenance management, optional human approval, and configurable inference backends, including fully local deployment with open-weight models. Motivated by SKA-era data-analysis challenges, MAASAI is also designed to support other astronomical domains. We evaluate MAASAI through radio-image benchmarks, single- and multi-step workflow demonstrations, and literature-grounded reasoning. Compared with a commercial-model baseline, MAASAI improves macro-averaged F1 scores from 0.53 to 0.72 for extended/diffuse emission classification and from 0.37 to 0.88 for source morphology classification. Workflow demonstrations show the coordination of measurements, source extraction, archive queries, and catalogue processing. A 94-question literature benchmark yielded generally favourable automated assessments, with comparable ratings from a pilot expert evaluation of 59 answers. These results highlight how tool-augmented multi-agent systems extend foundation-model reasoning to specialised astronomical analyses through established scientific software.

papers.title: Leading-order dynamical QED corrections to the thermodynamics of isospin-asymmetric QCD
papers.abstract: We present a first lattice calculation of the leading-order effect of dynamical photons on the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero isospin chemical potential $\mu_I$, across the onset of charged-pion condensation. In QCD this onset is a second-order transition, which dynamical photons are expected, on general grounds, to drive first order. However, a direct simulation is not possible since unequal quark charges render the QCD+QED action complex at nonzero $\mu_I$. We therefore expand the free energy density $f$ in the electromagnetic coupling $e$ around $e=0$, where the sign problem is absent. The leading-order expansion coefficient, $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$, is the convolution of the photon propagator with the electromagnetic current-current correlator, which we measure with a newly proposed planar source on existing (2+1)-flavor pure-QCD ensembles at nonzero $\mu_I$ and pionic source $\lambda$. At physical quark masses and a single lattice spacing, after extrapolating to vanishing $\lambda$, we find that $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$ is, within errors, independent of $\mu_I$ below the onset and rises sharply across it.

papers.title: Optimization of Piezo Operation for Superconducting TESLA Cavities at EuXFEL
papers.abstract: Superconducting cavities with high-Q factor require precise tuning to match the RF frequency, ensuring stable electromagnetic fields and minimizing RF power consumption. At the European XFEL (EuXFEL) accelerator, TESLA cavities are tuned using slow tuners (step motors) for coarse adjustments and fast tuners (piezoelectric actuators) for fine-tuning and compensating disturbances such as Lorentz Force Detuning (LFD). Piezo actuators, critical to this system, require high-voltage (up to 100V) and high-current (up to 1A) driving signals for effective LFD compensation. However, they are vulnerable to overvoltage, overcurrent, and overheating, and their protection is crucial since replacing damaged piezos in fully assembled modules is infeasible. Additionally, piezo-induced vibrations can affect the machine's stability. Optimizing piezo excitation, by reducing voltage, current, and current slope while ensuring effective LFD compensation, improves equally efficiency, reliability and machine stability. This paper explores the optimization of piezo excitation at EuXFEL, detailing methods and results applicable to other facilities with superconducting cavities as well.

papers.title: Marginal-Cost Clustering for Courier Dispatch: A Parallel Decomposition for Pickup and Delivery with Time Windows and Fleet Sizing
papers.abstract: Courier dispatch poses a pickup and delivery problem with time windows in which requests are batched, windows are soft, couriers start where they are and take open routes, and a fixed dispatch charge makes fleet size a decision. We contribute to the cluster-first, route-second family a grouping criterion that scores a request by its marginal cost, the travel and lateness it adds to the route a courier already plans, rather than by its distance to a centroid, one point standing for a whole workload in space and time. The marginal cost instead knows where a courier is, when it becomes free and what it already carries. Each pass, we hold the marginal costs fixed while we solve one integer program that assigns every request to a courier and chooses which to open, then improve its solution by a descent that relocates and swaps requests between couriers. We then route each dispatched courier exactly. That subproblem is naturally a mixed-integer program, and we solve it by label setting over visited sets, which we prove optimal and cheap enough to run every pass. On instances we generate and on adapted Li & Lim benchmark batches, we beat the best of six published clustering rules by 29% as published and by 12% once those rules carry the same descent. Against an adaptive large neighbourhood search at matched wall-clock we are ahead on the generated instances and level on the benchmark, and we handle 1000 requests and 300 couriers in about a minute.

papers.title: A Unified View of Operator Splitting and Interior-Point Methods
papers.abstract: First-order splitting and interior-point methods offer contrasting computational trade-offs for convex conic quadratic programs, yet their linear systems look remarkably similar. We make this connection precise through the Moreau slack, an unconstrained variable from which multipliers and (ordinary) slacks satisfying exact or barrier-perturbed complementarity are recovered. The remaining feasibility equations define a unified residual whose roots are KKT points at zero barrier parameter and central-path points at positive barrier parameter. Applying splitting to this residual yields projection methods at zero barrier parameter and barrier splitting at positive parameter; Newton's method in the latter setting gives an implicit interior-point method. At fixed positive barrier parameter, matching the splitting metric to current barrier curvature equalises the primal variable corrections under the same regularisation and leaves a factor of two between the Moreau-slack corrections. With metrics frozen at a barrier solution, local analysis identifies when doubling improves (local) convergence and when the primal solve remains the bottleneck. Metric choices that simplify linear solves (eg make them diagonal) become Newton regularisations, exposing a shared convergence cost associated with computational convenience. Finally, a computable defect in the regularised Newton equations gives an accuracy-based criterion for reusing a splitting factorisation.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand
papers.abstract: Generative AI has demonstrated human-level performance on technical work tasks, yet evidence on how these task-level capabilities are changing labor demand remains scarce. We study the firm-level adoption of GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant, across 5,414 multinational firms accounting for 38% of the U.S. programming workforce. To identify causal effects, we exploit a natural experiment generated by firms' predetermined software procurement cycles. Early AI-adopting firms hired more workers before the launch of GitHub Copilot and had larger, more technical, and older workforces. After one year, GitHub Copilot adoption reduces quarterly technical hiring by 29% among review-induced adopters, with no effect on separations, overall technical headcount, or vacancy duration. The hiring slowdown is concentrated in the subset of junior technical roles that involve the highest share of coding work. Overall, AI coding assistance causes firms to shift demand towards more experienced workers and roles that pair some coding with broader design responsibilities.

papers.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
papers.abstract: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while function-guided reconstruction adds the circuit's purpose and each pin's role. Hidden test cases compare outputs with the reference cycle by cycle; power, delay, and area earn credit relative to the reference only when every case passes. Across 432 trials of 6 LLM agent configurations, successful agents recover algorithms and numerical conventions, yet only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials pass every case. Function-guided reconstruction raises the mean functional score, the cycle-weighted share of passed cases, from 24.6% to 30.9%. Of the 58 fully passing designs, only three improve on the reference's combined power, area, and delay, so behavioral recovery and efficient implementation remain distinct challenges.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem
papers.abstract: For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton. Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.

papers.title: Kaon-pair production with NNLO effects
papers.abstract: The Monte Carlo framework McMule has been extended to support the processes $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ and $e^+\,e^-\to K^0\,\bar{K}^0$. Our results include NNLO initial-state QED corrections together with NLO mixed corrections. The latter are evaluated in the FsQED approach, using disperon QED. The implementation is fully differential and can be used with any kaon form factor. We present the total cross section for energies relevant to the CMD-3 experiment and observe very large corrections. For $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ we also present selected differential observables for energies around the $\phi(1020)$ resonance.

papers.title: Wrist-Camera Video Diffusion as Generalizable Robot Policies
papers.abstract: A generalist manipulation policy should perform new tasks, operate in unfamiliar scenes, and transfer skills across robot embodiments. We present Wrist Video Policy (WVP), a closed-loop manipulation framework that learns how manipulation unfolds through video prediction and recovers executable motion through geometric estimation. Our key idea is to represent robot motion through wrist-camera trajectories, which determine the corresponding end-effector poses through a fixed hand-eye transformation. We pair a video generator that predicts future wrist views with a pose estimator adapted from a pretrained 3D model to recover the corresponding camera trajectories. Model stitching maps the generator's predicted latents directly into the estimator's intermediate feature space, bypassing RGB decoding. This decomposition allows task knowledge to expand through broad human and robot video data while reusing geometric motion estimation across tasks and embodiments. The resulting pose estimator transfers across Franka Panda, PiPER-X, and Galaxea R1 Pro without further fine-tuning. Across tabletop and laundry-room settings, WVP generalizes to tasks ranging from precise grasping and inserting to handling deformable objects, achieving a success rate of over 50% in zero-shot out-of-distribution evaluations. Our project page is at https://wrist-video-policy.github.io.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet with IFENN: A Generalized Framework for Coupled Poroelasticity Problems
papers.abstract: Complex, high-dimensional, large-scale poroelasticity simulations using traditional numerical solvers can be prohibitively expensive in terms of computational resources. We introduce an innovative framework for poroelasticity problems that integrates physics-informed machine learning (PI-ML) models with high-performance FEM solvers. This integration is achieved through the Integrated Finite Element Neural Network (IFENN) setup, which uses a staggered scheme between an FEM solver for mechanical equilibrium and a PI-ML model for fluid-flow predictions. We introduce a novel Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet (PIF-MIONet) architecture, in which a fusion network encodes the outputs of the MIONet branches. The MIONet encodes different input functions, and the fusion network enables early interaction between the inputs, supporting generalization across multiple scenarios while adhering to the underlying physics of the poroelasticity problem. We study different examples, covering 2D and 3D domains and considering variable material properties and time discretizations. We test the models on unseen loading histories, demonstrating accuracy and generalizability across scenarios. For complex geometries and boundary conditions, we show that with both physics and data considered in the loss function, a PI-ML model can be trained using only 0.1\% of the training increments used for pure data-driven training. In addition, we expand the PIF-MIONet to incorporate a domain decomposition approach, which was found to be particularly useful when modeling flow over more complex geometries with more localized phenomena. For the first time, IFENN is implemented using the open-source multiphysics simulator GEOS for the FEM part, providing a path for the framework's application to industrial-scale simulations and complex multiphysics problems.

papers.title: Underlying-event properties in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV measured with the ALICE detector at the LHC
papers.abstract: This contribution reports measurements characterizing the underlying event at midrapidity in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV, based on LHC Run 3 data collected by ALICE. The charged-particle number and summed transverse-momentum densities are measured as a function of the leading-particle transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}$) in the toward, transverse, and away regions, defined relative to the azimuthal direction of the leading charged particle. The particle densities in the transverse region are observed to increase steeply at low $p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}$, followed by a plateau for $p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}>5$ GeV/$c$. The results are compared with measurements at lower center-of-mass energies to illustrate the energy dependence of the underlying-event activity, and with predictions from PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4.
authors: Jes\'us Eduardo Mu\~noz M\'endez (for the ALICE Collaboration)

papers.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
papers.abstract: Slay the Spire 2 (STS2) is a single-player deck-building game that requires long-term planning under heavy randomness. We present AlphaDefect, an expert-level AI system for STS2: for each character, one network trained with proximal policy optimization (PPO) makes every decision of a run, in combat and outside it. At the highest difficulty, Ascension 10, on two versions of the game current in November 2026 and on test seeds not played in training, AlphaDefect wins 62-77% of runs across six characters with greedy play and 68-80% with test-time search, after 1.3 to 6.7 billion decisions of training per character; runs uploaded by human players of all levels are won 11-20% of the time at the same difficulty. The networks read the game as entity records that identify each card, relic and enemy through a learned embedding and attributes from the game data, together with consequences of public information computed by the engine. Ablations show how much the agent depends on this encoding: without these identities, the network did not win a single run, and without the computed consequences it won 8.3 points fewer. To our knowledge, AlphaDefect is the strongest publicly reported STS2 agent as of November 2026.

papers.title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
papers.abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

papers.title: Fifth-order KdV solitary waves in a nonlinear electrical transmission line
papers.abstract: We report the controlled experimental observation of solitary waves governed by the fifth-order dispersion Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To achieve vanishing cubic dispersion, we use a mutual inductive coupling between nearest-neighbor inductors within a nonlinear electrical transmission line. We then experimentally characterize the resulting solitary waves through direct spatiotemporal measurements of the dispersion relation, its oscillatory tail profiles, amplitude-width scaling, and amplitude-velocity relation, finding good agreement with semi-analytical predictions. Collision experiments between two (co- or counter-propagating) solitary waves also show that their self-similar profile persists after interaction, up to a time shift. Dissipation effects are also quantified.

papers.title: A locally conservative LDG method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem
papers.abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem representing the interaction between incompressible flows and porous media flows through the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman interface conditions. A fully discrete numerical scheme has been proposed and analyzed employing backward Euler temporal discretization and a locally conservative LDG scheme for the space discretization. The well-posedness of the numerical scheme has been obtained under a small data condition. Optimal a priori error estimates have been proven in the energy norm, as well as the L2-norm for t>0. Numerical experiments ensure the efficiency of the theoretical results

papers.title: Planar Graphs Embed into Graphs with Treewidth $O(\log n /\epsilon)$
papers.abstract: We construct a stochastic embedding of $n$-vertex planar graphs into graphs of treewidth $O(\log n/\epsilon)$ and expected distortion $1+\epsilon$ for any parameter $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. This result yields randomized polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTASes) for a broad class of connectivity problems on planar graphs, including the $k$-MST problem. The treewidth bound is asymptotically optimal and settles a conjecture of Chang, Cohen-Addad, Conroy, Le, Ma. Pilipczuk, and Mi. Pilipczuk (2025). The key idea is a new construction of a stochastic balanced cut of size $O(\log n/\epsilon)$ and expected distortion $1+\epsilon/\log n$ for every edge. We construct these cuts using the minimax principle, an approach that differs significantly from existing cut constructions based on a random clustering hierarchy. Our embedding extends to minor-free graphs using the Robertson-Seymour decomposition, giving the same treewidth bound. Using this decomposition, we obtain the first randomized PTASes for many connectivity problems in minor-free graphs, including the Steiner tree problem and its prize-collecting variant.

papers.title: Quantitative thick-fiber property
papers.abstract: We introduce the quantitative thick-fiber property, an analogue of the Entov--Polterovich non-displaceable fiber theorem for maps whose coordinate functions need not Poisson commute. We prove that this property holds for closed symplectic manifolds admitting a suitable, not necessarily linear, functional on the space of continuous functions. Conversely, we establish an obstruction and show that the property fails for certain irrational symplectic four-tori and Kodaira--Thurston manifolds. These results reveal a new rigidity--flexibility distinction: whereas the Entov--Polterovich theorem gives a universal fiber-rigidity phenomenon, its quantitative counterpart holds on some closed symplectic manifolds and fails on others, thereby defining a new symplectic rigidity invariant. We also introduce the non-displaceability width of a continuous map, defined as the infimum of the radii for which a non-displaceable thick fiber exists, and use it to obtain quantitative obstructions to uniform approximation by maps with small Poisson brackets.

papers.title: A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollob\'as--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint
papers.abstract: We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollob\'as--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.

papers.title: A hybrid effective field theory description of diffuse baryons
papers.abstract: Galaxy feedback mechanisms that displace baryonic gas on large scales are a dominant uncertainty in many cosmological analyses. Measurements that directly probe the baryonic component, such as Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure (FRB DM) and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect, can therefore be used to place constraints on feedback and inform other analyses, such as weak lensing. Thus far, analytic methods to model the effects of feedback are either limited to large scales, missing the regime of high signal-to-noise, or have many parameters, weakening constraining power. We propose a Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT) approach, relying on the full gravitational displacement field computed in an $N$-body simulation. We account for feedback via a Lorentzian suppression with a single effective parameter, $c_f^2$. To describe the diffuse baryon field, we extend the arguments by Andrew et al. (arXiv:2604.25828), leveraging most baryons being in a diffuse state to reduce a full bias expansion to just the linear bias, $b_{1,d}^L$. With just these two parameters, we fit the diffuse gas power spectrum in most variants of the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations at percent-level accuracy out to $k=1\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at redshift $z=0.5$ and $k=1.5\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at $z=1$. Further, by fitting the diffuse gas power spectrum including terms argued to be negligible, we show that their contribution is minimal. Applying this prescription for diffuse electron gas enables constraints on both cosmology and astrophysics without the need to marginalize over many unknown parameters.

papers.title: UMAMI: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Evidence-Grounded Dietary Decisions
papers.abstract: Dietary decisions require identifying a food's nutrient content and considering individual dietary needs, but recognizing food from an image alone does not provide this information. Visually similar foods can have different nutrient profiles, so selecting the wrong food record can lead to incorrect decisions even when nutrient rules are applied correctly. Furthermore, satisfying nutrient constraints does not necessarily establish a food's relevance to a person's intake.
