papers.abstract: Immersive Video (IV), a live-action stereoscopic 180-degree video format, has been shown to elicit a strong sense of Presence and enhance psychological closeness to individuals depicted in the video. However, whether these effects persist beyond exposure and are accompanied by subsequent self-initiated behaviour remains unclear. In this study, 84 participants were assigned to either an IV or a 2D video group, and psychological and behavioural outcomes were tracked over a two-week period. Psychological outcomes were assessed before and immediately after exposure and at approximately 3, 7, and 14 days post-exposure, while self-initiated behaviour was assessed during follow-up. Psychological closeness remained significantly higher in the IV group than in the 2D group for up to 7 days and remained elevated above baseline within the IV group at 14 days. Lasting-impression ratings were also significantly higher in the IV group throughout the follow-up period. Among participants who completed both scheduled follow-up assessments, 45.9% in the IV group met the operational criterion for early self-initiated engagement, compared with 13.2% in the 2D group. Furthermore, a higher proportion of participants in the IV group reported active or socially oriented behaviours. These findings suggest that IV can elicit psychological effects that persist beyond exposure and may encourage subsequent self-initiated engagement.

papers.title: JKO-GRPO: Augmenting GRPO with Wasserstein Proximal Steps for Flow-Matching VLAs
papers.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $\pi_0,\pi_{0.5}$ generate continuous action chunks by flow matching, and online reinforcement learning (RL) can improve them beyond supervised fine-tuning. Existing methods, such as Flow-GRPO and $\pi_{\mathrm{RL}}$, optimize likelihood ratios of stochastic denoising transitions, which reweight the sampled actions by their advantages but do not use the distances between them. We propose JKO-GRPO, which augments Flow-GRPO with Wasserstein proximal steps, with two contributions: (1) At each state, we treat the group of sampled actions as an empirical distribution and formulate policy improvement as a Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) step. We use a soft discrete $c$-transform to construct transport targets from group-relative advantages and combine shared-noise regression of the deterministic flow sampler onto these targets and combined with the clipped Flow-GRPO objective without Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization. (2) We extend this approach to sequential VLA control through random-time branching: we select one or multiple action-chunk indices along old-policy trajectories and independently apply group-level JKO updates using candidate continuations from the corresponding states.

papers.title: Kinetic inductance of two-dimensional viscous electron fluid
papers.abstract: Modern high-mobility two-dimensional electron systems are pure enough to manifest hydrodynamic regime of electron transport similar to dynamics of classical fluids. With the bulk scattering controlled by momentum-conserving electron-electron collisions, these novel hydrodynamic materials demonstrate systematic violation of conventional metallic behavior due to the Drude model in stationary electric transport. In this letter, we study the linear reactive AC response of 2D electron fluid in a narrow channel geometry and show that the essentially non-local viscous dissipation induces non-trivial size effect in it. In particular, kinetic inductance, which represents collective inertia of the entire electron fluid, is enhanced by non-uniform flow profile and, in contrast to diffusive transport, dominates the electrical impedance already in collisional regime by virtue of viscous skin effect. The onset of reactive behavior falls within the microwave frequency domain in the state-of-the-art 2D hydrodynamic conductors which makes them promising material system for applications in high-frequency electronics at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
papers.abstract: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.

papers.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
papers.abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,\alpha}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,\alpha}$ is of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$.

papers.title: Reducing Authorship Attribution Risk in Student Texts Through Style-Conditioned Rewriting
papers.abstract: Building NLP applications for education is constrained by data scarcity due to student privacy concerns and data regulations. To address this, we propose a style-aware approach to rewriting student forum posts that retains analytical value while reducing identifiability. Our method isolates content, structure, and style as separate conditioning channels and aggregates over student-disjoint exemplar partitions within style clusters, extending Differentially Private In-context Learning (DP-ICL) with cluster-restricted retrieval. Across three educational NLP datasets, our approach achieves high style fidelity, preserves downstream task performance, and reduces authorship attribution risk relative to the original student-written texts, including against a dedicated authorship-attribution model.

papers.title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for CM elliptic curves of analytic rank one
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for elliptic curves over the field of rational numbers with complex multiplication and analytic rank one.

papers.title: Group Buying through Bankruptcy Rules: Cost Sharing and Endogenous Pricing
papers.abstract: Group buying allows independent buyers to pool their demand and benefit from quantity discounts that would not be available to them individually. While collective purchasing reduces total procurement costs, it raises a fundamental allocation question: how should the resulting savings be distributed among heterogeneous buyers? We address this question by integrating cost-allocation and bankruptcy approaches into a unified group-buying framework. Starting from a continuous quantity discount function, we examine cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and develop an endogenous pricing representation in which each buyer's effective discount may depend on the demand profile of the entire group. We then establish a connection between group buying and bankruptcy theory by interpreting the aggregate savings from cooperation as the estate and each buyer's potential savings as its claim. This formulation allows us to derive cost-allocation mechanisms based on the proportional, constrained equal awards, constrained equal losses, and Talmud rules. For each rule, we obtain the corresponding buyer-specific price function and characterize the associated variable discount factor. We further examine the relationships between bankruptcy-based and cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and use a numerical example with simulated data to compare their implications. The proposed framework links alternative fairness principles for allocating cooperative savings to economically interpretable pricing mechanisms, providing a unified basis for analyzing how group purchasing gains are distributed among heterogeneous buyers.

papers.title: Initial Field Test of a Quadrupedal Robot at SLAC Beam Dump East (BDE): A Sandbox for Robotics in Accelerator Operations
papers.abstract: Deploying field robotics in large scale particle accelerator facilities offers significant potential to enhance operational efficiency, promote facility sustainability, and reduce personnel exposure to radiation and other hazards. As key underlying technologies mature, field robotics are seeing broader deployment across various industrial sectors. However, accelerator facilities have remained cautious in adopting these systems, primarily due to concerns regarding cost versus return on investment and the risk of equipment collisions. In addition, operational experience with SLAC's Remotely Operated Accelerator Monitoring platform, ROAM highlighted critical technical challenges, including radiation tolerance and poor network connectivity in enclosed accelerator areas. This paper presents the findings from a recent test drive of a Boston Dynamics SPOT quadrupedal robot equipped with a SPOT Arm payload conducted at SLAC's Beam Dump East facility. We evaluate the technical feasibility and operational considerations of deploying quadrupedal field robotics within accelerator environments. Furthermore, we report key practical challenges, such as protective suits that impede navigation sensors and low light infrared navigation in unlit spaces. Finally, we outline potential development pathways toward adaptive learning and autonomous execution for future routine field robotics operations in accelerator facilities.
authors: M. A. Montironi (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory)

papers.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
papers.abstract: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

papers.title: TASC: Time-to-Collision Anticipation and Selective Crowd Attention for Non-Holonomic Service Robots
papers.abstract: Service robots that share corridors and lobbies with people must keep moving without endangering them. Reactive planners can stop indefinitely in dense crowds (the freezing robot problem), whereas the attention-based learned navigators that dominate the standard crowd benchmark assume holonomic motion or emit discrete actions unsuited to a differential-drive base. This paper presents TASC, a navigation system for a non-holonomic service robot that integrates an attention-based crowd encoder, an anticipatory collision feature, and a continuous-control policy. We adapt the dual-selection attention module, originally developed for discrete-action value learning, to proximal policy optimization for continuous velocity control, and add a closing-speed time-to-collision feature, a conservative estimate of the time to contact that serves as both an observation and a reward term. The policy is trained on a high-fidelity 3D robot model in NVIDIA Isaac Lab with 10,000 parallel environments, social-force-model pedestrians, and randomized crowd sizes. In 30,000 evaluation episodes, each run to its end, the policy timed out in fewer than 0.5% at every tested crowd density. This liveness comes at a cost: pedestrian collisions rise from 4.5% with five pedestrians to 17.4% with ten. In an ablation with four seeds per variant, policies retrained without the time-to-collision feature succeed 4 to 7 percentage points less often. The policy runs in Gazebo without retraining and on a commercial differential-drive service robot through a ROS 2 package with an inference latency below 10 ms, verified in a hardware-in-the-loop test with virtual pedestrians.

papers.title: Stable eigenmodes of the Large-scale circulation in Turbulent Convection
papers.abstract: Turbulent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection (RBC) is a canonical system for studying buoyancy-driven turbulence. Its defining feature is a system-size large-scale circulation (LSC), whose dynamics reflect the coupling between coherent motion and turbulent fluctuations. Starting from the Boussinesq Navier-Stokes and temperature equations, we derive three coupled stochastic equations for the LSC angular velocity and its associated dipolar temperature field. The deterministic dynamics contain an unstable no-LSC set and two symmetry-related stable finite-LSC states. Linearization about either finite-LSC state yields one purely relaxational eigenmode and a pair of damped oscillatory eigenmodes whose frequency is set by the LSC turnover rate. Turbulent fluctuations continually excite the latter, providing a dynamical origin for the observed quasi-periodic oscillations. Experiments in a thin-disk cell directly resolve both eigenmodes and show their predicted Rayleigh-number scalings. The same stochastic dynamics also provide a route to rare cessations and reversals. This theory-experiment framework provides a tractable example of how coherent circulation states, intrinsic modes, and fluctuation-driven transitions emerge in turbulent convection, with broader relevance to geophysical and astrophysical flows.

papers.title: Diversity in Unity, Theory in Practice: Hierarchical Multitask Benchmarks for Chinese Minority Languages
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid advancement of LLMs, their performance on linguistically and culturally diverse minority languages within a unified national context remains underexplored. We present CMiLBench, a collection of hierarchical multitask benchmarks designed to translate theoretical notions of "diversity in unity" into practical evaluation for three representative Chinese minority languages: Tibetan, Mongolian, and Uyghur. CMiLBench comprises 24,663 instances across 5 difficulty levels and 17 tasks spanning foundational ability, cultural specificity, and safety alignment. We adopt existing dataset adaptation, minority knowledge construction, and high-resource benchmark translation to construct CMiLBench. We assess 14 state-of-the-art commercial and open-source LLMs with a hybrid framework that integrates automatic metrics and LLM-as-a-Judge scoring. The comparative experimental results reveal the gap between theoretical capability and practical utility. CMiLBench serves as a foundational and scalable evaluation resource to bridge the digital language divide and promote the informatization and intelligentization of low-resource Chinese minority languages.

papers.title: Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss bounds dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling
papers.abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling dresses the vacuum with virtual photons whose response to the coupling strength exceeds that of any coherent probe, yet these photons never leave the cavity and cannot be detected. A parametric drive at the dynamical-Casimir resonance converts them into real photons that a detector can collect. We show that this conversion is self-limiting: converting the virtual photons of an ultrastrongly coupled probe into real, extractable photons opens the cavity port that removes them, so the retained metrological gain is set by the accumulated cavity loss rather than by the pure-state ceiling. In the driven quantum Rabi model the pure-state quantum Fisher information on the coupling reaches $1.7\times10^{5}$ times the coherent baseline; at a cavity linewidth of $246$~MHz, typical of coplanar-waveguide flux-qubit circuits, master-equation dynamics retain $0.96\%$ of it. In a 32-qubit Dicke model the retained fraction is $2.6\%$ at the largest photon basis computed. Eighteen lossy configurations from both models fall on one curve of the accumulated loss, the product of linewidth and interrogation time, which halves the retained information at $0.13$. The extraction cost, not the lossless ceiling, is the figure of merit for any protocol that reads bound vacuum correlations through a lossy port.

papers.title: Quantum tomography of ququart states of optical vector vortices based on measurements in mutually unbiased bases
papers.abstract: In this paper we present an original method for quantum state tomography of vector optical vortices with an axially symmetric transverse polarization profile. We present an interference technique which allows one to distinguish states of vector vortices with a fixed topological charge with high accuracy. We also demonstrate the feasibility of experimental quantum tomography of the density matrix in the logical ququart space built on vector vortices, with high fidelity for all 20 basis states. It is shown that the proposed tomography scheme provides a uniform characterization of states in all mutually unbiased bases of the ququart space.

papers.title: Probability-Feasible Historical Transport: Sharp Bounds and Falsification Tests for Distributional Pre-Trend Designs
papers.abstract: Distributional difference-in-differences studies often assume that the post-policy gap between treated and comparison groups is a mixture of pre-policy gaps. This historical-transport assumption can fail in ways that one-statistic checks miss. When policy events are pooled, the average counterfactual can be a valid distribution although no event's counterfactual is, and pooled bounds can exclude the true average effect. Mixtures of past gaps can assign negative probability to outcomes, and cutoff-by-cutoff bounds can be incompatible. We characterize sharp bounds and give breakdown radii, a grid-free confidence region, and tests with and without an experiment. The tests reject transport in the National Supported Work data and expose impossible state counterfactuals behind a pooled minimum-wage bound. For the 1993 Earned Income Tax Credit expansion they pass through 1995, when bounds put single mothers' employment gain relative to childless women at 5 to 7 points; the gain stays positive after dropping early welfare-waiver states.

papers.title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation
papers.abstract: We develop a direct quantum simulation algorithm for finite homotopy approximations to the non-isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations. A primitive-variable formulation gives polynomial residuals in the fields and their spatial and time derivatives, including density-weighted time derivatives. On a periodic grid, applying each spatial stencil uniformly to every factor in a shifted product preserves the dynamics of the finite homotopy hierarchy in an affine linearisation. Because each deformation equation depends only on lower homotopy orders, the lifted generator matrix is strictly block lower-triangular and hence nilpotent. The resulting finite-polynomial solution evaluates the final state directly without time-stepping error, while explicit short-time convergence conditions bound the homotopy truncation error on a fixed grid. In two-dimensional Taylor-Green flow, initial pressure balance removes the leading longitudinal acceleration and delays the onset of dilatational kinetic energy from quadratic to quartic in time. At Mach numbers 0.2 and 0.4, the fifth-order hierarchy reproduces viscous dissipation over a longer interval than pressure-dilatation at the same relative tolerance. We identify auxiliary variables representing the same evolving product, compile the finite-polynomial evolution into logical quantum circuits, and recover a signed velocity Fourier mode via Hadamard interference. Together, the Taylor-Green energy budgets quantify the accuracy windows of each homotopy order, while coarse-grid circuits verify the signed readout and measure gate counts. For higher-order evolution on finer grids, merging coincident stencil terms and combining block-encoded products along strictly increasing homotopy-order paths substantially reduce the predicted normalisation cost.

papers.title: SuperFine3D: Efficient Global-Local Recursive Refinement for Extremely Detailed 3D Geometry Generation
papers.abstract: High-resolution images contain rich visual details that require fine geometric structures for faithful 3D reconstruction. However, generating extremely detailed 3D geometry from images requires substantial computational resources and training data, making high-resolution geometry generation challenging for existing state-of-the-art models. In this paper, we present SuperFine3D, an efficient framework for generating extremely detailed 3D geometry through global-local recursive refinement. SuperFine3D learns a shared refinement operator from paired coarse-to-fine representations and recursively reuses it to progressively synthesize finer geometry beyond the training resolutions, without requiring additional paired supervision at target resolutions. To make recursive refinement computationally efficient, we introduce spatial-cell attention, which restricts high-resolution interactions to local spatial neighborhoods while maintaining bounded communication across neighboring cells. We further propose spatially anchored cross-scale guidance, which leverages globally contextualized coarse geometry to guide local detail synthesis and preserve structural consistency. In addition, geometry-aware training objectives encourage the refinement process to preserve stable geometric structures while introducing fine-grained surface details. Experiments demonstrate that SuperFine3D generates geometry at a $4096^3$ decoder-grid resolution, corresponding to a sparse $256^3$ latent lattice, using a shared refinement operator trained only on $512^3$--$1024^3$ representations. Compared with a full-attention recursive baseline, SuperFine3D achieves a $9.4\times$ speedup in end-to-end inference and reduces peak GPU memory usage by $23.0\%$, while improving cross-scale structural consistency and producing cleaner surfaces with finer geometric details.

papers.title: Contamination at the Operating Point: Train-Test Identity Overlap Inflates Low-FMR Face Recognition Accuracy by an Order of Magnitude
papers.abstract: Face verification systems are deployed by selecting a decision threshold that achieves a target false match rate (FMR); performance is then reported as the corresponding false non-match rate (FNMR). In practice, deployed systems operate at FMR $\le 10^{-6}$, but widely used benchmarks can share identities with the models' training corpora. Prior work (Wu et al., 2024) measures the resulting optimistic bias as a small additive change in 10-fold accuracy (up to 1.01 percentage points). We show that the bias is neither small nor constant: it is a multiplicative error that grows as FMR falls. First, we audit train-test overlap with a detector calibrated against a null distribution (rather than a hand-tuned threshold). Relative to WebFace42M, we flag 88.6% of MS1MV3 identities and 14.3% of IJB-C subjects as present, despite WebFace260M's published de-overlap explicitly naming IJB-C. Manual review of 100 flagged IJB-C subjects confirms 69.2%, implying a residual overlap of roughly 9.9%. Second, holding the model fixed, removing only the contaminated identities from the test set increases FNMR by 3.6$\times$ at FMR=$10^{-4}$, 6.3$\times$ at FMR=$10^{-5}$, and 13.9$\times$ at FMR=$10^{-6}$, while a same-size random removal does not. The effect is traced to a shorter impostor tail that lowers the threshold. The magnitude of the shift depends on the training corpus and does not cancel betweent margin between our model and a publicbaseline by half. Third, we give the first direct measurement of the effective number of independent impostor comparisons in IJB-C: only 2.7 million effectively independent comparisons at FMR=$10^{-6}$, which is below all commonly accepted reporting rules. Finallyth a known training corpus, we build areal-face protocol with audited zero overlap that resolves FMR=$10^{-8}$.

papers.title: Explainable Emotion and Mental Health Reasoning in Large Language Models Using Theories of Emotion
papers.abstract: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled a wide range of applications. However, their ability to simulate human-like behavior and reasoning remains unclear. While emotion detection is a better-established Natural Language Processing (NLP) task, existing approaches primarily focus on directly classifying text into predefined emotion classes, often overlooking the appraisal process that explains why an individual experiences a particular emotion in a given situation. In this work, we propose Psychology-based Chain-of-Thought (PsyCoT) reasoning, a theory-driven prompting strategy grounded in the Schachter-Singer and Cognitive Appraisal theories of emotion. We propose and evaluate PsyCoT for subjective NLP tasks, including emotion analysis, emotion intensity prediction, stress analysis, and depression severity identification. Our evaluation covers four levels of classification complexity: binary, multiclass, multi-label, and ordinal scaling, spanning 11 languages. We assess the performance of five state-of-the-art LLMs across these selected subjective NLP tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that PsyCoT prompt variants improve the standard chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting across the evaluated tasks. Across all evaluated tasks, PsyCoT yields F1 score gains ranging from 0.5% to 28.1%, depending on the model, task, and language configuration.

papers.title: Attacking Tabular Foundation Models: An Experimental Taxonomy of Context Poisoning and Test-Time Evasion
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models condition predictions on labeled examples supplied at inference time, creating an attack surface that differs from conventional model training. We study four manipulation families (label flipping, backdoor context poisoning, clean-label context selection, and test-time evasion) and organize them by attack stage, label consistency, and distributional realism. TabPFN-2.5, TabICL, and XGBoost are evaluated on CIC-IDS2017 and N-BaIoT using a common preprocessing and evaluation pipeline. Backdoor context poisoning provides strong targeted control over the in-context models with little change in clean accuracy, whereas selecting real, correctly labeled boundary-crowding rows causes no systematic accuracy degradation up to a 20% bias fraction. A simplified surrogate-transfer constrained PGD attack inspired by, but not equivalent to, CAPGD also produces test-time evasion, outperforming equal-budget random noise in most settings. The comparison shows that attack effectiveness depends strongly on both where manipulation occurs and how much freedom the attacker has to alter the data.

papers.title: Network contextuality beyond binary outcomes
papers.abstract: Can a joint measurement reveal nonclassical behaviour in independently prepared systems that share no entanglement? We study network contextuality by extending the two-qubit test of bi-contextuality [G. Ruffolo et al., arXiv:2507.08461 (2025)] to projective measurements with more than two outcomes. In one laboratory, an observer measures the systems individually or jointly performs two compatible global measurements constructed from them. The individual probabilities constrain the possible classical correlations at each source. For our preparations, every noncontextual model with outcome-deterministic and source-independent assignments predicts a nonzero average product of the two global outcomes. The joint quantum measurement gives zero. We construct explicit product states realizing this contradiction for $N=d$ independent sources, each preparing one $d$-dimensional system, with $2\leq d\leq9$. We derive an inequality in observed probabilities, prove its single-source bounds are exact for these preparations, and give sufficient thresholds for violations under independent depolarizing noise. For this family of preparations the dimension range is sharp: for every $d\geq10$ the individual probabilities admit a zero assigned average, so the certificate fails. The same data admit a noncontextual explanation when source independence is relaxed.

papers.title: Support functions of sections of $p$-minimal tubes
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact $p$-minimal hypersurface in ${\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ with boundary in two parallel hyperplanes. We study the convex hulls $\Omega(\tau)$ of its horizontal sections through their support function $H(\tau,\cdot)$, without any assumption on the topology of $M$. We prove that $H$ is a viscosity subsolution of a degenerate elliptic inequality. For $n=2$ it is of Monge--Amp\`ere type, and its equality case for minimal surfaces with circular sections is Riemann's system. A posteriori, $H$ is locally semiconvex and every hull is a smooth convex body; the inequality then also holds in the sense of measures, with the edges of the hulls appearing as atoms of Alexandrov's area functions. Averaging over directions gives a catenary-type inequality for the mean width of the hulls. It yields lifetime bounds for $p$-minimal tubes when $n>p$. For minimal surfaces in ${\mathbb R}^3$ it gives a sharp bound for the distance between the planes in terms of the perimeters of the hulls of the boundary curves, with equality only for a catenoid. For one convex curve in each plane this recovers, by a different method, the nonexistence and rigidity theorem of Bernstein and Breiner. The bound extends to non-convex curves and to boundaries with several components. Finally, we show that the Meeks annulus conjecture is equivalent to the absence of atoms in the area functions of the hulls of all intermediate sections.

papers.title: Asymptotically Optimal Representation of Tree-Like Graphs
papers.abstract: We show how to represent a graph with $n$ nodes, $m=n+k=O(n)$ edges, and $h\le k$ nodes with more than one incoming edge in asymptotically optimal space, in a way that supports basic navigational operations quickly.

papers.title: Randomized MST Certification beyond Cacti
papers.abstract: We study minimum spanning tree certification under explorable edge uncertainty. Edge weights lie in open intervals or singleton sets, and querying an edge reveals its weight at a known positive cost. On general graphs the best known randomized competitive ratio is $1+1/\sqrt2$, while the optimal ratio $3/2$ is known only for cacti. We go beyond cacti in two ways, with conditions that refer to the uncertain edges outside the upper-limit tree rather than to the graph alone. For unit query costs we give a $3/2$-competitive algorithm, which is best possible, whenever every block has at most two such edges; this includes all graphs whose blocks are cycles or theta graphs. The algorithm replaces the constant budget of the water-filling method by budgets chosen with lookahead to the next fundamental cycle. For arbitrary positive query costs and every fixed $k\ge1$, we obtain ratio $1+\sqrt{k/(2(k+1))}$ whenever every block has at most $k$ such edges, in particular when every block has cycle rank at most $k$. This is below $1+1/\sqrt2$ for every $k$, and we show that it is the best ratio attainable with a constant water-filling budget.

papers.title: Scattering amplitudes in AdS$_5\times$ S$^5$ from the pure spinor superstring
papers.abstract: We formulate a BRST-invariant prescription for the integration of zero modes in the pure spinor superstring on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The measure includes contributions absent in flat space and admits a description in terms of picture changing operators or a non-minimal regulator. The prescription is valid for genus-zero amplitudes with arbitrary multiplicity and external states and removes a central obstacle to amplitude computations in this background. We use it to perform the first direct worldsheet computation of two and three-point amplitudes of half-BPS supergravity states. The properly normalised three-point amplitudes exactly reproduce the results of planar ${\mathcal N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory.

papers.title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
papers.abstract: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. The conclusions hold on residual subsets of a nonempty $C^1$-open set and follow from Chaidez's contact blender and localized contact perturbations. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy. The proof compares long-bar counts with graph volume through contact tomography and filtered continuation. Under strong translated nondegeneracy, we show that super-exponential translated-pair growth in a compact interior window forces super-exponential growth of short bars born in the surrounding window.

papers.title: Hilbert measures of non-coregular representations of the circle and orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We give explicit constructions of the Hilbert measure, which transports the integral of an invariant smooth function from a representation to the image of the Hilbert embedding, for certain representations of the circle, orthogonal, and special orthogonal groups that are non-coregular, meaning that the algebra of invariants is not a polynomial algebra. These include all $4$-dimension real circle representations, a family of $6$-dimensional circle representations, and $k$ copies of the defining representations of the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups when $k$ is large enough that the representation is not coregular. For the circle representations, we also construct the Hilbert measure on the singular symplectic quotient at level zero.

papers.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
papers.abstract: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors. We present Wactorz, an open-source runtime in which LLM-generated agents are long-lived, supervised actors: a planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts that actor alone, with its state intact, when it crashes. All coordination rides on MQTT, so agents can be spawned on, and live-migrated between, edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi, and every internal event is a topic external systems can subscribe to. The recorded demo builds a camera-to-lamp automation from one chat request, adds a second agent that is auto-wired to the first by topic and carries a deliberate division-by-zero, watches that agent repair its own code without losing its count, then deploys a fresh Raspberry Pi node and live-migrates the agent onto it, in under four minutes of wall-clock time and \$0.13 of model usage. This extended version adds what the two-page demonstration paper could not: the Wiring view of the topic graph, Wactorz as a library for hand-written agents, how trained models are stored, sent to nodes and replaced, the security model, and the system's limitations.

papers.title: Mass Forcing: On-Policy Mass-Aware Distillation for Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) has emerged as a promising paradigm for real-time video synthesis, distilling pretrained diffusion models into few-step autoregressive generators. However, its reverse-KL objective is mode-seeking and can collapse the student's conditional video distribution onto a narrow subset of modes, leading to reduced sample diversity, diminished temporal dynamics, and color oversaturation. Existing methods mitigate this issue mainly via coverage-oriented student initialization, but we observe that such coverage is transient: across three initializations, the fraction of dynamic videos drops sharply during subsequent DMD training, indicating that the mode-seeking objective, not the initialization, drives this degradation. We propose Mass Forcing, a probability-mass-aware framework that moves on-policy DMD supervision from whole videos to individual states. Each update branches several continuations from a shared student-generated prefix, making the student's probability mass at that state measurable against the teacher. First, Mass Forcing estimates relative teacher-to-student density ratios among these continuations through latent-space score integration and uses them to rebalance conditional DMD updates, amplifying rollouts underrepresented relative to the teacher. Second, since mismatched mode probabilities do not necessarily induce strong local score corrections, it aligns generated rollout sets with a reweighted reference distribution defined by the same mass estimates, providing cross-rollout supervision. Experiments on MovieGen and VBench show that Mass Forcing improves video fidelity and sustains temporal dynamics throughout training, achieving the highest Total scores among compared methods and a Dynamic Degree of 83% after 1,000 generator updates, versus 12-32% for the baselines, with no additional inference-time overhead.

papers.title: Viscous damping of axisymmetric oscillation modes of uniformly rotating relativistic stars
papers.abstract: We study the effects of bulk and shear viscosity on the damping of axisymmetric oscillations of uniformly rotating relativistic stars, using the first-order viscous hydrodynamics formulation of Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha and Kovtun (BDNK). The equations of motion are implemented in a two-dimensional numerical code under the Cowling approximation, assuming the fluid evolves on the fixed spacetime of a rotating star. We build two sequences of polytropic stellar models and investigate how damping depends on rotation rate (from the non-rotating case to the mass-shedding limit) and compactness. Our study focuses on the quasi-radial $l=0$ $F$ mode and the $l=1,2,3$ fundamental modes, covering a dataset of 288 perturbed stellar models. For all modes and chosen viscosities, the BDNK runs show that oscillations decay within a few milliseconds, much faster than in the perfect fluid case. The $F$ mode damping is dominated by bulk viscosity, consistent with its global compression of the star, while the $l=2$ and $l=3$ modes are mainly damped by shear viscosity. The $l=1$ mode is largely insensitive to both viscosity coefficients, and its decay rate is dominated by numerical dissipation. Rotation renders the $F$ mode sensitive to shear viscosity. Since the inherent numerical damping does not affect the slopes of the decay rates, our viscous sensitivity estimates faithfully identify the dominant damping mechanism for each mode, shear or bulk viscosity, and reveal robust trends with rotation rate and compactness.

papers.title: Tightness of the Partition Bound for Multiterminal Secret Key Capacity
papers.abstract: We consider secret key agreement among \(m\) terminals, each observing one component of a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless multiple source. The terminals communicate over a noiseless public channel, and a target set \(A\subseteq[m]\) seeks to generate a shared secret key, with the remaining terminals acting as helpers. The partition-based Csisz\'ar--Narayan upper bound on secret key capacity is known to be tight without helpers but can be strict in their presence. We give a complete characterization of its tightness: for \(2\leq |A|\leq m\), the bound is tight for every source if and only if \(|A|\in\{2,m-2,m-1,m\}\). To prove tightness, we use the supermodularity of conditional entropy and the structure of optimal supports in the linear program for communication for omniscience. We first establish the result under strict supermodularity and then remove this assumption by a perturbation argument. For all remaining pairs \((m,|A|)\), we extend Chan's six-terminal counterexample. We also study optimal partitions when there are two target terminals and the source is a Markov random field on a connected graph. We show that an optimal bipartition separating the targets can be chosen so that both blocks induce connected subgraphs. For cycles, this reduces the number of candidate bipartitions from exponential to at most quadratic in \(m\).

papers.title: Velocity-Window Dependence of the Broad H$\alpha$ Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: Broad Balmer emission lines probe black hole masses and nuclear kinematics in high-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGNs). In JWST "little red dots" (LRDs), integrated broad-H$\alpha$ widths span a remarkably narrow range at fixed line luminosity, raising the question of whether this tightness persists once outer-wing emission is included. Holding each object and its broad-H$\alpha$ luminosity fixed, we measure the finite-window line dispersion $\sigma(V)$, the flux-weighted second-moment width within $\pm V$, from $V = 1500$ to $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in JWST/NIRSpec spectra and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Type-1 AGNs. Across 20 high signal-to-noise LRDs, the observed scatter in $\log_{10}\sigma(V)$ at fixed $L_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ rises from 0.036 to 0.084 dex between $V = 2500$ and $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, a paired increase of 0.048 dex with a 95% bootstrap interval of 0.026-0.064 dex, compared with 0.020 dex across 167 broader SDSS AGNs. Injecting synthetic profiles into the empirical noise of the same 20 spectra shows that single-Gaussian and core-plus-wing models both accommodate this rise, leaving intrinsic wing diversity, truncation, and wing noise unseparated. In the clearest dual-line spectrum, RUBIES-EGS-55604, H$\beta$ strengthens relative to H$\alpha$ from line center to wing under two spectral decompositions of the same grating spectrum. Alongside integrated widths in JWST, SDSS, and 334 Euclid DR1 AGNs, these results show that the observed tightness of the H$\alpha$ scaling depends on the velocities included in $\sigma(V)$, requiring mass and kinematic models to match both transition and velocity interval.

papers.title: GravHMR: Coupling SLAM and Human Mesh Recovery in a Shared Gravity Frame
papers.abstract: Recovering globally consistent 3D human motion from monocular videos remains challenging under dynamic camera motion. Although SLAM and human mesh recovery (HMR) provide complementary camera and body estimates, directly combining them often leads to inconsistent orientations and accumulated trajectory drift. We present GravHMR, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples SLAM and HMR through a shared gravity-aligned reference. By allowing gravity to be estimated independently of the HMR backbone, GravHMR accommodates world-grounded HMR models with or without explicit gravity-view representations. Specifically, Yaw-Aware Orientation Optimization (YAOO) resolves heading inconsistencies by correcting body and velocity orientations about the shared gravity axis. Conditioned on these corrected orientations, Gravity-Aware Trajectory Optimization (GATO) anchors root trajectories in the metric SLAM world by jointly leveraging 2D reprojection, the metric scale implicit in the human body, and the body's own motion. On EMDB-2, GravHMR achieves state-of-the-art performance with 154.0 mm W-MPJPE100 using ViPE and 189.8 mm using masked DROID-SLAM, outperforming TRAM (222.4 mm) under the same masked DROID-SLAM camera estimates. It further reduces W-MPJPE100 by 44.3% over GVHMR (276.5 mm) and by 20.0% over GVHMR + HTD-Refine (192.4 mm) with the same HMR backbone.

papers.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Web-scale recommender models evolve primarily through retraining or fine-tuning. We propose \emph{weight coding}, a methodology for model evolution through direct, executable weight edits. A large language model (LLM) agent inspects model structure and parameters, formulates hypotheses, and implements edits using evaluation feedback. The loop progresses from localized changes to targeted searches and composition, allowing edited components to adapt to one another. A cached engine enables rapid forward evaluation without backpropagation. On Pinterest's 147M-parameter Image Search two-tower retriever, weight coding improves held-out recall@10 of production model by up to 15.0 percentage points (+24\% relative) with few edits in about 1/4 GPU hours of a full post-training finetune, while a common launch only improves around 1\%. After reinitializing the entire 13.6M-parameter interaction module randomly while retaining the surrounding trained model, searching 2,448 mixing and normalization parameters yields 9.8 points above production. Offline gains span the full funnel including dense retrieval, generative retrieval and ranking, with up to 1.37B learnable parameters and different edits for each architecture. Steering edits provide explicit control of model performance over segments like freshness and product. Weight coding requires no serving change and online A/B tests increase saves per user from the edited retrieval source by 8.4\% to 10.7\%, aligned with the target business objectives. Our results establish weight coding as a practical and useful tool for model development and and behavioral control in a real web-scale production system, with potential to extend to both pre-training and post-training stages across the funnel.

papers.title: Subsurface Model Programming: Frontier Large Language Models Natively Interpret and Edit Dynamic Reservoir Models
papers.abstract: Multiphase flow simulation in heterogeneous porous media supports decisions in hydrocarbon recovery, geological carbon sequestration, and geothermal extraction. We introduce Subsurface Model Programming, a workflow in which large language models (LLMs) read and edit reservoir simulation decks directly without numerical gradients or external optimization algorithms. We evaluate four benchmarks using geometric checks for connectivity and open-source simulators for dynamic tasks. In one text-only response, the LLM correctly classified all six reservoir-layer well-pair labels and all three flow-path labels between open completions. On PUNQ-S3, a single proposal modified 54 of 1,761 active cells (3.1%) and reduced well-balanced water-cut RMSE by 71.9%. On the SPE10 sector model, the best of five LLM proposals yielded 1.795 million standard cubic meters of cumulative oil over ten years, 8.9% more than the best plan from 25 particle swarm optimization evaluations. On the 533,403-cell UNISIM-IV-2026 compositional model, five rounds of script-based editing reduced combined field-and-well NRMSE from 37.98% to 11.62% (a 69.4% reduction) and field production error by 73.9%. Replacing exhaustive stochastic search with physically auditable causal interventions in just one to five runs provides a generalizable foundation for autonomous reservoir development, rapid history matching, legacy model diagnosis, and coupled multiphysics engineering.

papers.title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations
papers.abstract: We study the subshifts \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) associated with the intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-\beta x+\alpha\pmod1\), where \((\beta,\alpha)\in\Delta_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{\beta,\alpha}=\alpha/\beta\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((\beta,\alpha)\) for which \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(\Delta_-\). The approximating parameters can be chosen so that both kneading invariants converge to those of the original map.

papers.title: Dr. Grasp-RL: Diverse and Robust Dexterous Grasping via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Human interaction with physical objects relies on a combination of dexterity and robustness. In robotic manipulation, dexterity requires not only flexible end effectors but also a diverse repertoire of manipulation strategies, while robustness requires closed-loop adaptation to disturbances and unexpected situations. Two prominent research directions in dexterous grasping have largely addressed these capabilities separately. Generative approaches model multimodal distributions to produce diverse grasp poses, but their reliance on open-loop execution can limit robustness. Reinforcement learning approaches learn closed-loop grasping policies, but can converge to a narrow range of successful grasping strategies, limiting behavioral diversity. We introduce a time-reversed curriculum with a coordinated reset mechanism that enables a simple MLP policy trained with PPO to capture multiple modes of the grasp-pose distribution while maintaining closed-loop control. Experiments demonstrate both diverse grasping behaviors and robust closed-loop execution. Trained on only approximately 400 objects, our policy further demonstrates strong generalization when evaluated on more than 20,000 unseen objects.

papers.title: JEPA-Shield: Safe Diffusion Planning with Latent World Models via Conformal Shielding
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable planning from images, but their predictions do not directly establish whether a robot will satisfy physical constraints. We present JEPA-Shield, which connects a frozen action-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world model to task-space safety enforcement. Two downstream models predict relative motion from imagined latent rollouts and decode unsafe geometry from the current image. Split conformal prediction turns end-to-end motion-prediction errors into multi-horizon uncertainty tubes. A backup-based shield checks these tubes against physical constraints and screens both candidate trajectories and final proposals in diffusion-inspired sampling-based model predictive control. Under the stated exchangeability and initial-backup assumptions, we establish probabilistic constraint satisfaction at action-block boundaries for a returned plan executed without replanning. We also introduce VParkBench, with geometric car and tractor-trailer parking tasks and a editable photorealistic Gaussian-splatting environment. In closed-loop evaluation, JEPA-Shield achieves success rates of 84.4%, 82.3%, and 99.0%, respectively, with no observed constraint violations. Ablations show complementary benefits from shielding and uncertainty calibration. The results demonstrate the importance of grounding latent world-model predictions in task-space quantities and explicitly accounting for prediction uncertainty in safety-critical planning.

papers.title: Rotationa Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
papers.abstract: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

papers.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions.

papers.title: Dyadic Representation of Fractional Integrals on Spaces of Homogeneous Type and Related Boundedness Phenomena
papers.abstract: We establish a dyadic representation formula for fractional integral operators in the setting of spaces of homogeneous type. The formula expresses such operators in terms of simpler dyadic model operators, such as so-called paraproducts and shifts, and provides a unified framework that applies to different notions of fractional integrals arising in this general context. Motivated by the derivation of this representation, we also investigate the structure of fractional integral operators in spaces of homogeneous type. In this setting, two natural definitions, referred to as volumic and metric, are in general non-equivalent and exhibit markedly different boundedness properties. While the former enjoys well-known $L^p$--$L^q$ estimates, the latter may fail to satisfy any such bounds without additional assumptions; nevertheless, weaker forms of boundedness can still be recovered under suitable conditions. The representation formula is intended as a tool for the study of Schatten-type properties of commutators $[b,T]$ of fractional integrals and pointwise multipliers, which will be addressed in a forthcoming companion work by T. Hyt\"onen and the author. Beyond this application, the representation itself may be of independent interest and useful in other contexts.

papers.title: Just another Markovian embedding for open quantum systems
papers.abstract: In this work, I present one more method for analysis of non-Markovian open quantum systems by embedding them into larger Markovian systems. As many other approaches, this method starts from finding a rational approximation for the bath correlation function in the frequency domain, the difference is that I retain $\omega \to -\overline \omega$ symmetry for the poles of the approximation. This allows to reduce the dimension of embedding from one- to half-degree-of-freedom per pole. In case of odd number of poles, the resulting equation describing dynamics of the system turns out to be not a Lindblad, but a hybrid quantum-classical master equation.

papers.title: fx(hash): Salvaging The Source Code of 28k Generative Artworks
papers.abstract: fx(hash), the most radically inclusive generative art NFT platform, went bankrupt and shut down on August 17, 2026. The ownership of its 2,705,350 artworks is immutable on the Tezos and Ethereum blockchains, but the source code that generates them is off-chain and in peril. We salvaged all 28,193 generative programs contributed by 5,532 international artists and archived them in Software Heritage. Here we explain why NFT generative art is fragile and the steps we took to salvage these software cultural landmarks.

papers.title: Hashing Theorems Modulo Rewrites and Binder Permutation Enables Equivalence Search over 200k Mathlib Theorems
papers.abstract: Like all code, Lean libraries accumulate technical debt and structural deficiencies over the course of their development. A particular concern is duplicate theorems: different parts of a big library can unwittingly contain and prove the same theorem, duplicating maintenance efforts. Tools can help detect redundancy and clean up. For instance, Mathlib's duplicate-declarations linter compares theorem types syntactically after sorting top-level binders and erasing binder information and universe levels. If detecting an equivalence requires unfolding, reorientation, or logical transformations, it escapes this comparison. In this work, we present a method to detect theorems which are equivalent with regard to argument order and currying/uncurrying of dependent types. We implement our method for Lean. By applying it to Mathlib, a library of more than 200k theorems, we demonstrate that it is computationally cheap and scalable. We discuss how our work may enhance efforts to tackle the maintenance burden of Lean libraries.

papers.title: Mixing time and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the torus shuffle
papers.abstract: The torus shuffle acts on an $n\times n$ board of $n^2$ cards: each step chooses a row or a column uniformly at random and rotates it cyclically by one unit in a uniformly chosen direction. We prove that the half-lazy version of this chain has total variation mixing time of order $n^3\log n$ and logarithmic Sobolev constant of order $n^{-3}$ on each communicating class. The order of the mixing time is the one conjectured by Diaconis. The proof of the upper bound has two steps. First, the entropy of a function on the board is at most a constant times $n$ times its mean loss when a single row or column is completely rearranged. Second, this mean loss is at most a constant times $n^2$ times the Dirichlet form of the shuffle. The second step bisects each line recursively and charges the cost of a column rotation only to the intervals that contain the column, so that the costs over all scales add up without a logarithmic factor. A Fourier observable gives the matching lower bound on the mixing time.

papers.title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
papers.abstract: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.

papers.title: Aggregation Dispersion: An Information-Geometric Diagnostic of Oversmoothing in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Message-passing neural networks (MPNNs) learn node representations by iteratively aggregating information from neighbors, but stacking too many layers causes all representations to converge, an effect known as oversmoothing. We propose a geometric perspective on this phenomenon. At each depth $k$, the propagation operator assigns to every node $v$ a walk distribution $p_v^{(k)}$, a probability distribution over source nodes. These walk distributions form a point cloud on the probability simplex, whose contraction to a single point characterizes complete mixing of the propagation operator, and thus oversmoothing. To measure this contraction, we use the Fisher-Rao metric, the unique Riemannian metric on the simplex invariant up to scale under sufficient statistics, whose scaled chordal distance under the square-root embedding $p \mapsto \sqrt{p}$ is the Hellinger distance. The resulting diagnostic, the aggregation dispersion $D_k$, is the variance of the embedded point cloud on the unit sphere. We prove that: (i) $D_k = 0$ if and only if the $k$-th step propagation matrix has rank one, a necessary and sufficient condition for complete operator mixing; (ii) $D_k$ is non-increasing with depth; (iii) the spectral gap of the propagation matrix controls the rate of this decay; and (iv) for contractive MPNNs, the aggregation dispersion upper-bounds the representation dispersion up to graph- and initialization-dependent constants. Across 14 model configurations and 11 datasets, $D_k$ attains the highest mean absolute Pearson correlation with test accuracy across depths among eight diagnostics ($|r| = 0.721$, using log-transformed diagnostic values), numerically comparable to the post-training effective rank ($|r| = 0.688$), while requiring no training.

papers.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-K\"ahler varieties, III
papers.abstract: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-K\"ahler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives. The proof involves the geometry of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, whose Kuznetsov component allows to realize double EPW sextics and cubes as moduli spaces of Bridgeland-stable objects, relatively over the parameter space of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds. A key step is that the canonical Chow-K\"unneth decomposition of special Gushel-Mukai fourfolds is multiplicative; we use this to show that generically defined cycles on the third power of a special Gushel-Mukai fourfold inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. Along the way, we also show that the canonical Chow-K\"unneth decomposition of any Gushel-Mukai sixfold is multiplicative.

papers.title: AEP:Towards Trustworthy Agent Communication, Networking, and Collaboration
papers.abstract: As privately owned agents become increasingly capable, collaboration in open agent networks is limited by partial topology knowledge, ownership boundaries, and the risk of exposing or contaminating private context. Existing agent-to-agent protocols are useful when collaborators are already known, while shared-memory and broadcast-based systems rely on visibility and trust assumptions that do not hold in decentralized, low-trust environments. We introduce Open Private Agent Collaboration (OPAC), an asset-centric paradigm for cooperation among private agents with open membership, partial observability, and ownership-aware access control. Rather than treating collaboration as the exchange of final responses, OPAC enables agents to selectively discover, exchange, audit, and integrate policy-controlled context assets. This shifts the unit of cooperation from transient messages to reusable external context, while keeping disclosure and integration subject to privacy and security constraints. We instantiate OPAC with the Agent Exchange Protocol (AEP), a decentralized framework that combines semantic discovery, demand-driven coordination, safety-gated asset exchange, and ledger-backed evidence derivation. By distinguishing physical topology from each agent's local cognitive topology, AEP allows agents to discover task-conditioned collaborators under an unknown network structure, release only admissible assets, and update future cooperation decisions from auditable interaction evidence. AEP therefore provides a middle ground between pure request-response interaction and globally shared memory, offering a practical foundation for trustworthy agent-native networking through selective, auditable reuse of distributed context assets.

papers.title: Using fixed $w$ to reproduce evolving $w_0$-$w_a$ dark energy at the field level
papers.abstract: Recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hint at dynamical dark energy, making the accurate modelling of such cosmologies increasingly important for future analyses. In this work, we show that because, when written in superconformal time $\tau$, the $N$-body equations of motion depend on the background cosmology only through the expansion history $a(\tau)$, matching $a(\tau)$ allows us to map one cosmology onto another. As a first, observationally relevant, application of this new method, we match a Chevallier--Polarski--Linder (CPL) cosmology to a constant-$w$ cosmology with the closest $a(\tau)$. This allows us to use a single fixed-$w$ simulation to reproduce the simulation predictions of the target CPL cosmology at the field level at redshifts $0\le z\le3$. We validate this matching with 100 pairs of CPL and fixed-$w$ \textsc{mg-glam} simulations, spanning $0.1\le\Omega_{\rm m}\le0.5$, $-1.4\le w_0\le-0.5$ and $-1.8\le w_a\le-0.15$. For a DESI-like cosmology, the matter power spectra of the matched and target simulations agree to 0.24\% for $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and 0.8\% up to $k\lesssim3\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at $0\le z\le3$, and the density phases are reproduced with a stochasticity below 0.02\%. Displacements, velocities, momenta, redshift-space multipoles, bispectra and the halo and void abundances are similarly well predicted. For most models we consider, we achieve subpercent error in the power spectrum up to scales $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at all redshifts, with density stochasticity below 0.03\% over the same scales. The method allows constant-$w$ simulations and field-level emulators to be used for CPL cosmologies, and generalises to any cosmology with no additional scale dependence.

papers.title: Similarity-Constrained Reweighting for Complex Query Answering on Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for Complex Query Answering (CQA) on knowledge graphs estimate the likelihood of answers that are not reachable via direct traversal. Recent work has proposed extending such queries with soft entity constraints, which require the target variable to be similar or dissimilar to specified sets of entities. We study a more general formulation where similarity constraints are specified on an arbitrary variable in a query, and introduce SCORE: a computationally efficient and interpretable method for incorporating similarity constraints on an arbitrary variable of a query. SCORE is based on a lightweight and interpretable score adjustment function that only requires tuning two hyperparameters on a validation set. Our experiments show that SCORE effectively incorporates preferences while maintaining strong query answering performance. It significantly improves ranking quality when constraints apply to the target variable and performs effectively in the more general case involving constraints on intermediate variables, and its performance remains robust when applied to several existing methods for CQA. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/dfdazac/score.

papers.title: Liouville systems II: Critical points at infinity in the resonant case
papers.abstract: For a Liouville system at a resonant parameter, we construct a bounded, locally Lipschitz pseudogradient, which classifies the non-compact ends of its flow at finite energy levels. If the reduced functional is Morse and the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical pair, each unbounded forward trajectory with energy bounded below converges in the bubbling parameters to a pair with negative coefficient. Conversely, each such pair, up to a permutation, is realized by an open set of escaping trajectories.

papers.title: Motoric signatures to detect original authorship versus cognitive effort in instructed motor responses of an emerging speaker with ASD
papers.abstract: There is at present no objective, agnostic method to track levels of message authorship and agency in non-speakers who rely on assisted typing to communicate. Part of the problem is that nuances in spontaneous gestural movements of the typer transpire largely beneath awareness of both the typer and the communication-regulation-partner. Such spontaneous movements co-occur with the intentional ones producing the typed messages but are currently not considered part of the communication system. We introduce an assay that probes various levels of cognitive loads in an ecologically valid environment. Then, in collaboration with an emerging speaker-typer and his communication-regulation-partner, we empirically estimate motoric stochastic signatures during both independent and assisted typing. Under varying levels of cognitive loads, the assay and biometrics distinguish motoric patterns in spontaneous typing of phrases in response to open-ended questions from those in instructed typing of the same phrase. The non-dominant bodily motions, co-occurring with the dominant (typing) side reveal not only levels of cognitive mental effort and agency of the typer but also levels of creative thoughts through motoric preambles present only in open-ended mode. This level of semantic authorship is detectable in both the geodesic paths along the manifold representing the Gamma stochastic parameters of the motions fluctuations and those of the physical 3D spatial trajectories. The head and facial micro-motions capture these non-dominant-body nuances, offering a personalized motoric metric of cognitive effort, agency, authorship and a comprehensive suite of assays to open new research avenues for assisted typing with haptic support.

papers.title: A sharp conjugate radius bound for open four-manifolds with positive bi-Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that every complete noncompact Riemannian four-manifold without boundary with bi-Ricci curvature at least $b>0$ has conjugate radius at most $\pi\sqrt{2/b}$. Equality holds on the round cylinder $\bS^3(\sqrt{2/b})\times\bR$. For $b=2$, the bound and the equality model agree with Gromov's prediction for open four-manifolds under a scalar curvature lower bound of $6$.

papers.title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity
papers.abstract: As medical VLMs are increasingly evaluated for clinical decision-support scenarios, knowing when to trust their predictions is critical. Closed-ended medical VQA has become a common benchmark format because it enables automated scoring. Yet, systematic investigation into whether this format changes the reliability problem remains scarce. We identify a failure mode that we call stable wrongness: models can produce incorrect yes/no answers that remain confident and repeatable even when patient-specific visual evidence is removed or mismatched. This failure violates the premise behind sampling-stability uncertainty methods, including recent hallucination-aware calibration (HAC) variants: disagreement is informative only when errors are unstable. When shortcut-driven errors are themselves stable, sampling agreement can remain deceptively high. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity (CAS), which shifts reliability estimation from answer stability to evidence sensitivity. CAS uses cross-modal counterfactual interventions, such as text-only, black, and corrupted images, to audit whether a committed yes/no answer remains supported when visual evidence is invalidated. Across 7 VLMs and 3 benchmarks, CAS outperforms the best HAC-family scores across all evaluated settings, achieving a macro-averaged AUROC gain of +0.150 for error detection. Mechanistic analysis further shows that CAS recovers hidden errors in the HAC-confident region and that its strongest standalone signal is counterfactual decision-boundary shift rather than hard prediction stability. Our findings suggest that closed-ended evaluation should test visual dependence, not only answer stability, in safety-critical medical contexts.

papers.title: Products of supersoluble groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=AB$ be a finite group, where $A$ and $B$ are supersoluble. We prove that every nonabelian composition factor of $G$ is isomorphic to $\PSL_2(p)$ for some prime $p\ge5$ and that the nonsoluble length of $G$ is at most one.

papers.title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware
papers.abstract: Efficient AI computation depends on hardware that evolves over time, shifting the strategies needed to implement performant code. For CPU kernels, a key evolving factor is the set of available architectural extensions, which expose specialized hardware instructions that change the techniques used to optimize kernels. We study how effectively coding agents use these new, potentially unfamiliar extensions to write fast code. We introduce KernelShift, a benchmarking pipeline and a set of environments for evaluating coding agents in kernel optimization across evolving CPU architectures. Its agent-assisted, human-verified pipeline turns code repositories into benchmark instances, and its environments let agents optimize code with feedback from the target hardware. Using this pipeline, we construct 99 kernels from real-world, actively developed repositories (ncnn, llama.cpp, Arm SIMD Loops, and KleidiAI), including inference workloads derived from real model executions. KernelShift supports incorporating new kernels and hardware configurations as libraries and processors evolve. We evaluate agents with proprietary and open-weight models across progressively newer architectural extensions (Arm Neon, SVE, SVE2, and SME2), examining how performance changes as hardware evolves. On established extensions, agents beat the auto-vectorized compiler everywhere (2.4-19.8x) and exceed general-purpose libraries such as ncnn (getting up to 2.74x over its Neon kernels), but fall behind Arm's hand-tuned KleidiAI kernels (0.70x). In end-to-end inference of two LLMs, agent-written kernels achieve a 1.3-1.6x prefill speedup over llama.cpp's fast path. However, current agents do not yet reliably adapt to new extensions that require unfamiliar programming models, such as SME2's matrix tiles.

papers.title: Scalar Tuned Lens Summaries Offer Limited Incremental Value for Mid-Generation Abstention
papers.abstract: Mid-generation abstention aims to stop an unpromising response before spending its remaining computation budget. Intermediate transformer states may help predict eventual correctness, but whether scalar summaries of their vocabulary predictions add useful evidence is less clear. We compare Tuned Lens entropy and divergence features with final-state and raw intermediate-state probes under matched, causal evaluation. Across eight instruction-tuned models on MATH-500, raw intermediate states improve ranking, whereas scalar-only probes usually trail the final-state baseline. Scalar hybrids have positive exceptions, but their advantage over position-matched permutation controls is small. Cross-fitted residual comparisons further show that gains over a final-state probe need not require aligned scalar features. Actual stopping runs on two model sizes and two benchmarks reveal a separate accuracy--computation trade-off, with token savings overstating wall-time savings for scalar policies. The evidence supports a restricted empirical conclusion about these scalar features, not a general negative claim about intermediate representations.

papers.title: How Multi-Timescale Memory Cools Optimization: Theory and Evidence from AdEMAMix
papers.abstract: Augmenting AdamW with multiple momentum timescales improves large language model pretraining, yet the mechanism driving these gains remains poorly understood. We identify an interaction between multi-timescale optimizer memory and the geometry of normalized networks: memory changes parameter norms and thereby controls how fast parameters rotate. Starting from exact norm dynamics under decoupled weight decay, we show that the parameter norm depends on the temporal correlation of the updates, with weight decay controlling how long these correlations influence optimization. We show how an independently weighted slow momentum can substantially increase the norm of parameters, while contributing negligible power to the instantaneous update, therefore acting as an endogenous annealing schedule. We study this mechanism in AdEMAMix for language-model pretraining. Controlled interventions show that this scheduling mechanism has clear practical consequences and is an important factor behind AdEMAMix's advantage over AdamW.

papers.title: On simultaneous left- and right-homometric sets on the positive affine line group
papers.abstract: On a non-abelian group $G$, the homometry problem comes in two flavors, depending on whether differences are computed on the left or on the right. A natural question is to determine whether simultaneously left- and right-homometric subsets of $G$ exist. This question has been answered positively in the case of dihedral groups by Genuys and Popoff. We here prove that no such subsets exist on the positive affine line group, if we impose that the subgroups generated by their left- and right-differences be non-abelian.

papers.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
papers.abstract: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincar\'e-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. In exact linear normal coordinates, a polynomial restricted to an orbit gives a sum of exponentials, to which van der Poorten's bound of $2s-3$ zeros applies for a nonzero sum with $s\ge2$ distinct exponents. For integer orbits of polynomial maps, I combine exact modular orbits, Strassmann bounds and archimedean estimates in an adelic sieve. At every prime, increasing the modular depth eventually excludes a time class exactly when the interpolation along its center-manifold shadow has no zero in $\mathbb {Z}_p$.

papers.title: Temporal Evolution of Inner Circumstellar Geometry in Herbig Ae/Be Stars Revealed by Multi-epoch $H\alpha$ Spectropolarimetry
papers.abstract: We present multi-epoch $H\alpha$ spectropolarimetric observations of three Herbig Ae/Be stars, HD 58647, MWC 120, and MWC 147, obtained at epochs separated by $\sim$1-1.3 yr. By combining $H\alpha$ line profiles with velocity-resolved linear polarization and $Q$-$U$ diagrams, we investigate temporal changes in their inner circumstellar environments. The $H\alpha$ profiles retain broadly similar morphologies and overall velocity extents between epochs, although noticeable variations in line strength and peak intensity are observed. In contrast, the polarization spectra and $Q$-$U$ trajectories exhibit pronounced changes in morphology, orientation, and velocity-dependent behavior.
