PADS then periodically estimates category-level observation effects from recent policy rollouts and dynamically reallocates the training distribution toward questions where visual observations provide informative learning signals, while optimizing solely for final-answer correctness. Experiments across diverse visual perception and multimodal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over competitive tool-use MLLMs, with causal analysis further validating the data-centric perspective for learning effective visual tool use.

papers.title: A hybrid high-order discretization of a volume integral formulation for eddy currents on unstructured polyhedral meshes
papers.abstract: Volume integral formulations are attractive for eddy-current simulation because they require a mesh only of the conducting region. However, their dense interaction matrices make it important to control the number of unknowns needed for a prescribed accuracy. We propose an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation on general unstructured polyhedral meshes. The method combines high-order polynomial approximation with local mesh refinement around defects and material interfaces. For bounded positive spatially varying resistivity and magnetic permeability uniform throughout space, we establish well-posedness and a priori error estimates using a constructive right inverse of the discrete divergence. Numerical experiments demonstrate convergence for smooth solutions and compare mesh refinement with increasing the polynomial degree. Selected comparisons show that higher degree on coarser meshes can reduce the number of current unknowns coupled by the Green operator and the associated storage for a prescribed accuracy. Finally, a three-dimensional eddy-current testing benchmark assesses the predicted impedance against experimental measurements, using local refinement around a narrow slot and reusing the system matrix and its factorization throughout the probe scan.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery of sparse governing equations with parameterized operators
papers.abstract: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations. We also examine the influence of the hyperparameters, discretization scheme, and noise, and compare pSTLSQ with two benchmark methods. All three methods identify the correct terms at low noise levels, but differ in parameter accuracy, cost, and sensitivity to initialization and the candidate library.

papers.title: The abc index: Exact Retrieval for Learned Sparse Representations
papers.abstract: In learned sparse retrieval (LSR), queries have tens of terms with learned weights, on which classic dynamic pruning is believed to fail, and approximate indexes such as Seismic and HNSW are considered faster than exact ones. We challenge this view with abc, an exact index built only from standard IR techniques: term-at-a-time (TAAT) evaluation, Block-Max MaxScore, binary packing and doc-id reordering. They are combined in a new design and engineered for modern CPUs. On MS MARCO encoded with four LSR models, the abc index is the fastest exact index at every k: 6.5-84x faster than the exact search of Qdrant, 13-55x faster than that of Lucene, and 2.9-18x faster than BMP with an index 5-7x smaller. Against approximate indexes, it takes 1.5-3.6x less space, and its latency grows much more slowly with k: they are up to 4.3x faster at k=10, but at k=1000 it overtakes them, by up to 7.4x. Exactness comes with an extra benefit: there are no parameters to tune.

papers.title: VAPY: Circuit Optimization with Backpropagation
papers.abstract: Parameter sensitivities of analog circuits enable the use of gradient-based design optimization methods and unlock a range of sensitivity analyses. However, it remains a challenge to compute exact design parameter sensitivities for circuits that use PDKs, which use Verilog-A device models comprised of thousands of lines of code. Finite difference methods, which estimate gradients through simulation, require N + 1 to 2N simulations for each gradient depending on the method, which can become prohibitively expensive when many parameters are optimized. We present VAPY, a Verilog-A to JAX transpiler that compiles Verilog-A device models into autodifferentiable JAX code, enabling optimization with Circulax, a JAX-based circuit simulator. VAPY employs taint analysis to ensure only the necessary control-flow is rewritten with JAX-compatible calls, reducing control-flow overheads. We use VAPY and Circulax to optimize three analog circuits implemented in the SkyWater SKY130 PDK, which is built on the BSIM4 device model. VAPY-generated model gradients closely match finite-difference gradients, achieving comparable design quality in over 40X fewer circuit solves and up to 40% lower loss than Bayesian optimization.

papers.title: WorldWeave: Rethinking Embodied Navigation through Cross-Task World Modeling
papers.abstract: Mobile embodied agents continuously alter their observations through their own motion, while external dynamics further shape future interactions. Different mobile embodied tasks therefore capture complementary patterns of state evolution, yet jointly learning world dynamics across such interactions remains less explored. We investigate this problem through Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) and Embodied Visual Tracking (EVT), which respectively involve navigation toward a stationary goal and interaction with a moving target. We propose WorldWeave, a cross-task world model that couples shared predictive dynamics with task-specific adaptation. Instead of conditioning state transitions on heterogeneous physical actions, WorldWeave learns latent actions from observed state changes via inverse-forward dynamics, establishing a shared transition representation across tasks. The resulting future-state predictions are adaptively integrated into task-specific representations for downstream decision making. Experiments across multiple VLN and EVT benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over specialized baselines.

papers.title: Praxis: Practical Witness Encryption for NP
papers.abstract: Witness encryption encrypts a message to an NP statement so that whoever holds a witness can decrypt. Over a decade after its introduction, known constructions for general NP statements are far from practical or rest on heuristic or broken assumptions. We propose Praxis, a practical scheme for NP, and prove it extractable in the bilinear generic group and random oracle models under Module-SIS. Our instantiation encrypts to a Groth16 verifier on BN254, set up honestly, which serves every NP relation at the same cost: at $100$-bit security, its ciphertext is $7.88$ GiB, encryption takes $2^{34.2}$ base-field multiplications, and decryption with a Groth16 proof $2^{33.0}$ on average. We give Lean 4 proofs of correctness and extraction at this instantiation's parameters. Praxis starts from the rank-gap template of the recent feasibility result [Hair and Sahai, arXiv 2026]. Where they raise the gap to keep decryption polynomial, we fix it, so decryption ends with a search that is exponential but concretely fast: $O(2^{\lambda/4} N^{1/4})$ expected operations for a statement in $N$ Boolean unknowns at $\lambda$-bit security. A quadratic arithmetic program makes our hidden matrix low rank, so where their ciphertext encodes a basis of a matrix space, ours holds factors of width two, which a pairing multiplies. Weights and identities from an extension field tie copies of this matrix, so an adversary telling encryptions apart yields a witness or a Module-SIS solution. For the same Groth16 statement and $100$-bit security level, Praxis reduces the ciphertext size and the cost of encryption of either of their constructions by over ten orders of magnitude, and that of decryption by over six.

papers.title: PhysPPF: Learning Robotic Manipulation with Past, Present, and Future Physical Representations
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced robotic manipulation, yet complex tasks requiring both precise 3D contact and long-horizon coordination remain challenging. Most existing studies enhance spatial perception or temporal reasoning in VLAs separately. Spatial methods primarily inject geometric or affordance priors into current-frame perception without tracking multi-step transitions, while history-aware and world-model VLAs typically capture past context or future dynamics in 2D feature or pixel spaces, either lacking explicit 3D contact cues or incurring high generation overhead. To address this, we propose PhysPPF, a VLA framework that performs unified spatiotemporal modeling in a compact physical token space. Spatially, WWH (What-Where-How) distills pretrained perception teachers exclusively during training into compact token groups capturing what 3D structures occupy the scene, where to interact, and how the gripper should approach, without test-time 3D encoders. Temporally, operating directly in this WWH space without pixel reconstruction, PPF (Past-Present-Future) consolidates executed states into a bounded past physical memory and jointly infers present and future physical tokens via an asymmetric world model. Parallel gated branches then inject these past, present, and future representations into a flow-matching action expert to guide manipulation without cross-temporal interference. Extensive experiments on SimplerEnv, CALVIN, and LIBERO show that PhysPPF consistently outperforms existing spatial, history-aware, and world-model VLAs with modest latency and parameter overhead, improving over the StarVLA baseline by +17.2 points on SimplerEnv, +29.3 points on CALVIN, and +3.5 points on LIBERO.

papers.title: CCAMoE: Cache-Conditioned Adaptive Inference for Offloaded MoE
papers.abstract: Expert offloading enables Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained GPUs, but expert transfers and CPU execution limit decoding performance. Speculative decoding can mitigate these costs, yet separate draft weights consume scarce GPU memory and longer drafts increase verification demand. In this paper, we present CCAMoE, a unified runtime that coordinates adaptive speculative decoding with concurrent expert-cache updates. Its design has three key features: 1) Cache-only drafting, which reuses resident target experts to generate proposals and routing hints without separate draft weights; 2) Draft-guided cache updates, which anticipate expert demand and overlap transfers with computation to support subsequent drafting and verification; and 3) Cost-aware draft-length control, which balances expected acceptance against execution cost. Together, these mechanisms coordinate proposal generation and cache preparation through a shared evolving cache, improving proposal quality while reducing verification cost. Across various MoE models, GPU platforms, and workloads, CCAMoE consistently achieves the lowest decoding latency, with up to 2.33$\times$ speedup over state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Analyzing Atypical Local Features in Museum Artifacts using Generative Image Inpainting
papers.abstract: This study proposes a method for analyzing local visual features in museum artifacts that may appear atypical or unexpected. Objects in the same category often share a similar overall shape, while local details such as patterns, decorations, and facial expressions may reflect regional or cultural characteristics. We use the appearance distribution learned by an image generation model as a reference for what is generally expected within an artifact category. For each target region, we exclude images from that region and fine-tune a generative model using only images from the remaining regions. We then mask selected parts of artifact images from the target region and ask the region-excluded model to complete them. If the completed result differs greatly from the original image, the masked part may contain features that are difficult to predict from the appearance learned from other regions. We measure this difference using LPIPS and treat it as reconstruction difficulty for the generative model. We conduct experiments on images of kokeshi dolls, drums, and masks from the collection of the National Museum of Ethnology. For each category, we select several target regions, build region-excluded LoRA models, and perform inpainting on predefined local parts. The results show that typical shapes and simple decorations are often reconstructed consistently, whereas some region-specific colors, patterns, cord arrangements, and painted details are replaced with more common appearances. These results suggest that region-excluded inpainting can serve as an exploratory tool for finding region-specific local visual features in museum artifact images.

papers.title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning
papers.abstract: Action Quality Assessment (AQA) aims to evaluate the quality of human actions, yet existing methods are predominantly developed and evaluated on individual datasets with different task formulations and assessment criteria. We introduce X-AQA, the first unified training and evaluation framework for general-purpose AQA with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We construct X-AQA-40K, a training corpus comprising 40,163 samples from 22 data sources across four domains: competitive sports, fitness exercises, rehabilitation, and general skills. We convert heterogeneous annotations into a unified question-answering format, incorporating dataset-specific annotation guidelines and official scoring rules when available. Using this corpus, we fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B to develop a single MLLM capable of handling diverse AQA tasks. We further establish X-AQA-Bench, which evaluates both in-distribution (ID) performance on datasets represented during training and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization on four held-out datasets. The resulting model outperforms all evaluated open-source MLLMs on X-AQA-Bench and achieves competitive performance relative to proprietary MLLMs. Ablation studies further demonstrate that multi-domain joint training and explicitly providing assessment criteria in prompts both improve OOD generalization. X-AQA establishes a unified foundation for advancing general-purpose AQA across diverse real-world domains. Data and models are released at \hyperlink{https://huggingface.co/collections/Kelly0510/x-aqa}{here}.

papers.title: SBTenv: A Literature-Validated Split-Belt Treadmill Simulation Environment
papers.abstract: The split-belt treadmill is an important tool for studying human locomotor adaptation. Physics-based simulations complement such experiments by allowing hypotheses about the mechanisms of adaptation to be tested directly, and high-throughput simulation is increasingly needed as these models grow in complexity. However, no open-source split-belt treadmill environment exists in MuJoCo, a physics engine widely used for high-throughput simulation. Here, we present SBTenv, a split-belt treadmill environment built in MuJoCo and validated against published experimental data from a rimless wheel walking passively on a split-belt treadmill. By modeling compliant contacts at the spoke tips, SBTenv reproduces the experimental average steady velocity ($R^2=0.643$, RMSE $=0.0162$ m/s) without the empirical geometric correction required in prior simulations. We expect SBTenv, openly shared, to enable high-throughput simulation of musculoskeletal and robotic locomotion on a split-belt treadmill.

papers.title: Statistical Signatures of Velocity-Space Turbulence in the Earth's Magnetosheath
papers.abstract: In collisionless plasmas, the particle distributions are often far from local thermodynamic equilibrium, providing a significant source of free energy that leads to complex velocity-space dynamics. In turbulent plasmas, the possibility of a cascade of the free energy in velocity space, analogous to the spatial cascade of fluid and electromagnetic field energies, has been suggested. However, observational evidence of plasma turbulence throughout phase space remains limited. Using measurements from the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission in a special campaign in the Earth's magnetosheath, we present the first statistical study of signatures consistent with velocity-space turbulence across a wide range of plasma conditions. We observe two main populations in the ion velocity-space spectrum -- an isotropic $-3/2$ spectrum and an anisotropic $-2$ spectrum organized by the ion $\beta$ and bulk flow. In addition, the spectral power laws in the spatial and velocity domains are uncorrelated, while the velocity-space spectral index is correlated with estimated real-space energy transfer rates. These results reveal how the ion spectral properties are systematically organized by plasma conditions and related to real-space turbulence. This connection has broad implications for turbulence and the energy partition between thermal and non-thermal particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.

papers.title: Reconstruction-Guided Dual-Branch Learning for LiDAR Anomalous Object Detection
papers.abstract: Detecting unexpected objects is essential for autonomous driving safety. Most existing LiDAR anomaly detectors rely on semantic discrimination, which primarily captures category-discriminative features but may overlook deviations from broader feature relationships in normal scenes. Reconstruction offers a complementary perspective by assessing consistency with learned normal patterns. However, pointwise reconstruction errors alone struggle to distinguish anomalies from normal variability in complex outdoor point clouds. We propose Structured Residual Reasoning (SRR) to extract additional anomaly evidence from residual structure across feature channels, time sequences, and geometric space. We further establish that semantic discrimination and normal-pattern reconstruction capture fundamentally different yet complementary anomaly evidence: category compatibility and consistency with learned normal patterns, respectively. At matched background false-positive rates, SRR recovers more objects missed entirely by the semantic branch while producing fewer false positives in normal-only scenes. Building on this finding, we propose Reconstruction-Guided Dual-Branch (RGDB) learning, in which SRR-derived normal-pattern consistency cues guide a semantic-conditioned anomaly decoder to complement reconstruction-based predictions during training. At inference, the two branches jointly exploit their complementary anomaly evidence. Experiments show that standalone SRR establishes a strong reconstruction-based baseline without semantic labels from the target-scene training data, while RGDB achieves state-of-the-art performance on the STU validation set.

papers.title: Centerline-Guided Multi-Class Road Surface Segmentation
papers.abstract: Road-surface extraction from satellite imagery supports geo- graphic mapping, but a binary mask leaves road axes, transverse extent, and junction structure implicit. Learning these proper- ties together is challenging because narrow corridors, merging roads, and occlusions require different geometric cues. We present a centerline-guided multi-class segmentation framework that makes these dependencies explicit. A hierarchical encoder sup- plies shared features, while predicted centerline features and soft probabilities condition specialized regular, intersection, and over- pass decoders. A two-component width branch supplies transverse geometry to regular-surface decoding, and learned feature fusion produces the complete road mask. Unlike independent prediction heads or a fixed union of component masks, this design exchanges geometric information during decoding while retaining separately inspectable outputs. Evaluation of the four-semantic-output con- figuration on CHN6-CUG achieves 65.53% complete-surface IoU, improving on a binary SegFormer-B4 baseline by 1.01 percentage points and reducing false-positive pixels by 11.94%. The results support geometry-aware surface refinement and a richer raster representation for road-map inspection.

papers.title: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics
papers.abstract: Open-weight language models are vulnerable to trigger-conditioned behaviors introduced through sparse post-training weight modifications, creating supply-chain risks beyond conventional provenance checks. We present Neural Sentinel, a cross-architecture study of gradient-guided backdoor insertion and model forensics spanning 18 checkpoints across 14 architecture families (124M-31.3B parameters), including state-space and recurrent models. On Phi-2, modifying approximately 0.0002% of parameters induced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps (332 seconds), with mean next-token KL divergence of $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ and 100% top-1 agreement over evaluated positions of eight fixed reference prompts. Separate experiments produced structured tool-call-formatted outputs without establishing downstream execution. We identify three procedure-dependent response regimes -- Gradient-Permeable, Scale-Threshold, and Gradient-Fragmented -- and evaluate PPO-based weight-space exploration, which showed no statistically significant advantage over random search. For defense, Neural Sentinel combines weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and contextual output inspection. In a 22-artifact development cohort, its reference-optional scanner classified 4/5 backdoored artifacts as BACKDOORED; the remaining positive and all 17 clean artifacts were SUSPICIOUS. These findings establish the feasibility of sparse conditional-output insertion and evidence-producing forensic triage, while identifying limitations in behavioral-drift assessment and clean-model admission.

papers.title: BIRD-Persona: A Persona-Aware Benchmark for SQL and pandas Analytics Code Generation
papers.abstract: Production text-to-code systems use large language models to turn natural-language analytics requests into executable SQL and pandas code. Existing benchmarks cover both tasks but do not isolate when performance diverges between them. We introduce BIRD-Persona, a persona-stratified extension of BIRD-Python that adds novice and expert rewrites to tasks with matched SQL and pandas ground truth, along with schema variants and task-structure annotations. Across 1,534 tasks, nine models, and 245,592 evaluations, SQL outperforms pandas for eight of nine systems. The gap varies by condition: expert, schema-explicit prompts improve both paradigms but help SQL more; schema representations have mixed, model-dependent effects; and selected-column burden widens the gap while subqueries do not. By making user phrasing a controlled benchmark dimension, BIRD-Persona supports persona-aware and paradigm-aware evaluation of natural-language analytics systems. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/optum-cognition-lab/BIRD-Persona.

papers.title: A $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-Approximation for Weighted 3-Set Packing
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted $3$-set packing, for every fixed rational $\varepsilon>0$, improving on the 1.6908-approximation reported by Tong and Xu (2026). The algorithm has two phases. It first performs bounded local search using a rounded $12/7$-power potential. It then combines compatible exchanges that insert at most three sets and increase the original weight. The analysis relates the gap left by the first phase to the gain available to the second phase. We prove a structural inequality that bounds the weight of a comparison packing by $3/2$ times the current weight plus one sixth of a sum of small-exchange gains. Each gain accounts for all sets that the exchange must delete. A greedy rule recovers enough of these gains to obtain the approximation guarantee. We derive the structural bound from local optimality by analyzing finite computation trees and averaging the error caused by their limited depth. The running time is $n^{4^{O(1/\varepsilon)}}\operatorname{poly}(L)$, where $n$ is the number of input sets and $L$ is the input encoding length. The same guarantee holds for maximum-weight independent set in induced $K_{1,4}$-free graphs.

papers.title: Extended Deterministic Learning under Local Finite-Time Excitation
papers.abstract: This paper develops an extension of classical deterministic learning (CDL) for the regulation of uncertain nonlinear systems, referred to as Extended Deterministic Learning (EDL). CDL relies on periodic or recurrent closed-loop trajectories to ensure that the locally active radial-basis-function (RBF) neurons satisfy a partial persistence-of-excitation (PE) condition. During regulation, however, the state approaches a constant operating point and continued excitation disappears. EDL preserves the local-learning mechanism of CDL while enabling locally accurate learning under a local finite-time excitation (local FTE) condition, which requires neither persistent excitation nor recurrent system trajectories. Specifically, an adaptive RBF controller is combined with filtered finite-time data storage. Under local FTE, the resulting scheme guarantees that all closed-loop signals are uniformly ultimately bounded, the regulation state converges exponentially to a small neighborhood of the desired operating point, and the neural weights associated with the locally active RBFs converge exponentially to small neighborhoods of their ideal values. Consequently, the unknown nonlinear dynamics are learned locally and accurately over the experienced region without requiring persistent excitation after the finite learning interval. A numerical example illustrates the improvement in local learning achieved by EDL over CDL.

papers.title: Hierarchical Sub-Array Beam Training for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface-Enabled Hybrid Near-Far-Field Multiuser Communications
papers.abstract: Low-resolution discrete phase shifters (PSs) are attractive for extremely large-scale arrays, but phase quantization distorts near-field (NF) beam patterns and degrades beam training and multiuser transmission. Moreover, the distinct codebook structures required by NF and far-field (FF) users complicate hybrid NF-FF beam training and codeword switching. To address these challenges, we introduce flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM) surface shaping as an additional geometric beamforming degree of freedom. We establish the hybrid NF-FF channel and beam pattern models, characterize the grating lobes induced by discrete PSs, and develop a phase-quantization compensation method. A deformation-range analysis shows that wavelength-scale shaping can achieve beam patterns comparable to those obtained with continuous PSs. We further propose a hierarchical sub-array beam training (HSABT) scheme that progressively doubles the activated central aperture according to the beam-width and beam-depth characteristics. A beam-intersection-based sampling strategy improves the angle-distance resolution, while a measurement-driven adaptive NF-FF beam-switching mechanism selects the final codeword without relying on the Rayleigh distance or prior user-location information. HSABT is also extended to multi-path channels through adaptive peak detection and inter-level energy-consistency-based candidate tracking. For high-gain multiuser transmission, we develop an alternating-optimization-based design and a complementary non-iterative key observation method, and analyze their convergence, computational complexity, and steady-point properties.Simulation results demonstrate continuous-phase-comparable beam patterns, reduced training overhead, more accurate main-path acquisition than exhaustive polar-codebook training, and higher multiuser sum rates than conventional rigid-array benchmarks.

papers.title: LEAF: Calibrated and Robust Wavelet Estimation of the Hurst Exponent
papers.abstract: Wavelet logscale regression for the Hurst exponent H of fractional Brownian motion (fBm) is sensitive to outliers and biased in finite samples. We introduce the Log-Energy with Adaptive Floor (LEAF) ordinate, which averages the logarithms of squared wavelet coefficients after adding a floor proportional to a pilot estimate of the level variance. If standardized coefficients share a common law across levels, a floor proportional to the true level variance preserves the population slope, and a consistent pilot preserves it asymptotically. We derive the asymptotic variance and influence function, and identify the variance-minimizing floor for median-pilot LEAF, whose influence grows only logarithmically. With outliers of ten increment standard deviations in up to 1% of observations, median-pilot LEAF reduces root mean squared error by a factor of 1.8 to 2.6 relative to calibrated log-energy. At H = 0.5 with 1% outliers, the error falls from 0.139 to 0.059. For small to moderate H, the main source of bias is the departure of expected wavelet energies from the ideal power law at fine scales. We estimate H from an estimating equation calibrated by simulation under fBm. Calibrating the mean logscale diagram alone delivers nearly all of the gain: it nearly eliminates bias in matched simulations and improves on the Abry--Veitch estimator most at small H. Simulations also show how scale-dependent tails can erode the gains of a robust pilot and how misspecification can undermine calibration.

papers.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
papers.abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $\gamma = 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

papers.title: Ultrahigh Thermal Conductivity and Mirror-Parity Constraints in a Corrugated Two-Dimensional Oxide
papers.abstract: Contrary to the expectation of poor heat transport in oxides, first-principles calculations predict an ultrahigh lattice thermal conductivity of 756 $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ at 300 K in corrugated two-dimensional B$_2$O$_2$. Acoustic phonons dominate heat transport, with the flexural acoustic (ZA) branch contributing 40.62$\%$. Triplet resolved analysis including acoustic and optical partners finds that mirror forbidden three phonon scattering is negligible within numerical precision for sampled ZA modes. These results highlight horizontal mirror symmetry as a constraint on phonon scattering in corrugated oxides.

papers.title: Where the Image Sits: Vision-Text Order Bias in Jev
papers.abstract: Jev-style system-1 decision models read a choice from a single prefill. They restrict the next-token distribution to the supplied option labels and return a distribution over the options, with no generation and no parsing. Recent work shows that generative vision-language models are sensitive to the relative order of image and text tokens. We ask whether that sensitivity reaches this Jev-style readout. The answer is always read at the end of the prompt, so moving the image changes the distance from the visual evidence to the decision, but never the position at which the decision is read. Using four placements---prefix, pre-question, pre-options, and suffix---and holding the option listing fixed, we measure argmax flips, total variation, accuracy, calibration, and label marginals. Suffix placement flips 41.0% of decisions and lowers accuracy by 18.6 points. Averaged over the four slots, the curve is monotone, not U-shaped. That shape differs from prior results on generative vision-language models. The effect survives a battery of controls. We also introduce prefix--question averaging (P+Q), a two-forward readout that averages the prefix and pre-question distributions. It is at least as accurate as prefix and outperforms the prior baselines. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/Youzhi333/Visual_Tex_Order_Bias_Jev.

papers.title: Coupled Dynamical System for Sparsemax Attention
papers.abstract: We present a family of coupled dynamical systems that compute sparsemax attention. Each system fuses query-key similarity and normalization into a single physical relaxation. Specifically, we cast sparsemax attention as a constrained energy minimization problem and derive a pair of coupled differential equations: one drives the energy minimization and the other enforces the constraint. At equilibrium, the system state gives exactly the sparsemax attention probabilities. We realize this formulation with continuous Ising spins and with Kuramoto oscillators. These relaxations run natively on emerging non-von Neumann platforms such as Ising machines, which have demonstrated orders-of-magnitude higher energy efficiency than digital processors, yet have so far been used mostly for unconstrained quadratic combinatorial optimization. Because analog hardware has limited precision and is noisy, we simulate both systems under these non-idealities, and inference quality degrades gracefully. Our formulation extends these emerging computing substrates from combinatorial optimization to attention, opening a path toward a new class of physical accelerators for transformer inference.

papers.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
papers.abstract: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

papers.title: Walks2Maps: Learning Indoor Geometry from Crowdsourced Wi-Fi RTT and Motion Trajectories
papers.abstract: Everyday smartphone walks offer a scalable source of indoor geometry, but their motion traces drift and their radio measurements are distorted by multipath. We present Walks2Maps, a physics-guided framework that reconstructs a shared metric map from Wi-Fi round-trip-time (RTT) and motion observations, without a floor plan, surveyed access-point (AP) coordinates, or position labels. Walks2Maps jointly estimates pedestrian trajectories, AP locations, and per-trajectory stride scales, then recovers the pathway layout from the reconstructed paths. Shared AP observations connect walks recorded in different local frames, while metric ranges constrain their relative geometry and scale. An asymmetric range loss accommodates multipath-induced excess delay. On 22 phone trajectories collected along 11 routes on an office floor with 30 APs, Walks2Maps achieves median AP and trajectory errors of 0.87 m and 0.89 m, respectively, and a walked-area F1 score of 0.985. Ablations show that radio similarity can recognize places while still producing a distorted map; retaining the metric information in RTT resolves this ambiguity. Asymmetric modeling further reduces AP error by 54% relative to a symmetric loss. These results demonstrate how radio and motion measurements can jointly reveal indoor geometry without a dedicated mapping survey. We will release the dataset and toolkit.

papers.title: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity
papers.abstract: A seller jointly chooses allocation and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values, statewise participation, and payment restrictions, allocation determines both required rents and their delivery capacity. We separate these effects under a common subjective law. For three values and shared-top beliefs, explicit score and capacity conditions characterize globally optimal lower-value lotteries, including top-rent overflow and welfare differences among revenue optima. A two-buyer construction establishes a strict allocation advantage over every reserve under the same fixed reporting certificate and positive margin. A transport test and exact band-boundary incentive equalities identify separate conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings. For three bands and a common affine belief interval, an explicitly certified reserve attains the ceiling under stated score conditions. A case scaled to public collectible-auction records yields a nominal shared-top allocation gain of 24.72 cents per auction. A one-cent report-by-report margin yields matched gains of 1.48 cents under projection and 3.32 cents under shared-top beliefs; the three-band point-belief gain of 2.50 cents disappears with common-interval protection. These comparisons bound the additional recurring costs an allocation redesign can cover at the specified reporting requirement.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the fractional inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrodinger equation with time-dependent damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the global well-posedness and scattering of solutions for a nonlinear Schrodinger type equation with fractional Laplacian, inhomogeneous nonlinearity and time-dependent damping.We give an elementary proof based on Strichartz estimates combined with estimates of the nonlinear term in mixed-norm spaces. To avoid the loss of regularity in the Strichartz estimates, we consider the radial data.

papers.title: General-purpose language models are neurosymbolic reasoners able to annotate proteins from sequence
papers.abstract: Determining the function of genes across the tree of life is one of the major challenges in biology. Generative AI approaches to this problem generally fall into two categories: language models trained on biological sequences that are able to predict structure and function from signals in those sequences; and generalist language models trained on text, that are able to reason about biological function symbolically. A default operating assumption is that protein language models do not perform well on symbolic tasks, and that generalist language models do not perform well on sequence tasks. However, a recent report showed that frontier generalist models perform surprisingly well on next-residue prediction tasks. We set out to explore whether these capabilities extended to protein annotation. We assigned different frontier generalist models a variety of protein annotation tasks, including predicting the presence and coordinates of Pfam domains, loss of functional catalytic residues, and predicting structure and activity. On all annotation tasks, the frontier models performed well above chance; we did not benchmark them against specialised tools. The models also make characteristic hallucination errors, and they state them as confidently as their correct calls. Though untested against specialised methods, the nascent ability of frontier models to perform protein annotation from sequence alone is intriguing. The ability to reason over sequence, structure, and symbols in a single model allows for a neurosymbolic approach where a combination of sequence, experimental data and knowledge from the literature can be holistically combined to improve on de novo functional annotation of the protein universe. Prompts, test sets, model outputs and code: https://github.com/ai4curation/fable-sequence-to-function. Summary of results: https://ai4curation.io/fable-sequence-to-function/

papers.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
papers.abstract: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

papers.title: Numerical Study of Flow and Cavitation in Single-Liquid Injectors with Sharp-Edged and Chamfered Orifice Inlets
papers.abstract: In the current work, the investigators used Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) to investigate water flow and cavitation in single-liquid injectors with sharp-edged and chamfered orifice inlets. The k-{\omega} Shear Stress Transport (SST) turbulence model was used along with the Zwart-Gerber-Belamri (ZGB) cavitation model and the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method. The CFD predictions for the volumetric flow rate were validated against existing experimental data for the sharp-edged and chamfered orifice inlets. Pressure drops ranging between 0.07 MPa and 0.59 MPa were considered along with orifice length-to-diameter ratios of 2, 5, and 10. Strong cavitation was observed for the sharp-edged orifice inlet cases with a length-to-diameter ratio of 5 and a pressure drop larger than 0.2 MPa. A hydraulic flip was observed for the sharp-edged orifice inlet with a length-to-diameter ratio of 5 and a pressure drop of 0.59 MPa, which was consistent with the findings from the previous experimental study. Cavitation inception was observed for the chamfered orifice inlet cases with a length-to-diameter ratio of 5 and pressure drops larger than 0.2 MPa. For the sharp-edged orifice inlet with orifice length-to-diameter ratios of 2 and 10, a strong cavitation was observed inside the orifice.

papers.title: Energy- and Thermal-Aware Resource Management on Mobile IoT Endpoints: A Survey
papers.abstract: Energy-aware and thermal-aware management of computing resources on portable and mobile Internet-of-Things (IoT) endpoints is still practiced pillar by pillar: radios, processors, and flash are optimized in isolation, yet sealed system-on-chip (SoC) products share sleep states, interconnects, and thermal limits. Pillar-local joule or temperature gains therefore often disappear after integration, and published savings are frequently incomparable. This survey asks how radio, compute, and storage should be coordinated so that deep sleep remains reachable, and which reporting rules make endpoint energy and thermal claims comparable. We synthesize literature from roughly 2000 to early 2026 with three instruments: a five-phase wireless power anatomy for power-aware networking; a four-branch taxonomy for collective power--performance optimization under mixed regimes; and eight evaluation gates that separate energy outcome, control cost, thermal feasibility, and evidence quality. We qualify the radio-limited premise with compute-, storage-, and thermal-dominated counterexamples, compare modeling and monitoring families, treat thermal behaviour as a shared constraint by separating sensing interfaces, compact models, throttling actuators, and the short-peak versus sustained-throttling regimes that reverse room-temperature rankings, give an illustrative phase-budget example with a sensitivity check and a model-selection workflow, and close with open problems on composability and reproducible measurement. The intended readers work on sustainable computing, mobile systems, and embedded energy management.

papers.title: Information Access and Gain-Loss Framing in Six Large Language Models and Human Decision Makers
papers.abstract: A risky choice can be described by what will be saved or what will be lost, and people often choose differently depending on that wording. We test whether six large language models (LLMs) show this gain-loss framing effect, and whether it shrinks when they can first read more about the options. GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3 235B and Llama 4 Maverick made 11,519 choices across four risk scenarios, each in its original wording, two paraphrases and a mirrored version in the opposite wording. Before choosing, a model could open up to 0, 2, 3 or 4 of seven information cards. With no cards, all six models showed large framing effects: the share choosing the safe option was 27 to 79 percentage points lower under loss than under gain wording. The gap was smaller at 2 cards than with no cards in every model. Against a 10-point threshold set in our analysis plan, GPT-4.1 fell within it at 4 cards and Qwen3 only at 2 cards; in the plan's pooled comparison over all versions, GPT-4.1 was within it from 2 cards and GPT-4o from 3. GPT-4o-mini and Llama 4 Maverick kept gaps of 28 to 66 points with cards, and for GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3 the gap grew again from 2 to 4 cards. Part of the drop from 0 to 2 cards may reflect a change in prompt format, and most card content counted against the risky option, which may favor the safe choice. In an exploratory comparison with 198 students who saw the same scenarios and cards but opened cards one at a time and chose how many, decisions made after opening 0 or 1 cards showed a 19-point difference between the gain scenarios, asked first, and the loss scenarios, asked later, and no clear difference appeared in decisions made after opening more, though this design cannot show that cards reduced framing in people. With these cards, in the balanced comparison 17 of 18 card gaps were below the model's no-card gap, but few were within the threshold.
authors: Jeremy M. Gernand (The Pennsylvania State University)

papers.title: Modeling Joint Tail Risk and Dependence for Cryptocurrencies via a Copula-Based Semiparametric Framework
papers.abstract: This study proposes a Bayesian copula-based bivariate semiparametric framework for jointly forecasting Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) while modeling cross-asset tail dependence. The marginal dynamics are specified using four ES-CAViaR-type models, including extensions incorporating Rogers-Satchell and Garman-Klass volatility measures. To construct the copula inputs, we use the empirical ranks of standardized residuals, which depend on the marginal parameters, thereby linking marginal tail dynamics and dependence modeling without requiring fully specified marginal distributions. Clayton and BB1 copulas are considered, and adaptive Markov chain Monte Carlo methods are used for estimation and joint tail-risk forecasting. A simulation study under a DCC-GARCH-$t$ data-generating process evaluates the finite-sample forecasting performance of the proposed framework. Using Bitcoin and Ethereum data, we evaluate one-step-ahead forecasts from 2020 to 2025 through a rolling-window forecasting scheme and compare the proposed models with Bayesian DCC-GARCH-N and DCC-GARCH-$t$ benchmarks. Rolling copula estimates also reveal time-varying asymmetry in Bitcoin-Ethereum tail dependence, with lower-tail dependence remaining higher than upper-tail dependence for most of the period. The proposed framework delivers competitive forecasting performance for both marginal and joint tail risk.

papers.title: Radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
papers.abstract: We study the radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes found in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings. Two branches of lower and primary are found for phantom scalarized black holes. The coupled scalar--metric perturbations reduce to a Schr\"odinger-type equation, after eliminating redundant metric perturbations. The lower branch including the pure quartic solutions has one growing mode, while positive zero-energy solutions for the primary branch could establish stability through the $S$-deformation method. Stable primary solutions are found for the exponential coupling. Also, we explore the connection between radial stability and thermodynamic analysis for two branches. Furthermore, we show that canonical scalarized black holes obtained from Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial coupling reveals unstable lower and stable primary branches.

papers.title: DisSparse: Pipelined Top-$p$ Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by the memory demands of the key-value (KV) cache, whose size scales linearly with context length. Dynamic sparse attention reduces this bottleneck by fetching and attending only to a critical subset of tokens. The dominant primitive in dynamic sparse attention research and deployment is fixed-budget top-$k$ selection, which is favored because its deterministic block count aligns with the static memory allocation that systems like vLLM rely on. Top-$k$ uses a fixed budget regardless of how attention mass is distributed across heads, layers, and decode steps, leading to either wasted bandwidth on heads with peaky attention or dropped context on heads with diffuse attention. Top-$p$ (nucleus) selection adapts naturally to this variation but has seen limited adoption in production serving systems due to two system-level challenges: variable block counts that break deterministic block allocation and computationally expensive selection kernels that exceed the cost of attention itself. We present DisSparse, a serving system that integrates top-$p$ sparse attention into vLLM end-to-end. DisSparse decouples block selection from the scheduler's critical path, hides selection latency behind layer computation via a two-stream pipeline, and introduces a single-pass histogram-based top-$p$ kernel. We further observe intra-block sparsity, the inflation of selection budgets caused by mixing high- and low-importance tokens within fixed-size KV cache blocks, and address it with a token relocation kernel guided by accumulated prefill attention scores. Across long- and medium-context benchmarks on multiple models, DisSparse achieves 1.17x to 1.80x speedup in sparsity analysis (block selection) over state-of-the-art top-$p$ methods with negligible accuracy loss and supports up to 8x larger maximum batch sizes than dense vLLM under the same memory budget.

papers.title: Environment-Aware Probabilistic State Estimation of Continuum Robots from Planar Imaging
papers.abstract: Continuum robots are compliant along their entire length, making them well suited to navigating confined environments where contact with surrounding structures is often unavoidable. However, this compliance makes their modeling more complex compared to rigid robots, especially under contact, so their state must often be estimated from information available during operation. In many applications, the environment is known in advance, for example from preoperative imaging in medicine or from design models in industrial inspection. We present a probabilistic state estimator that represents the known environment as a signed distance field, informing the estimated shape. Continuous in arclength and time, it estimates the full state from asynchronous measurements anywhere along the robot. It also fuses planar images of body-fixed markers from a moving camera with commanded actuation, so the robot needs no embedded sensors. In a simulated aortic arch and a hardware phantom, the estimator tracked the robot into the target branch, and with a single view, using the known environment lowered the tip error from 2.5% to 1.6% and from 20.0% to 11.3% of the robot length, respectively. The continuous estimate of the full state and its uncertainty can support navigation and control of sensorless continuum robots.

papers.title: VG3R: Video Generation Model for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Video generation models are widely used as 3D priors for novel view synthesis and 3D scene generation. Fine-tuned for perception, generation models also excel at dense prediction such as depth estimation. However, methods that apply video generation models to 3D reconstruction either predict depth without cameras or generate geometry and estimate cameras through many iterative denoising steps, which makes them slower. In this paper, we present $\textbf{VG3R}$, which turns a pretrained video generation model into a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model. Our key observation is that such a model already captures the depth and camera motion of a video, but not in the form required for reconstruction. We introduce two components: $\textit{clip-level shift prediction}$, which corrects depth distortion caused by the unknown shift in decoded inverse depth, and a $\textit{multi-layer camera head}$, which predicts per-frame cameras parameters by combining features across transformer blocks. Using Wan2.1 as its video backbone, VG3R reconstructs a scene and estimate the camera of every frame without iterative denoising. It achieves the lowest ATE and reconstruction errors among methods built on video generation models, runs about 4 and 14 times faster than Aether and Geo4D. VG3R also demonstrates competitive depth estimation and 3D reconstruction performance compared with geometry foundation models. Project page: https://github.com/KTH-RPL/VG3R

papers.title: SupportChain: Trace-Calibrated Aggregation of Quote-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Multi-Hop RAG with Small Readers
papers.abstract: Strong results in multi-hop retrieval-augmented question answering come from graph indexes read by models of 70B parameters or more, and building such an index calls a large language model over the whole corpus. We present SupportChain, which splits a question into hops, binds each hop's answer to a sentence quoted from a retrieved passage, estimates how reliable each execution is from its own trace, and merges several executions by the support of their answers, the pooled reliability of the executions that agree, stopping once support is high enough. With a 9B reader under the HippoRAG~2 protocol, SupportChain reaches 63.0 F1 on MuSiQue, above the best earlier result of 59.2, which used a 20B reader. With the same reader and embedder, it is significantly better than HippoRAG~2 on all five datasets, by up to 17.2 F1, and it builds no index. Merging by support is significantly better than majority voting, and than letting the reader choose among the candidates, on three of the five datasets and level with both on the other two. The reliability model needs only 100 answered training questions.

papers.title: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
papers.abstract: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.

papers.title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change
papers.abstract: Digital twins of agent networks need to flag unreliable forecasts and help users choose interventions. Both decisions depend on what happens over several steps: an error can spread through the network, and an edit whose trajectory is easy to predict may still yield a poor collective outcome. We ask when information about error propagation improves failure detection and whether a learned twin can select effective network edits despite imperfect forecasts. We propose Propagation-Aware Validation for Networked Digital Twins (PAV-Twin). Its monitor combines Jacobian-based propagation features with recent errors and ensemble disagreement to estimate the risk that a forecast exceeds an error threshold. Its planner simulates each candidate edit and ranks the edits by their predicted collective outcomes. In simulations, the monitor gained 0.13 in area under the precision-recall curve on larger oscillator networks with familiar topologies and 0.09 on larger networks with held-out topologies, relative to a graph baseline without propagation features. Gains were small in contractive consensus. Giving the graph baseline the same features narrowed the gap. In a separate planning study, ensemble simulation recovered about 99% of the possible improvement over random intervention selection in oscillators and nearly all of it in consensus. With a simplified oscillator twin, selecting by predicted outcome also gave lower regret than selecting by trajectory fidelity. These results show when propagation features help flag unreliable forecasts and why the quality of intervention choices should be measured directly.

papers.title: Bound to be Complete: Efficient Verification for SQL Equivalence via U-Expressions
papers.abstract: Automated verification of SQL query equivalence is a fundamental problem in database area. Recent works developed verifiers with guaranteed completeness, which can generate counterexamples to disprove non-equivalent queries and are useful in various scenarios. However, they have to solve complex formulas and can fail to produce counterexamples within a reasonable time budget. This paper presents a new complete verifier called SQLution, which not only greatly reduces the verification time, but also supports more SQL features. The key insight is to represent SQL semantics using U-expression, a functional algebra that can model SQL with significantly simpler formulas than prior works, thereby leading to more efficient SMT solving. To turn this insight into a practical verifier, SQLution further tackles two technical challenges associated with modeling SQL using U-expression, namely, the lack of tuple ordering and the presence of unbounded summations. In particular, to support tuple ordering, SQLution proposes order semantics encoding which combines U-expressions with first-order logic. To handle unbounded summation, SQLution introduces unbounded summation expansion to transform them into bounded summations, which can be directly encoded into FOL formulas. Evaluation shows that compared with state-of-the-art verifiers, SQLution can support all 271 non-equivalent query pairs derived from the Spider dataset and reduces verification time by up to 98.6%.

papers.title: Logarithmic Tracing and Equilibrium Selection in Asymmetric Coordination Games
papers.abstract: We study equilibrium selection in asymmetric pure coordination games with finitely many players and actions. A logarithmic regularization defines a tracing-type path of interior equilibria from the uniform strategy profile. We reduce the equilibrium conditions to single-peaked scalar functions and show that, when one associated payoff index is uniquely minimal, the connected equilibrium branch from the uniform profile converges to the corresponding coordinated outcome. With two players, this condition is equivalent to maximizing the sum of square-root payoffs, extending the known two-action result to finitely many actions. A three-player example shows that the square-root rule does not generally extend to more players.

papers.title: Higher-Order Modulational Instability in Spin-Orbit-Coupled Bose-Einstein Condensates: Finite-Raman Effects and Branch-Resolved Spectral Redistribution
papers.abstract: We investigate higher-order modulational instability and the nonlinear spectral redistribution in a spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) binary Bose--Einstein condensate with equal interactions. For finite Raman coupling, the system is nonintegrable and exhibits both nonoscillatory and oscillatory instability regimes. Raman coupling reshapes the instability bands and changes what harmonics can grow. Direct simulations show that this reorganization modifies the subsequent nonlinear sideband dynamics. In the zero-Raman limit, SOC shifts successive harmonics between instability bands and stability gaps at a fixed carrier wavenumber. It thereby controls higher-order instability, distinct breather branches, and frequency-hopping sequences. We derive exact algebraic coefficients for the carrier and arbitrary-order sidebands. This yields an exact geometric power spectrum for the complete infinite sideband sequence and a unified description of carrier depletion, directional imbalance, and sideband decay, including an exact relation between the instability gain and the minimum spectral decay rate. For two coexisting breather branches with the same background and modulation wavenumber, the higher-gain branch can have a smaller maximum carrier depletion, a slower high-order spectral decay, and a weaker directional imbalance. SOC can also restore a symmetric sideband spectrum when the SOC-induced momentum shift compensates the carrier wavenumber, even when both $k$ and $k_L$ are nonzero. These analytical and numerical results clarify how SOC and Raman couplings organize higher-order instability and nonlinear spectral redistribution, providing a unified framework for studying coherent nonlinear-wave dynamics in multicomponent condensates.

papers.title: Exploring the phase diagram of dense and hot matter with HBT interferometry
papers.abstract: We investigate the HBT radii of pions produced in Au+Au collisions at selected energies from the STAR-BES program, using an event-by-event hybrid model that combines AMPT initial conditions, 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic evolution with a QCD equation of state at finite baryon chemical potential, and hadronic transport with SMASH. The goal is to explore the source's space-time structure and its possible connection to the structure of the QCD phase diagram. The hybrid chain was first validated by comparing identified-particle spectra and anisotropic flow, yielding a globally consistent description of the experimental data, with more evident discrepancies at the lowest energies.

papers.title: Lifted Multiple Shooting for Parallel-in-Time Contact-Rich Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Planning through contact requires accounting for the coupled dynamics of a robot and its environment, including inertial effects, contact forces, and friction. However, the non-smoothness and multimodality of contact dynamics and contact geometry makes gradient-based optimization challenging. In this work, we propose lifted multiple shooting, a trajectory optimization transcription that can be solved directly using nonlinear program solvers. By introducing contact impulses as optimization variables, our formulation allows the optimizer to satisfy the state-transition constraints using friction-cone-feasible impulses while separately enforcing their consistency with the contact model. Our formulation supports a broad class of contact constitutive relations, with sensitivities computed through implicit differentiation. To enable efficient planning over long horizons and for high-dimensional systems, we further introduce IP-PAS, a parallel-in-time primal-dual interior-point solver that achieves O(log T) parallel computational depth. We evaluate the proposed methods on six fully dynamic contact-rich planning tasks, including nonprehensile pushing and in-hand manipulation, without contact-guiding costs. Lifted multiple shooting improves success rates by up to 81.5 percentage points over standard multiple shooting, while IP-PAS achieves solution quality comparable to serial methods with up to a 3.1x speedup and scales to horizons of 40,000 timesteps.

papers.title: Reverse Seam-Carving: Structured Whitespace Preconditioning for Fixed-Die P&R
papers.abstract: At high placement utilization, limited whitespace increases cell displacement during legalization and clock tree synthesis (CTS), degrading routed wirelength. Existing P&R methodologies use uniform density targets or reactive whitespace redistribution, without optimizing whitespace structure before placement. We propose Reverse Seam-Carving (RSC), a pre-placement methodology that redistributes whitespace into core-spanning low-density seams between denser regions, while preserving die area and utilization. We further develop SeamGain, a semi-analytical model that selects the RSC configuration from a single reference run of the uniform flow; one SeamGain-selected run obtains 86% of the best-of-sweep wirelength reduction. In the OpenROAD flow with ASAP7, RSC achieves (maximum, average) post-route wirelength reductions of (27.6%, 15.4%).

papers.title: On Monotonic Hamming Sphere Landscapes
papers.abstract: Monotonic Hamming Sphere Landscapes (MHSL) are introduced: binary landscapes whose fitness is nonincreasing with Hamming distance from a unique global optimum, while points on the same Hamming sphere may be ordered arbitrarily. The class includes OneMax, every nondecreasing unitation function with a unique optimum, and positive linear functions with sufficiently balanced weights. The one-to-one MHSL, called Hamming sphere encodings (HSE), are counted in total and up to hypercube symmetry and shown to be a vanishing fraction of all landscapes. For the elitist (1+1) EA, every MHSL in which no two spheres share a fitness value has the optimization-time distribution of OneMax, which with known results makes these landscapes the easiest for mutation rates below one half. The same equivalence and optimality are proved for a two-member genetic algorithm with tournament selection and no crossover, whose hitting time on these landscapes reduces to a chain with quadratically many states. All 40,320 one-to-one three-bit landscapes are then evaluated for the (1+1) EA and the two-member genetic algorithm under eight mutation rates, three crossover operators and two selection schemes. Below one half, the easiest symmetry classes are all and only the HSE; above one half they are the hardest. Differences among HSE are small and stem from selection and from the hypercube symmetries respected by mutation and crossover. Targeted five-bit experiments likewise find their fastest landscapes within the HSE class.

papers.title: AlpaSafe: Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Reasoning-based driving vision-language-action (VLA) models propose multiple candidate trajectories at each decision, yet only one is executed. Standard evaluation scores the best candidate, assuming an oracle selector that deployment lacks, and leaves the risk of the executed candidate unexamined. Existing online evaluators typically close this gap with a purpose-trained scene or world model, often rolling out each candidate through it at inference time. We introduce AlpaSafe, a risk-aware trajectory selector that reuses the scene representation a frozen driving VLA computes while proposing its candidates. AlpaSafe reads the last hidden token of the VLA's prompt prefill. A lightweight head, trained on the closed-loop simulation outcomes of the candidates, fuses this token with each candidate trajectory and predicts a relative score and collision/offroad logits. A fixed rule removes candidates dominated on the two risk logits and selects the highest-scoring candidate among those remaining, adding neither rollouts nor VLA training. Experiments on 525 AlpaSim scenes show that AlpaSafe outperforms Alpamayo's default first-sample rule and uniform random selection in selected regret and top-1 agreement, and reduces the collision-at-fault or offroad rate from 6.41% and 6.10% to 4.93%. The selector has 1.7M parameters and takes 0.75 ms per decision.

papers.title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding naturalistic brain activity requires going beyond the stimulus alone, as external inputs continuously interact with an individual's evolving brain state. A world model captures such dynamics in a latent state by inferring it from neural observations, predicting stimulus-driven evolution, and updating with new observations. However, existing brain world models fail to maintain a persistent latent state over time, and standard metrics of neural prediction accuracy cannot tell whether a model tracks an individual's brain state or relies solely on the stimulus. To directly test state inference, prediction, and updating, we introduce BrainStateBench, which evaluates a model's latent state through a frozen linear probe on whole-cortex, movie-driven fMRI. Its State task tests whether a model captures trial-to-trial variability in an individual's responses to repeated stimuli, while Forecast and Updating evaluate future activity predictions without and with new observations, respectively. To track individual brain state across time, we propose Spectator, a linear latent world model trained with a joint-embedding predictive objective. Spectator encodes short- and long-horizon observation histories into a two-timescale latent state and predicts state transitions linearly from the current state and stimulus. Stimulus-only encoders reach 0.320 in fMRI prediction correlation without observing the brain (0% on State), while prior deep brain world models reach 0.239 yet score at most 0.4% on State. In contrast, Spectator achieves 0.349 correlation alongside 5.5% on State, 16.0% on Forecast, and 20.3% on Updating, outperforming all baselines while forecasting over 20x faster than deep forecasting models.

papers.title: A generative framework for unified representations bridging electrophysiological and haemodynamic brain activity
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological and haemodynamic recordings resolve brain activity at complementary temporal and spatial scales, yet paired acquisition remains difficult to scale. We propose a generative framework that aligns paired multimodal recordings in a unified representation space and generates modality-specific haemodynamic responses from EEG. In paired cohorts, the framework generated fMRI BOLD and fNIRS haemoglobin responses that reproduced regional dynamics, cortical maps, functional connectivity and task structure. Generated BOLD followed Real BOLD time courses and cortical patterns, while Generated haemoglobin responses tracked task-evoked HbO and HbR dynamics. The framework enabled decoding across visual, motor-imagery and mental-arithmetic tasks, independent-record decoding, external BOLD localization and low-sample augmentation. Paired feature-space calibration supported bidirectional retrieval. The proposed framework extends cortical analysis and brain decoding to EEG recordings when Real haemodynamic data are sparse.

papers.title: Subquantum Pilot-Wave System Theory: Structural and Amplitude Nonequilibrium under Source Fields
papers.abstract: A source in the Schrodinger equation changes the norm of the guiding wave, apparently conflicting with the conservation of probability. In source-extended de Broglie-Bohm dynamics the conflict disappears: probability is carried by the particle ensemble, while the wavefunction guides its motion. The difficulty is then different. What does quantum equilibrium mean when the particle distribution remains normalized but the guiding density does not? We show that the departure has two independent components: a structural one, measured by the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the particle distribution and the normalized guiding density, and an amplitude one, measured by the Born weight. The Born rule holds precisely when both are equilibrated. Their evolution is governed by the complex source-to-wavefunction ratio; scale covariance further distinguishes an independently prescribed source, against which the amplitude of the wave matters, from state-dependent generators for which rescaling remains a symmetry. We develop a source-aware analytical--computational method, combining exact or semi-analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport, ensemble quadrature and independent numerical checks. Free-space impulses expose the limits of global diagnostics and an exact jump rule; a driven ring has constant Born weight but either periodic or secular structural departure; oscillators show both source-generated structural change and amplitude-only evolution, including a finite-horizon weak-drive plateau far below its frozen-particle value; and a coupled two-body model exhibits nonlocal guidance and evolving particle entanglement. The source-free, initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Simple Baselines for Fetal Brain Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) offers a promising approach to fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis, where pathological data are scarce. Existing methods rely mainly on brain age prediction or image reconstruction, but are limited by noisy gestational age (GA) labels, lack of lesion localization, or poor cross-domain generalization. We propose FetalBUAD, a UAD framework based on voxel-level brain age estimation. A joint multi-task network predicts global brain age, voxel-level brain age maps, and brain segmentation to establish an internal biological brain age reference, reducing reliance on clinically recorded GA. Uncertainty-aware voxel-level brain age gap maps are then used for anomaly localization. Experiments on 1,317 internal fetal brain MRI volumes and an external benchmark demonstrate state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance and improved cross-domain generalization. FetalBUAD also generates anatomically interpretable maps that localize diverse fetal brain abnormalities. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/birthlab/FetalBUAD.

papers.title: Interstitial Magnetoelectricity in Altermagnetic Electrides
papers.abstract: Electrides and altermagnets are two distinct yet intriguing classes of quantum materials, characterized by interstitial anionic electrons and nonrelativistic spin splitting, respectively. The recent prediction of Stoner-instability-driven altermagnetic electride provides a natural bridge between these two fields. Here, we investigate the magnetoelectric response and its related spin-polarized transport in the altermagnetic electride Zr$_2$N monolayer. Using the tight-binding Hubbard model and first-principles calculations, we find that the electric field can break the magnetic compensation between the two interstitial anionic electrons, inducing a finite net magnetization and giving rise to an interstitial electron mediated magnetoelectric response. The magnetoelectric response is further demonstrated through the electrical control of spin conductivity. Our results reveal a magnetoelectric effect in altermagnetic electrides, paving a way towards electride-based spintronic devices.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis and uniqueness of positive solutions to slightly subcritical fractional problems in symmetric domains
papers.abstract: We prove that the fractional Lane-Emden problem \[ (-\Delta)^s u = u^{p}\quad \text{ in }\Omega, \qquad u>0\quad \text{ in }\Omega, \qquad u=0 \text{ in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\Omega, \] admits a unique and nondegenerate solution when $\Omega$ is a smooth and bounded domain which is symmetric and convex with respect to $N$ orthogonal directions and the exponent $p$ is slightly subcritical. This result is new even in the case when $\Omega$ is a ball and $N\geq 2$. Our proof relies on a sharp characterization of the asymptotic behavior of low energy solutions, which we develop in general smooth bounded open sets.

papers.title: Shoonya: Zero-Socket In-Process Small Language Models for Graph Databases with Schema-Epoch KV Caching, Live Catalog Logit Masking, and Verifier-Advantage Distillation
papers.abstract: Coupling a property-graph database to an external language-model server imposes a three-part socket tax: serialization overhead dwarfing microsecond graph reads, repeated prefill of verbose schemas, and blind decoding divorced from the live catalog and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) engine. We present Shoonya, from-scratch commercially clean (0.0% non-commercial or share-alike data) tri-modal (Python, Rust, OpenCypher) small language models (16.8M to 1.07B parameters) co-designed with shoonya-infer, a zero-dependency pure-Rust runtime embedded inside the samyama-graph-enterprise address space.
