We then develop a saddle-point approach for the toroidal metric, which yields an asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov lower bound and an asymptotic Hamming-type upper bound. For \(3\mid q\), we embed ternary Hamming codes into \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) and obtain another asymptotic lower bound for the toroidal metric. In addition, we derive an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes. We compare these lower bounds with the baseline and prove that they are nontrivial in the corresponding parameter ranges. Finally, we compare the asymptotic bounds numerically.

papers.title: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
papers.abstract: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a M\"{o}bius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

papers.title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
papers.abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $\Delta t$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.
authors: mar.quest | Marburg Center for Quantum Materials and Sustainable Technologies
G. S. Matthijs Jansen (I. Physikalisches Institut
International Center for Advanced Studies of Energy Conversion)

papers.title: Polynomial spaces are locally Paley-Wiener: local spectral geometry, sampling, and interpolation
papers.abstract: We identify the local Paley-Wiener structure of multivariate polynomial spaces on centrally symmetric convex bodies and apply it to sampling and interpolation. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density in the interior, the normalized reproducing kernel at scale $1/n$ converges to the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on the dual unit ball of the Baran metric. We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral body must admit an exponential Riesz basis. Combining this result with Ortega-Cerd\`a's theorem for smooth spectra, we show that in dimension $d\ge2$, a $C^2$ boundary with everywhere positive curvature forces a positive proportion of extra sampling nodes. This rules out uniformly stable complete interpolation on such bodies. The same lower bound on the number of nodes applies to positive cubature exact through degree $2n$, since such a rule preserves the squared $L^2$ norm of every polynomial of degree at most $n$. The corresponding local-to-global problem remains open. If the local spectral body at every interior point admits an exponential Riesz basis, can one choose exactly as many nodes as polynomial coefficients at each degree so that sampling and interpolation are uniformly stable on the whole body?

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction
papers.abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of Koray's Theorem
papers.abstract: In this note, I provide a direct and self-contained proof of Koray's (2000) theorem, by which a neutral and unanimous social choice function is universally self-selective if and only if it is dictatorial. Koray's (2000) original proof relies on results by Sen (1970) and Houthakker (1950) to construct a social welfare function for each alternative set. He then shows that these functions are Paretian and independent of irrelevant alternatives, allowing him to apply Arrow's (1950, 1951) impossibility theorem. Instead, I construct a cyclic preference profile and show that the voter who ranks the chosen alternative first is the dictator on every finite nonempty alternative set.

papers.title: Fourier Bases from Optimal Eigenfunctions of Paley Graphs of Square Order
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

papers.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Migration
papers.abstract: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers. We design a migration in which owners enroll post-quantum keys cheaply with their existing signatures before ECDSA is retired at a scheduled time, while a zero-knowledge proof of the wallet's BIP-39 seed can correct any such enrollment until a common deadline afterward; an account nobody enrolled stays frozen and recoverable by seed proof without a deadline. Each proof binds the new key, a nonce and a fee cap, so neither a paying sponsor nor a reordering block builder can redirect or replay it. Validators switch to hash-based keys first, at a finalized checkpoint and under a stated bound on the attacker's voting power. We prove the account guarantees under explicit assumptions, model-check the rules, and implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client. A three-layer recursive hash-based STARK yields a seed proof of about 190 KB that fits one transaction, verifies in 38 ms and takes a median of 111 s to generate on a laptop; four proofs aggregate into one. In a ten-node simulation with mainnet-derived accounts and fee demand, block space rather than proving sets the duration: the 4.45 million accounts with at least 0.1 ETH would migrate in 29.4 days if all enroll before ECDSA is retired and in 235 days if all recover after it in batches of four. In a mass enrollment, an enrollment waits a median of 19.1 minutes in the public mempool, longer than published estimates for a fast quantum computer to extract its key, so owners with a seed and an unexposed key should migrate by seed proof.

papers.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
papers.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Di\c{t}\u{a}'s family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.

papers.title: Motion-Sickness-Aware Vehicle Control via DKUC-Based Inverse Design and Iterative Feedback Tuning
papers.abstract: Tuning existing vehicle controllers for motion-sickness reduction requires a desired vehicle response that reflects physiological comfort. The six-degree-of-freedom subjective vertical conflict (6DoF-SVC) model can evaluate sensory conflict induced by vehicle motion, but it does not directly provide a target motion for controller design. This paper proposes a 2-step framework to construct such a reference. First, a target SVC trajectory is generated from the baseline response by limiting conflict peaks while imposing a minimum activity level. Second, a lifted linear model identified using Deep KoopmanU with Control (DKUC) is inverted to map the target SVC trajectory to a regularized reference expressed in vehicle-acceleration and angular-velocity coordinates. The resulting motion reference is then used in an Iterative Feedback Tuning (IFT)-style procedure for fixed-structure PI and LQR controllers. In the considered simulation scenario, the selected SVC target reduces the sequence norm by 6.95% relative to the baseline. Controller tuning with reduced response models decreases the regularized PI and LQR objectives by 49.5% and 32.3%, respectively. These results show that a nonlinear physiological comfort objective can be converted into a practical motion reference for tuning fixed-structure vehicle controllers.

papers.title: Rigidity and Non-Rigidity of Disk Pseudo-Rotations below $C^2$
papers.abstract: For every $0<\beta\le1$, we prove $C^0$-rigidity of area-preserving $C^{1,\beta}$ disk pseudo-rotations with non-Brjuno rotation number. At the $C^1$ endpoint, every non-Brjuno rotation number of zero exponential type admits non-rigid examples. We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation. We show that this boundary conclusion fails in the bi-Lipschitz class by constructing non-rigid examples for every rotation number of finite positive exponential type. The proof of rigidity is based on a finite-information closing theorem under H\"older regularity. For the construction of counterexamples, we use disjoint supports instead of a summable perturbation scheme.

papers.title: Quantum dynamical transitions when the corresponding classical phase space has a separatrix: extension of the QKNH theorem beyond double wells
papers.abstract: In classical Hamiltonian systems with a slowly time-dependent parameter, adiabaticity breaks down at a separatrix, leading to probabilistic post-adiabatic transitions between different phase-space regions described by the Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard (KNH) theorem. Quantum mechanically, dynamical tunneling allows adiabaticity to persist where it breaks down classically, making the quantum-classical correspondence for separatrix crossing non-trivial. We recently established a quantum version of the KNH theorem (QKNH) by introducing the concept of a sweep-rate-dependent quantum separatrix in the instantaneous energy spectrum of the time-dependent system. The QKNH theorem relates the splitting of a quantum ensemble between the outgoing dynamical sectors at the quantum separatrix to their relative growth rates, and thus provides a quantum analog of the classical KNH rule. Here, we demonstrate that these findings are not restricted to double-well systems with tunneling through a potential barrier. We investigate a slowly driven quantum pendulum, in which the avoided crossings arise from above-barrier reflection. The resulting Landau-Zener probabilities have the same local lattice form as in the double-well problem, allowing the application of the QKNH theorem.

papers.title: Interior $W^{2,p}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend Caffarelli's interior $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity theory for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation to the $k$-Hessian equation, $3\leq k\leq n-1$, under sharp Sobolev or H\"older assumptions on the solution. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,\beta}$ for some $1-2/k<\beta<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1<p<\infty$; if the density is positive and belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\alpha}$, then $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,\alpha}$ for $0<\alpha<1$. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we also establish global $W^{2,1}$ regularity on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{1,1}$ domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary values.

papers.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding K\"ahler-Ricci Solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that complete expanding K\"ahler--Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in complex manifolds, provided their closures admit neighborhoods with holomorphic immersions into Euclidean space. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete K\"ahler--Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

papers.title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

papers.title: ShEPhERD-score: Fast, adaptable three-dimensional alignment of molecular features
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) molecular similarity scoring and alignment are widely employed in ligand-based virtual screening and molecular design, and are increasingly used for training and evaluating machine learning models. Existing open-source methods utilize various molecular representations spanning shape, electrostatics, pharmacophores, and hybrid representations, but their implementations as independent software packages with distinct application programming interfaces (APIs), optimizers, and limited GPU support make them difficult to compare, combine, or extend. Here, we develop ShEPhERD-score into a unified, modular platform for differentiable 3D molecular similarity scoring and alignment by combining diverse molecular representations with high-performance Numba CPU and Triton GPU kernels to support both large-scale library screening and pairwise similarity workflows. In matched comparisons with open-source 3D similarity tools on the DUDE-Z virtual screening benchmark, ShEPhERD-score performed comparably or better in eight of nine cases. Across the scoring modes in ShEPhERD-score, throughput ranges from 17,800 to 1.03 million alignments/second for ten-million-conformer libraries using a single NVIDIA L40S GPU. Moreover, we found that the most effective scoring mode varied by protein target, indicating that target-specific calibration against validation data may be valuable before large-scale screening and underscoring the need for a unified platform that provides diverse molecular representations. Together, these capabilities establish ShEPhERD-score as a single, extensible toolkit for rapid virtual screening and machine learning workflows.

papers.title: Adaptive Filtering With Reduced Computational Complexity Using SOPOT Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Implementing finite impulse response (FIR) adaptive filters by employing the sums of signed-powers-of-two (SOPOT) arithmetic may lead to simpler hardware and consequently reduced power consumption. In this paper, one evaluates the effects of SOPOT arithmetic on the adaptive filter's recursion algorithms. The filters' coefficients and algorithms' underlying variables are fully operated using SOPOT arithmetic in the whole iterative process. More specifically, one evaluates convergence rate, numerical stability, and accuracy since using few signed-powers-of-two (SPT) terms propagates numerical errors during the adaptive cycle that may impair the algorithm behavior. The SOPOT approximations are obtained through the technique known as Matching Pursuits with Generalized Bit-Plane (MPGBP) algorithm, with notable cost-performance trade-off and low computational complexity. Results are provided for the Least-Mean-Squares (LMS), the Normalized Least-Mean-Squares (NLMS) and the Recursive-Least-Squares (RLS) algorithms, considering adaptive filters employed for system identification and change detection.

papers.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. Here, we present an architecture that integrates an agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring that state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. We demonstrate this architecture on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrument in an oxidant-screening campaign for synthesizing an organic dye. Within human-defined campaign limits, the agent submitted measurement jobs, interpreted mass spectrometry (MS) and diode-array detection (DAD) data, flagged failed experiments, and produced an oxidant ranking. This ranking matched that obtained from scripted peak integration, and organic chemists confirmed the agent's spectral interpretations and failure assignments. In a simulated environment that replays the archived LC-MS data, where the agent chose which wells to inject under varying injection limits, it measured the highest-yielding condition at about its seventh injection, against 14.5 on average for a random order, and identified it in every campaign with a limit of eight or more injections. An agent can therefore close the analysis-to-design gap while its actions stay bounded and verifiable, which is a step toward greater autonomy for SDLs.

papers.title: Entanglement Geometry Beyond Polygons: Graph-Theoretic Entanglement Inequalities
papers.abstract: Entanglement entropies of pure multipartite states can be constrained by organizing subsystem cuts as edges (hyperedges) of graphs (hypergraphs). Starting from the one-party entanglement polygon inequality, we derive these constraints from strong subadditivity and pure-state complementarity, with optimal coefficients and explicit equality conditions. Our central result determines, for a distinguished two-party cut and an arbitrary weighted family of cuts, the optimal polygon coefficient: the smallest total weight of the cuts separating a member of the distinguished pair from a remaining party. A refinement involving three mutual information terms gives the exact minimum of the weighted sum at fixed entropies of the two parties and of their union, attained by at most three independent bipartite pure states. The analogous coefficient is also optimal for a distinguished one-party cut and for any distinguished cut that the family does not split. This criterion recovers the cycle and complete-graph inequalities and shows that uniform incidence parity, which we prove sufficient for polygon inequalities on hypergraphs, is not necessary. Averaging strong subadditivity over both sides of a bipartition gives a sharp $k$-marginal inequality with coefficient $2\binom{n-2}{k-1}$, and we determine uniformly optimal coefficients for collective hyperstar inequalities. For paths and overlapping hyperchains, the deficits are exact sums of conditional mutual information terms; genuinely multipartite entangled cluster states saturate the hyperchain inequality while the chain inequality remains strict. We characterize pure chain equality states, bound the trace distance to cycle equality states independently of the number of parties and local dimensions, and obtain bond-dimension bounds for matrix product states and sequential-recovery error estimates.

papers.title: Exact Fractional Chern Insulators from Hubbard Interactions
papers.abstract: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

papers.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
papers.abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{24}\in K$.

papers.title: How graviton mass shapes angular correlations in a relic gravitational-wave background
papers.abstract: A nonzero graviton mass makes waves emitted at the same epoch travel different distances at different momenta. A finite band therefore samples a shell that is both closer to the observer and thicker. We derive the distribution of source radii and use it to calculate the band angular-power ratio $C_\ell^{BB}(m_{\rm g})/C_\ell^{BB}(0)$ for a relic stochastic gravitational-wave background. For a common source field with a scale-invariant spatial spectrum, a thin shell has the same angular power at every radius. Radial averaging cannot exceed this power, so any suppression relative to the massless single-epoch spectrum is due to shell broadening. We also ask whether source mixing can mimic massive propagation across two frequency bands. For two independent emission episodes whose mixing fractions are fixed across multipoles, massless propagation requires the low-band auto-power and the cross-power, each normalized by the high-band auto-power, to lie on a straight line when plotted against one another. This holds for arbitrary angular spectra of the two sources. A massive benchmark near the low-band propagation threshold violates this relation. A joint massless fit with power-law sources nevertheless gives an rms logarithmic residual of $0.013$ over $2\leq\ell\leq10$.

papers.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the square torus
papers.abstract: For each finite $s>1$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$. The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a finite-dimensional family of one-dimensional solutions of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier. At and above the index two, we match the second-order normal frequency shift separately on each triangle using harmonics of the axial solution. For every fixed $2<s<\infty$ we also obtain a solution for which $\log\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\asymp\sqrt{\log t/\log\log t}$ at every sufficiently large time.

papers.title: Old Matches, New Frames: Schedule-Gated Stereo Memory from Human Vision to Machine Matching
papers.abstract: Human vision and video stereo networks both reuse disparity evidence across time, yet a refresh of the input can invalidate a match formed milliseconds earlier. What tells a system whether an old match still counts? We answer this from limited human data in three steps. First, nine temporal mechanisms share a frozen binocular-energy front end and an equal-capacity readout, so held-out behavior isolates the temporal selection rule: on 240 conditions from 10 observers, down-weighting aged evidence that has lost binocular support lowers subject RMSE from 12.6% to 10.3% and reproduces a period-dependent reversed-depth illusion, across all 59 readings of the unpublished protocol and 8 front-end perturbations. Second, four propositions establish what such data can identify: gating is identified at the level of the refresh schedule, and candidate binding is invisible to standard stimuli but exposed by a single-eye geometry flip that separates the readouts by up to 7.1%. Third, the identified rule becomes a two-field stereo memory that separates sample validity from hypothesis support. It removes a 50 ms recovery lag after geometry flips, and its regime analysis explains why plain integration stays preferable on MPI-Sintel, where 71.1% of pixels change appearance but not disparity.

papers.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
papers.abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.

papers.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
papers.abstract: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states. Training reorganized the ensemble: initial pairwise distances did not consistently predict final distances. Nevertheless, all 30 trained networks were correctly matched to their initial weights among ten candidates per dataset. Networks sharing an initialization also developed recognizable final hidden representations across different batch schedules, although direct comparisons with initial activity did not recover identity. Learning order remained readable as well. A linear probe decoded the order of two earlier tasks with 100% accuracy on 80 held-out networks after ten epochs of a common final task. Earlier intermediate weight states were partly predictable, but individual initial weights could not be reliably reconstructed. Final weights thus retain selective historical information rather than a complete trajectory record. Perturbed networks recovered classification performance without returning to their unperturbed training paths. This separation persisted across datasets, intervention times, and network layers. Moreover, 2,157 of 2,160 aligned endpoint pairs showed no positive loss barrier at sampled interpolation points, indicating low-loss connections between distinct solutions rather than convergence to one weight vector. Together, these findings show that a shared task constrains networks to related successful solutions without erasing their individual histories. Final weights reflect not only what a network has learned, but also where learning began and how it unfolded.

papers.title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
papers.abstract: For a crystallographic root system $\Phi$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}\Phi$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $\rho + \lambda$, where $\rho$ is the Weyl vector and $\lambda$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $\rho$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

papers.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
papers.abstract: Fully constraining the neutron star equation of state requires combining observations from various channels that probe different density regimes. We perform a joint multiprobe inference of the equation of state using gravitational-wave observations from binary neutron star mergers, NICER mass-radius measurements of X-ray pulsars, and radio timing mass measurements of massive pulsars. We constrain the parametrized equation of state and perform Bayesian model selection among a set of candidate equations of state. The joint analysis yields a radius of $R_{1.4} = 11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83} \, \rm km$ for a canonical $1.4 \, M_\odot$ neutron star, and a maximum non-rotating neutron star mass of $M_{\rm max} = 2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23} \, M_\odot$ with $90\%$ credible intervals. Gravitational-wave and NICER observations constrain the equation of state at low to intermediate densities, while massive pulsar observations constrain it at high densities by requiring the equation of state to support the observed neutron star masses. We find no simple correlation between the stiffness of an equation of state and Bayesian evidence across different observational probes.

papers.title: The state of nuclear data for fusion activation simulations
papers.abstract: This report compares decay-heat calculations made with four nuclear data libraries, TENDL-2025, ENDF/B-VIII.1, JEFF-4.0 and JENDL-5, against the JAEA FNS decay-heat benchmark. The main comparison uses the 2000 campaign, in which 73 foils were irradiated for five minutes in a mostly 14 MeV neutron field and their decay heat was measured for about an hour. The 1996 seven-hour campaign, with 29 foils and cooling times of up to 400 days, is compared separately and is not included in the rankings. Over the 69 elemental foils solved by all four libraries, the median deviation from the measurement (the mean absolute C/E deviation of each foil) is JENDL-5 17 percent, TENDL-2025 19 percent, JEFF-4.0 22 percent and ENDF/B-VIII.1 44 percent. No library is best everywhere: JENDL-5 on 24, JEFF-4.0 on 18, TENDL-2025 on 17 and ENDF/B-VIII.1 on 10 of the foils. For each element the report breaks the heat down by product and lists the nuclear data on which the libraries differ, and the final sections propose measurements, including enriched-isotope irradiations, that would resolve the largest differences.

papers.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. III. Reissner-Nordstr\"om spectra from zero to extremal charge
papers.abstract: Earlier calculations left open how gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of charged black holes recover the Schwarzschild spectrum and how the modes near algebraically special frequencies relate to the exact special solutions. We extend our Kerr analysis to Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes by analytically continuing the ingoing horizon solution and locating the zeros of the incoming amplitude at infinity. For each of $\ell=2$ and $3$, we trace the first 42 overtone families from the Schwarzschild limit to extremality. The charge trajectories distinguish crossings of the negative imaginary axis from turns near it and separate the unconventional Schwarzschild modes from neighboring branches. At zero charge the polar algebraically special mode is a QNM. At extremal charge the exact axial special modes are total-transmission modes. Of the 84 families, 75 approach distinct extremal frequencies with finite damping, and nine approach zero frequency with vanishing excitation. At exact extremality we also compute, for the first time, gravitational QNMs on the unconventional Riemann sheet reached across the negative imaginary axis. At intermediate charge, the clearest resonant enhancement of both excitation factors occurs for the $\ell=3$ overtone pairs $(22,23)$ and $(23,24)$.

papers.title: A hyperbolicity obstruction near regular charged centers
papers.abstract: A conserved charge creates a tension at a spherical center: the flux remains fixed while the area of the symmetry spheres shrinks. We ask whether curvature-dependent electromagnetic responses can reconcile bounded central curvature with hyperbolic propagation in four-dimensional Einstein gravity when both parity-even and parity-odd couplings are allowed. The background equations force a positive charge potential and its first curvature derivative to vanish at the central curvature endpoint. On branches with a positive electromagnetic kinetic coefficient and a positive effective gravitational coefficient, this endpoint flattening produces a physical extraordinary mode of the fully coupled equations whose squared angular characteristic speed is strictly below minus one at radii arbitrarily close to the center. Its characteristic cone has no hyperbolicity direction in common with the ordinary photon and graviton modes. The result requires no central curvature expansion, remains valid at points where the curvature Legendre Hessian vanishes, and extends to positive-definite mixing of finitely many Abelian fields. An exact analytic example with a nonlinear gravitational curvature sector admits a real, subluminal extraordinary photon cone near the center. In a fixed-action black-hole family, the obstruction extends outside the outer horizon over a near-extremal parameter interval.

papers.title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
papers.abstract: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $\delta>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^\delta(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^\delta(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{\delta \to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^\delta(K)) |}{\delta^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $\delta$ instead of $\delta^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
papers.abstract: Within the core-accretion framework, gas giants acquire the bulk of their mass through accretion shocks during runaway gas accretion. The shock thermodynamics---governed by radiative cooling efficiency, accretion history, and equation of state (EoS)---sets the post-shock entropy and initial thermal state, strongly influencing both observables and subsequent evolution. We construct a coupled evolutionary model predicting the initial thermodynamic states, intrinsic luminosities, and upper limits on the magnetic field strengths of gas giants across diverse accretion histories. We couple radiation hydrodynamics and $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociation to long-term interior evolution by training a fast physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate model on 1000 first-principles simulations resolving the shock physics. This surrogate model supplies post-shock outer boundary conditions for MESA to evolve the planetary envelope beyond runaway accretion. It yields higher post-shock temperatures than the canonical cold-start model, with the discrepancy widening with planetary mass, while the post-shock entropy jumps sharply when $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociates at $\sim 2000$ K. Gas giants evolved with these boundary conditions attain intrinsic luminosities 4--10 times higher than cold-start models. Under optimistic assumptions, the maximum magnetic field strength at $2\,\mathrm{R_J}$ reaches a few gauss for a $0.3\,\mathrm{M_J}$ planet, $\sim 100$ G for $1\,\mathrm{M_J}$, and $\sim 500$ G for $3\,\mathrm{M_J}$. Incorporating detailed radiation hydrodynamics and realistic thermodynamics into accretion shock models yields higher initial entropies, brighter intrinsic luminosities, and stronger magnetic fields, providing improved constraints on the masses and accretion rates of directly imaged exoplanets.

papers.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

papers.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $\lambda$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+\lambda=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.

papers.title: The isolation number of uniform hypertrees
papers.abstract: An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $\iota(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Let $T$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. We prove that if $T$ has order $n$ and at least two edges, then $\iota(T)\le\lfloor n/(2r-1)\rfloor$, where $r\ge3$. Moreover, the bound is attained for every admissible order. Furthermore, we characterize all hypertrees attaining it by a construction using six types of marked hypertrees of orders $2r-1$, $3r-2$ and $4r-3$. For connected graphs of order $n$ with at least two blocks, all of which are triangles, we obtain the sharp bound $\lfloor n/5\rfloor$ on the cycle isolation number and characterize the graphs attaining it.

papers.title: The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.

papers.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
papers.abstract: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(\pi/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. We also study orthogonal families in a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] For \(1<p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] For \(1<p\le2\), uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(s\) for every \(1\le s<p\), with a quadratic bound in the restricted type constant at \(s=2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} We also record the subcritical type implication for Pythagorean orthogonality and the sharp factor \(p\) for Roberts orthogonality. {For each \(1<p<2\), as the modulus of roundness \(\nu_X(p)\) approaches \(2\), the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant tends uniformly to \(1\) over real Banach spaces of Rademacher type \(p\). The same limit holds for the ratio of the two constants restricted by mutual Birkhoff--James orthogonality.}

papers.title: $X(2370)$ without exceptionalism from reanalyzing $J/\psi \to \gamma + 3P$ data
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/\psi$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/\psi\to\gamma PPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\eta^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $\eta(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $\eta_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0\eta$ and $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

papers.title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
papers.abstract: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of topology and latent states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian: a flexible generative transition can absorb graph-induced changes of the conditional mean, whereas a Gaussian transition discards the information in the residual shape. We develop a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, and a frozen diffusion emulator represents the conditionally centered residual. First, a score--topology duality expresses edge-wise likelihood gradients as edge projections of the residual diffusion score, so topology learning requires neither transition densities nor differentiation through the sampler. Second, we prove identifiability from intermittent observations, invariance of the population minimizer across noise levels, and global strong convexity above an explicit smoothing threshold for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. With known support and oracle state pairs, the asymptotic covariance approaches the Cram\'er--Rao bound as smoothing vanishes and is strictly smaller than that of any Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimator under an explicit non-Gaussianity condition; for unknown sparse support we characterize the boundary limit, and we quantify the topology bias caused by residual-score mismatch. Third, we couple score-driven graph updates with an approximately fully adapted generative particle filter and prove, for bounded residuals under explicit excitation and forgetting conditions, a mean-square closed-loop bound with a step-size-independent small-gain condition. Synthetic and real-data experiments confirm these gains under non-Gaussian forcing.

papers.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
papers.abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

papers.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
papers.abstract: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.

papers.title: Holomorphic Feynman diagrams in four dimensions and the quantum BPS ring
papers.abstract: We compute at all loop orders the kernels of the holomorphic Feynman graphs governing loop corrections to supersymmetry transformations and regularized operator products in the holomorphic twist of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric gauge theories. Interpreting their current equations as those of an electrical network---with Schwinger parameters as resistances and holomorphic momenta as injected currents---we iterate series, parallel and star-triangle reductions on Schwinger space to obtain the fan, spider and cubic product-forest kernels at all loop orders. Assuming that twisting commutes with quantization for composite operators, we obtain every perturbative correction to the supersymmetry transformation in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, acting on operators with arbitrary holomorphic derivatives. Using the marked higher operations of Gaiotto, Kulp and Wu, we construct the quantum product and prove that on cohomology of the quantum supercharge it is associative, graded commutative and unital, furnishing the multiplication of the quantum BPS ring; in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory every multi-graviton operator thus admits an explicit finite all-order completion. For the classical gauge groups, every perturbative differential image in the multi-trace ring vanishes upon Cartan restriction. In $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, we find new fortuitous classes and one-loop lifts across several gauge groups, no two-loop lift in the sectors tested, and rationally certified three-loop lifts in $SO(11)$, $SO(12)$ and $SO(13)$. The lowest example we find lies in the level-$34$ BMN sector of $SO(13)$. The glueball lifts in $SO(11)$ and $SO(13)$ remove the excess classical powers relative to their symplectic duals. Beyond $\mathcal N=4$, we find two-loop lifts in the Leigh-Strassler and $\beta$-deformations, and two- to four-loop lifts in abelian and $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theories.

papers.title: From dynamic strain aging to Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi dynamics of propagating Portevin--Le Chatelier bands
papers.abstract: Type-A Portevin--Le Chatelier bands are propagating strain localizations whose velocity exhibits strong intermittent fluctuations. We derive a coarse-grained connection between the dynamic-strain-aging model of H\"ahner and Rizzi and the Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi (ABBM) mean-field model of avalanche dynamics. A propagating band is reduced to a single phase coordinate while retaining the elastic feedback of the tensile machine. This feedback generates the increasing drive and restoring terms of the ABBM description. A finite-time adjoint calculation determines the stress mobility of the band and is checked independently by direct stress continuation. The mobility is approximately proportional to the hardening parameter, whereas the band speed scales approximately as its square root. Short-range heterogeneity in the plastic strain deposited by the band is converted by the global machine feedback into a Brownian effective force. The resulting reduction provides a microscopic route from dynamic strain aging to ABBM-like avalanche dynamics of propagating PLC bands.

papers.title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

papers.title: Is It Worth Collecting Additional Covariates?
papers.abstract: In many studies, basic covariates are routinely recorded at negligible cost, whereas acquiring additional covariates requires expensive or time-consuming procedures. Thus, a natural question is whether it is worth to collecting these additional covariates. Using the reduction in prediction interval width as criterion, we evaluate and test the gain brought by the additional covariates and hence answer this question. We consider the gain both marginally and conditionally on the observable characteristics. The conditional formulation captures subpopulation heterogeneity and supports individualized data acquisition decisions. To avoid restrictive parametric assumptions, we adopt a model-free framework that accommodates flexible nonparametric or machine learning methods. We propose an efficient influence function based method, with proven theoretical properties to achieve our purpose under mild nuisance convergence rates. Interestingly, we find the natural conformal prediction based method cannot achieve the same purpose: It fails in the marginal case and imposes much more stringent or even infeasible requirement on the nuisance parameter estimation procedures. We demonstrate the superior finite-sample performance of the proposed procedures through simulations and real data applications.

papers.title: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: We present a tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states with Chebyshev recursion and maximum entropy spectral analysis in a tree tensor network tangent space, for quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented tensor network state calculations in the tangent space of the ground state, the core advantage of TaChe is that it can substantially reduce the computational complexity, memory usage, and numerical instability associated with tensor network state compression. Implemented on the GPU platform, it produces accurate spectra with speedups of up to $46.8$ over the previous Chebyshev tensor network method and $13.7$ over one-site time-dependent variational principle propagation in the reported benchmarks. Applications to acetonitrile, thermal aggregate emission, finite-temperature charge transport on a \(6\times6\) lattice, and internal conversion in aggregates of up to 100 molecules demonstrate the efficiency and versatility of TaChe in simulating complex molecular systems.

papers.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
papers.abstract: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in\ZZ_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of essential simple ideal arcs based at a distinguished cusp of a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: Character codegrees in $\pi$-separable groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_{\pi}(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $\pi$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(\chi)=|G:\ker\chi|/\chi(1)$) are $\pi$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $\pi$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_{\pi}(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}$-characters $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}(G)$.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties I. Fibrations over curves
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or the function field of a curve, and let $X\to C$ be a projective fibration over a curve over $K$. We prove a height inequality for relatively nef adelic line bundles $\bar L$ on $X$ with $L$ nef. For a nef, relatively ample line bundle $L$ over a finitely generated field, we deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model. Over $\mathbb{C}$, for an ample line bundle $L$ and a smooth positive polarization, the Euler--Lagrange equation is the Calabi--Yau equation. On the projective bundle $X=\mathbb{P}_C(E)$ of a vector bundle $E$ of degree zero, our energy on quotient metrics on $L=\mathcal{O}(1)$ agrees with Donaldson's functional when the determinant metric is fixed. We propose a construction of canonical heights on parameter spaces using envelopes of local energies.

papers.title: Relative periodic orbits of a free spinning loop
papers.abstract: A closed elastic string with no external forces can hold any shape while its material moves steadily along the curve (a steady axial motion), because its tension and the force needed to turn the material around a bend are both proportional to the curvature. I compute the periodic motions that grow from the simplest of these motions, the spinning ring, by Newton's method on a chain of masses. They include rotating waves that turn at twice the rotation rate of the material, standing "flappers" with two to five lobes, and period-doubled and period-tripled orbits. The chain only approximates the string. The orbits and their strong instabilities change little with more masses and are properties of the continuous string. Most weak instabilities change with the number of masses and are artifacts of approximating the string by a finite chain. The saddle flapper of a loop stretched 30% beyond its natural length is neutrally stable at small heights and unstable at large ones. Near a stretch of 1/12 the saddle flapper resonates with the breathing of the ring. Below that stretch the flapper slows as it grows and above it the flapper speeds up, and near the resonance two families of saddle flappers overlap. An unstable saddle flapper trades energy back and forth with an in-plane oval, and at large amplitude the energy spreads to the shortest waves of the chain. For Keller's linear string, whose tension is proportional to the stretched length, every motion is periodic, and every knot carries an exactly periodic flapper. For a Hookean string the curvature of a knot couples a ripple to stretching waves that travel at a different speed, and in the simulations a ripple on a sliding knot does not return to its starting shape. Whether a Hookean knot carries any periodic flapper is open.

papers.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
papers.abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

papers.title: Construction of a Deployable Closure Model for the Transport of Turbulence Dissipation Rate with Hard-Constrained Physics-Informed Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We present a hard-constrained physics-informed machine learning (PIML) method for constructing a deployable closure model for the transport of turbulence dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each performing a single task. The closure module represents the closure with a small network, while the state module represents the flow state during training. The closure network is coupled to the state network through the governing equation residuals. This coupling allows us to learn the closure without using reference closure values as training targets. The coordinate module learns monotone input coordinates that help both networks resolve sharp changes. Within the network architecture, the boundary condition (BC) module imposes boundary values exactly using the Theory of Functional Connections, and the realizability module keeps the closure realizable. We study decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) and learn $\psi$, the closure function governing dissipation rate decay, from trajectories obtained in experiments and direct numerical simulations. Here, the state module is a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), the BC module imposes the initial state and the closure's low and high Reynolds number limits, and the realizability module ensures growth of the Taylor microscale. The framework reduces the root mean square of the closure variation across ten random seeds by about 95\% relative to the unconstrained model over the training and held-out range. The deployed 18-parameter closure network requires only the Taylor scale Reynolds number $Re_{\lambda_g}$ and can be exported as a standalone C function.

papers.title: A Minimal Toy Model of Charged Superradiant Spin-Down in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract: Long-lived extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive to slow changes in the mass and spin of their central black holes. We construct a deliberately minimal toy model in which an effective hidden charge opens a charged-superradiance channel, a bosonic cloud grows from a seed, and energy and angular momentum are transferred from a rotating black hole to the cloud. The model is not a Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation. Instead, it consists of a threshold function, one phenomenological rate coefficient, and balance equations that conserve the combined black-hole-cloud energy. This reduction yields an analytic relation between mass loss and spin-down and makes the roles of the growth coefficient, seed energy, and superradiant margin transparent. For an illustrative system with initial mass $2\times10^6 M_\odot$, spin 0.90, effective charge-to-mass ratio 0.30, and a one-year evolution time, the chosen benchmark reaches $M/M_0=0.8933$ and $a_\star=0.7704$. These values are then passed to FastEMRIWaveforms as two stationary Kerr snapshots. The resulting figures show that the endpoint state has a shifted time-domain oscillation pattern and a lower-frequency harmonic structure relative to the initial state. Because the snapshots are regenerated independently, they do not constitute a phase-connected, time-dependent waveform and cannot by themselves support a detectability claim. The value of the construction is instead diagnostic: it isolates a compact set of assumptions, exposes parameter degeneracies, and identifies the minimum ingredients required for a future self-consistent calculation. In this sense, the model provides a reproducible bridge between charged-superradiance intuition and EMRI waveform studies without presenting its benchmark as an astrophysical forecast.

papers.title: Fold Weighting for Cross-Validation Under Continuous Distributional Drift
papers.abstract: Cross-validation weights all folds equally, so under drift the oldest folds count as much as the newest. We model drift by a H\"older condition in total variation distance and give finite-sample bounds on the excess deployment risk of the configuration that sliding-window cross-validation selects. Each bound splits into drift, estimation, and validation-noise terms. With equal weights the drift terms saturate as the record grows. With fold weights fixed in advance, the drift terms become weighted averages, which shrink as weight moves toward deployment. The noise term grows as the weights concentrate and shrinks with the batch size. The drift terms are linear in the weights and the noise term is convex, so minimizing the bound over the weights is a convex problem. Applications to U.S. earnings and flight delays show both sides of this trade-off. Weight on recent folds pays off when a change in the best predictor persists and each period has many observations, and equal weights do best when changes are short-lived.

papers.title: StreamingDPD: A 1.28-GSa/s Instantaneous-Power-Gated Depthwise TCN Accelerator for Real-Time 320-MHz Digital Predistortion
papers.abstract: State feedback between successive samples limits the streaming throughput of recurrent neural networks for digital predistortion (DPD). We present StreamingDPD, an accelerator that processes 320-MHz signals at 1.28 GSa/s. Its 207-parameter instantaneous-power-gated depthwise temporal convolutional network (IPG-DWTCN) uses $|x[n]|^2$ to gate feature channels and causal dilated depthwise convolutions to model power amplifier memory. The network maps to a spatially unrolled fixed-point pipeline with shift-based quadratic activations and layer-wise mixed precision, sustaining one complex sample per cycle per lane. Its algorithmic cost is 554 floating-point operations per complex sample, 30.1% fewer than the recurrent baseline with the best linearization performance. In RF playback measurements on three power amplifiers driven by 40- to 320-MHz Wi-Fi 6/7 and 5G NR waveforms, IPG-DWTCN achieves the lowest mean adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) and ranks first or ties for first in mean error vector magnitude (EVM) against five neural baselines of comparable size. Four-lane FPGA hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 320-MHz 4096-QAM Wi-Fi 7 waveform achieve -45.82 dBc ACPR and -42.94 dB EVM at 1.28 GSa/s. At the same sample rate, post-layout evaluation of a single-lane 12-nm FinFET ASIC yields a 0.10 mm$^2$ core, a 52-cycle (40.63 ns) latency, and an estimated typical-corner power of 142.21 mW (111.10 pJ/sample). Relative to the prior 22-nm recurrent DPD ASIC, the design provides 5.1 times the throughput at about one-seventh the energy per sample.

papers.title: On the $\phi^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $\phi^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.

papers.title: Tunable Microresonator Arrays Induced by Geometric Phase
papers.abstract: Unlike periodic field-intensity patterns, which can be generated by interference of coherent beams of uniform intensity, periodic structures in a material are usually created by periodic modification of its properties or geometry. In contrast, we show here that a millimeter-long bundle of four conventional side-coupled optical fibers with a slowly varying transverse arrangement can support a nearly periodic array of whispering-gallery-mode microresonators, whose period can be tuned mechanically down to about $100\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.

papers.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
papers.abstract: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (P\'eclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

papers.title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation. We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair. On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $\pi_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates.
