The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.

papers.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
papers.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the H\"older topology.

papers.title: Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
papers.abstract:
We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $
u^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $
u$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-\mathsf{r}
u^{ rac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-
u t}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim 
u^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $
u$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\sim
u^{- rac13}$.

papers.title: Metric random tilings: counted geometric disorder and its diffraction
papers.abstract: Random tilings gain entropy through the many ways fixed shapes can meet. What disorder remains possible when every face keeps its neighbours and every edge its direction? In metric random tilings, shared edges take discrete lengths that must close every face. For three equally spaced lengths, four of the eleven uniform tilings admit a number of geometries that grows exponentially with area. On the honeycomb this multiplicity survives even when the boundary and inventory of each flower patch are prescribed. Breaking the equal spacing lowers the estimated honeycomb entropy from about half a Boltzmann constant per face to about a fifth. Shifting all lengths together preserves every pattern and its probability, yet changes the coherent diffraction intensity by nearly three orders of magnitude on matched honeycomb samples. Metric random tilings thus realize bulk disorder at fixed topology and reveal how strongly its diffraction signature can vary at fixed configurational entropy.

papers.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the most efficient jet. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $\sigma\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $\Gamma_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

papers.title: Metadata for the Flux Density Calibration of the April 2021 and March 2022 Event Horizon Telescope Science Data
papers.abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has been conducting science observations annually since 2021 after the initial campaigns in 2017 and 2018. In this memo, we report on the metadata associated to the observations from 2021 April and 2022 March at 1.3mm wavelengths. We follow a similar path for the collection, processing, and validation of the metadata used for the initial amplitude calibration of the 2018 EHT data. In this release, we introduce some differences regarding the treatment of sensitivities and gain curves for some stations. In addition, we describe the changes to the EHT array since 2018.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Spacecraft performance in the L2 environment
papers.abstract: The Euclid mission was designed around the need for thermo-optical and mechanical stability, stray-light suppression, low outgassing, and precise guiding. After three years in space, a wealth of data is available to assess the performance in these areas. We review the L2 halo-orbit design and consumables budget. Solar stray-light gradually increases by 14% per year and is consistent with meteoroid puncturing, but remains low overall. Data loss from high solar activity has declined notably since the maximum of the 25th Solar cycle passed. The thermodynamical response of the optical elements to a thermal step impulse follows sigmoidal growth curves, entering the asymptotic equilibration regime after 21--46 hours. Water-ice contamination has affected data from both instruments and requires continued monitoring; we review detection and decontamination methods, and Euclid's contamination history. High-precision measurements of the zodiacal background reveal, at eight sigma significance, the subtle modulation caused by the changing perspective on the dust distribution due to the L2 halo-orbit libration. These data also show that conservative pre-launch estimates overestimated the out-of-field stray-light by factors of 4 (H band) to 27 (I band). Telemetry data demonstrate excellent guiding, and enable highly significant detections of solar radiation pressure and of thermal-emission recoil from Euclid's unilluminated dark sides. Lastly, we present a list of 34 meteoroid impacts, discuss their mechanical and optical signatures, and derive a minimum detectable impactor mass of 5e-7 g.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Calibration strategy and observations
papers.abstract: This paper reviews how Euclid's top-level calibration requirements were translated into a calibration plan, how this plan is implemented and maintained during the survey, and how it performs in the current DR1 release. We show that DR1 already meets or exceeds most end-of-mission spectrophotometric calibration requirements. The construction of spectroscopically complete and pure samples relies on ongoing data acquisition for the Euclid Deep Survey, while point-spread-function modelling and shear calibration are still converging to their stringent accuracy requirements. With all DR1 data reprocessed with the DR1 pipeline configuration, more subtle effects have been detected and characterised, and correction strategies have been developed for DR2. These include improved absolute flux calibration, astrometry, charge-persistence correction, shutter effects, wavelength calibration, and spectrophotometric corrections for water-ice contamination. Finally, synthetic photometric transformations between Euclid and each of Roman, the James Webb Space Telescope, and the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope, are presented.

papers.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
papers.abstract: A defender releases an integer-valued secret $X$ (a count, a discretised measurement, a clock value) as $Y = X + N$, where $N$ is an independent integer-valued mask whose expected absolute value, the expected distortion of the released value, is at most $c$. An adversary who knows the prior of $X$ and the law of $N$ observes $Y$ once and makes a single guess. We determine exactly how small the adversary's success probability, the posterior Bayes vulnerability, can be made, and which masks achieve it. For a secret supported on an interval of $m$ integers we give the optimum and an explicit optimiser for the uniform prior; by the maximal-leakage formula, the same mask minimises the worst-case-prior one-guess leakage for every prior with that support. For a biased bit, the simplest prior a defender can exploit, we characterise the masks that leak nothing on average, give the critical budget at which this becomes possible, and determine the entire cost-vulnerability frontier. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks, with infinitely many affine pieces accumulating at the critical budget, where the frontier meets the prior vulnerability with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both vulnerability and cost are exactly additive. The results give exact, prior-aware design guidance for additive integer noise against one-guess adversaries.

papers.title: On the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. For such an operator with bounded measurable coefficients in dimension $n \ge 2,$ fix a center $x_0$ and a volume $V > 0,$ and let $E$ be the corresponding canonical set. We prove that a bounded open set $D$ of volume $V$ containing $x_0$ satisfies the mean value inequality at $x_0$ for every integrable subsolution on $D$ if and only if $E \subset D \subset \operatorname{int}\overline{E}.$ In particular, every such strong mean value set agrees with $E$ almost everywhere. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ''mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume contains the entire unit sphere and has a hole of positive measure inside the unit ball.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
papers.abstract: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
papers.abstract: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.

papers.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
papers.abstract: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives of finite duration can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate comparisons, some protocols reach a prescribed entropy tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. At criticality, a slow scalar field can persist even when little horizon entropy remains available for preparation and subsequent relaxation. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of order $\varepsilon^4$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient governs the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow mode on the normal side. This weight vanishes in proportion to the mode's decay rate near the transition. Horizon area growth is quadratic in the covariant scalar flux. When the horizon remains smooth and its area growth uniformly controls the radial drift of the scalar field, the time needed to suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$. Charge transfer fixes the signed area swept out by the time integral of this same flux, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.

papers.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
papers.abstract: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

papers.title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

papers.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
papers.abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterized by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.

papers.title: Improving Efficiency and Power in Small Rare-Disease Trials Through Prespecified, Data-Adaptive Covariate Adjustment
papers.abstract: Covariate adjustment can potentially improve efficiency in randomized clinical trials, but in rare diseases, limited prior knowledge makes it difficult to specify an adjustment at the design stage. Targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) with the Super Learner (TMLE+SL) can outperform fixed adjustment methods, such as the G-computation estimator, by leveraging machine learning to learn both the covariates and the functional form of the adjustment from the trial data. Estimating the known treatment mechanism can improve efficiency further. In simulations reflecting real rare-disease trials, TMLE+SL yielded valid inference and achieved greater efficiency and power than conventional analyses. Finally, we also provide practical guidance on specifying TMLE+SL in rare-disease trials.

papers.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
papers.abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov, the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

papers.title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: Cross-Attribute Externalities of Fairness Interventions
papers.abstract: Fairness interventions often targets disparities associated with a single sensitive attribute in binary classification tasks. However, when multiple sensitive attributes are associated with a data subject, improving fairness with respect to one attribute does not necessarily improve it across all attributes: it may exacerbate disparities associated with other sensitive attributes, including those that are unavailable to the practitioner. We refer to these unintended effects as cross-attribute externalities of fairness. We study how fairness with respect to one sensitive attribute varies when an initially unfair classification or regression model is corrected with respect to another attribute. We characterize these externalities using Wasserstein barycentric disparities and develop a distributional framework that captures changes in both marginal and joint fairness measures. This highlights a limitation of conventional fairness evaluation, in which the success of an intervention is assessed mainly for the attribute it targets. In a jointly Gaussian model, we derive explicit trajectories for marginal and joint disparities and identify conditions under which an intervention eliminates disparities with respect to its target attribute while increasing disparities associated with another attribute. We also derive sharp partial-identification bounds on the resulting externalities when a sensitive attribute is unavailable and extend our results to categorical sensitive attributes. We illustrate these externalities using classification and regression real-data: in the classification experiments, interventions increase unfairness with respect to the hidden attribute in the majority of scenarios across more than half of the datasets considered; in the regression experiments on the ACSIncome dataset, correcting for race reduces sex disparities, whereas subsequently correcting for age increases them.

papers.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.

papers.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval, and outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$. Near this threshold $a_*$ the distance between the two modes is of order $(a-a_*)^{1/2}$, and the width of the interval is of order $(a-a_*)^{3/2}$. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one. The proof bounds the sign changes of the first and second differences of the finite walk, including those created at the boundary, and passes them to the limit.

papers.title: Katz Kernel Based Stratification of Breast Cancer Patients
papers.abstract: The integration of mechanistic signaling networks into clinical research has become a cornerstone of precision oncology. By capturing the complex biochemical interactions within a cell, these networks provide a functional map of disease progression that goes beyond simple genomic mutations. Consequently, the development of specific signaling models of patients has significant relevance, allowing for a more granular representation of individual disease profiles. In this setting, there is a growing need for robust methodologies capable of comparing graph based pathway structures to identify similarities and differences across patient cohorts. Such comparisons are essential for the identification of clinically meaningful subgroups, and the discovery of novel biomarkers. Standard graph kernels, while mathematically rigorous, often remain too generic for this purpose. They frequently fail to capture features specific to gene signaling networks, resulting in suboptimal clustering performance. In this paper, we present a domain specific graph kernel designed for mechanistic signaling networks. Unlike generic approaches, our method explicitly incorporates biological constraints and gene interaction patterns into the kernel formulation, enabling a more accurate characterization of both topological structure and functional behavior. We assess its performance on breast cancer datasets, focusing on its ability to support disease subtyping. Our results suggest that our approach can effectively contribute to patient stratification.

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. In the Szeg\H{o} setting, local rigidity was established by Lu--Tian (2004) on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and, more recently, by Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026) on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces.

papers.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a formula for the Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple determination of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even degree cohomology. This is then applied to the study of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we analyse the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,q}$ as well as ample divisor complements in orbifold K3 surfaces and Calabi-Yau threefolds, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
papers.abstract: Variability in syntactic structure and parsing ambiguity are fundamental aspects of natural language which modern LLMs have to learn to deal with proficiently. Previous "post-mortem" studies have shown that fully trained Transformers indeed approximate canonical parsing algorithms such as inside-outside, but little is established theoretically about how this is actually learned. Here, we make a first step towards addressing this by studying the learning dynamics in synthetic context-free grammars with variable parse tree topology. The stagewise learning curves are fully interpretable, in the sense that all of the loss stages a) can be computed analytically, and b) can be clearly associated to the representation of a hidden latent tree variable, which allows to lift ambiguity and utilize information from wider contexts. By probing representations, we visualize the emergence of inside-outside computation across depth and during training: while during early stages local (bigram/trigram) information is used and involves only a few initial layers, gradually the Transformer develops an encoder-decoder structure where the most abstract latent information is encoded in the middle, and the latter half of the network is used to progressively refine the final token prediction. This organization of computation is reminiscent of findings in real-world LLMs, and importantly applies here to a synthetic model which allows full analytical control of the data statistics, thus opening the door to theoretical progress.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Properties of the S=1/2 Zigzag Spin Ladder
papers.abstract: We investigate finite-temperature properties of the spin-1/2 zigzag Heisenberg ladder with an anisotropic off-diagonal $\Gamma$ interaction. Thermal states are calculated by an infinite time-evolving block decimation method combined with purification, while exact diagonalization is used to analyze low-lying excitations. The entropy is strongly suppressed at low temperatures inside the gapped phases, whereas it remains enhanced near several ground-state phase boundaries. For the N\'eel phase at $J_2/J_1=0$, the model can be mapped by spin rotations onto the exactly solvable XYZ chain. The thermal gap extracted from the low-temperature specific heat agrees with the exact one-spinon gap, while the finite-size excitation gap obtained by exact diagonalization is consistent with a two-spinon excitation.

papers.title: The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
papers.abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. We also prove that the intersection of two Grothendieck noncommutative $\cM$-bimodules is also Grothendieck. These answer several open problems in the literature.

papers.title: Quasisymmetry of self-similar carpets
papers.abstract: We classify self-similar carpets obtained by repeating a fixed pattern in the same orientation on a square grid. All boundary cells are retained. The first approximation has a nonempty family of Jordan polyomino holes with pairwise disjoint closures in the interior of the unit square. Every quasisymmetry between two such carpets is the restriction of a square symmetry. Thus quasisymmetric, bi-Lipschitz, and isometric equivalence coincide. Two patterns give equivalent carpets exactly when their subdivision parameters have a common positive power and their retained cells agree up to symmetry on the common grid. The criterion extends to patterns periodic from the first generation. We also construct an area-zero square carpet with uniformly relatively separated peripheral circles and a quasisymmetric involution that sends a corner into an open side. Its quasisymmetry group is dihedral of order eight, and its isometries are the four rotations. It belongs to the quasisymmetric class of the standard middle-third carpet and to a different isometry class.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,\alpha}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,\alpha}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: Species sampling priors through exact augmentation
papers.abstract: Discrete random probability measures are central to Bayesian nonparametric modeling. In practice, their use often favors a few tractable priors with full weak support. Full support alone, however, does not specify how prior mass reflects beliefs about clustering, recurrence, discovery and other sample features. We develop a novel and general construction of species sampling process (SSP) priors from an index distribution and finite allocation probabilities, linked to these sample characteristics. Every proper SSP admits an exact two-stage representation through an almost surely finite index and a finite conditional measure. Averaging over the index recovers each realized SSP on every measurable set. Reversing this identity constructs priors whose tie probabilities, expected occupancy and discovery rates can be assessed without evaluating the infinite weights. We characterize compatibility among index laws, schedules and weights, and construct light-tailed, heavy-tailed and multimodal families with full weak support under suitable hyperpriors. A prior with paired weights combines full weak support with invariance under size-biased permutation in its defining order, an explicit finite index law and partition prediction. Exact simulation, recursive reweighting and finite posterior augmentation follow. Examples distinguish prior elicitation, exact averaging and fixed-level approximation.

papers.title: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text
papers.abstract: We study AI-assisted measurement when one text label applies to many administrative records, the target is a monetary total, and the human readings that anchor the machines disagree. The testbed is 121,070 grant-purpose texts from US tax filings (799,675 records, $126.4B), labelled by a rule-based classifier and three language models, with a designed sample of 651 texts read independently by three people under one codebook, who then adjudicated the 152 texts they split on. We state exact conditions for a fixed-predictor difference estimator and for a cross-fitted predictor whose folds are assigned to the whole frame independently of the sample, under Poisson sampling, and assess the implemented fixed-size procedures by simulation: 8 predictors whose own totals span $12.5-15.0B agree to within $0.4B once rectified. Two rules that accept machine labels at a stated dollar-weighted error, weighted conformal p-values under a dollar measure and Learn-then-Test on the design estimate of the error, are evaluated on nested held-out folds and on design re-draws with synthetic truths; their error control in deployment is not established, and the count-based rule accepts no text under a dollar-drawn sample. In a replay that counts every reference label a policy queries, pilot included (not the readings behind it), a two-phase review policy whose calibrator is fitted on its own first phase reduces the RMSE of the total by 42% at 100 queries relative to dollar-proportional sampling, while pure Neyman allocation fails with an uncalibrated predictor. Independent readers shift the estimated total by $3.93B, 2.7 times the sampling interval; the adjudicated reading puts it at $13.49B; institution-level intervals under-cover at every size. Reference-dependent results are re-run under each reader. The results identify benefits and limits of using learned predictions to decide what a person should verify.

papers.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cveti\v{c}-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-St\"ackel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.

papers.title: Dynamics of R\'enyi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
papers.abstract: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on R\'enyi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for R\'enyi-2. Focusing on R\'enyi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ans\"atze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica. In the limit of large subsystems, these functions exhibit a striking structural simplification: locality of the dynamics together with bulk spectral dephasing reduce their functional dependence to a single fundamental frequency. Our formalism provides a setting where ETH-like statements naturally coexist for both arbitrarily small and large subsystem sizes. We discuss extensions of our results to higher R\'enyi entropies. Beyond clarifying the spectral foundations of entanglement dynamics, these results lay some of the groundwork for future applications of spectral filter methods to the computation of R\'enyi evolution in deterministic systems.

papers.title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory
papers.abstract: Local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare and stabilize entangled many-body states. In frustration-free control, the target manifold is fixed by local constraints, whose violations are detected by measurement and removed by feedback. We develop an exact theory of this mechanism for Dicke states of $N_q$ qubits, which span the permutation-symmetric subspace with one Dicke state per magnetization sector. Local singlet projectors define the constraints and detect departures from permutation symmetry. The dynamics closes exactly on the span of the $N_q(N_q-1)/2$ singlet-pair projectors and maps onto a classical first-passage process: measurements move the pair endpoints, while feedback absorbs pairs on measured bonds. The closure reduces the exponentially large many-body Liouvillian to a generator of polynomial size, fully quantifying the preparation process. In one dimension we solve it in closed form. Its slowest rate, $\Lambda_{\rm pair}=2[1-\cos(\pi/N_q)]$ in units of the measurement rate, is the full Liouvillian gap. For any such scheme, the relaxation time is bounded below by the inverse fraction of pair configurations on which feedback acts; local feedback reaches $O(N_q)$ of $O(N_q^2)$ configurations and thus needs a time at least linear in $N_q$. A second exact closure gives the final state for any initial condition. Extensions to modified transport, restricted feedback, and physical errors yield an exact transport-to-absorber crossover, geometric preparation laws, and a bound on the stationary leakage. An exact second-moment closure determines the ensemble fluctuations: measurement noise is conserving, while feedback generates the shot noise of removal and correlations between pairs. Preparation, acceleration, robustness, and fluctuations are thus all governed by one exactly solvable process: the transport and absorption of local constraint violations.

papers.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

papers.title: Attainable and unattainable gauge-dependent quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the gauge dependence of quantum precision in ultrastrongly coupled light--matter systems. The unitary between gauges carries the coupling $g$, so each truncation defines a different family. The quantum Fisher information traces an exact parabola across frames. Harmonic matter minimizes it at a universal $\theta_\ast=\Omega/(\Omega+\omega)$, set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound is attainable. Frames differ by a factor $9.6$ with opposite trends. Diverging virtual-excitation gain at the Dicke point is a gauge artifact and saturates.

papers.title: Ricci pseudo symmetric Anisotropic Fluid Spacetime admitting Hyperbolic solitons with Ricci vector field
papers.abstract: This work focuses on an anisotropic fluid spacetime with these unique forms of the stress-energy tensor associated with radial pressure and a transverse pressure p. In an anisotropic fluid spacetime , we mani- fest curvatures symmetry such as Ricci pseudo-symmetric and prove that Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime is generalized quasi- Einstein spacetime. We deduce the Einstein gravitational field equation of Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime. In the framework of pseudo-Riemannian geometry, specifically, we study the quasi-conformal Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime, which exhibit the dark matter era. Moreover, we discuss the hyperbolic Ricci soliton and Hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field. Finally, we turn up the char- acteristics of hyperbolic Ricci soliton and hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field.

papers.title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
papers.abstract: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.

papers.title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
papers.abstract: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR instrument aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM for elevation matching. We ask whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Additionally fusing a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source substantially improved the accuracy. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single offset per ground track, then point by point. For most tracks, the per-track corrections nearly agreed with those from the airborne LiDAR DTM. Point-by-point corrections, however, did not agree. This was because the error of the generated DTM was close to the elevation differences that point-by-point correction must resolve, and most of this error lay at scales that even a 10 m-resolution DTM can represent. Under similar conditions, a super-resolved DTM may be usable in place of a 1 m-resolution DTM for per-track correction, but improving the accuracy, or using it for point-by-point correction as well, requires reducing the error at these scales rather than reproducing fine relief.

papers.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
papers.abstract: We develop a unified virtual element framework for compatible polytopal discretizations of differential forms in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. On general polytopal meshes, a central challenge is to construct de Rham subcomplexes and establish stability estimates with mesh-independent constants. We construct a trimmed complex of conforming virtual differential forms recursively from local Hodge--Laplace boundary value problems and obtain a complete subcomplex by imposing additional moment constraints. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom from which polynomial projections can be computed. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and each virtual complex has cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual complexes and in every form degree, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and thereby prove a mesh-uniform equivalence between the $L^2$ norm and the scaled degree-of-freedom norm. Through the cochain isomorphisms induced by the degrees of freedom, these norm equivalences yield uniformly bounded liftings of fully discrete data into the corresponding continuous spaces, in particular for the Discrete de Rham method. We also derive canonical interpolation error estimates and discrete Poincar\'e inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge--Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity.

papers.title: Theory of Optical and Magneto-Optical Properties of [111]-Oriented Site-Controlled Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: Site-controlled [111]-oriented quantum dots (QDs) are promising sources of non-classical light, yet their optical spectra exhibit apparently conflicting symmetry signatures. At zero magnetic field, excitonic spectra are commonly interpreted as $C_{2v}$-like, whereas measurements in Faraday geometry display selection rules characteristic of $C_{3v}$-like symmetry. Here, we show that both regimes can be described consistently without invoking any change in the underlying structural symmetry. Combining 8-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ theory, a self-consistent Hartree-informed configuration interaction scheme, and group theoretical analysis, we introduce a controlled symmetry reducing perturbation that lowers the QD symmetry to $C_s$. At zero field, the optical response remains predominantly $C_{2v}$-like because the additional low-symmetry transitions carry only weak oscillator strengths. In Faraday geometry, the same reduced-symmetry structure produces four dominant, nearly circularly polarised trion transitions, reproducing the experimentally observed $C_{3v}$-like response. By contrast, an exact $C_{2v}$ description inferred from the zero-field spectrum permits only two such trion transitions and therefore fails at finite field. Our results thus provide a unified description of the zero and finite magnetic field optical response without any restoration or enhancement of the underlying structural symmetry. More generally, we demonstrate that a higher-symmetry-like optical spectrum does not uniquely identify the exact symmetry of a QD, therefore also providing useful guidance for other QD and nanostructure systems that lie beyond the ones studied here.

papers.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
papers.abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2<1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions. We also show that the asymptotic variance for the Schwarzian derivative is at least $5.68\ldots$, which defeats the hypothesis that the Nehari criterion would be almost sharp.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

papers.title: Native vacancies and antisites in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
papers.abstract: Manganese selenide grows both as rock-salt $\alpha$-MnSe, a type-II antiferromagnet, and as metastable wurtzite w-MnSe, an antiferromagnet whose type of order is not known. In DFT+$U$, a spin-degenerate stripe order of w-MnSe lies 14 meV per formula unit below the A-type order, which is predicted to be altermagnetic. We compute the neutral Mn and Se vacancies and the two antisites of both polymorphs with a linear-response Hubbard $U$, between the Se-rich limit bounded by MnSe$_2$ and the Mn-rich limit set by the measured formation enthalpy. In $\alpha$-MnSe the Mn vacancy is lowest over most of the window (0.92 eV under Se-rich conditions), a candidate acceptor for its p-type conduction. In w-MnSe the Se antisite is lowest under Se-rich conditions, narrowly in the A-type order and, by an estimate, more clearly in the stripe order, and the Se vacancy under Mn-rich conditions. Changing the order shifts the formation energies by up to 0.26 eV, most for the Mn vacancy. Only the Se vacancy has nearly the same formation energy in both polymorphs; the other defects differ by 0.4-1.1 eV, although DFT+$U$ places wurtzite below rock salt, contrary to experiment. Three of the four defects leave an uncompensated moment of 3-5 $\mu_\mathrm{B}$. In the A-type order, band unfolding shows that the sign-reversing splitting of the most strongly split valence band, about 230 meV and 3 eV below the valence-band maximum (band-edge states are not resolved), changes its peak height by less than 8%, the resolution of the analysis, at 3% defects, while elsewhere the curve deviates by 18-45 meV (rms).

papers.title: Universality in Quantum Many-Body Spin Ratchets
papers.abstract: We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. This setup breaks parity symmetry and exhibits chiral transport. It has been shown that the drift velocity in the case of integrable, SU(2)-symmetric quantum spin ratchets is universal, and conjectured that the same holds in the non-integrable case. Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.

papers.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty II
papers.abstract: Building on our earlier work, we present an $L^2$-$L^1$ inequality for radial Fourier eigenfunctions, relating this to the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane. We also propose a generalisation of the aforementioned uncertainty principle, and draw a connection with entropic uncertainty.

papers.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
papers.abstract: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

papers.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
papers.abstract: We study the Jacobians of a genus-two family with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We realize these abelian surfaces as factors of cyclic-cover Jacobians and determine their integral rank-two monodromy. For the real embedding with $\sqrt5>0$, the projective image is the Hecke group $\Delta(2,5,\infty)$; the conjugate real image is nondiscrete. After a finite base change, we give an explicit degree-four map from Cohen--Wolfart's Hecke cyclic curve to the genus-two curve. Four deck translates of the induced Jacobian pullback give an integral isomorphism from the fourth power of the surface to the eight-dimensional primitive order-$20$ factor, with an explicit nonproduct polarization. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ torsion-line covers are normalizations of quadratic fibre products of genus-one triangular modular curves. We also describe the associated split and nonsplit Cartan-normalizer covers. Finite-field hypergeometric traces give the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation with a twist by the quadratic character of $2$.

papers.title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set. As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero. An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.

papers.title: A true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
papers.abstract: We give a true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehat{\phi}$ denotes its interpretation on $\omega$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehat{\phi}$ is a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.

papers.title: A High Precision Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
papers.abstract: We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts 512 quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1620,160]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ time-domain waveforms with exact parameter and temporal derivatives via automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained jointly on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 109 SXS evaluation waveforms (106 physical systems) over $[-1500,100]M$, it achieves a mean balanced relative strain error of 0.0305 and a mean finite-window detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of 0.1536%, outperforming SEOBNRv5PHM, NRSur7dq4v2, and IMRPhenomTPHM across common support, with compiled batched float64 inference reaching 445 waveforms/s on an A100 GPU.

papers.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

papers.title: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference
papers.abstract: Tensor network (TN) kernel machines speed up supervised learning by using low-rank TNs to reduce computation and memory. Most of these methods, however, are deterministic: they ignore parameter uncertainty, and their model complexity has to be tuned manually. Bayesian TN kernel machines remove both limitations, but only for the CANDECOMP/PARAFAC decomposition (CPD), which has a single rank. For the more general tensor train (TT), manual tuning is even more costly, since every one of its ranks must be chosen. In this paper we propose Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines (BTT-KM), which place hierarchical ARD-type priors on the TT cores and infer all TT ranks and feature dimensions from data. Mean-field variational inference leads to a Bayesian alternating least squares algorithm with the same computational complexity as its deterministic counterpart, and gives a closed-form predictive distribution. On synthetic data, BTT-KM shrinks an over-parameterized initialization to a low-rank model close to the ground truth, and on UCI benchmarks it is competitive with state-of-the-art methods, with predictive coverage closest to the nominal value.

papers.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
papers.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

papers.title: The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
papers.abstract: In one dimension, the symmetric binomial tree replicates quadratic payoffs using the Delta of its own price function. For every $d\geq 2$ and every centered, isotropic, minimally complete $(d+1)$-state model with $d$ risky assets, by contrast, some quadratic payoff requires a replicating hedge different from that Delta. In this nonredundant finite-state setting, centered one-step payoffs are spanned by the $d$ asset innovations; centered second-order (Gamma) contributions are therefore represented as first-order trading gains, potentially inducing additional asset holdings. We call this effect Gamma-to-Delta aliasing and measure it by the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)=\mathbb{E}[(\xi^\top H\xi-\operatorname{tr}H)\xi]$, where $\xi$ is the normalized one-step innovation and $H$ the Gamma matrix. For quadratic claims the replicating holding exceeds the price Delta by exactly $\sqrt{h}\,\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)/2$, where $h$ is the time step. Trading this holding in a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)|^2/4$, a fixed multiple of the ordinary discrete-Delta error that does not vanish in relative terms as $h\downarrow0$. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete models is $\sqrt{d-1}$, so the worst-case relative excess variance is $(d-1)/2$; both are attained uniquely by the equal-probability regular simplex. For unit-Frobenius positive-semidefinite Gammas and for unit rank-one Gammas, the sharp minimax value is $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also show how aliasing trades off against unhedgeable quadratic risk when more states are allowed, and derive the leading implementation cost for smooth claims.

papers.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
papers.abstract: $XV$ ($X$ is Si, Ge, Sn, or Pb, and $V$ is the carbon vacancy) color centers are promising platforms for quantum computing and quantum information science due to their favorable optical and spin properties. They are commonly fabricated by ion implantation, which inevitably introduces vacancies and carbon self-interstitials (C$_i$) into the lattice. However, the microscopic formation mechanism remains unclear, limiting the yield and stability of $XV$ centers. Here, first-principles calculations are conducted to systematically investigate the roles of $V$ and C$_i$ in $XV$ formation. We find that $XV$ formation is energetically favorable, with large binding energies and low diffusion barriers. Nevertheless, $XV$ readily captures C$_i$ to form substitutional defect $X_s$, or captures an additional $V$ to form the complex $XV_2$. Charge transition levels show that oppositely charged reactants never meet in these reactions, and that Coulomb repulsion blocks them only when both reactants carry charges of the same sign, which for the capture of C$_i$ requires strongly n- or p-type conditions. These competing defect reactions destabilize the split-vacancy configuration and could account for the low formation yield of $XV$ centers, so that they appear at concentrations well below those expected from the implanted dose. Our results elucidate the microscopic origin of this intrinsic instability and suggest that Fermi-level control may suppress defect conversions and stabilize the split-vacancy configuration.

papers.title: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.abstract: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

papers.title: Fluctuating resource availability stabilizes coexistence beyond the oscillatory tragedy of the commons
papers.abstract: Fluctuations in ambient conditions such as temperature and humidity can alter the effective availability of a shared resource at a given abundance. Standard evolutionary games with environmental feedback treat the payoff matrix as a deterministic function of resource abundance, leaving open how fluctuations in availability affect the oscillatory tragedy of the commons.
