Using noise-corrected replicator dynamics and individual-based birth-death simulations, we show that zero-mean fluctuations in resource availability can stabilize an interior equilibrium and suppress coupled strategy-resource oscillations. We derive an analytical criterion, in terms of the payoff structure and feedback dynamics, for when increasing noise favors local stability. These findings identify environmental variability as a mechanism that can promote strategy coexistence and help maintain shared resources in systems prone to recurrent depletion.

papers.title: Finite refutations in countably additive quantum probability
papers.abstract: We axiomatize countably additive quantum probability and prove a completeness theorem for finite refutation beyond compactness: inconsistency is witnessed by refutations each of whose branches ends in finitely many jointly unsatisfiable commitments. Adjoining the hypothesis that every event has a predetermined, context-independent outcome makes the theory inconsistent, although every finite subset of the resulting axioms has a model. For a countable theory of closed bounds on sentence values in our real-valued infinitary logic, inconsistency is equivalent to a winning strategy for a challenger in a game against a model builder. The challenger chooses each test in response to the builder's commitments, and the plays that follow a winning strategy form such a refutation. For the quantum theory with predetermined outcomes, every winning strategy must branch infinitely at some node. In the strategy we construct, countable additivity locates the four-dimensional subspace in which a finite Kochen-Specker parity argument applies. In their standard models, our axioms describe the closed subspaces and the density-operator probabilities of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. We prove in ZFC that the sets of probability values definable uniformly across standard models are exactly the $\sigma$-projective subsets of the unit interval.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\ge750$ satisfies the Borodin--Kostochka inequality $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta-1\}$, conjectured for all $\Delta\ge9$. Reed (1999) established the inequality for $\Delta\ge10^{14}$, and Liu, Sun, Wang and Zeng (2026) lowered the threshold to $5.3\times10^6$. To extend a random partial colouring over large cliques, we find repeated colours using adaptively chosen vertex-disjoint stars and apply Hall's theorem to the available colour lists. We verify the required probability bounds by rational and interval arithmetic with directed rounding.

papers.title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.

papers.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. This answers a question of M. Tkachenko (2014) and extends the separable case of the author's 1994 theorem on Tychonoff pseudocompact groups to regular spaces. The proof rests on a new result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is feebly compact and $Z$ is regular, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Previously this was known only when $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are Tychonoff. Using topological games of Banach-Mazur type, we extend the group theorem to regular separable Baire groups from a wider class of spaces, which contains all $p$-spaces, all feebly compact spaces and all products of a $p$-space with a feebly compact space. We also obtain local versions: the theorem holds for locally separable, locally feebly compact groups.

papers.title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
papers.abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.

papers.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $\sigma$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

papers.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
papers.abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.

papers.title: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.

papers.title: von Neumann-Morgenstern stable sets in job matching problems
papers.abstract: We show that a von Neumann-Morgenstern (vNM) stable set generically exists in the many-to-one job-matching model. Unlike the core, which can be empty in this model, a vNM stable set exists whenever there is a unique efficient matching: the set of all individually rational (IR) and efficient outcomes form a vNM stable set. If an economy has multiple efficient matchings, a vNM stable set may not exist. If the vNM stable sets are required to be rich in a certain sense, then such a rich vNM stable set exists if and only if the set of efficient matchings is essentially unique, and the set of all efficient and IR outcomes forms the unique rich vNM stable set.

papers.title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
papers.abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.0-2.6$\times$.

papers.title: Weak-coupling selection and finite-torus entropy in the triangular Ising antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: An antiferromagnetic second-neighbor interaction favors stripe order in the triangular-lattice Ising antiferromagnet, but uniform stripes cannot close when both primitive periods are odd. At each fixed odd size $L\geq5$, we minimize this interaction over the ground states of the zero-field nearest-neighbor model on an $L\times L$ torus. We prove a minimum total interface length of $4L$ and classify all $L^2(L^2-1)/2$ selected states. Under the uniform measure on these states, the area fractions of the three stripe orientations approach a uniform distribution over all nonnegative triples summing to one. Thus selection reduces an exponential degeneracy to polynomial growth, while the whole-sample orientation fractions remain broadly distributed. We also derive explicit two-sided entropy-density bounds for periodic spin ground states and honeycomb dimer coverings on $M\times N$ tori, where $M$ and $N$ are the periods along the two primitive lattice directions. For all $M,N\geq3$, the errors relative to the bulk residual entropy are bounded by explicit constants times $\min(M,N)^{-2}$, without an aspect-ratio restriction. These bounds give finite-size accuracy guarantees and control the exponentially small fraction of unperturbed ground states that survive the selection.

papers.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
papers.abstract: Predicting spin polarization and light attenuation in optically pumped atomic devices requires solving the coupled diffusive quantum master equation (DQME)--light system. Its nonlinearity, spatially nonlocal coupling, and physical admissibility constraints make high-fidelity numerical simulation challenging. We develop a structure-preserving high-fidelity solver that combines second-order finite differences for three-dimensional atomic diffusion, explicit pseudo-time marching for atomic populations, and an exponential integrator for light propagation. Under a derived time-step restriction, the solver preserves population normalization and nonnegativity, as well as the positivity and monotonic attenuation of the light intensity. Three complementary test cases based on an analytical reduction, asymptotic limits, and an analytical invariant are constructed to verify the solver. To accelerate repeated parameter queries, we eliminate the light field and construct a reduced-order model (ROM) using proper orthogonal decomposition and Galerkin projection of the resulting integro-differential formulation involving only atomic populations. An exact quadratic expansion of the spin-exchange term and discrete empirical interpolation of the optical-pumping term make the cost of evaluating the reduced operators independent of the full-order dimension. Numerical tests verify the solver and demonstrate ROM accuracy outside the training set. The GPU implementation completes simulations with millions of unknowns in minutes, while single-core ROM evaluations take seconds, achieving respective speedup factors exceeding 150 and 7000 relative to the single-core high-fidelity solver.

papers.title: Quantum manifestations of converse symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: Quantum synchronization holds promise in advancing quantum technologies such as sensing, communication, and computation. A key challenge in this rapidly developing field is to identify mechanisms that can promote the emergence of synchronous dynamics. Here, we show that quantum synchronization can be enhanced by introducing controlled heterogeneity in the form of coupling mismatches. Using spin van der Pol oscillators as a model system, we show that this mechanism constitutes a quantum analog of the phenomenon of converse symmetry breaking previously identified in classical oscillator networks, where a synchronous state is stabilized by explicit symmetry breaking. We quantify how quantum effects modify this behavior by tuning the degree of quantumness through variations of the spin quantum number. These findings suggest that quantum synchronization can be enhanced in experiments by harnessing rather than suppressing heterogeneity.

papers.title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
papers.abstract: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.

papers.title: Thin-shell wormholes from magnetic black holes in exponential electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Transparent magnetic wormholes can share a black hole exterior while their supporting matter controls the response of the throat. We construct symmetric thin shells from the magnetic black hole of exponential nonlinear electrodynamics and derive their equilibrium stresses and linear radial stability criterion. Restricting the seed to its zero-bare-mass magnetic branch ties the charge and coupling along the fixed-mass family. In the sampled configurations, calibrated linear barotropic shells are unstable, whereas variable phantom and variable Chaplygin laws admit locally stable radial sectors. Explicit radius dependence strengthens the phantom restoring term; the Chaplygin response cancels the divergent inverse lapse contribution and permits stable sectors close to a non-extremal seed horizon. The surface density remains negative, although an inner interval satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. At the seed photon sphere, the two variable laws share an exact stabilization threshold. The complete radial averaged null energy remains negative even when the proper shell energy tends to zero. Numerical null geodesic imaging uses independent, minimally coupled light and transparent junctions, with celestial sources and rotating thin disks truncated at the ISCO. For observer-side disk emission with the prescribed ISCO truncation and a throat below the seed photon sphere, inclined images coincide with the seed black hole image. A throat above that sphere removes selected returning contributions while preserving much of the bright primary structure. Illuminating the opposite exterior adds inner disk arcs, but a central dark region can survive because the disk does not illuminate every transmitted direction. The resulting image degeneracy depends jointly on the retained null trajectories and the emitting support, rather than on the presence of a horizon alone.

papers.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Koll\'ar and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.

papers.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
papers.abstract: How quickly can we construct the martingale with prescribed initial and terminal laws that is closest to Brownian motion in the sense of the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem? The construction requires the initial law of an auxiliary Brownian motion. One can take this law to be the distribution of a minimizer of the lifted Bass functional. In dimension one, Backhoff, Pammer and Schachermayer proved, under additional assumptions, that the gradient flow of this functional converges exponentially to a minimizer. We extend this result to arbitrary dimension. Under the assumptions of the paper, the gradient flow starting from a bounded random vector converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the minimizer with the same mean. We prove this by showing that, for a fixed random vector $X$ with the prescribed initial law, the lifted Bass functional is strongly convex on each set of $\sigma(X)$-measurable vectors with a prescribed mean and a common $L^\infty$ bound.

papers.title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB~20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
papers.abstract: We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}_\mathrm{host}$). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of $\sigma_\mathrm{RM}\simeq3.5$ rad m$^{-2}$. This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magnetoionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.

papers.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate right and left matrix Riemann--Hilbert problems and derive parametric formulas for reconstructing both components. These formulas also use a transported profile determined by the initial ratio of the two momenta. Under suitable regularity and positivity assumptions, we show that a solution of the right Riemann--Hilbert problem, together with this profile, yields a local solution of the 2-mCH system. For a common constant background, we construct a family of smooth reflectionless solutions associated with a single pair of discrete eigenvalues. The scalar soliton, obtained when the profile vanishes, is the only travelling wave in this family.

papers.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.

papers.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
papers.abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

papers.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-\'etale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This settles a case left open by Manin's construction. We also obtain unirationality results for Du Val del Pezzo surfaces of degrees $1$ and $2$, and discuss applications to the Hilbert property, equivariant unirationality, and the real plane Cremona group.

papers.title: Mean Field Games of Optimal Trading with an SPDE Model of the Limit Order Book
papers.abstract: We develop a mean field game (MFG) model for optimal trading in which the interaction among traders is mediated by the dynamics of the limit order book. The bid- and ask-side order densities are modeled as stochastic processes taking values in infinite-dimensional function spaces, and solve semilinear stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) with stochastic, time-varying order submission rates and multiplicative infinite-dimensional noise. This extends an existing limit order book framework to capture the aggregate impact of strategic traders executing market orders on the order densities. In this way, trading activity affects the order densities, which determine the market depths near the best quotes and hence the mid-price, and the mid-price, in turn, affects the traders' decisions. We establish the well-posedness and regularity of the resulting density-price system and use it to formulate an $N$-player optimal trading game in which the traders' market orders enter the book through their aggregate order flow. We then study the corresponding MFG, which involves semilinear SPDEs driven by common noise processes and a highly nonlinear stochastic differential equation (SDE) for the mid-price, as the number of traders tends to infinity. Under regular market conditions, we characterize the mean field (the limiting aggregate trading rate) as a fixed point of a nonlinear consistency condition, expressed as a forward-backward SPDE-SDE system, and prove its existence and uniqueness under suitable technical conditions. Finally, we show that the limiting optimal trading strategy induces an $\epsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with $\epsilon_N = O(N^{-1/2})$, and provide a numerical illustration of the mean field consistency equations.

papers.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Forecast Treatment Effects in Economics?
papers.abstract: I use LLMs to forecast treatment effects from pre-registrations and pre-analysis plans, evaluating forecasts against results released after the models' cut-off dates. The screened sample includes 1,459 questions from 36 papers. For the most recent time period and model, the median absolute error is 0.053 SD, the average absolute error is 0.098 SD, and the MSE is 0.021, falling to 0.015 after adjusting for sampling variance where standard errors are available. Forecasts substantially outperform benchmarks predicting zero or other papers' mean effects. These results suggest considerable scope for forecasts to inform policy and research.

papers.title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
papers.abstract: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $\chi$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $\chi L\leftrightarrow\bar\chi\Psi$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_\chi$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.

papers.title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
papers.abstract: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(\alpha'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.

papers.title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
papers.abstract: Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$. For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel. For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$. We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $\sigma Z$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $\sigma\ge0$. The large-$\sigma$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls. Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.

papers.title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$\nu$NS measurement
papers.abstract:
Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$
u$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$
u$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CE$
u$NS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV$_{ee}$. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on and 86 kg$\cdot$days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields $N_s = 1565 \pm 155$ CE$
u$NS events and a relative precision of 9.9\%. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events, with $N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.92 \pm 0.14$.

papers.title: Precision measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at a nuclear reactor by CONUS+
papers.abstract: We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) from reactor antineutrinos, using the CONUS+ germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields a signal with high statistical significance, corresponding to $1565 \pm 155$ CE$\nu$NS events, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events within 0.5 $\sigma$. The flux-averaged cross section is $(0.57 \pm 0.09)\times10^{-40}$ cm$^{2}$, and the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV is $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.226 \pm 0.022$.

papers.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
papers.abstract: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity (1.625 m/s^2) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

papers.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

papers.title: Doubly robust estimation of direct and spillover effects using multiple pre-treatment periods
papers.abstract: Under interference, the treatment of some units affects the outcomes of others, so that the effect on a treated unit consists of a direct and a spillover component. A non-treated comparison group then generally identifies neither component, but the difference between the total effect on the treated and the spillover effect on the comparison units. Under certain identifying assumptions, both components may be identified separately when multiple pre-treatment periods are available, even in the absence of an uncontaminated comparison group. Under a no-anticipation assumption, pre-treatment outcomes are free of both components for every unit. Extrapolating the pre-treatment trend within a group, as in interrupted time-series approaches, therefore identifies the counterfactual outcome in the absence of any treatment, provided that the model used for the extrapolation is correctly specified. Applied to the treated it gives the total effect on them, applied to the non-treated at a given level of exposure the spillover effect on them. Disentangling the two components in addition requires effect homogeneity across treated and non-treated units with the same exposure and covariates, as well as common support in exposure. We derive doubly robust and Neyman-orthogonal expressions for the effects of interest, which permits controlling for possibly high-dimensional covariates by machine learning. A simulation study confirms the root-$n$ consistent behaviour of the estimators and the reliability of the standard errors under specific regularity conditions. We apply the framework to the compulsory licensing of enemy-owned patents in the United States in 1919. Licensing raised patenting in the licensed subclasses and in technologically close ones alike, so that a comparison-group design understates the total effect.

papers.title: Time-Varying Quantile VAR Models: Estimation and Inference
papers.abstract: We develop an econometric framework for impulse response analysis in time-varying quantile vector autoregressive (TV-QVAR) models. Unlike standard conditional-mean setting, TV-QVAR systems face a fundamental analytical challenge: neither time-varying parameters nor conditional quantiles propagate linearly through dynamic recursions. To overcome this, we establish a uniform Bahadur representation for local quantile VAR estimation, propose a smoothed check-function approach for tractable parameter inference, and introduce the best linear projection of the time-varying quantile impulse response (TV-QIR) function to recover well-defined dynamic causal effects. Applying our methodology to U.S. industrial production growth and credit spreads from 1919 to 2025 uncovers pronounced structural shifts in tail interdependence, showing that downside asymmetry is concentrated at short horizons and diminishes as the forecast horizon lengthens.

papers.title: Bias Correction and Inference for Panel Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: We develop a large-$n$, large-$T$ theory for the unsmoothed fixed-effects quantile regression estimator that allows for serially correlated panel data. An exact rank-score identity for the profiled criterion, with a convexity argument, delivers the leading incidental parameter bias of the slope estimator, of order $T^{-1}$, in closed form, paralleling Hahn and Newey (2004) for smooth nonlinear panel models. When $n$ and $T$ grow at the same rate, the estimator is asymptotically normal but in general not centred, and conventional intervals are invalid. In stationary panels whose dependence decays geometrically or polynomially, with $n/T$ bounded, serial correlation changes the structure of this bias: the long-run variance of the quantile score enters it, and feedback from past errors to current regressors adds a term that can bias the estimator even at the median. A split-panel jackknife with contiguous half-panels removes the bias, whereas one with interleaved half-panels does not in general, and a cluster-robust variance estimator, clustered by individual, yields valid inference. Under independence over time, the admissible growth of $n$ relative to $T$, up to $n=o(T^3)$, depends on the regularity of the conditional error densities, and the jackknife is valid throughout this range.

papers.title: Covariant density functional from relativistic Brueckner theory with Chebyshev-expanded couplings
papers.abstract: We construct a density-dependent covariant energy density functional (CE-ME1) from full-Dirac-space relativistic Brueckner--Hartree--Fock (RBHF) self-energies and the corresponding equation of state. The space-like component of the vector self-energy is accounted for at the Fermi surface through reduced scalar and time-like self-energies, which are mapped onto local Hartree $\sigma$, $\omega$, $\delta$, and $\rho$ channels. The density-dependent couplings are represented by cubic Chebyshev polynomials over the density range $0.08\leq\rho\leq0.48~{\rm fm}^{-3}$. A constrained energy-and-saturation calibration uses 199 RBHF energy-per-particle values from published microscopic computations at six isospin asymmetries, while maintaining positive, monotonic couplings. The Bonn-A RBHF saturation point, incompressibility $K_\infty=258$ MeV, symmetry energy $J=33.1$ MeV, and slope $L=65.2$ MeV are reproduced. The predicted curvature $K_{\rm sym}=33$ MeV differs from the published RBHF value of $-67$ MeV, illustrating the derivative sensitivity of the local reduction. The combined energy RMS is $0.613$ MeV, measuring model discrepancy rather than statistical uncertainty. Uniform matter remains mechanically stable and causal above saturation within the calibrated range. In cold charge-neutral $npe\mu$ matter, CE-ME1 reasonably reproduces the interpolated RBHF pressure and proton fraction over most of the interval, although the pressure discrepancy increases near its upper edge. The DD-ME2 benchmark is stiffer and predicts a lower proton fraction at high density.

papers.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
papers.abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

papers.title: BPS Chaos and Fortuity in Higgs Branches I: The Gepner Point
papers.abstract: The BPS states in Calabi-Yau compactifications of type II string theory can sometimes be described using quiver quantum mechanics whose Higgs branch is a complete intersection manifold. Their degeneracy resembles that of BPS black holes. A small fraction of these states corresponds to multi-center supergravity brane configurations and can be continued to the (near-Higgs) Coulomb branch. We identify them as monotone states. The overwhelming majority of states, known as pure-Higgs states, are fortuitous states, which concentrate at a particular $R$-charge. This division has a precise mathematical meaning as two different types of cohomologies of the Higgs branch target space. We argue that a natural probe of BPS chaos in these models is the Berry/Chern curvature. In the case of the Gepner model, we use localization techniques in an auxiliary two-dimensional CFT to compute the curvature, its RMT properties, and deviations from it.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
papers.abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed to infer a global average with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. Because the configuration is a single draw from equilibrium, a floor $R_n$ remains, and no relative tolerance below $\kappa\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$. Before equilibrium, a certificate built on the displacement loses sight after about $\frac n4\ln m$ steps, half as long as the count of fixed cards in the same sample. At the two-dimensional Ising critical point the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$, with mean-field limit $\sqrt2-1$. For correlated fields, the usual 95\% interval can cover the ensemble mean in only 7\% of cases, and no bound on the floor from one realisation holds under stationarity alone.

papers.title: Quantile Regression Postprocessing with Negative Electricity Price Forecasts
papers.abstract: Negative electricity prices create market-relevant risks for trading, bidding, renewable revenues, and flexibility valuation. Quantile regression-based postprocessing is a widely used approach for converting point forecasts into predictive distributions. We show that the standard specification, which imposes a single linear relationship between the point forecast and predictive quantiles, can become structurally incoherent when the conditioning point forecast is negative. In such cases, the resulting predictive distribution may exhibit not only ordinary quantile crossing, where adjacent quantiles are in the wrong order, but also a severe version of crossing, which we refer to as tail-quantile inversion. This can reverse downside and upside risk signals. To address this problem, we propose sign-dependent QR-based postprocessing specifications that allow the quantile function to differ between positive and negative point forecasts. Using German day-ahead electricity prices as the main empirical setting, we show that these specifications improve predictive accuracy, particularly for negative point forecasts and extreme probability levels. When combined with joint estimation across quantiles, they eliminate quantile crossing and tail-quantile inversion. A robustness analysis for the U.S. SPP market confirms the main coherence results, although the gains in predictive accuracy are less pronounced. We demonstrate the economic relevance of the forecasts using a battery arbitrage strategy, where probabilistic forecasts improve trading performance relative to a point-forecast benchmark and the sign-dependent specifications can provide additional gains. The results demonstrate that the sign of the point forecast should be explicitly accounted for when constructing probabilistic forecasts in markets where negative prices can occur.

papers.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $\sigma$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,\sigma)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action $\alpha$ satisfies that $\overline{\alpha(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,\sigma)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $\alpha$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $\alpha:G\curvearrowright (D,\sigma)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action with $\overline{\alpha(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

papers.title: Distribution-free predictive inference with instrumental variables
papers.abstract: We study the problem of predictive inference with outcomes missing not at random, when instrumental variables are available. While conformal prediction and weighted conformal prediction provide valid distribution-free inference when outcomes are missing completely at random and missing at random, respectively, inference is generally not possible without additional assumptions when outcomes are missing not at random. In this work, we consider a setting where we remain within the distribution-free framework but instead have access to an instrumental variable (IV). We explore the theoretical possibility of IV predictive inference and establish that it is characterized by a parameter that we refer to as the identification index. We derive an impossibility result for the case where the identification index is not sufficiently large, showing that any distribution-free approach fails to provide informative inference in this case. For the case where the identification index is sufficiently large, we introduce a practical method that achieves informative predictive inference. Our method leverages modern semiparametric efficiency theory which involves deriving the efficient influence function of the identifying functional for sharp IV bounds of the quantiles of the missing outcome, delivering a double robustness property in the coverage guarantee of the proposed framework for IV-based predictive inference. We illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed procedure through simulations and two real-data applications---FES wages and NHANES III self-reported heights.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
papers.abstract: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanovi\'c's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.

papers.title: Frangible prime gaps
papers.abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erd\H{o}s. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.74161, 2.79201]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

papers.title: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall
papers.abstract: An assistant that brings up memories unasked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption. This decision is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with store size N. On replays of LongMemEval, a similarity threshold tuned to 5% false alarms at N=8 reaches 84-100% at N=2048 across embedding models and cue types; LoCoMo and LLM judges show it too. We prove that a gate which thresholds the best of N independent irrelevant scores at false-alarm rate alpha works at a per-item false-positive rate of about -ln(1-alpha)/N, which pins its hit rate to the far left of the ROC and makes it regularly varying in N under regular variation. If the relevant memory is equally likely to be any of the N, whatever a gate reads and however it decides, at false-alarm rate alpha it hits at most alpha+sqrt(alpha(1-alpha)chi^2/N), with chi^2 the divergence between a relevant and an irrelevant memory, and with equal-variance binormal scores the best-score gate is optimal. At matched false alarms the deployed score recalls 14-26 points more than raw cosine. A cue-swap conformal gate, which ranks the current cue among other cues on the store, has a finite-sample false-alarm guarantee under exchangeability. With the user's unfiltered history as background it keeps false alarms at 3-6% on LongMemEval at the hit rate of a label-tuned threshold; on LoCoMo it overshoots or turns conservative depending on the source of its reference cues. In a chronological replay with the user's earlier messages as references, it fires on 5-8% of questions on stores without their answer and on 6-8% of session-opening turns, against 57% for the deployed gate at N=2048. A cross-encoder pays the same price, and on a prospective-memory benchmark similarity gates recall at most 9% of constraints at controlled false alarms. Code and data: https://github.com/RiverChenStillCompiling/price-of-scale

papers.title: The \(\mathcal A_\alpha\)-Spectral Tur\'an Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
papers.abstract: For integers $3\leq s\leq r$ and $0<\alpha<1$, we study the maximum spectral radius of the convex combination of the degree and adjacency tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graph. For $n\geq r$, every extremal graph is complete $r$-partite. For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly in $\alpha$, the only possible extremal graphs are $T_r(n)$ and $K_1\vee T_{r-1}(n-1)$. There is a unique parameter $\alpha_n$ at which both attain the maximum; the former is uniquely extremal below $\alpha_n$ and the latter above it. Writing $c=((r-1)/r)^{s-1}$, we show that $\alpha_n=c+(s-1)c/n+O_{r,s}(n^{-2})$. The limiting maximum after normalization by $n^{s-1}$ is $\binom{r-1}{s-1}\max\{r^{1-s},\alpha(r-1)^{1-s}\}$. A sharp row-quotient bound at $\alpha=c$ identifies the limiting part proportions; local comparisons then determine the exact integer part sizes.

papers.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
papers.abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.

papers.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
papers.abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we obtain its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1 n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for $F_o$-radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction and, for $1 n$ we use an anisotropic Morrey representation formula.

papers.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

papers.title: Fr\'echet Kriging for Metric Space-Valued Spatial Data
papers.abstract: Spatial prediction of non-Euclidean data, such as probability distributions, symmetric positive semidefinite matrices, and networks, arises in many modern applications. Such data are naturally modeled as elements of general metric spaces, where classical kriging methods that rely on vector space structure are no longer directly applicable. We introduce Fr\'echet kriging, a general framework for spatial prediction of metric space-valued data. Fr\'echet kriging replaces the weighted average in classical ordinary kriging with a weighted Fr\'echet mean, while the weights are determined by characterizing the spatial dependence structure through a generalized variogram. This construction allows the proposed method to preserve the intrinsic geometry of the response space without requiring an embedding into a linear space. We establish theoretical properties of the proposed predictor, including a surrogate optimality property and consistency under variogram misspecification. Simulation studies for univariate distributions and symmetric positive semidefinite matrices demonstrate favorable predictive performance compared with existing approaches. We further illustrate the practical utility of the proposed framework through applications to joint probability densities of daily minimum and maximum temperatures and inter-industry monetary flow networks.

papers.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $\mu$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$, then $\mu$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

papers.title: Pattern-dependent stability of binary exponential perturbations
papers.abstract: We study how the arrangement of binary frequency perturbations affects the stability of exponential systems on an interval of length one. For frequencies $\lambda_n=n+s_n\delta$, with $s_n\in\{-1,+1\}$, we represent synthesis in Fourier coordinates by a shifted-sinc operator $N_{\delta,s}$ and identify its Gram operator as $G_{\delta,s}=N_{\delta,s}^*N_{\delta,s}$. The optimal squared synthesis bounds are $1\pm\rho_{\delta,s}$, where $\rho_{\delta,s}=\|P_-T_{2\delta}P_+\|$ measures the interaction between the two sign classes. Using the finite-matrix representation of periodic perturbations, we prove that, for each fixed $0\leq\delta<1/2$, the minimum lower bound among $p$-periodic binary patterns converges to the worst binary lower bound as $p\to\infty$. At Kadec's critical amplitude $\delta=1/4$, the alternating pattern has a positive lower bound, whereas a step pattern reduces to a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has lower bound zero. Every fixed periodic pattern nevertheless remains a Riesz basis. We discuss the resulting periodic extremal questions and record a direct perturbation estimate giving explicit stability neighborhoods around stable reference patterns.

papers.title: CBTV: Colour Bean Tracking Velocimetry for Dense Granular Flows
papers.abstract: In a dense granular flow, a particle that moves more than about half the spacing between frames is easily confused with a neighbour, and so dense flows are recorded at high frame rates. We present Colour Bean Tracking Velocimetry (CBTV) for particles of a few distinct colours. CBTV first matches small groups of neighbours by position and colour. It then links the remaining particles by relaxation particle tracking velocimetry (PTV) among particles of the same colour, with a search radius set in each frame from the detections. CBTV was compared with ten published trackers on 15 simulated granular flows, with every tracker given the same detections and one global setting. At 2.8 to 13 diameters per frame, on four flows, CBTV keeps 0.595 of the links, against 0.338 for the best published tracker on each cell. It leads that tracker on every cell outside a rotating drum, where every method fails, and trails on none. CBTV was configured on these four flows with their ground truth in view. At steps 1 to 8, on 45 benchmark cases not used in its tuning, CBTV leads the best published tracker on 14 cases and ties on 31, with no deficit. This test is not fully out of sample, because one setting was fixed after a look at part of the benchmark. The ties lie at small displacements. On two unseen flows, a colour-gated relaxation variant built in this work kept more links than CBTV on average. All tests are simulated.

papers.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers under conditions on local mixing and local energy estimates. We verify these conditions for one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature and for finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.

papers.title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
papers.abstract: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. Generative models provide continuous latent representations, but their latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, creating a regime where the latent dimension $D$ exceeds the evaluation budget. We introduce SABLE, a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces with an isotropic distribution and limited budget. SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate for prediction and acquisition, treating higher-order structure as surrogate discrepancy. After $N$ observations, the slope update has dimension at most $N-1$, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most $N$ dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using an exploration schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. An efficient recompression scheme reduces information to $\mathcal O(M)$ pseudo-observations, bringing the overall time complexity per step to $\mathcal O(M^2D+M^3+D\log D)$ while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. Across synthetic benchmarks and latent-space optimisation tasks, SABLE achieves high sample efficiency and reduces decision time by several orders of magnitude at large budgets.

papers.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
papers.abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

papers.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
papers.abstract: We derive the primordial $\langle\zeta\zeta h\rangle$, $\langle\zeta hh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.

papers.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_{\chi})$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.

papers.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(\lambda,p)=\sup_{\|u\|_{H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)}\le1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\bigl(e^{4\pi u^2}-1-\lambda|u|^p\bigr)\,dx, \qquad p\ge2, \] Chen--Jiang--Lu--Zhu gave the first classification of attainment away from the thresholds across the full range of $p$. We prove attainment at both thresholds for $p=2$ and at the unique threshold for each $2 4$, we obtain the expansion \[ S(\lambda,p)=4\pi+\mathcal C_p\lambda^{-2/(p-4)} +D_p\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \qquad \lambda\to\infty. \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting problem at unit $L^2$ mass, and $D_p$ selects the limiting profiles. For fixed $\lambda$ above the quartic threshold $\lambda_*(4)$, we prove \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(\lambda,p)-4\pi\bigr) =2\log\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\lambda}<0, \] where $\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. An exact radial transformation extends these results to every planar norm.

papers.title: Production of the weakly bound $T_{cc}^+$ state combining the coalescence model with its mass spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the production of the doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc}^+$ within the coalescence model. The formation probability is evaluated with the Wigner distribution function. In contrast to previous studies, which usually adopt a Gaussian wave function, we obtain the molecular wave function by numerically solving the coupled-channel Schr\"odinger equation with the one-boson-exchange potential fitted to the mass spectrum of $T_{cc}^+$. The resulting wave function is the universal form of a weakly bound $S$-wave molecule in momentum space (a Yukawa-type exponential in coordinate space), dressed by the dipole form factor of the OBE interaction, and is thus more suitable for such a state. As the input of the coalescence model, we use the transverse-momentum distributions of the constituent $D$ and $D^*$ mesons fitted to the ALICE and LHCb data, and also generated by PYTHIA for comparison. We compute the transverse-momentum distributions of $T_{cc}^+$ in $pp$ and Pb-Pb collisions. The two collision systems differ in which part of the wave function is probed: for the extended Pb--Pb source the universal pure-Lorentzian form suffices, whereas for the compact $pp$ source the short-distance part of the wave function, captured by the dipole form factor, becomes relevant. These results provide a theoretical reference for future experimental measurements of $T_{cc}^+$.

papers.title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.

papers.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
papers.abstract: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $\xi$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $\xi$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.

papers.title: The Art of Toda Brackets: A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
papers.abstract: One of the fundamental aims of the present book is to provide a reference for the computation of unstable homotopy groups using methods developed by the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. The theory of Toda brackets is fundamental to the study of composition relations among homotopy classes. Appendix~A.3 brings together all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained primarily through Toda brackets, with explicit generators. Appendix~A.2 explains the conventions used to name the generators. The book presents calculations, with explicit generators, of the $2$-primary components of $\pi_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq28$ and all $n$, together with selected calculations in degree $29$; (two possible group structures remain for $\pi_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11))$). The odd-primary components in the range considered can be computed with little additional effort, essentially by consulting the relevant entries in existing tables. As a further check, we examine our result for $\pi_{23}(\mathit{SO}(9))$ using the unstable Adams spectral sequence.We also give some geometric applications.

papers.title: Optical appearance and radial stability of thin-shell wormholes in fractional-power magnetic electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes in fractional-power magnetic electrodynamics and relate optical appearance to local radial stability. Finite magnetic self-energy fixes the seed mass and links the charge to the nonlinear scale. Transparent disks illuminate both exteriors, and independent Maxwell rays reach a static observer. For the standard Born--Infeld magnetic subset, static emitters are compared with circular motion outside the innermost stable orbit and an inward plunge below it. The wormhole--black-hole intensity difference separates light transmitted from the opposite disk from emission removed by throat excision. The illuminated inner edge depends on the admitted disk crossings rather than the throat radius alone. Increasing charge contracts the critical curve in the sampled family. Motion suppresses the face-on intensities and produces an azimuthal brightness contrast at inclination. A broad outer shoulder arises from partial compensation between decreasing emissivity and increasing circular frequency weights, before the profiles recover a decaying weak-field tail. All nine prescribed throats satisfy a local radial stability test for a calibrated modified cosmic Chaplygin law describing an effective exotic layer.
