The rest comes from Noisy Gap Cycle, a problem of Assadi and Sundaresan: tell whether a graph is a union of cycles of length $k$ or $2k$. With long cycles it needs linear space in all four models: we extend their random-order lower bound to quantum algorithms and obtain the first quantum random-order lower bounds for natural graph problems. With short cycles, $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ classical bits suffice in random order, but adversarial order requires polynomial quantum space.

papers.title: Beyond ideal cavities: quantifying the impact of cavity dissipation on light-matter strong coupling
papers.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities promises to reshape molecular reactivity and properties in a non-invasive and tunable way, yet cavity experiments remain notoriously difficult to interpret and reproduce, highlighting the need for accurate theoretical predictions. Significant progress has been made through ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) methods, but these generally assume ideal, lossless cavity fields, an approximation commonly justified by the assumption that cavity losses are negligible and by the need to keep the methods computationally tractable. Here we show that this approximation is far from innocent: incorporating cavity dissipation through the experimentally accessible quality factor Q reduces the Rabi splitting of p-nitroaniline by more than 10% and red-shifts the minimum polaritonic gap by 0.24 eV, even when the system remains firmly in the strong-coupling regime. This implies that convergence towards the ideal-cavity limit requires quality factors substantially larger than those needed to establish strong coupling itself. Our approach, based on a damped harmonic oscillator description of the cavity field and a time-dependent unitary transformation yielding a real Hermitian Hamiltonian, is demonstrated here within the quantum electrodynamics coupled-cluster singles and doubles framework (QED-CCSD). Its general formulation allows straightforward integration into existing ab initio QED frameworks without increasing the computational cost of the underlying methods, providing a practical and efficient route to quantitatively account for realistic cavity conditions in first-principles simulations of molecular systems in cavities.

papers.title: Generalized Commutator on Octonion Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be an octonion algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and let $A,B\in\mathcal O$, not both zero. We study the image of the generalized commutator $\Phi(x,y)=A(xy)-B(yx)$ on $\mathcal O$. We prove that $\Phi$ is surjective if and only if either one of $A$ and $B$ is invertible and $A\neq B$, or $A$ and $B$ are nonzero zero divisors and $A-B$ is invertible. In the remaining cases, the image of $\Phi$ is a hyperplane or a four-dimensional maximal totally isotropic subspace of $\mathcal O$, except when $A$ and $B$ are linearly independent zero divisors and $A-B$ is not invertible, in which case the image spans a six-dimensional subspace. Along the way, we show that every octonion of trace zero is a commutator. We also prove that the image of $Axy-Byx$ on any quaternion algebra over $F$ is a vector subspace, extending a result of Panja S., Saini P. and Singh A. (Images of polynomial maps with constants, Mathematika 71 (2025), no. 3, Paper No. e70031) for $2\times 2$ matrices over algebraically closed fields, and we give examples of other generalized polynomials whose images are not vector subspaces.

papers.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
papers.abstract: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.

papers.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large $c$ CFTs
papers.abstract: We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) eigenstates to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH) in 2D conformal field theories with a large central charge. We prove that the first two qKdV charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\,\Delta)$ plane, where $c$ is the central charge and $\Delta$ denotes the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a comprehensive toolkit for testing GETH within the scope of vacuum-family observables, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectation values of vacuum-family local observables, is provided in this paper. We argue that GETH is satisfied when the infinite tower of qKdV charges is considered. A more restrictive form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible in terms of the first few qKdV charges, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. Specifically, at levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not determined by any finite number of the lowest-index qKdV charges. The question of whether additional microscopic information about the eigenstate is required is left for future work.

papers.title: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Amp\`ere equations with periodic measures
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Amp\`ere equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $\mu$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $\mu(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $\mu_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^n\mu(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,\mu_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,d\mu(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<\alpha\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+\alpha},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Amp\`ere problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.

papers.title: NeuroLens: Learning Latent Embeddings of Neural Semantics from Chronic Recordings
papers.abstract: Understanding how neural activity represents higher-order cognition and how these representations evolve during learning is a central pursuit in neuroscience. However, tracking meaningful representational changes remains challenging because recorded neural populations change across days. Here, we introduce NeuroLens (Latent Embeddings of Neural Semantics), a self-supervised model based on the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (LeJEPA). An adaptive encoder maps changing neural populations into a common latent space, where a temporal predictor forecasts future latent states. Across mouse and human intracortical recordings, NeuroLens learns representations that improve decoding of abstract variables, including decisions and sentence meaning. In chronic mouse neural recordings during visual decision-making, these representations capture gradual transitions between learning stages and the progressive orthogonalization of neural states associated with different choices. They also reveal distinct timescales of cortical reorganization across tasks during learning. With multi-day pretraining, these representations also support stable decoding across days, including leading performance on the FALCON benchmark. Together, these findings support NeuroLens as a framework for tracking learning-related representational changes while maintaining stable decoding over long timescales.

papers.title: Lithium Niobate Surface-Acoustic-Wave Resonator for Very-High-Frequency Isolated Power Conversion
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric devices offer a promising magnetic-free alternative for high-frequency power conversion. Here, we demonstrate a lithium niobate surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator that is optimized for isolated power transfer and show advantages in operating frequency, power density, power handling, and electrical isolation. Our application-optimized 40-MHz SAW resonator, with two electrically isolated interdigital transducers (IDTs) and acoustic Bragg mirrors, achieves a 25.7 W output power at a temperature rise of about 15 {\deg}C with only passive cooling through the back mounting side. With a chip size of 0.095 cm$^3$ and an acoustic mode volume of 0.00255 cm$^3$, our device features a peak chip power density of 270.5 W/cm$^3$ and a mode-volume power density of 10,078 W/cm$^3$. Our device shows an isolation voltage of 2.17 kV. Driven by a GaN full-bridge inverter, our device can drive different load resistors with a calculated peak power transfer efficiency of 87.5%. Our results show the potential of SAW devices as a core component for next-generation power systems.

papers.title: From Redundancy to Minimality: Fixed-Point-Guided Hierarchical Reduction of Learned Piecewise-Linear Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding a nonlinear dynamical system from time series requires not only reproducing its trajectories, but also identifying a simple representation that preserves its essential dynamical structure. Almost-linear recurrent neural networks (AL-RNNs) are piecewise-linear RNNs in which only a subset of units use ReLU nonlinearities, so that nonlinear capacity is explicitly controlled by the number of ReLU units. Their activation patterns define linear regions, represented as symbols, whose observed transitions form a symbolic transition graph. However, directly training AL-RNNs with few ReLU units to realize minimal dynamical representations can be unreliable. We ask whether an AL-RNN with more ReLU units can instead be trained first and systematically reduced to a minimal dynamical representation. We introduce a fixed-point-guided hierarchical reduction procedure that progressively linearizes selected ReLU units, merging neighboring linear regions and graph nodes while preserving distinct symbols containing fixed points (FPs). The resulting reduction tree defines a hierarchy of progressively simpler candidates. Each reduced candidate is initialized from the parent parameters and retrained through gradual linearization with guidance from the parent dynamics. We also prove that, under certain assumptions, reproducing $Q$ distinct fixed points requires at least $Q$ FP-containing symbols, providing a certificate of symbol-level minimality when this bound is attained. Across six tasks spanning attractor reconstruction and flip-flop memory, our learn-reduce-retrain strategy substantially improves the recovery of minimal models, including settings where direct training rarely succeeds. These results show that redundant nonlinear capacity can serve as a scaffold for discovering and realizing minimal dynamical representations.

papers.title: A homotopical enhancement of Neisendorfer's algebraic models
papers.abstract: We give an $\infty$-categorical enhancement of Neisendorfer's equivalences between the homotopy categories of rational simplicial sets, commutative dg algebras (cdgas), cocommutative dg coalgebras (cdgcs) and dg Lie algebras (dgls), where these objects have respective hypotheses of connectedness, nilpotency and finite type. We do so by proving that linear duality is a partial Quillen equivalence between weak finite type connected cdgcs and cdgas, and that Quillen's Chevalley--Eilenberg adjunction is a partial crossed derivable equivalence between cdgcs and dgls, a concept we introduce in this paper to axiomatize precisely the behavior of this adjunction.

papers.title: Impact of Gain Layer Doping Concentration on the Performance of 4H-SiC LGADs
papers.abstract: Gain layer doping concentration determines the electric field profile in a low gain avalanche detector (LGAD) and is therefore the primary design parameter. This work reports its influence on the charge collection and timing behavior of 4H-SiC LGADs. Two mesa-isolated devices with cold He ion implanted termination differ only in gain layer doping, $4\times10^{17}$~$cm^{-3}$ and $5\times10^{17}$~$cm^{-3}$, and are characterized together with a PIN diode from the same wafer using the ultraviolet transient current technique (UV-TCT). The 25\% doping difference produces a gain difference of about two orders of magnitude at the same applied bias, representing a gain range of 3.7 to 216. Under UV-TCT excitation, the higher-doped device exhibits time-resolution minima within a gain range of about 20--80 across the investigated laser intensities, consistent with the transition from electronic-noise-dominated jitter to multiplication shot noise. The non-monotonic timing response is also observed under a $^{90}Sr$ beta source with a Si LGAD reference: the higher-doped device reaches 51.7 ps at 280 V and then degrades, while the lower-doped device requires more than 450 V. This measured gain window provides an experimental reference for further optimization of the gain-layer design.

papers.title: FAER: A Negative-Result Audit of Offline Trajectory Replay Selection on GSM8K
papers.abstract: Offline trajectory replay selects model-generated reasoning traces from a frozen cache for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), yet cache-side answer correctness need not predict downstream accuracy on unseen problems. We report a failure-retaining audit of offline response SFT on GSM8K with Qwen3-1.7B fp16 LoRA over a frozen 384-row cache (256 training rows and 128 excluded held-out rows). Across three seeds (13, 17, 23) on a 256-problem test split, all three 32-row replay rules (uniform, format-feedback, and feedback-aware) obtain mean strict accuracies (0.7786, 0.7682, and 0.7956) below the no-update base model (0.8008), and every paired 95% confidence interval spans zero. Selector ranking is post-hoc unidentified (3 completed selectors versus the repaired protocol's minimum of 5, with rank correlation spanning both signs). Under an 8,192-supervised-token windowed schedule, 9 of 12 runs halt under calibration drift or unresolved nonfinite training loss or gradients, leaving only full-cache replay completed at 0.7721. A repaired campaign with dynamic loss scaling halted at its learning-rate pilot under reference-solution loss drift before accessing the 346-problem locked test split. Because the gold-rationale positive control was never executed, these negative results cannot separate cache quality, selector quality, and learner-protocol limits. Our one positive finding separates parser repair from prompt changes on a 64-problem audit split: reparsing fixed base generations with a Decimal extractor raises parse rate from 0.8750 to 1.0000 and accuracy from 0.7344 to 0.8281, whereas appending a format suffix flips 0.2500 of canonical answers. A preregistered replication on 512 fresh GSM8K training problems reproduces this parser-only gain (+8.40 pp, 95% CI [+6.05, +10.94]) for this checkpoint. We contribute a ledger-traceable negative-result record and 9 lessons learned.

papers.title: Optimal Resource Scaling for Early Fault Tolerant Iterative Quantum Phase Estimation under Cost Error Tradeoffs
papers.abstract: The iterative quantum phase estimation algorithm (IPEA) is better suited for NISQ and early fault-tolerant hardware compared to the original algorithm, which requires the inverse quantum Fourier transform. However, current error mitigation and correction implementations lead to imperfect unitaries, causing erroneous phase feedback in IPEA. To improve the reliability of phase bits is to repeat the k^th iteration for the 2^k-th power of the unitary $N_k^*$ times, followed by a majority decision. However, due to variations in their circuit complexities, different iterations incur varying resource costs ($w_k$) and different per-shot error probabilities ($q_k$). Given tight resource constraints, we ask what the optimal number $\{N_k^*: 1\le k \le L\}$ of shots per bit is: $$\arg \max_{\{N_k\}} \mathbb{P}(\text{all } L \text{ bits correct}) \text{s.t.} \sum_{k=1}^L w_k N_k \le W$$ We construct upper and lower surrogate objectives via concentration and anti-concentration inequalities and prove an asymptotic optimality guarantee for whenever the budget satisfies $W = \sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}(\ln L + \omega(1))$, where $c_k=-\ln\left(2\sqrt{\left(1-\frac{q_k}{2} \right) \frac{q_k}{2}}\right)$, which, for $q_k\ll 1$, is proportional to $\ln\frac{1}{q_k}$. Optimizing the tractable lower surrogate yields a true success probability within a $(1-o(1))$ factor of the exact optimum. We observe that when resources are abundant, $W \gg \ln(L)\sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}$, optimal allocations are proportional to $\ 1/c_k$. However, when resources are sufficient but not abundant, $(\ln(L)+\omega(1))\sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\le W \le O\left( \ln(L)\cdot \sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\right)$, an additional $-\frac{1}{c_k}\ln\frac{w_k}{c_k}$ correction accounts for error propagation from less-significant to more-significant bits.

papers.title: Measurement-induced dynamics and emergent symmetries of particles moving in a one-dimensional lattice
papers.abstract: Continuous measurements simultaneously reveal and modify the dynamics of a quantum system. In this work we consider the tunneling motion of particles between the sites of a one-dimensional lattice. We investigate how weak continuous probing of the occupation of a single lattice site induces entanglement and selects definite values for system properties such as wave function parity and permutation symmetry. Our simulations show how continuous measurement can steer systems of two and three particles, with no prior permutation symmetry, into stable bosonic, fermionic and parastatistical symmetry sectors.

papers.title: A Few Reveal Many: Constraint-Enhanced Learning of Many-Body Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Discovering properties of many-body quantum systems is challenging due to the large number of parameters involved. Here, we show that harnessing fundamental constraints among quantum observables improves quantum learning, enabling the inference of exponentially many quantities from a linear number of direct measurements. We leverage this result to design constraint-enhanced algorithms for evaluating key quantum features such as Entanglement and Magic in 100-qubit simulators. At a fixed number of measurement shots, they achieve up to an 83% reduction in relative error compared with protocols based on constructing "classical shadows" of quantum states. Quantum constraints themselves are therefore a resource for exploring large quantum systems, guiding the allocation of the measurement budget to highly informative observables.

papers.title: Montesinos Knots with Delta-Unknotting Number One
papers.abstract: The $\Delta$-unknotting number for a knot is defined as the minimum number of $\Delta$-moves needed to deform the knot into the trivial knot. In this paper, we discuss Montesinos knots whose $\Delta$-unknotting number is equal to one. We propose a conjectural characterization of Montesinos knots with $\Delta$-unknotting number one and provide examples admitting distinct $\Delta$-moves, each of which deforms the knot into the trivial knot. Furthermore, we present examples illustrating the relationship between the locations of $\Delta$-moves and $X$-moves for knots with $u^{\Delta}(K) = 1$, considering separately the cases $u(K) = 1$ and $u(K) = 2$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Throat as a Minimal Geometric Alternative to the Singularity in Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: A basic question in the study of regular black holes is whether the Schwarzschild singularity can be replaced by a geodesically complete interior while retaining a single horizon. An asymptotic throat offers a minimal geometric realization of this possibility. The areal radius approaches a finite, nonzero limit at a future internal infinity, without requiring a change in spatial topology or a bounce. We extend the geometric analysis beyond monotone contraction to interiors in which the areal radius oscillates about its limit. For both null-type and spacelike-type inner ends, we derive a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for causal geodesic completeness and criteria for bounded curvature in parallel-propagated frames. Explicit examples of both types have complete inner ends and satisfy all four standard energy conditions at sufficiently large exterior radii. Applying these criteria to the oscillatory solution of the B\"ohmer--Vandersloot model of effective loop quantum gravity, we find a causally complete spacelike-type inner end. Its scalar curvature invariants converge to those of the limiting Nariai-type solution. Along each radial null geodesic, however, a parallel-propagated curvature component is unbounded along a sequence of turning points as the affine parameter tends to infinity.

papers.title: Surveying for Close Binaries among Lithium-rich Giants
papers.abstract: One of the scenarios proposed to explain low-mass red giants with anomalously high lithium (Li) abundances involves tidal interaction with a close binary companion. If dominant, this enrichment channel predicts an enhanced binary fraction among Li-rich giants relative to Li-normal ones. We aim to test the binary interaction scenario by using multi-epoch radial velocities (RVs) to measure the close binary fraction of a statistically robust sample of Li-rich giants. The surveyed sample contains both red clump (RC) and first-ascent red giant branch (RGB) targets, allowing us to examine potential differences in the binary fraction with evolutionary stage. We monitored 70 giants (40 RC and 30 RGB) using ESPRESSO at the VLT, 57 (32 RC and 25 RGB) of which already had four or more visits over a $\sim$7-month baseline; the analysis here is based on these latter targets. For the targets with RV variation larger than that expected for intrinsic jitter, we performed Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the probability that the observed RV variation is due to a stellar ($P_{SB}$) or substellar ($P_{SS}$) companion. After removing targets consistent with stellar jitter, 11 ($34 \pm 8$%) RC and eight ($32 \pm 9$%) RGB stars remained as binary candidates or stars with a companion. Of these 19, three targets ($16 \pm 8$% of the filtered sample) are confirmed stellar binaries. The distributions of $P_{SB}$ and $P_{SS}$ are statistically indistinguishable between the RC and RGB samples. We find no evidence in our current data for a binary fraction for Li-rich giants (in either evolutionary stage) larger than that expected for a regular Li-normal population, suggesting that binary interaction is unlikely to be the dominant mechanism driving Li enrichment. Extending the RV baseline to probe longer orbital periods will be important to continue exploring the plausibility of this scenario.

papers.title: Finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions
papers.abstract: We study finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions, regularized in the relative momentum of each pair so that they remain Galilean invariant. Pauli blocking alone then makes the trimer dispersion deviate from free center-of-mass motion, so the trimer energy can be lowest at finite total momentum. Allowing this motion expands the $abb$ region among pairs and trimers and removes the region where an odd-wave pair is lowest. The $aabb$ quartet lies below all these branches at every sampled coupling, and in a strip starting on the crossing of the two dimer-pair channels its lowest breakup channel is a moving $abb$ trimer and an atom. At weak interspecies attraction, a variational bound shows that two odd-wave Cooper pairs bind into a quartet, whose binding exceeds that of the coexisting trimer by orders of magnitude as the attraction weakens. At stronger interspecies attraction, the quartet binding relative to two unlike-species dimers disappears when the odd-wave interaction is switched off, although the even-wave interaction dominates the interaction energy. Relative to the in-vacuum case, the Fermi sea enhances the weak-coupling quartet binding, and at fixed scattering lengths the quartet binding grows with density while the coexisting trimer becomes much shallower. These results show that neither the most strongly bound pair nor the dominant interaction energy alone determines whether the quartet binds.

papers.title: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
papers.abstract: Axis bending of a mode-evolution coupler realizes the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol [Opt. Express 34, 1214 (2026)]. We identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement is generated by the transverse momentum $\hat p_x$, which in a real two-mode supermode basis is purely $\sigma_y$: exactly the form of the CD term, and the one form that detuning and coupling cannot supply. Equating the two gives the axis slope in closed form, as a ratio of two matrix elements at a single cross section, or $\dot{x}_0=\dot\theta/(\gamma\Delta\beta^{2})$ in coupled-mode variables. It agrees with a numerical offset search to 0.3% and is shown to be the earlier curvature condition viewed from the Kramers-Henneberger frame. Beam propagation simulations compare the bent coupler directly with the unitary-transformation realization built from the same reference structure: the two reach supermode fidelities of 0.994 and 1.000 against 0.886 for the untreated coupler, show comparable bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, and differ inside the device by the frame transformation that relates them.

papers.title: Faster Estimates from Binned Test Scores---With Discussion of Normality, Bias, and Reliability
papers.abstract: Education agencies often summarize test score distributions by counting how many students scored in 3 to 5 bins. Means and standard deviations (SDs) can be estimated from bin counts using a HETOP model, which assumes that scores are normally distributed within each school or district. However, most HETOP software takes minutes to hours if the number of schools or districts is large. We present a fast HETOP algorithm that produces HETOP estimates in less than a millisecond per district. The algorithm is implemented in the fast_hetop function of the binest package for RL: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/binest/refman/binest.html#topic+fast_hetop HETOP estimates of the mean are highly reliable; estimates of the SD are not as good. Maximum likelihood estimates are generally excellent but can be biased and unreliable if scores are not normal or scores are concentrated in the top or bottom bin. Empirical Bayes shrinkage improves unreliable estimates. Standard errors are smaller if the data represents the whole population of students rather than a sample. HETOP estimates are usable for many purposes, but it would be better if education agencies reported means and SDs directly.

papers.title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support K\"ahler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

papers.title: t-J model at 50
papers.abstract: I briefly overview the original formulation of the t-J model starting from Hubbard model, as well as stress its unique features, i.e., advantages and shortcomings when discussing its physical properties. Particular emphasis is put on a brief characterization of connection between magnetism, unconventional superconductivity, and the Mott-Hubbard localization of the correlated carriers in a narrow band. In the second part I summarize the model generalization to the three--orbital situation. The main purpose is to list some basic features of the physics associated with t--J model.

papers.title: The overlooked price feedback: Why simulations overstate distribution grid peaks from home batteries under real-time pricing
papers.abstract: Simulation studies of home batteries under real-time pricing commonly find that synchronized charging creates new peaks in distribution grids. Yet all home-battery simulation studies reviewed here treat wholesale prices as exogenous, ignoring the effect of battery dispatch on prices. Charging in low-price hours raises the wholesale price, which dampens the incentive to charge. In equilibrium, charging is spread out across hours. This paper examines how accounting for this feedback changes peaks in local grids. A simulation of household battery dispatch under real-time pricing, calibrated to German data, finds that, if half of households own a battery, exogenous prices raise the coincident import peak by 83 % relative to the no-battery benchmark. With endogenous prices, the same fleet reduces the peak by 6 %. This finding is robust across alternative price functions, price paths, peak measures, and scenario assumptions. While new local peaks remain possible where batteries are geographically concentrated, these results suggest that published studies overstate the local peak-load effects of price-responsive batteries.

papers.title: Asymptotically H\"{o}lder gradient regularity for degenerate or singular parabolic normalized $ p$-Laplace equations
papers.abstract: We study bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular parabolic equation \[ u_t-|Du|^{\gamma}\Delta_p^{\mathrm{N}}u=f \qquad \text{in } Q_1, \] where \[ \Delta_p^{\mathrm{N}}u := \Delta u+(p-2) \left\langle D^2u\frac{Du}{|Du|}, \frac{Du}{|Du|} \right\rangle, \qquad -1 0$ such that \[ |p-2|+|\gamma|\leq\varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+\alpha,\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient H\"older exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $ 1 $ as $(p,\gamma)\to(2,0)$. This extends the result of Andrade and Santos (Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{61}, Paper No. 196, 2022) for $\gamma=0$ to the joint regime $(p,\gamma)\to(2,0)$ and answers affirmatively the question raised in Remark~1.1 therein.

papers.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

papers.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
papers.abstract: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon. Vortex electrons add a new tool to the well-established electron-atom scattering tool box. Our results are important for applications of vortex electrons: they show that, when large total angular momentum is involved, the Breit interaction must be taken into account in calculations.

papers.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
papers.abstract: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.

papers.title: Scaling Density Functional Theory with Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) strikes a practical balance between accuracy and computational cost in many problems of computational chemistry and materials science. However, many DFT calculations are limited by fixed atom-centered basis sets, which dictate how accuracy and cost scale with system size. We propose Gaussian Splatting for Density Functional Theory (GS-DFT), which represents molecular orbitals as a cloud of Gaussians whose positions, shapes, and mixing coefficients are optimized jointly by gradient descent to minimize the energy without training data. Conceptually, GS-DFT is 3D Gaussian splatting with the renderer replaced by quantum mechanics. We introduce two key solver components: adaptive density fitting with screening for efficient evaluation of two-electron integrals, and a regularized differentiable orthogonalization of the molecular orbitals. Empirically, the optimized basis reaches the accuracy of the largest conventional basis sets with a fraction of the parameters, converging systematically in energy, density, and nuclear forces. At equal parameter count, it captures the stretched-bond and anion physics that fixed bases only recover with specialized basis augmentation. The resulting solver exhibits quadratic peak memory scaling in the cloud size, allowing us to simulate systems of up to 2,742 atoms (10,406 electrons) without any modifications at triple-zeta scale using a single four-GPU node.

papers.title: Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
papers.abstract: Two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions arise from differential recursions with rational initial data: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. At order $p=3$, their rational coefficients yield the triangles OEIS A140136 and A336110, together with a positive palindromic numerator triangle for the odd sector. In general, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn companions, and an explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual series. The Narayana quadratic ($p=2$) and the $S_4$-symmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia quartic ($p=3$, with two tetrahedral edge resolvents) serve as explicit low-order benchmarks. For every $p \ge 3$, we prove that the distinguished reduced generating function has exact algebraic degree $2(p-1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(x,h^{p-1})$ and that every Horn companion is algebraic. Over $h$, the rational uniformization lifts to the Fermat curve $s^{p-1}+w^{p-1}=1$ of genus $(p-2)(p-3)/2$ with generic monodromy and Galois group $S_{2(p-1)}$. This uniform cover establishes the universal boundary factorization at $H=h^{p-1}=0$ and explains the cubic characteristic factor $\mathcal{A}_p^3$ (carrying a projective $S_3$ action) in the discriminant via $(2,3)$-cusp geometry, illustrated by exact sextic and octic equations and higher-order slices. Conversely, a nonexact differential on the Fermat curve combined with full $S_{2(p-1)}$ monodromy proves that the distinguished self-dual function is transcendental for all $p \ge 4$. The complete factorization of the generic reduced discriminant remains open.

papers.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal matching covered graphs
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is {\em matching covered} if each of its edges lies in a perfect matching. A matching covered graph is {\em minimal} if the removal of any edge results in a graph that is no longer matching covered. Lov\'asz and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B 23 (1977) 127--138] proved by ear decompositions that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ edges, and this bound is sharp for all even $|V(G)|\ge6$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (4) (2026) 559--606] determined the extremal graphs achieving this upper bound. In this paper, we prove that every minimal matching covered nonbipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(5|V(G)|-10)/2$ edges. Moreover, we show that if $G$ is not bicritical, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-14)/2$ edges and if $G$ is 3-connected and has at least 14 vertices, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-26)/2$ edges. All three bounds are sharp, and all the corresponding extremal graphs are characterized.

papers.title: Critical escape dynamics of an active particle moving on curved surfaces
papers.abstract: On the macroscopic scale, active (self-propelled) objects moving through complex environments are often subject to effects arising from both the curvature of the surrounding surface and external influences such as gravity. We study the Kramers escape problem for active Brownian particles in two settings: motion in an external potential driven solely by gradient forces, and motion on a curved manifold subject to an additional constant gravitational force. In the absence of translational noise, a sharp dynamical transition occurs when the self-propulsion velocity $v_0$ reaches a critical velocity $v_c$ required for an escape. Above this threshold, the escape rate $k$ follows a universal scaling form, $k \propto \exp\left[-\mathrm{const}(v_0-v_c)^{-\gamma}\right]$, with an exponent $\gamma=3/2$ for the escape in a potential and $\gamma=1/2$ for the escape on a curved manifold in the presence of gravity. These distinct exponents reveal how the interplay of activity, surface curvature, and gravity determines the critical escape dynamics. Our theoretical predictions are verified by numerical simulations.

papers.title: Tails, Trails, and Transients: Comets, NEOs, and Supernovae in Rubin Early Data Preview 2
papers.abstract: We identify effective single-visit imaging hidden within the deep coadded images of the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2 (EDP2). We develop a workflow to locate known small Solar System bodies in these data, using our Ponder orchestrator with the Sorcha survey simulator to predict their positions and the Rubin Science Platform to identify shallow coadds and extract image cutouts. Because cometary activity and near-Earth object (NEO) trails produce extended morphologies, both remain identifiable in shallow coadds. From approximately 700 comet cutouts, we identify 59 activity detections spanning 32 objects. We discover activity in 2025 NC6, previously unknown to be active, and independently rediscover two comets through their activity. We recover 336 NEO cutouts, including 29 with predicted trails over 25 pixels. We demonstrate how the same provenance-driven methods can recover stationary transients in Rubin coadds, including ones predating the alert stream. Of 47 publicly-reported transients coinciding with EDP2, 36 occupy shallow coadds. We show Rubin photometry agrees with published lightcurves to within 0.2 mag. The imaging provides additional bands, host-galaxy context, and deeper supernova pre-discovery limits than discovery surveys could reach. We showcase seven transients, including SN 2025nbh, which we identify as lying in the outskirts of AGC 114905, an ultra-diffuse galaxy central to the dark-matter-free debate; the supernova offers an independent galaxy distance measurement. Shallow coadds are a relatively unexplored facet of Rubin data with applications beyond the examples presented here; regions with varying numbers of contributing visits will persist throughout the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

papers.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
papers.abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.

papers.title: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

papers.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
papers.abstract: How much information can a single neuron remember? How many memories can neural networks retrieve without creating false memories? These questions are related to a basic question: how many Boolean threshold functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_0+\langle a,x\rangle)$, $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, are there? In this paper, we show that the number $T_n$ of distinct Boolean threshold functions is \[ T_n=2\binom{2^n-1}{n}\bigl(1+O(n^{-99})\bigr). \] Equivalently, the capacity of a single threshold neuron is $n^2-\log_2(n!)+1+O(n^{-99})$ bits, improving the $O(n)$ error term in the result of Kahn--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi to $O(n^{-99})$. To prove this, we show that, for $1\le r\le n-1$, and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ are chosen at random from $\{-1,1\}^n$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left\{ \langle v_1,\ldots,v_r\rangle\cap\{-1,1\}^n =\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_r\} \right\} =1-O(n^{-99}). \] In the context of the Kanter--Sompolinsky Hamiltonian for memory retrieval, this identifies $r=n-1$ as a sharp threshold, at which, for almost every collection of $r$ memories, the only ground states are these memories and their negatives, confirming a weaker form of the Kalai--Linial--Odlyzko conjecture. It also settles a recent open problem posed by M. Anthony on the specification number of Boolean threshold functions. In addition, we show that, for every $1\le r\le n-1$, \[ \mathbb P\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\text{ are linearly dependent}\} =2\binom r2\,2^{-n}+O\!\left(2^{-n}e^{-cn}\right), \] confirming a conjecture of Kahn--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi.

papers.title: Measuring Dual-Superconductor Length Scales in the QCD Vacuum at HERA
papers.abstract: In the dual-superconductor picture, the QCD vacuum behaves like a superconductor for chromoelectric fields, with characteristic penetration and coherence lengths. These scales have so far been studied primarily through lattice calculations of static flux tubes. We show that they are also imprinted on exclusive diffraction, where the transverse profile of a gluonic hotspot reflects the response of the vacuum to a localised colour source. Using the Clem vortex profile, we fit all 104 H1 and ZEUS measurements of exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction and find $\chi^2/{\rm ndf}=0.72$, the penetration depth $\lambda=0.19(2)~{\rm fm}$, the hotspot core size $\xi_v=0.087(14)~{\rm fm}$, and the Ginzburg--Landau parameter $\kappa=2.6(8)$, placing the effective vacuum description in the type-II regime. The corresponding vector mass $1/\lambda=1.03(11)~{\rm GeV}$ agrees with the lattice gluelump mass, and the extracted parameters reproduce the QCD string tension.

papers.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
papers.abstract: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the R\'enyi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

papers.title: Magnetic Lifting of BIC Symmetry Protection Enables Nonreciprocal Beam Steering and Angular Information Encoding
papers.abstract: Symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum (SP-BICs) offer exceptional optical confinement but remain nonradiative. Here, we demonstrate that magnetically lifting their protecting symmetry enables nonreciprocal beam steering with intrinsic angular information encoding. In a magneto-optical photonic crystal slab, an in-plane magnetic field converts an SP-BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC and, together with vertical dielectric asymmetry, continuously displaces the associated band extremum away from the Gamma point. The steered beam exhibits two independent locking relations: its wavelength is locked to the elevation angle, while its polarization orientation is locked to the azimuthal angle. These relations embed complementary spectral and polarization information into the scanning beam, providing additional sensing channels for multidimensional LiDAR. Moreover, the nonreciprocal dispersion gives different resonance frequencies at opposite wave vectors, supporting resonant emission at +k while back-reflected light at the same frequency is off resonance at -k, opening a route to intrinsic self-isolation and reduced optical feedback. These findings establish a unified framework connecting magnetic beam steering, angular information encoding, and nonreciprocal feedback suppression, with prospects for compact reconfigurable light sources and integrated optical engines.

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
papers.abstract: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $\kappa$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $\Omega\left(\kappa^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1\delta\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<\delta<1$ and sufficiently large $\kappa$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $\kappa$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

papers.title: The Uniqueness of Exponential Second-Order Expected Utility
papers.abstract: A decision-maker entertains several probability models of the state of the world, distrusts each of them, and is unsure which of them holds. She therefore carries two relative-entropy penalties: one on departures from a given model and one on departures from the reference she places on models. The literature that introduced this structure treats the equality of the two penalty parameters as a tractable special case. We show that it is in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: her criterion carries a single relative-entropy penalty if and only if the two parameters agree, that is, when she charges the same price for doubting a model as for doubting her weights on models. Under that one condition the two layers collapse: the criterion is an exponential second-order expected utility based at the Bayesian predictive distribution, for every compact model set and every prior, with no large-sample limit anywhere. When the condition fails, the caution she displays blends her two parameters, with a weight equal to the share of an act's predictive variance that comes from disagreement among the models; since that share varies across acts, no single parameter and baseline represent her, and the same variation identifies the two parameters separately. The exponential aggregator and relative entropy are each forced: no other continuous and strictly increasing aggregator delivers the collapse, and within the power-divergence family only relative entropy does.

papers.title: Exact Ehrhart Series of Birkhoff Polytopes via Constant Terms and Finite-Field Evaluation
papers.abstract: The Ehrhart series of the $n$th Birkhoff polytope is $\sum_{r\geq0}H_n(r)z^r$, where $H_n(r)$ counts nonnegative integer $n\times n$ matrices whose row and column sums all equal $r$. We present an exact method for computing this series using constant terms and finite fields. A root filter expresses $H_n(r)$ as a weighted sum of the values $h_r(M)^n$, where $h_r$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial and $M$ ranges over multisets of $m$th roots of unity with $m=r+1$. Constant-term cancellation reduces the evaluation of $h_r(M)$ to a sum over repeated elements $a$ of $M$. For a particular $a$ of multiplicity $\mu_a$, the computation uses a generalized Todd coefficient of degree $\mu_a-2$. Sums of $h_r(M)^n$ over selected multiplicity classes are handled using symmetric function techniques. Together with the remaining individual evaluations, this gives $O_n(m^{n-5}+m^4)$ field operations for each admissible prime and fixed $n\geq5$. An explicit bound and the Chinese remainder theorem recover the integer counts, and Ehrhart symmetry determines the full series. The same method applies to the World Cup problem, which counts the same matrices with diagonal entries required to be $0$. We prove correctness and compute complete Birkhoff series through order $14$ and World Cup series through order $13$. The Birkhoff series for orders $10$--$14$ and the World Cup series for orders $9$--$13$ are tabulated in the appendices.

papers.title: Efficient Cost-Aware LLM Evaluation via Bayesian Bandit Gittins Indices
papers.abstract: Exhaustively evaluating every candidate LLM configuration on every benchmark item to identify a high-performing one is costly. We formulate configuration selection as a cost-aware Bayesian bandit problem and propose GittinsEval, inspired by Bayesian-optimal Gittins-index policies for Markov chain selection. We augment this policy with a separate anytime recommendation rule over both fully and partially evaluated configurations, using an LCB-style score to account for posterior uncertainty. GittinsEval is computationally efficient, requiring only lightweight online updates after offline precomputation. Across tasks with varying numbers of candidates and examples, GittinsEval is consistently competitive, with particularly strong gains over the Bayesian optimization baselines on few-candidate large-example benchmarks and over cost-unaware frequentist baselines on large-candidate tasks. Crucially, GittinsEval often attains near-zero simple regret using only 1%-2% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost; it also offers a stopping rule that typically triggers at 1%-10% with an appropriate cost--quality tradeoff parameter.

papers.title: Evidence for the emergence of stellar magnetic fields during rapid mass transfer
papers.abstract: Binary interaction fundamentally alters the evolution of massive stars, yet the physical consequences of mass transfer remain poorly constrained. Here we present high-resolution spectroscopic observations of Plaskett's Star (HD 47129) that reveal small radial-velocity variations of its magnetic secondary, coherent with the system's 14.4 d orbital period. These measurements support an evolved, post-mass-transfer configuration in which the narrow-lined primary is a partially Roche-lobe-filling stripped star with a mass of $5.9^{+1.8}_{-1.4},M_\odot$, while the secondary is a $40.8^{+9.3}_{-6.7},M_\odot$, rapidly rotating magnetic accretor. The system provides a rare opportunity to observe the immediate aftermath of mass transfer in a massive binary and offers compelling new evidence linking binary interaction to the emergence of strong stellar magnetism. Because magnetic fields regulate angular-momentum loss and transport, their formation through mass transfer could alter the subsequent evolution of massive binaries, with consequences for stellar populations, supernova progenitors and yields, and the formation of gravitational-wave sources.

papers.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
papers.abstract: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

papers.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
papers.abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schr\"{o}dinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.

papers.title: Equilibrium Numbers in Non-Square Bimatrix Games
papers.abstract: Bimatrix games may have an exponential number of mixed Nash equilibria if both dimensions of the game are allowed to grow. Bounds on their maximal number give structural insights that have been used to construct hard-to-solve games. We show new sharp or asymptotically sharp bounds on the (polynomial) number of equilibria for generic games where one dimension of the game is fixed and the number of strategies of the other player grows. These results go beyond the hitherto studied square games. Our methods employ combinatorial properties of polytopes, and recent obstructions that relate to the graph of those polytopes. For $n\ge5$, we construct $3\times n$ games that have all $2n+1$ vertices of the best-response polytope as equilibrium strategies, proved using a simple case of the 4-color theorem for planar graphs. Generic $4\times 5$ games are shown to have at most 17 equilibria, using computer calculations with existing datasets for all combinatorial types of the relevant polytopes. For $d\times n$ games, we construct games where all but a fraction of $O(1/n)$ of the maximum number of vertices are equilibrium strategies.

papers.title: Towards Accurate Prediction of Mutation-Induced Changes in Protein Structure
papers.abstract: Proteins can possess numerous mutations relative to their wild-type amino acid sequences with minimal impact to their structure and function. However, in other cases, even a single amino acid mutation relative to the wild-type sequence can lead to a large change in structure or even a disease phenotype. While the accuracy of wild-type protein structure prediction has improved significantly in recent years, it remains difficult to accurately predict the structure of mutant proteins. Here, we characterize the local mutation-induced structural changes in proteins for a dataset of wildtype and the corresponding single-amino acid mutant x-ray crystal structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB). We find that mutation-induced structural changes in these proteins are localized at the site of the mutation, decaying rapidly with increasing spatial distance from the mutation site. In addition, we evaluate how well AlphaFold3 can recapitulate the observed mutation-induced structural deformations in the x-ray crystal structures. We find that the accuracy of the AlphaFold3 predictions decreases strongly with increasing mutation-induced deformation. In contrast to the results for AlphaFold3, the Pearson correlation between a single physical feature, i.e. the change in solvent accessibility, and the mutation-induced deformation does not depend on the magnitude of the deformation. Our results and analyses provide a framework for further studies aimed at predicting the structural changes in proteins caused by single amino acid mutations.

papers.title: Optimal Allocation of Grid-Forming Frequency Shaping Control
papers.abstract: Various inverter-based control strategies have been proposed to improve frequency security for power systems with high renewable penetration. Among them, the grid-forming frequency shaping control is particularly promising due to its ability to shape the post-contingency aggregate system frequency dynamics into first-order with prescribed rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and steady-state frequency deviation. Moreover, the shaped aggregate dynamics depends on the harmonic sum of all inverter transfer functions rather than on their distribution. In light of this, here we explore how to allocate shaping control resources to minimize the transient control effort needed to achieve ideal coherent dynamics. We formulate it as a constrained optimization problem by tackling two main difficulties. First, we make the squared $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm legitimate quantification of transient control cost under step power imbalances through a system transformation. Second, we simplify the $s$-domain constraint for Nadir elimination into a standard constraint that is easy to implement in optimization. The resulting non-convex optimization problem can be solved by existing successive convexification method. The effectiveness of the allocation has been verified on the modified Icelandic Power Network test case.

papers.title: Advanced 400G-SerDes Modulations and Equalizers for GPU Cluster in AI Era
papers.abstract: High-speed GPU cluster interconnects are evolving from 200 to 400 Gbps to meet the growing computing demands of artificial intelligence. We investigate high-order modulation and advanced equalization for 400 Gbps interconnects. Theoretical bit error rate (BER) expressions for 4/8-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and approximate expressions for six PAM6 formats generated from 32-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (32QAM) are derived. In additive white Gaussian noise, PAM6 generated by framed-cross 32QAM achieves the best BER performance among the PAM6 formats. PAM6 and PAM8 incur peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) penalties of approximately 4.2 and 7.2 dB, respectively, relative to PAM4 at the KP4 forward error correction (KP4-FEC) limit. Simulations compare PAM4, PAM6, and PAM8 at a line rate of 440 Gbps (net rate of 400G) under different bandwidth limitations. As bandwidth becomes more constrained, bandwidth requirements increasingly dominate performance over noise tolerance. PAM4 requires the lowest PSNR to reach the KP4-FEC limit in mildly bandwidth-limited channels, whereas PAM6 performs best under moderate limitations. PAM8 offers a significant advantage under severe limitations because of its lower bandwidth requirement and reduced susceptibility to high-frequency attenuation. With maximum likelihood sequence estimation, PAM6 and PAM8 reach the KP4-FEC limit under all evaluated channel conditions, while PAM6 requires a lower PSNR in most channels, highlighting its potential for 400G-SerDes systems.

papers.title: Stochastic optimisation method for estimating large deviations
papers.abstract: A stochastic optimisation method was recently proposed to efficiently compute large deviation functions, used in statistical physics to characterise the fluctuations of nonequilibrium systems, modelled as Markov processes. The method, called LDSTOP, combines numerical techniques from control theory and machine learning to iteratively construct the "driven process", a controlled version of the Markov process used as a model of nonequilibrium system that realises a given fluctuation or large deviation of that system in an optimal way. Compared to other methods based on spectral approximations, importance sampling, cloning or splitting, LDSTOP is simple, flexible, and scalable, as it works by simulating single trajectories that are gradually guided towards the driven process. Here, we illustrate these advantages by applying the method on the full range of Markov processes considered in applications, namely, discrete-time Markov chains, continuous-time jump processes, and diffusion processes. For each type, we define the objective function to be optimised, explain different options available for representing the driven process (using, e.g., neural networks), and provide implementation details through simple applications. With these contributions, we aim to showcase the method's efficiency, as well as its ease of use when combined with available machine learning packages, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX, for simulating stochastic processes and solving high-dimensional optimisation problems.

papers.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
papers.abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.

papers.title: Leveraging Industrial Foundation Models at the Edge of Particle Physics Detectors via Distillation Learning and Hardware Co-design
papers.abstract: Data acquisition (DAQ) systems at future particle physics experiments stand to benefit from the extremes of AI/ML development: large-scale foundation models can enhance the performance of feature extraction algorithms, and small-scale on-detector deployments can enable real-time intelligent data handling. This work provides the first tokenizer fine-tuning of an industrial foundation model for particle physics DAQ. Starting from the backbone of Google Research's TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model), we address real-time regression tasks for drift chamber trackers and dual-readout calorimeters by jointly training the pretrained tokenizer and a newly initialized residual adapter, then fitting task-specific linear heads while keeping the transformer backbone frozen. Furthermore, the resulting TimesFM teachers can be distilled into students and co-designed with FPGA implementation to support real-time operation at future colliders. The distilled and compressed models achieve competitive performance, while distillation reduces reliance on labeled training data. Further, the pipeline of distillation and model compression from TimesFM is generic and can be easily adapted to a variety of 1D waveform tasks across domains.

papers.title: Uniform Inference for Parameters Identified by Conditional Quantile Restrictions
papers.abstract: Many structural and dynamic economic models imply that key parameters are identified by conditional quantile restrictions. Building on the exponential weighting approach of Bierens (1990) and the penalized maximum statistics of Chen et al. (2025), we develop a uniform inference method for such parameters. We construct an adaptive $\ell_1$-penalized statistic from a process indexed by quantiles and weighting directions. The statistic aggregates evidence across quantiles and regularizes maximization over directions. A shifted bootstrap is used to estimate local power for penalty selection. Under the stated conditions, adaptive selection asymptotically preserves or improves worst case local power relative to the unpenalized test over a prespecified set of alternatives. The improvement is strict when a positive candidate penalty raises the population level criterion above its value at zero. We also extend the process and bootstrap theory to the setting with pre-estimated nuisance parameters. We characterize their contribution to the limiting process, correct the variance estimator, and establish Gaussian multiplier bootstrap validity for null inference. Monte Carlo experiments favor the CvM-KS method for size control under pre-estimation and show that adaptive penalization can improve empirical power relative to the unpenalized test.

papers.title: First measurement of the forward rapidity dependence of $W$ boson transverse helicity fractions
papers.abstract: The transverse helicity fractions of $W$ bosons are measured as a function of the $W$ boson rapidity, $y_{W}$, in the range $0 \leq y_{W} \leq 5$ using $W\to\mu\nu_{\mu}$ decays in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV recorded by the LHCb experiment and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $5.1$ fb$^{-1}$. The fractions are extracted from a template fit to the muon transverse momentum and pseudorapidity. The results show a strong rapidity dependence and agree with next-to-leading-order Standard Model predictions, providing the first determination of the transverse helicity fractions of $W$ bosons in the forward region.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca

papers.title: A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: In vacuum anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, the geometry admits a perfect tessellation by a geodesic network. This tessellation characterizes the background exactly, and a partial entanglement entropy (PEE) tensor-network toy model of AdS/CFT can be defined on it. It has so far been unclear whether this construction can be extended beyond vacuum AdS. In this paper we take the first step in this direction. We show that the exterior region of the Schwarzschild black hole and its Einstein--Rosen bridge are perfectly tessellated by a specific geodesic gas emitted from the boundary, so that Crofton reconstruction holds in these regions. We then prove that such a geodesic tessellation and the Crofton reconstruction it defines extend to more generic Riemannian manifolds. This allows us to construct a PEE tensor-network model of holographic duality on more generic geometric backgrounds. In the case of the PEE tensor-network model for the Schwarzschild background, we can concretely realize the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Ryu--Takayanagi formula and the ER=EPR proposal. Our approach opens a new route towards holographic toy models beyond AdS/CFT.

papers.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
papers.abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d 0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p 1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

papers.title: Functional Renormalization for Random Matrix Theory: The relational background field method
papers.abstract: The construction of a reliable renormalization group (RG) flow for discrete gravity models that preserves their underlying symmetry group, typically $U(N)$ or $O(N)$, remains an open problem. For random matrix models, which are the focus of this paper, this symmetry is intrinsically tied to the interactions encoding the random geometry of two-dimensional quantum Euclidean spacetime. We develop a novel approach based on the introduction of a partial matrix-valued intermediate field. In the large-$N$ limit, measure concentration strongly suppresses fluctuations of its singular values, allowing it to play the role of a self-consistent background field. This provides the basis for a relational RG in which the notion of scale is dynamically induced by the effective Gaussian measure in the basis where the intermediate field is diagonal. Our construction preserves the symmetry of the original model and admits a well-defined continuum limit. We show that the resulting infrared theory is described by a three-dimensional non-local Euclidean field theory with a non-trivial Wilson-Fisher-like fixed point and a single relevant direction. Remarkably, the associated critical exponent exactly matches the standard double-scaling exponent. We finally discuss extensions of the background-field approach to other discrete gravity models, such as random tensor models, and to different symmetry groups, as well as connections with more formal RG frameworks and information geometry.

papers.title: Positive normalized solutions for a singular regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: We study a singular Dirichlet problem driven by a regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian under a prescribed modular constraint. We construct nonnegative constrained minimizers for nonsingular approximating problems and, under the stated variational and boundary-control hypotheses, obtain a positive normalized weak solution as the reaction regularization vanishes. The approximation preserves the prescribed modular and yields subsequential strong Sobolev convergence of the states together with convergence of their constraint multipliers, while the gradient regularization remains fixed. Finally, we present a normalized singular problem on the unit disk as an illustrative example.

papers.title: Higher-Order Interactions in Complex Systems: Mechanisms, Behaviour, Representation and Reducibility
papers.abstract: Higher-order interactions couple three or more elements in ways not decomposable into pairwise contributions. They are associated with phenomenological signatures, collective thermodynamic or dynamical properties such as explosive synchronization and discontinuous transitions. Neither such signatures nor a many-body description establishes a many-body mechanism, since both depend on how the system is represented. Connecting work on higher-order network dynamics and multivariate statistical dependence, this review distinguishes the mechanism governing a system, the behaviour it produces and how either is represented.
