Behaviour comprises phenomenological signatures and statistical dependence. Representation covers which variables are included and how relations are encoded. We examine direct many-body mechanisms, nonlinear but pairwise mechanisms producing similar signatures, indirect routes through shared environments or eliminated variables, and temporal aggregation, an artefact of observation. The same behaviour can arise from different mechanisms, and a higher-order mechanism has no universal behavioural consequence. We formulate reducibility, whether a higher-order model can be replaced by a lower-order one, relative to an admissible model class, a target and a tolerance, and apply it to synchronization, ecology, statistical mechanics and contagion. Information-theoretic and inferential methods are reviewed for detecting higher-order dependence, testing lower-order alternatives and reconstructing interaction structure. What data can establish about the model is a question of identifiability, distinct from reducibility. Observational data alone cannot uniquely establish the mechanism without structural assumptions, resolved dynamics or interventions. We close with open problems in linking mechanisms to measurable signatures, coarse-graining, identifiability and causality. (Abridged)

papers.title: Affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures
papers.abstract: In 2025, the affine dual curvature measures $\widetilde{C}_m^a(K,\cdot)$ of convex body $K$ were introduced by Cai, Leng, Wu, and Xi, and the even Minkowski problem for the affine dual curvature measures was solved. In this paper, the necessary and sufficient condition of affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures with $m>1$ are proposed.

papers.title: Fractal Hyper-Trees I. Combinatorial foundations: definition, enumeration, invariants, morphisms and the algebra $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: Fractal Hyper-Trees (FHTs) are hypergraphs organized in levels: each level consists of disjoint connected clutters, and every edge strictly contains each lower component that it meets. Connected clutters and Schr{\"o}der hierarchies are the two extreme cases. Every FHT decomposes uniquely into the children of its top component, which carry smaller FHTs, and a host, an arbitrary connected clutter on these children. This gives an exact recurrence by size and depth and a species equation; the counts begin 1, 1, 4, 23, 231, 16947, 490083358 and are exact through nine vertices. Four interior moves (fusion, fission, aggregation, explosion) connect the FHTs on a given vertex set; every FHT on at least two vertices descends to the star by moves at distance at most one from the root, and $\kappa-1$, with $\kappa$ the number of edges, is its distance to the star. For FHTs with automorphism group $S\_4$, twisting the real group algebra by the sign character gives $\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{H}\oplus M\_3(\mathbb{C})$, the finite algebra of Connes' description of the Standard Model. Conversely this algebra determines the group up to isomorphism and the class of a real 2-cocycle. The axioms select neither the group nor the twist: with the twist fixed as the sign of the action on the vertices, the algebra occurs exactly when $\mathrm{Aut}\,F\cong S\_4$ and some automorphism is odd on the vertices, at every size $v\ge4$. Every finite group is the automorphism group of a flat FHT, and every faithful action on a finite connected simplicial complex is rigidified into a flat FHT with the same reduced integral homology. All computations are deposited and their kind (exhaustive, sampled, exact or numerical) is stated.

papers.title: Proposing, never assigning: fair allocation of shifts in experimental particle physics collaborations from ranked wishes under institutional quotas
papers.abstract: Experimental particle physics collaborations staff the operation of their detectors with shifts, taken in the control room or remotely by members drawn from dozens of institutions. The established practice for filling them is a credit system with self sign-up: institutions owe a quota of credit, and people take the seats they want when booking opens. This paper describes a method in which seats are instead allocated from ranked wishes under institutional quotas, the result is issued as offers that each person accepts or declines, and an independent checker recomputes every rule before anything is published: the platform proposes, never assigns, and proves that it kept the rules. The credit and quota model is inherited from current practice. Around that core the paper adds a quota rule that keeps indivisible blocks fair to institutions whose share of a period is smaller than one block, and four rules that make fairness visible beyond the count: shares of owl, weekend and holiday blocks, seats shown in the laboratory's clock and the institution's own, reachable pools for institutions that cannot travel, and booking order by balance. On a synthetic collaboration of 48 institutions and 256 eligible members, the method allocates 70 to 72 of 72 seats per period in two rounds, with a mean rank satisfaction of 84 to 95% and no rule broken; after a year of running every institution of four members or more is within 13% of its cumulative share, and the smallest institutions, which one block overshoots by arithmetic, are brought within the same range by pooling in pairs. The method is stated completely enough to be reimplemented; a reference implementation exists and is available to collaborations under license. It applies as it stands to any scientific collaboration that staffs a facility in blocks of shifts under institutional quotas.

papers.title: The smallest square tileable by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles
papers.abstract: Croft, Falconer and Guy (Unsolved Problems in Geometry, Problem C5) exhibit a tiling of the 27 x 27 square by eight pairwise incomparable integer rectangles and remark that it is not known whether 27 is the smallest side length of a square that can be tiled by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles, no restriction being placed on the number of tiles. Knuth has since stated, in a 2019 draft of a section of The Art of Computer Programming, that 27 is indeed the smallest. We give a complete, independently reproducible proof: for every integer n = 2, the n x n square admits no tiling by k pairwise incomparable integer rectangles. The proof combines two structural reductions with an exhaustive search over the 167538 surviving candidate tile sets, carried out by two independently written programs. The same search shows that at least eight tiles are needed at n = 27 and that the tile set of Croft, Falconer and Guy is the only one that tiles this square; it does so in exactly two arrangements up to symmetry. We also give explicit eight-tile tilings of the n x n square for every n >= 27, and seven-tile tilings for every n >= 34. With the classical lower bounds (every tiling of a rectangle by two or more pairwise incomparable rectangles uses at least seven, and no square of integer side less than 34 can be tiled by seven pairwise incomparable integer rectangles), this determines the least number of tiles for every square: there is no tiling for n = 34. The complete software, build instructions and output logs are included as ancillary files.

papers.title: Coherence-generating power deviation: Fluctuations and input selectivity beyond average coherence generation
papers.abstract: Coherence-generating power (CGP) tells how much coherence a quantum process produces on average from incoherent inputs, but an average can hide where that coherence comes from. We introduce the coherence-generating power deviation (CGPD), the standard deviation of the generated Hilbert--Schmidt coherence over the uniform simplex of incoherent states. CGPD turns coherence generation into a landscape: a small value signals robust production across input populations, whereas a large value reveals selective conversion of particular population imbalances. By representing unitary coherence generation as a quadratic response on population space, we obtain exact first and second moments in arbitrary finite dimension. We prove that every nontrivial unitary generator must fluctuate, and we separate this unavoidable isotropic fluctuation from excess anisotropy. The resulting distinction between average strength and input selectivity has direct consequences for benchmarking, reliability guarantees, input-ensemble susceptibility, and four-copy measurement protocols; it also extends naturally to unital quantum channels. Matched quantum-walk and quasiperiodic-transport examples show that topology and localization can leave CGP unchanged while substantially changing CGPD, revealing structure invisible to the mean alone.

papers.title: Radial Limits and Euler Exponents of a False Theta Series with Character Modulo 8
papers.abstract: Let $T_k=k(k+1)/2$ and let $N_n(q)$ be the series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}(2k+1)^{2n+1}q^{T_k}$ for $k\ge 0$. We study the false theta function $D=N_0$ and the moment quotients $N_n/D$. We prove an exact transformation formula for twists of even order. It expresses each moment as a convergent series of derivatives of the Dawson integral, with the dual twist and its phase determined by a quadratic Gauss sum. The formula gives the finite radial values of the moments at roots of unity as nonzero cyclotomic integers and yields congruences between them. Inside the unit disc we consider the quotient of $D$ by the theta series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}q^{T_k}$. Each nonconstant coefficient of this quotient is minus twice a positive integer that counts divisors and restricted partitions. These counts give a Lyndon-word formula for the exponents in the formal Euler product of $D$. The factorization also identifies the unique real zero in $(-1,1)$. A comparison with a cubic polynomial shows that this simple zero is the only zero in $|q|<1/2$.

papers.title: PlainMap: a lightweight, restartable mapping pipeline for ancient and modern DNA
papers.abstract: Mapping sequencing reads to a reference genome requires preprocessing and alignment choices that can vary with library type, fragment length, sequencing platform, and reference genome. These considerations are particularly important for ancient and historical DNA, where short and damaged fragments complicate read mapping. We present PlainMap, a lightweight and restartable mapping pipeline for modern and degraded DNA sequencing data. PlainMap accepts a simple manifest of FASTQ files, identifies single-end and paired-end data from read headers, supports heterogeneous sequencing inputs, and provides alternative mapping strategies for modern and degraded DNA. Optional pilot subsampling allows users to rapidly compare mapped fragment recovery across different settings using identical subsets of raw data, without attempting to determine the most accurate mapping strategy. Chunking and checkpoint-based execution support processing large datasets and resuming interrupted analyses, allowing users to balance memory requirements, runtime, and restartability. PlainMap produces duplicate-filtered BAM files together with fragment-aware mapping and coverage statistics. Evaluation using heterogeneous Japanese sea lion and short-fragment cave hyena datasets demonstrated successful processing across mapping modes, consistent trimmed and merged read counts across chunk sizes, and recovery from interrupted analyses without repeating completed mapping steps. PlainMap is implemented as a single Bash script and is freely available at https://github.com/BiodiversityExtinction/PlainMap.

papers.title: A Single-Loop Method with Optimal Leading-Order Oracle Complexity for Optimization and Game Stationarity in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a single-loop first-order framework for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, with matching leading-order upper and lower bounds for optimization and game stationarity in a projected zero-respecting oracle model. We propose a single-loop projected damped extragradient method coupling projected extragradient updates with dual momentum and a moving proximal center. Each iteration uses at most three gradient evaluations, without nested subproblems. For game stationarity, a deterministic best iterate has first-order residual below $\varepsilon$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-5/2})$, where $L$ is the gradient Lipschitz constant, $D_Y$ bounds the dual feasible-set diameter, and $\Delta_\phi$ is the initial-point-dependent value-function gap. For optimization stationarity, a uniformly selected iterate has expected squared Moreau-envelope gradient norm at most $\varepsilon^2$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^2D_Y\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-3})$. Matching lower bounds are $\Omega(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ for game stationarity and $\Omega(L^2D_Y\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-3})$ for optimization stationarity over projected zero-respecting first-order methods. Under dual strong concavity, the same framework achieves leading first-order oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\kappa}L\Delta_\phi\varepsilon^{-2})$ under both criteria, where $\kappa$ is the dual condition number. Matching lower bounds hold for both criteria in the same oracle model. To our knowledge, this is the first work to close the oracle complexity gap for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization under both stationarity criteria by simultaneously improving upper and lower bounds in the projected zero-respecting oracle model.

papers.title: On the clumpy nature of super-early galaxies
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has revealed that galaxies during the Epoch of Reionization are composed of compact stellar clumps spanning more than two orders of magnitude in mass and size. We present an analytical framework that connects the global properties of high-redshift galactic disks to the formation, dynamical evolution and visibility of these systems. Starting from the classical Toomre instability, we derive analytical mass-size and surface density-size relations together with, for the first time, the intrinsic clump mass spectrum obtained by integrating over the entire unstable branch of the dispersion relation. The observed clumps are naturally reproduced for turbulent velocity dispersions $\sigma\simeq 10-80\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, while their location along the mass-size relation is determined by the compactness of the parent disk. The intrinsic spectrum extends over nearly two decades in mass, $5.5\lesssim\log(M_{\rm cl}/M_\odot)\lesssim7.3$, it is transformed by gas dynamical friction, which suppresses the high-mass tail, and is consistent with the observed clump mass-function slope, $dN/dM\propto M^{-1.89}$. Massive Toomre fragments are resistant to all the stellar feedback mechanisms considered, which generally become effective only after $\gtrsim 95\%$ of the initial gas has been converted into stars. This favors high star-formation efficiencies, allowing the resulting stellar clumps to largely preserve their initial Toomre masses. The results provide the first self-consistent analytical framework connecting the formation, statistical properties and visibility of stellar clumps in super-early galaxies.

papers.title: Self-Distilled Pronunciation and Accent Control for Neural Text-to-Speech
papers.abstract: Text-to-speech that reads raw text has no lexicon: a rare word is read as guessed, and a native Japanese listener accepts a word only if its reading and pitch accent are both right. A known remedy installs a reading-and-accent channel into a released model, but it needs many recordings. This paper removes the recordings: the frozen backbone reads a sentence containing a common word it already says correctly, and that output serves as the teacher for the same sentence with the word replaced by an annotated reading with its pitch accent. Screened raters judged the tag right on 0.80 to 0.93 of unseen difficult words on four backbones spanning autoregressive, diffusion, and encoder-decoder synthesis; plain kana, which cannot express an accent, got 0.38 to 0.60. On words needing no edit, naturalness is non-inferior on one backbone; on the other three, listeners prefer the unedited rendition by 0.19 to 0.26.

papers.title: Stripe-Like Superconducting Enhancement and Coexisting Magnetic Texture in an Infinite Layer Nickelate
papers.abstract: Despite their promise as structural and electronic analogs to cuprates, nickelate thin films consistently exhibit broadened superconducting transitions in many experiments that remain poorly understood. Local measurements are ideal for revealing the presence of defects or competing phases, which may cause this transition broadening through a phase-separation. Here, we use scanning SQUID microscopy to investigate local superfluid density and magnetic texture of optimally doped $\mathrm{Nd}_{1-x}\mathrm{Eu}_{x}\mathrm{NiO}_{2}$ (NENO) (x=0.25) grown via molecular beam epitaxy. We observed a weakly-magnetic texture coexisting with superconductivity. Spatially resolved susceptibility imaging reveals a highly non-uniform superconducting state, characterized by a robust stripe-like enhancement pattern appearing near the phase transition. By resolving the mesoscopic landscape of electronic and magnetic inhomogeneities, these findings suggest that a competing magnetic phase is a primary contributor to the unusually broad superconducting transitions of these optimally doped NENO samples. Understanding the uncovered superconducting enhancement may provide a path to raising superconducting temperatures in these materials.

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Slowly Rotating Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study slowly rotating, nonlinearly charged black holes in arbitrary spacetime dimension $d \geq 4$, using a generalized Lense--Thirring ansatz. Working to linear order in the rotation parameters, we solve the Einstein--nonlinear electrodynamics (NLE) field equations for restricted theories ${\cal L}({\cal S})$ depending on single invariant. We provide an extension of the four-dimensional "No Go theorem" proven in ArXiv:2203.01919 and demonstrate the uniqueness of Maxwell theory in $d \geq 4$. Similar to four dimensions, it is proven that the standard rotation generating trick fails to produce full rotating solutions for any nontrivial NLE in higher dimensions. We identify a family of NLE theories admitting slowly rotating solutions with vector potentials encoding rotation effect in Maxwell-like manner; in four dimensions this reproduces the previously found RegMax theory, while in $d\geq4$ we obtain the corresponding electric potential in closed form and the associated Lagrangian implicitly as a function of the radial coordinate.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
papers.abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.

papers.title: Polarforming-Enabled Power-Splitting SWIPT: A GNN-Based Optimization Approach
papers.abstract: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is a critical technology for the future of the Internet of Things (IoT). However, ensuring a stable power supply in such networks remains a significant challenge. This work introduces dynamic polarization control as an additional degree of freedom (DoF) in SWIPT systems. We propose a system where both the base station (BS) and the users can adjust their antenna polarization, a technique known as polarforming. In addition, each user device is capable of splitting the incident signal to perform simultaneous information decoding (ID) and energy harvesting (EH). The resulting non-convex optimization problem, which involves strongly coupled variables, is addressed using a graph neural network (GNN) that predicts the beamforming, polarization, and power-splitting variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-based dynamic polarforming optimization significantly outperforms fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under imperfect channel state information (CSI). Moreover, joint polarforming and GNN-based optimization maintains robust SWIPT performance under both polarization mismatch and imperfect CSI.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
papers.abstract: Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

papers.title: Controlled Islanding and Reconnection with Stability Guarantees via Submodular Optimization
papers.abstract: In large-scale networked dynamical systems, local faults or disturbances may propagate through the interconnections and compromise the stability of the entire network. Partitioning the network into disjoint subsystems, or islands, limits this propagation by isolating unstable portions of the network from those that remain stable. This paper studies a two-stage controlled islanding and reconnection problem. In the first stage, the network is partitioned into stable and unstable islands. In the second stage, selected stable islands are reconnected to recover connectivity lost during islanding while satisfying stability requirements. We derive Lyapunov-based sufficient conditions for both stages. To address the coupling between the islanding and reconnection decisions, we construct an augmented graph on which the bases of a graphic matroid induce exactly the admissible islanding and reconnection pairs. We further show that the resulting optimization problem admits an equivalent nonincreasing supermodular formulation. Based on this structure, we develop a local-search algorithm with counterexample refinement and establish a performance guarantee for its inner loop with fixed sample sets. Numerical studies on linear networked systems illustrate the proposed procedure, examine its sensitivity to fault locations, and compare the proposed method with a mixed-integer linear programming benchmark in terms of solution quality and computational performance.

papers.title: Physics as the label for measuring and correcting materials reasoning in multimodal models
papers.abstract: Vision-language and language models increasingly interpret materials data, yet most benchmarks score final answers rather than whether the quantities a model states while reasoning obey established physical constraints. We introduce MatPCR, a label-free benchmark that uses six programmatic oracle families spanning diffraction geometry, microscopy scale, Raman peak structure, and Materials Project-grounded checks of near-hull stability, computed band-gap class, and net magnetization to test the physical admissibility of each checkable quantity a reasoning chain states, summarized as the Physical-Consistency Rate (PCR). The oracles are necessary-condition checks; their precision is audited by human review with interval estimates, and their recall on real responses is not assumed. Across nine models and 4,334 checkable records, overall PCR ranges from 0.556 to 0.778, and paired item-level tests separate only differences larger than about 0.07. Constraint-Grounded Self-Verification reduces oracle-detected violations in all four tested models; paired before-after scoring shows that it also raises answer correctness, but that most revisions which clear the oracle move to an admissible rather than an exact value. An open verifier reaches ROC AUC = 0.850 in distribution, varies strongly across constraint families, and does not transfer at a useful level to any held-out constraint family. An exact identity quantifies how oracle error displaces the reported PCR.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

papers.title: Coherent Floquet quantum reservoirs for molecular property prediction
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses observables of a driven quantum system to make predictions from a sequence of inputs. The robust subharmonic response of discrete time crystals (DTCs) has motivated their use as quantum reservoirs. Here we develop a DTC-QRC architecture for molecular property prediction in which successive graph events or surface-hopping frames drive a fixed Floquet reservoir. An adjustable reset probability controls how long earlier inputs influence the state, and measurements of the final polarizations and pair correlations yield a feature vector of fixed dimension. Weak reset favors classification of inhibitor activity and blood-brain barrier penetration from long graph prefixes, whereas forecasting electronic gaps in ethene favors greater weight on recent nuclear motion. With nonlinear decoding, DTC-QRC outperforms an echo-state network on these tasks at matched input lengths and readout widths. For gap forecasting with this decoder and final-state readout, the dissipative reservoirs share a low-error drive window near the DTC transition reported for related spin chains. Dephasing lowers prediction performance in both molecular applications. In six-qubit classification without programmed reset on the Quafu superconducting quantum cloud platform, pair correlations retain more of their noise-free predictive power toward the DTC side, and the full readout performs best near the transition among the drives tested. The architecture provides a common framework for molecular screening and time-resolved property prediction using quantum reservoir computing.

papers.title: Timelike Entanglement from Spacetime Density Matrices: A Lattice Realization
papers.abstract: We develop a systematic framework for timelike entanglement in a two-dimensional free real scalar field, connecting spacetime density matrices with Lorentzian twist-operator correlators through independent microscopic and continuum calculations. Extending Gaussian diagonalization to generally non-Hermitian reduced operators, we determine their complete nonzero spectra in the generic regular case, together with all integer R\'enyi moments. The real-time replica construction relates these moments to twist correlators, with quantitative agreement in both magnitude and phase for the full four-point function on a circle, the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary two-point functions, and the massive form-factor predictions. In the massless continuum theory with Dirichlet boundaries, we further establish a finite causally connected window in which all integer moments are real, while the even moments are strictly positive for arbitrary initial states. For Gaussian states, all integer moments are strictly positive, and the resulting R\'enyi entropies are real. These results demonstrate that causal connectedness alone is not sufficient for a nonzero imaginary part of timelike R\'enyi entropy.

papers.title: A Station-Based Evaluation of Machine Learning-based Weather Forecasting Models in Northern Norway
papers.abstract: Recent machine learning weather prediction (MLWP) models have demonstrated remarkable forecasting skill on global reanalysis-based benchmarks. However, their performance remains unclear in challenging environments such as Northern Norway, where narrow fjords and rapidly changing weather result in highly variable local wind conditions. In this case study, we evaluate FourCastNet3 (FCN3), GraphCast, and ECMWF High Resolution Forecast (HRES) for wind speed forecasting using multi-year station observations from Northern Norway, focusing on their relative performance, generalization beyond the training period, and performance under high-wind conditions. Our results show that HRES slightly outperforms FCN3 and GraphCast, with an overall RMSE of 2.89 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, compared to 2.96 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for FCN3 and 2.94 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for GraphCast. Notably, the MLWP models maintain comparable performance beyond their respective training periods, with no clear evidence of noticeable degradation. FCN3 performs best under high-wind conditions, although all models substantially underestimate strong winds. Our findings suggest that MLWP has become competitive with NWP for local wind, but further refinements are still needed to capture complex terrain better.

papers.title: Heteroepitaxial Growth of PbSe on InP via III-V Buffer Layers
papers.abstract: Detector cost remains a barrier to the widespread adoption of mid-wave infrared (3-5 micron) technology. PbSe, an inexpensive narrow band gap IV-VI semiconductor that has been used since the early 1940s, delivers high performance for infrared detection despite the abundance of grain boundaries in polycrystalline films. Epitaxial growth, however, could provide superior crystalline quality and interfaces, but suitable substrates remain limited for PbSe. Recent PbSe heteroepitaxy has focused primarily on III-V, II-VI and group-IV substrates that each offer a comparatively narrow range of lattice-matched alloys for heterostructure engineering. Here we show that InP-based heteroepitaxy provides access to a broader materials platform while limiting the lattice mismatch with PbSe to approximately 4%. We grow 151-nm thick PbSe films by molecular beam epitaxy on 200-nm thick In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As buffers on (001) InP substrates. Reflection high-energy electron diffraction and X-ray diffraction show (001)-oriented rock-salt PbSe with an out-of-plane lattice constant of 6.12 Angstrom on both buffers. Photoluminescence (PL) is observed from room-temperature down to 12 K and the peak wavelength red-shifts from 3.7 to 5.0 microns. Under identical measurement conditions, the room-temperature peak PL intensities from films on In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As are approximately 1.9x and 1.3x that of a PbSe on GaAs substrate reference, respectively. These results establish an InP-compatible platform for integrating narrow band-gap PbSe with a broad range of ternary and quaternary III-V alloys, including, for example, structures in which In0.53Ga0.47As serves as both a short-wave infrared absorber and a template for PbSe growth.

papers.title: The density of long runs of non-$r$-free integers
papers.abstract: Fix $r\ge2$ and let $D_k$ be the natural density of the $n$ such that none of $n+1,\dots,n+k$ is $r$-free. We prove that $\log(1/D_k)=\frac{r-1}{\zeta(r)}k\log k+\frac{r}{\zeta(r)}k\log\log k-C_rk+o(k)$, where $C_r=\frac{1}{\zeta(r)}((r-1)\log\zeta(r)+r-1+r\log\frac{\pi}{r\sin(\pi/r)})$; for $r=2$ this is $C_2=\frac{6}{\pi^2}(1+\log\frac{\pi^4}{24})=1.4595513\dots$. This determines Mirsky's constant $\alpha(h)$, the density of the $n$ with $s_{n+1}-s_n=h$ in the squarefree numbers, to the same precision. Previously the only known estimate was $\log\alpha(h)\le-\frac54 h\log\log h+O(h)$; ours improves this by a factor of order $\log h/\log\log h$, and is two-sided. The upper bound rests on the observation that the primes $p\le z$ with $\prod_{p\le z}p^r\le\sqrt k$ sieve a window of length $k$ with no freedom of alignment, so that at least $(1/\zeta(r)+o(1))k$ positions must be covered by $r$-th powers of distinct primes exceeding $k^{1/r}$. The resulting sum over injections is $m!e_m$ with $m\sim k/\zeta(r)$, evaluated by a saddle point. For the lower bound the Chung-Erdos inequality recovers the full contribution of $m!e_m$ rather than merely its largest term, which is what makes the linear coefficient explicit. As a consequence the first-moment threshold for gaps between $r$-free numbers is $\frac{\zeta(r)}{r-1}\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}(1-\frac{(1+o(1))\log\log\log x}{(r-1)\log\log x})$; for $r=2$ the constant is $\pi^2/6$, that of Erdos's 1951 lower bound. We also prove that every covering system of length $k$ has modulus at least $\exp((\frac{r}{\zeta(r)}+o(1))k\log k)$, so the Chinese remainder construction yields only $\zeta(r)/r$, half of $\pi^2/6$ when $r=2$. Erdos's bound is thus equivalent to the assertion that the first run of $k$ consecutive non-$r$-free integers occurs at the first-moment threshold, not at the scale set by the minimal modulus of a covering system.

papers.title: Effects of Interaction Range on Fluid Multicriticality: A Computational Study of an Interconverting Lattice Model
papers.abstract: The range of intermolecular interactions plays a central role in determining the nature of phase behavior and critical phenomena. It is well established through studies of the Ising model that as interaction range increases, Monte Carlo simulations progressively approach meanfield predictions as the effects of critical fluctuations are suppressed. In this work, we investigate how varying interaction range influences fluid multicriticality using an interconverting lattice model that exhibits both Ising-like liquid-gas criticality and symmetric fluid tricriticality (similar to that in the superfluid $^4$He-$^3$He mixture). This minimal model serves as a representative system for exploring the evolution of competing critical points within a generic framework. We analyze the model using both meanfield theory and three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulations while systematically varying the number of interacting neighbors, $Z_n$, from 6 to 388 on a simple cubic lattice. We find that the system with nearest-neighbor interactions ($Z_n=6$) reveals only two types of multicritical behavior, while for larger interaction ranges, four distinct archetypes emerge. We demonstrate the convergence of the simulation results to those of the meanfield theory as the number of interacting neighbors tends to infinity, and we discuss the results within the framework of crossover critical phenomena.

papers.title: Positive Temperature Coefficient of Anisotropy due to $d^6L$ Groundstate in $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$
papers.abstract: Positive anisotropy temperature coefficients ($dK/dT>0$) usually arise from hybridization between magnetic 3d states and strongly spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) subsystems. Yet $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ shows $dK/dT>0$ (125-200~K) without an obvious SOC partner. We study pure and Cr-doped $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ across the transition from low temperature incommensurate to high-anisotropy magnetic phases. We identify a $d^6L$ groundstate in $\epsilon$-Fe$_2$O$_3$ while reduced hybridization yields $d^6 + d^6L^2$ in the Cr-doped phase, highlighting metal-ligand hybridization as a route to tune magnetic, electronic and orbitronic properties.

papers.title: The phase coordinates transformation in Moyal noncommutative framework 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator and Painlev\'e second equation
papers.abstract: This work aims to explore the physical application of Moyal noncom- mutative formalism with the the presentation of new transformations which connect the old canonical coordinates to purly noncommuting phase coordi- nates through the parameters describe the Moyal noncommutative deforma- tion. These transformations are consistent with the Moyal noncommunica- tive brackets and build sixteen components traceless anti-symmetric tensor. This formalism incorporates space-space and space-momentum noncommu- taivity rather then noncommutativity (Heisenberg quantum commutation ) only for the canonical coordinates. The transformations imply to construct noncommutative analogs of 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator with its superintegrability and Painlev\'e second equation. The associated deformed Hamiltonians additionally involve some extra symmetries and reveal a deep physical understanding of about the additional symmetries with noncommunicative structure. The Painlev\'e second noncommutative coordinates transformation are also efficiently applied to generate the first Yablonskii Vorobev polynomial with Painlev\'e second parameter transformation.

papers.title: Thresholdless IBW Emission and Alpha-to-Thermal-Ion Energy Channeling via Pole Resonance of Fusion-Product Ions
papers.abstract: Fusion reactions can release a substantial fraction, and in aneutronic reactions nearly all, of their energy as the kinetic energy of fusion-product ions. In magnetized plasmas, these energetic ions can form ring distributions in velocity space. Such distributions can drive Dory-Guest-Harris (DGH) electrostatic instabilities, but these self-instabilities require a finite energetic-ion density and can be stabilized by a thermal background. We show that the same background can instead enable a distinct instability mechanism: a cyclotron pole of the minority energetic-ion susceptibility destabilizes a stable ion Bernstein wave (IBW) eigenmode. When the energetic-ion harmonic is distinct from the thermal-ion harmonics, exact root-pole resonance is thresholdless in the ideal collisionless limit. A species-resolved power balance shows that the energetic ions supply the free energy while the thermal plasma receives it. In the LAPD proton--alpha example, $99.96\%$ of the alpha-particle power loss enters the coherent proton response. This self-excited, ion-directed transfer provides a possible linear building block for alpha-particle energy channeling in proton-Boron11 fusion.

papers.title: Bounded Ratios of Lorentzian Polynomials II: Quadratic Derivatives
papers.abstract: We study bounded monomial ratios for Lorentzian polynomials. We prove that, in degree $d\geq2$ and $n$ variables, the bounded ratios from quadratic derivatives generate all bounded ratios for every $M$-convex support if and only if $n\leq3$, $d=2$, or $(n,d)=(4,3)$. For four-variable cubics, the proof uses a decomposition into $M$-concave functions. We construct explicit counterexamples with full support for four-variable quartics and five-variable cubics, then extend these two examples to all remaining pairs.

papers.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
papers.abstract: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $\gamma$, scaling as $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} - \beta_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $\beta$-$\gamma$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $\sigma_{2\gamma-\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $\sigma_{\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $\gamma$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $\sigma_\beta\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $\gamma$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $\sigma_{\gamma}\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.

papers.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.

papers.title: Seismic P- and S-wave attenuation inversion in time-frequency domain based on Kramers-Kronig relations
papers.abstract: Seismic attenuation (inverse quality factor) inversion is important for gas reservoir prediction. Two key issues in seismic attenuation inversion are the development of a physically consistent reflection coefficient equation and stable inversion of seismic attenuation from seismic data. To address these issues, this study, within the framework of isotropic linear viscoelastic media, starts from the Kramers-Kronig relations and expresses the viscoelastic stiffness matrix as a function of seismic attenuation. Under the assumptions of weak attenuation and small elastic and attenuation contrasts across the interface, a frequency-dependent PP-wave reflection coefficient equation explicitly containing P- and S-wave attenuation terms is derived using scattering theory. The derived equation not only satisfies the causality constraint but also preserves a compact mathematical form. Based on this equation, P- and S-wave attenuation are estimated by a time-frequency domain Bayesian inversion. To improve resolution and stability, the inversion adopts a recursive frequency strategy with half-power overlapping Gaussian windows, in which the result at the previous frequency serves as the prior model for the next frequency, and prior models are built from well-log rock-physics modeling to provide low-frequency constraints. Synthetic seismic data tests show that the inversion resolution and accuracy improve as the inversion frequency increases and that the method remains robust at a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 dB. Application to field seismic data further demonstrates that the P-wave attenuation anomalies effectively identify gas reservoirs, whereas S-wave attenuation is insensitive to gas reservoirs. This study provides a new approach for extracting P- and S-wave attenuation information from seismic data and achieving high-resolution prediction of gas reservoirs.

papers.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
papers.abstract: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(\alpha\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/\alpha))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(\Gamma(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/\Gamma(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(\Gamma(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_\gamma\le n)\le n/\gamma\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(\eta>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\log\gamma)/\Gamma(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([\gamma,(1+\eta)\gamma+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

papers.title: Comment on "Space-time shifted solitons and solution interactions for a generalized nonlocal nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation"
papers.abstract: Zhou and Yu [Appl. Math. Lett. 178 (2026) 109937] studied the space-time shifted NLS equation $iq_t(x,t)=q_{xx}(x,t)-2\sigma q^2(x,t) \bar{q}(x_0-x,t_0+\lambda t),\,\, \lambda=\pm 1$. They claimed that for both choices of $\lambda$ the equation is integrable. For $\lambda=-1$, however, the equation is not compatible with the standard NLS system and hence is not an integrable reduction of that system. The Hirota expansion used in the commented article does not truncate as stated; consequently the given one-soliton solution is not a solution for $\lambda=-1$. For $\lambda=1$, consistency of the shifted reduction of NLS system requires $t_0=0$ as a mandatory condition. This condition is not reported; instead $t_0$ is incorrectly treated as an arbitrary constant in the paper. The notation used in the Hirota form is misleading, and we provide a corrected form. Additionally, the equivalence between nonlocal equations with real shifts and their unshifted counterparts under translation of independent variables is clarified.

papers.title: Planetary gas gaps and kinematic signatures in the planet forming disk around WISPIT 2
papers.abstract: The giant planet formation process in disks of gas and dust surrounding young stars is observationally still poorly constrained. Direct detection of protoplanets within the disk remains limited with current facilities. Indirect observational evidence of protoplanets through substructures or deviations from Keplerian rotation in the gas remains ambiguous in absence of detected planets. The lack of the combined detection of substructures and their corresponding planets makes it challenging to connect the planet formation process to the host environment. Observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) reveal clear detections of gas gaps and kinematic signatures in the WISPIT 2 protoplanetary disk that are cospatial with the locations of previously detected giant protoplanets. The newly identified gas gaps, observed in both the 12CO integrated intensity map and its rotation curve, correspond with the previously identified gaps in scattered light. Their morphologies are shown to be consistent with eccentric gaps, as expected from planet-disk interaction models of massive planets. The lack of eccentricity in the outer disk can be explained if a third planet is present in the system. The observations of WISPIT 2 provide a long-sought empirical bridge between kinematic signatures, gas gaps and giant planet formation in disks.

papers.title: Composition-dependent nonlinear viscoelastic-viscoplastic behavior and constitutive framework for digitally mixed polymers spanning the glass transition
papers.abstract: Multi-material PolyJet printing produces voxel-scale digital mixtures of an elastomeric photopolymer (Agilus) and a glassy photopolymer (Vero), giving a material family whose room-temperature response ranges from elastomeric to glassy. Large-deformation uniaxial compression over nearly three orders of magnitude in strain rate reveals a nonlinear, rate-dependent load-unload response that evolves continuously with composition, from recoverable elastomeric hysteresis to glassy yield with post-yield softening, hardening, and substantial residual strain. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) shows that each mixture has a single glass transition temperature ($T_g$) that shifts to higher temperature with both Vero fraction and frequency, so composition acts much as temperature or loading rate does. This time-composition equivalence motivates one constitutive structure for the whole family: an equilibrium hyperelastic network with three non-equilibrium, rate-dependent branches carrying reptational, intermolecular, and glassy resistance. Its properties are anchored at the two endpoints and interpolated by smooth composition scaling laws. The model captures the compression response of all seven calibrated compositions and predicts a withheld mixture from the scaling laws alone, as well as the plane-strain compression and uniaxial tension responses of three representative compositions. Resolving the predicted stress into its branches shows the load passing from the elastomeric to the glassy mechanism, and the work from elastic storage to dissipation, as Vero content and rate rise. The glass transition that DMA maps at small strain therefore governs the large-strain deformation mechanisms. The framework gives a compact, physically based description of digitally mixed polymers and a predictive basis for designing functionally graded, architected multi-material structures.

papers.title: Classification of abstract Bose field models
papers.abstract: We classify a class of abstract Bose field models in quantum field theory up to unitary equivalence. The class includes abstract free Bose field models, abstract van Hove--Miyatake models, and infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models. Moreover, as an application of our classification, we classify quadratic interaction models. In particular, our results answer a question of A. Arai concerning the classification of infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models.

papers.title: Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative L\'evy Processes
papers.abstract: Let X be a spectrally negative L\'evy process observed up to an inde- pendent exponential time T with parameter {\gamma} > 0. We study the joint law of the maximum drawdown and the maximum drawup of X on [0, T ]. The path is decomposed according to the two possible orderings of its in- fimum and supremum. Conditional on the values of these extrema and on their ordering, the resulting pre-, intermediate, and post- components are independent. We identify their laws as Doob h-transforms of killed spec- trally negative L\'evy processes and express the corresponding distribution functions explicitly in terms of the {\gamma}-scale functions W ({\gamma}) and Z({\gamma}) and their derivatives. Combining the conditional laws with the joint densities of the extrema yields integral representations of the joint distribution and moments.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification of fatigue initiation life for powder bed fusion metal additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Predicting fatigue life with quantified uncertainties is essential for the qualification of critical components produced by laser-based powder bed fusion additive manufacturing. We present a framework that propagates microstructure and defect uncertainties directly to a fatigue initiation life distribution for a specific part. In particular, microstructure and defect characterizations are obtained from electron backscatter diffraction and micro-computed tomography scan data, which in turn inform three physics-based simulations yielding the fatigue-affecting quantities: the elastic energy release rate, the surface energy along the crack path, and the fatigue indicator parameter. Accounting for the uncertainties in these quantities and the high correlations among them due to the shared underlying microstructure, we derive a closed-form probability density function for the fatigue initiation life. This provides an analytical distribution instead of conservative deterministic predictions and enables more informed decision making for the qualification and deployment of additively manufactured components. Applying the framework to 316L stainless steel parts produced by an EOS M290 laser powder bed fusion machine, we find that both grain sizes and void distributions influence the fatigue initiation life distribution. Specifically, for a fixed total void volume fraction, larger grain sizes cause a marginal reduction in fatigue initiation life, and a population of many small voids is more favorable for fatigue life than fewer, larger voids of equivalent total volume.

papers.title: Liquid-liquid phase transitions in dipolar liquids. Insights into Supercooled Water
papers.abstract: Dipolar liquids combine two coupled degrees of freedom, translational and dipolar. Intriguingly, these two sectors can reside in distinct thermodynamic states, with the state of one sector possibly favouring a specific state of the other. The onset of ferroelectric order in dipolar liquids is an example of this mutual stabilization. Since this coupling is often encoded in interaction potentials, projecting out one sector to derive an effective interaction for the other can uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying this phenomenon. A coarse-grained theory, solved in the large-dimensional limit, in which the distance between nearest-neighbour particles depends on their dipolar interaction through a density-dependent mechanical compliance shows that a ferroelectric transition can trigger a liquid-liquid transition. It also predicts a first-order liquid-liquid transition within the paraelectric phase that, in turn, can promote ferroelectric ordering. The anisotropic dipolar-dependent soft-core interaction is shown to lead to an effective Jagla-like isotropic two-length-scale interaction, known to support liquid-liquid phase transitions. Here, however, the two-length-scale pattern depends on density and dipolar configuration, and is therefore sensitive to dipolar order. Analysis of supercooled TIP4P/Ice water molecular dynamics simulations shows that first-coordination-shell features of the pair correlation functions are sensitive to dipolar interaction, supporting the foundations of the coarse-grained theory. Comparison of low- and high-density liquid water reveals enhanced spatial anisotropy of the first coordination shell in the low-density liquid, associated, within the theory, with increased effective excluded volume, showing that the liquid-liquid transition involves structural changes within the first shell, beyond reorganization of the interstitial region and tetrahedral order.

papers.title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
papers.abstract: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of photon statistics in strong gravitational fields and for non-comoving observers, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the relativistic Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order in the relaxation time. The results reveal novel phenomena absent in flat space. At second order, the gravitational field renders the transport coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse particle and energy fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect in electromagnetism. Using the first-order results, we derive the relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks around Schwarzschild black holes. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.

papers.title: Analysis of the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states in QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: In the present work, we study the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states with the quark content $uudc\bar c$ and the quantum numbers $I(J^P)=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}^-)$ in the framework of the three-point QCD sum rules. The initial pentaquark states are described by four local diquark-diquark-antiquark type interpolating currents with definite isospin. We construct the three-point correlation functions for the decay channels $P_c\to \eta_c p$, $J/\psi p$, $\Lambda_c\bar D$, $\Lambda_c\bar D^{*}$ and $\Sigma_c\bar D$, and derive the corresponding QCD sum rules for the strong coupling constants. At the hadron side, the correlation functions are expressed in terms of the hadron masses, pole residues, decay constants and strong coupling constants. At the QCD side, they are calculated by carrying out the operator product expansion with the full quark propagators, where the vacuum condensates up to dimension 10 are taken into account. After matching the two representations and performing the double Borel transformations, we extract the strong coupling constants from the selected Lorentz structures. With the obtained coupling constants, we evaluate the partial decay widths and discuss the possible assignments of the corresponding pentaquark states. The numerical results indicate that two of the compact hidden-charm pentaquark states can be related to the $P_c(4312)$ and $P_c(4457)$, respectively, while the other two lower-mass states may be regarded as possible hidden-charm pentaquark candidates to be searched for in future experiments. The present results may be useful for identifying the hidden-charm pentaquark states in future experiments.

papers.title: Freemium Model for Information Provision
papers.abstract: The paper explores a theoretical freemium model for the sale of information in a one-buyer common-prior setting, drawing on mathematical tools used to study of repeated zero-sum games and Bayesian persuasion. Unlike standard Bayesian persuasion models, the information seller (IS) is indifferent to the actions taken by the information buyer (IB) and is concerned solely with maximizing the revenue from selling information. Offering some information for free may increase the IB's willingness to pay for additional information. The information that the IB seeks is about the state of the world. Initially, the IB only knows the prior distribution over states. The IS supplies both free and paid information through signals whose state-dependent distributions determine the IB's posterior via Bayes' rule. The IB's utility is a function of the posterior. An optimal free signal maximizes the IS's expected revenue from the subsequent paid signal, which is equal to the IB's expected utility gain when moving from the posterior induced by the free signal to that induced by the paid one. The paper characterizes the optimal free and paid signals and derives a formula for the maximal revenue in terms of the IB's utility function. It shows that a revenue gain for the IS from the provision of free information is accompanied by a loss to the IB. Whether free information can increase the IS's revenue depends on the form of the IB's utility function. In the two-state case, that dependence is fully characterized. In the general case, only necessary conditions are obtained. In particular, if the IB's utility function is convex, the IS can never profit from providing free information. This occurs, in particular, when the IB uses the information to solve a decision problem. By contrast, when the IB is engaged in a strategic interaction with a third party, the IS may benefit from providing free information.

papers.title: On the interpretation of the kinetics of ligand-receptor binding
papers.abstract: When the rates of ligand binding are measured by methods such as surface plasmon resonance, it is common practice to use the observed rate constants for the onset and offset of binding to estimate an equilibrium constant for ligand binding. If this agrees with the equilibrium constant found as the EC50 for binding at equilibrium, this is taken as validation of the measured rates. This is correct only when binding produces no conformation change in the receptor, and ligand binding follows a single exponential time course. Here, we investigate a simple 3 state model in which binding is followed by a conformation change in the receptor. Three special cases of this model in which the time course of onset and offset of ligand binding are close to being single exponentials are analysed. These cases are (1) when binding is much faster than the conformation change, (2) when the conformation change is much faster than binding, and (3) when the rates of ligand dissociation and receptor activation are both fast. It is concluded that the measured rates will often yield an estimate of the equilibrium constant for ligand binding that is close to the effective, or macroscopic, equilibrium constant, the EC50 found by measuring binding at equilibrium, which depends on both of the underlying microscopic equilibrium constants describing ligand binding and the conformation change. The exception to this conclusion is the case when binding is much faster than the subsequent conformation change, though the estimate of the equilibrium constant for ligand binding still depends on both of the underlying microscopic equilibrium constants.

papers.title: Requirements for Synthetic-Frequency Switching in Integrated Photonic Fabrics
papers.abstract: Electro-optic synthetic-frequency coupling can coherently transfer light between the frequency modes of an integrated resonator, but its value in a multiport photonic switch depends on how connections share spatial paths, frequency channels, and control signals. Here we identify two distinct architectural roles of synthetic-frequency coupling in switching fabrics and the device requirements associated with each. As a channel-assignment resource, it cannot increase the number of orthogonal channels per port, but it recovers connections blocked by fixed input frequencies or unavailable output channels. A short coupling range is sufficient. In an 8x8 fabric with eight channels per port, coupling over the first three frequency spacings achieves 95.2% of the blocking reduction of unrestricted inter-mode coupling, and the range of coupled separations matters more than the specific choice of radio-frequency tones, consistent with limited-range wavelength conversion in wavelength-division-multiplexed networks. As a spatial-switching resource, frequency control can reduce the number of spatial switching elements only through a nonseparable joint element whose spatial state is programmable for each frequency channel, whereas a separate frequency-conversion stage cannot replace missing spatial connectivity. Finally, a thin-film lithium niobate resonator model with experimentally reported coupling and decay rates, embedded in a multistage Mach-Zehnder interferometer fabric, shows that with a single shared drive the power redistributed to non-target modes and the reduced transmission of frequency-preserving paths outweigh the added connectivity. These results define the through-channel transmission, mode selectivity, and control requirements for useful synthetic-frequency switching.

papers.title: A 21-Coloring of the Plane Without Monochromatic Unit-Area Rectangles
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s and Graham asked whether every finite coloring of the plane must contain a monochromatic rectangle of any prescribed area. Kova\v{c} gave a negative answer by constructing a $25$-coloring with no monochromatic rectangle of area $1$. We reduce the number of colors to $21$ by replacing the square cells in his construction with regular hexagons.

papers.title: Physiological Information Reliability: Contextual-Bandit Allocation of Coding Redundancy and Computation in Multimodal Cardiovascular Sensing
papers.abstract: A packet can arrive intact and still be nearly worthless. On a body-worn node the radio and processor share one small battery, yet ECG and photoplethysmography (PPG) windows differ widely in how much an estimator can recover from them. We propose Physiological Information Reliability (PIR): a hand-designed window-value proxy, PIV, built from signal quality and cross-modal heart-rate agreement, joins channel, energy and compute telemetry in one state vector, and a LinUCB bandit chooses coding redundancy and processing site. Over 25 paired seeds on a synthetic burst-erasure testbed, PIR-LinUCB used 4.3% less energy than a hand-written rule, with lower error and higher delivery. A rule that also reads PIV matches it on error and delivery but spends 3.7 mJ more per window. On five real fetal ECG recordings, PIV tracked heart-rate error better than signal quality alone (mean within-record Spearman $\rho = -0.50$ against $-0.40$). The evidence is simulated, small and non-clinical.

papers.title: A remark on polycyclic groups of birational automorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an algebraic variety of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of zero characteristic. Suppose that $G$ is a virtually polycyclic subgroup in the group $\mathrm{Bir}(X)$ of birational automorphisms of $X$. We show that the virtual derived length of $G$ does not exceed $2d$. Moreover, if $X$ is a surface, the bound can be improved to $3$, and this value is optimal.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

papers.title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
papers.abstract: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $\Gamma$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.

papers.title: Sturm--Liouville-Type Parity and Oscillation of a Cubic Spline Eigenbasis
papers.abstract: We study the eigen-structure of the kernel matrix arising from cubic smoothing splines on equally spaced knots. Using matrix-theoretic methods, we show that its positive eigenvalues are simple, that the associated eigenvectors alternate between even and odd, and that the eigenvector for the $k$th largest positive eigenvalue has exactly $k+1$ sign changes. Building on established results on oscillatory and centrosymmetric matrices, we provide a more explicit proof of the known oscillation property of the eigenvectors and establish their alternating parity. We then verify, by a separate argument, that both properties extend to the associated continuous cubic spline eigenfunctions, showing that the resulting spline basis exhibits both an alternating parity structure and an oscillation pattern analogous to that of classical Sturm--Liouville eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Teleparallel formulation of $E_{8(8)}$ Exceptional Field Theory
papers.abstract: The potential of $E_{8(8)} \times \mathbb{R}^+$ exceptional field theory, suited for studying three-dimensional maximally supersymmetric compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, is derived in teleparallel formulation. This means that, starting from an ansatz of the most general combination of the quadratic scalar contractions of the intrinsic torsion, which is manifestly invariant under generalised diffeomorphisms, one selects the potential by imposing the invariance under infinitesimal rotation of the maximal compact subgroup of the duality group. The teleparallel formulation makes manifest at geometric level the preeminent role of the intrinsic torsion in studying compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, where the intrinsic torsion is identified with the embedding tensor of the resulting gauged supergravity.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM-based AI agents integrated with materials synthesis tools: the case of atomic layer deposition
papers.abstract: This work provides an overview of the different strategies that can be used to evaluate the performance of AI models and agents based on large language models (LLMs) for materials synthesis. After providing a brief overview of the key technologies behind the current generation of AI agents based on LLMs, we summarize the different approaches to evaluating these models in the context of materials science and in particular on materials synthesis, with a specific emphasis on scenarios in which the models are directly integrated with experimental tools. We discuss evaluation strategies spanning knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, tool-use benchmarks, and closed loop benchmarks involving the interaction with experimental systems or realistic virtual tools. We use atomic layer deposition (ALD) as a case study, emphasizing how existing approaches in the literature both build from general approaches used beyond materials science and can be generalized to other materials synthesis techniques. Finally, we provide a practical evaluation framework to evaluate LLMs in the context of materials synthesis

papers.title: Fermion mass hierarchies in a three-generation Clifford model
papers.abstract: We examine whether an algebraic model of three fermion generations based on the complex Clifford algebra $\mathbb C\ell(10)$, in which an $S_3$ family symmetry relates the generations, can reproduce the observed mass hierarchies of the charged leptons and down quarks. Taking the internal Gram matrix as the fermion kinetic metric, we show that the original Yukawa interaction, with complex coefficients, gives precisely those ordered mass triples $0\leq m_1\leq m_2\leq m_3$ for which $m_3\leq m_1+2m_2$. This restriction excludes the observed hierarchies in both sectors and persists when the right-acting Higgs operator is allowed to range over the full Clifford algebra. This obstruction motivates a second Yukawa contraction in which a projector, constructed from the difference between an internal charge operator and its family average, acts from the left. The resulting interaction preserves the gauge and family symmetries and uses the same three Higgs doublets. With both contractions present, there is a fixed coupling ratio at which the two successive mass ratios in a single sector become arbitrarily large along a real vacuum path. Separately, a rational interval calculation establishes that one real Higgs vacuum, with different coupling ratios in the two sectors, reproduces the chosen running masses of the charged leptons and down quarks. A softly broken three-doublet potential realises this vacuum as a global minimum at tree level. The additional neutral scalars have flavour-changing couplings, and their exchange at a common mass of $2000\,\mathrm{TeV}$ satisfies the neutral-meson mixing criterion and the $\mu\to3e$ contact-interaction test considered here.

papers.title: The inverse eigenvalue problem for Partial Transposes of Two-Qubit States and Sharp Entanglement Bounds from Their Low-order Moments
papers.abstract: The negativity of a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho$ can be determined without full state tomography by measuring sufficiently many partial-transpose (PT) moments on multiple copies of $\rho$. When the available copies allow only low-order PT moments to be estimated reliably, how tightly do these moments bound the negativity? For two-qubit states, we answer this question by solving the inverse eigenvalue problem for their partial transposes: an ordered eigenvalue list $(x,y,z,-q)$, with $x\ge y\ge z\ge0$, $q>0$, and $x+y+z-q=1$, occurs as the spectrum of $\rho^{\Gamma_B}$ for some two-qubit state $\rho$ if and only if $q\le y$ and $qy\le xz$. The quantum steering ellipsoid of the $X$ state constructed to prove sufficiency gives a geometric interpretation of the two equality cases. We use these inequalities to determine the exact range of negativity compatible with the two lowest nontrivial PT moments, $p_2=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^2]$ and $p_3=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^3]$. We also compare our sharp negativity bounds with estimates from several existing methods and quantify how much the inverse eigenvalue constraints narrow the negativity interval as a function of $p_3$ at fixed $p_2$. Beyond negativity, we extend this approach to derive attainable bounds for the maximal CHSH value and directional coherent information at fixed $p_2$ and $p_3$. Our result establishes the strongest possible bounds on the negativity of an unknown two-qubit state from just two experimentally accessible PT moments, and shows the potential for obtaining similarly sharp bounds from low-order PT moments by solving the corresponding inverse eigenvalue problem for higher-dimensional bipartite states.

papers.title: Strangeness, entropy, and chemical non-equilibrium from p+p to Pb+Pb: the $K^+/\pi^+$ horn on the system-size axis
papers.abstract: The maximum ("horn") of the $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ excitation function in central Pb+Pb collisions near $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.6$ GeV is interpreted as the competition between strangeness production and the faster rise of entropy production at the onset of deconfinement. Statistical hadronization analyses by Letessier, Rafelski, and collaborators have shown that the horn is described quantitatively only if the light-quark phase-space occupancy $\gamma_q$ is free, with $\gamma_q$ near the pion condensation limit from 30$A$ GeV upward. We carry this analysis along the system-size axis provided by NA61/SHINE (p+p, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, preliminary Xe+La) and NA49 (Pb+Pb). Our main new result is the first non-equilibrium analysis, to our knowledge, of the Be+Be and Ar+Sc $4\pi$ multiplicities, published in 2021 and 2024: in Ar+Sc, chemical equilibrium of light quarks ($\gamma_q = 1$) is disfavored, but through the $K^+/K^-$ asymmetry rather than the pion yields, while the Be+Be data do not discriminate. For central Pb+Pb, our fits to the final NA49 data confirm the earlier result, most robustly at 30$A$-80$A$ GeV; the preference rests on the excess of produced hadrons per net baryon and on the Bose-Einstein enhancement of pions. Decomposing $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ into strangeness and pion yields per wounded nucleon, we find that the step between Be+Be and Ar+Sc is carried by a doubling of strangeness per participant, whereas the horn appears only in Pb+Pb, where the pion yield per participant is suppressed at 20$A$-40$A$ GeV. Parton-hadron transport (PHSD) reproduces the Pb+Pb horn but predicts one also in Ar+Sc and Xe+La, where none is observed.

papers.title: Formation of black hole stars via star--black hole collisions
papers.abstract: In dense stellar environments such as globular clusters and active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks, stellar-mass black holes (sBHs) may frequently collide with massive stars.
