We investigate this process using semi-analytic models, three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations, and one-dimensional stellar evolution calculations, focusing on collisions between sBHs and a $M_\star=100\,M_\odot$ main-sequence star with a radius $R_\star=16\,R_\odot$. We find that gas drag retains the BH within the stellar envelope unless the impact velocity exceeds $\sim2\sqrt{G(M_\star+M_\bullet)/R_\star}$. The post-collision outcome depends primarily on the BH-to-star mass ratio. For $M_\bullet\gtrsim30\,M_\odot$, the retained envelope is either quasi-spherical or disk-like, but remains dynamically unstable because of shock heating. In contrast, for $M_\bullet\lesssim10\,M_\odot$, the collision forms a ``black hole star'' (BH*): a quasi-hydrostatic, extended stellar envelope surrounding the embedded BH. These results agree with our analytic prediction that BH* formation necessarily requires $M_\bullet\lesssim0.2\,M_\star$. Follow-up \texttt{MESA} calculations further show that, for these low-mass BHs, the shock-heated remnant thermally relaxes without triggering runaway expansion. We discuss several astrophysical implications of BH*s, including their evolution, the possibility of gravitational-wave events from BH binaries assembled within a stellar envelope, and repeated star--sBH collisions as a pathway for rapid BH growth in dense stellar systems. This mechanism may contribute to the formation of massive BHs in high-redshift nuclear star clusters and may be relevant to the origin of the ``little red dots'' discovered by JWST.

papers.title: Dynamical formation of high-eccentricity compact binaries through BH--BH*/TZO collisions
papers.abstract: The rapidly accumulating discoveries of binary stellar-mass black-hole (sBH) coalescences, detected by LIGO, have opened a new window into the formation and evolution of compact binaries. In particular, residual orbital eccentricity may provide a distinctive signature of their formation channels. Here, we investigate a scenario in which high-eccentricity compact binaries form through the sequential capture of multiple sBHs by massive main-sequence stars, using a combination of hydrodynamical and semianalytic few-body simulations. We find that sBHs with $M_\bullet\lesssim 0.2\,M_{\star}$ can be captured by massive stars and settle into a quasi-hydrostatic black-hole star (BH*) through gas dynamical friction. A subsequent encounter with a second sBH can then produce a compact binary embedded within the stellar envelope. Our hydrodynamical simulations show that through captures with small impact parameter, some binaries are born with high eccentricity ($e\gtrsim 0.5$), with its orbital frequency already entering the LISA band. Our semianalytic models further demonstrate that gas dynamical friction can pump the eccentricity to $e_{\rm 10\,Hz}>0.9$ before gravitational-wave emission eventually circularizes the binary during the final stage of coalescence. Once formed, the binary can merge quickly in $\sim 10$ hours. This channel may operate in dense stellar environments, such as star clusters and active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks. The same mechanism can also be applied to Thorne-\.Zytkow objects. A high-eccentricity binary in the LIGO band could therefore provide a distinctive signature of this formation scenario.

papers.title: Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
papers.abstract: Recently, three related papers [arXiv:2412.13941, arXiv:2009.00897, arXiv:2409.03626] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [arXiv:1410.2540] using stackings and by [arXiv:1410.2579] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [arXiv:2412.13941] and [arXiv:2409.03626]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.

papers.title: Orbits of submaximal dimension for Sylow $p$-subgroups of finite classical orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup in a classical orthogonal group over a finite field with $q$ elements of characteristic $p$ large enough. The coadjoint orbits of the group $U$ play the key role in the description of irreducible complex characters of $U$. In the paper, we provide a classification of such orbits of pre-maximal dimension. As a corollary, we compute the number of all orbits mentioned above. It turned out that each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q - 1$ with integer non-negative coefficients, which agrees with the Isaacs' conjecture.

papers.title: Exact pair density wave in topological moire flat bands and universal superfluid stiffness
papers.abstract:
Pair-density waves (PDWs) are unconventional superconducting states beyond the BCS paradigm, but identifying them unambiguously in microscopic lattice models is generally challenging due to various competing orders. In particular, an exact realization of PDW in interacting models with topological bands remains elusive. Here we construct an interacting model on a twisted bilayer checkerboard lattice (TBCB) featuring topological flat bands, and rigorously show that an exact PDW ground state can be induced by quantum geometric nesting (QGN), owing to its momentum-space nonsymmorphic symmetry. We further prove that the superfluid stiffness of any nondegenerate QGN superconductor (including the PDW studied here and uniform superconductor) obeys the universal relation $D_s=2N_{m flat}
u(1-
u)m_{m pair}^{-1}$, where $N_{m flat}$, $
u$, and $m_{m pair}$ are the number of flat bands, flat band filling, and the two-particle effective mass, respectively. Our results reveal a rich interplay among PDW order, quantum geometry, and band topology.

papers.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction \xi of the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming \xi\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.

papers.title: Approximating thermodynamic equilibrium observables of quasi one-dimensional magnetic molecules and chains by thermal DMRG - a user perspective
papers.abstract: Density matrix renormalization group methods or tensor network methods in general can not only be used to determine ground states but also to evaluate thermal equilibrium properties. Although convergence is superior for one-dimensional quantum spin systems with nearest neighbor exchange and open boundary conditions, the hope is that these methods can as well be employed to approximate magnetic observables of magnetic molecules with more complex interaction patterns. Here, we assume the position of a user and study the accuracy that can realistically be achieved for several archetypical quasi one-dimensional structures using the TenPy suite. In our study, we aim at systems that are too large for exact diagonalization or Krylov space methods.

papers.title: Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
papers.abstract: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder-based network is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.

papers.title: Geometric Propulsion of a Scallop with Control-Dependent Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study a force-free single-hinge swimmer driven by two controls. When its axial hydrodynamic connection depends only on the opening angle, we show that the mean displacement per cycle vanishes in the periodic state at any driving rate. An independent control of the hydrodynamic response removes this restriction. For a factorized connection, the displacement at arbitrary driving rate is an integral of a measurable shape moment against the hydrodynamic modulation; in the slow-driving limit it reduces to a curvature flux which, at fixed potential and connection, is independent of the shape mobility. A reflecting harmonic model illustrates how thermal fluctuations modify this flux without generating it, and a hinged-bead model with variable passive slip gives a quantitative opening--closing test of the mechanism. We distinguish these propulsion results from the leading shape-sector dissipation, which depends on the mobility and is governed by a thermodynamic metric.

papers.title: Direct, Collision-Operator-Free Simulation of Electron-Ion Transport in Magnetized and Unmagnetized Plasmas
papers.abstract: Accurate electron-ion collision models are central to predicting transport in fusion and space plasmas, yet collision operators and Monte Carlo collision models assume that a charged particle meets one partner at a time and that its successive encounters are independent. However, an electron that turns back along the magnetic field passes the same ions again. We solve the Newton-Lorentz equations for test electrons among static ions with a prescribed Debye-screened potential. The method combines force summation within an interaction radius, a time-symmetric particle pusher, and adaptive time stepping, enabling stable and scalable simulations in unmagnetized and magnetized plasmas. Using simulation-based measures of momentum relaxation and cross-field diffusion, we compare the simulations with a reference in the same model that treats every encounter as independent. Without a magnetic field the scattering rate reproduces the binary-collision rate for the same potential to within 2%. When the gyroradius is smaller than the Debye length, the scattering rate stays within 10% of the reference, but the cross-field diffusion coefficient exceeds it by a factor that grows with the field, up to 17. The excess comes from repeated passes of the same ions, whose guiding-center displacements add up: when the ions are replaced by new random ones many times per scattering time, so that a returning electron meets different ions, most of the excess disappears. The framework therefore provides a computational benchmark for testing and improving reduced collision operators and transport models.

papers.title: Native-Space 3D CarveMix for Multi-Site T1w Stroke Segmentation
papers.abstract: Segmenting ischemic stroke lesions on T1-weighted (T1w) MRI acquired across different scanners and protocols without intensity standardization is difficult because lesions are subtle and share intensity characteristics with cerebrospinal fluid. Standard deep learning architectures trained across multiple centers plateau around Dice 0.66, with acute lesions ($\le 7$ days post-stroke) performing substantially worse due to severe sample scarcity. We combine a MedNeXt-L ($k=5$) backbone with on-the-fly 3D CarveMix augmentation that pastes real lesion patches into recipient training patches. By generating synthetic lesion placements dynamically within each fold with subject-level split isolation, the model sees more diverse lesion patterns without requiring pre-generated copies on disk. We evaluate on 1,453 native T1w scans from 55 clinical centers in the ISLES 2026 challenge. MedNeXt-L with CarveMix achieved a mean five-fold cross-validation Dice of 0.648 after 500 epochs. For comparison, the estimated Dice for plain MedNeXt-L at epoch 500 was 0.630, obtained by interpolation from its 1,000-epoch training trajectory.

papers.title: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
papers.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linear elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

papers.title: Brans Dicke scalar-tensor gravity and unimodular FRW cosmology with Coleman-Weinberg potential
papers.abstract: As an alternative gravity theories with respect to General Relativity, the Brans-Dicke scalar-tensor model is well known, in which the Brans-Dicke parameter the controls the best fit observational, and so its cosmological model is studied in the literature well. On the other side, the Coleman-Weinberg self-interaction scalar field potential coming from radiation corrections of Feynman diagrams is used to describe the best fit cosmic inflation phase and reheating phase. We study inflation in unimodular Brans-Dicke gravity with a Coleman-Weinberg potential. We investigate the observational constraints on the Brans-Dicke parameter \(\omega\) and identify its allowed range in light of current cosmological data. Also, in the slow-roll regime, we derive inflation parameters and study the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ in terms of the model parameters, and determine the region of the parameter space allowed by observations. Comparing these predictions with the P-ACT-LB-BK18 constraints, we find that the model is consistent with the data at the $95\%$ CL level for $77\lesssim\omega\lesssim1148$ and within the $ 68\% $ CL for $134\lesssim\omega\lesssim272$.

papers.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
papers.abstract: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.

papers.title: Quantifying AI data center nitrogen oxide (NO$_x$) emissions from space
papers.abstract: AI data center power demand is spurring rapid deployment of on- and near-site natural gas turbines. The resulting nitrogen oxide NO$_x$ pollution is a growing concern but has not previously been quantified with atmospheric observations. Here we demonstrate space-based detection and quantification of NO$_x$ emissions from the SpaceXAI Colossus 2 power plant in Southaven, Mississippi. Using observations from the geostationary TEMPO satellite instrument, we detect a strong increase in local mean NO$_2$ column concentrations after the plant began operations in late 2025. We then use TEMPO to estimate two-week-average NO$_x$ source rates from August 2025 to August 2026, calibrating against continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) data from US power plants. TEMPO first detected NO$_x$ emissions in December 2025 at 530$\pm$220 kg h$^{-1}$. We find that emissions increased through August 2026, averaging 870$\pm$165 kg h$^{-1}$ after February 2026, roughly 19$\pm$4 times higher than expected from the facility's March 2026 permit for 41 turbines operating under best available control technology (BACT) requirements ($\sim$47 kg h$^{-1}$). Emissions at the expected level would be undetectable by our TEMPO analysis.

papers.title: Pinchoff by surface diffusion
papers.abstract: Since Nichols and Mullins analysed the instability of cylindrical wires in 1965, numerical and asymptotic studies have predicted a self-similar neck at pinchoff under surface diffusion. Yet even the existence of a finite-time singularity for the flow of a smooth closed surface has remained open. We construct the first such examples, and establish their stability, modulo a finite-dimensional space. The same shrinking neck closes the central hole of an embedded torus in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and separates the lobes of a genus-zero dumbbell. In both cases the surface remains embedded until the singular time $T$ and converges smoothly away from the pinching point. Writing $A(t)$ for the waist radius and $r(z,t)$ for the radius near the neck, we prove that $A(t)=\{4\mu(T-t)\}^{1/4}(1+o(1)), \quad A(t)^{-1}r(A(t)\zeta,t) \longrightarrow U(\zeta) \quad\text{in }C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}).$ The profile $U$ above is also for the first time rigorously constructed here. It was numerically computed by Wong-Miksis-Voorhees-Davis, and identified by Bernoff-Bertozzi-Witelski as the ground state of a family of conical shrinkers. Our proof also yields a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows that admit positive symmetric conical shrinkers.

papers.title: Polynomial permutation stability, soficity, and universal polynomial groups
papers.abstract: We introduce polynomial permutation stability for maps between groups, extending ordinary permutation stability from homomorphisms to polynomial maps defined by iterated finite differences. We show that a group $G$ is polynomially permutation stable in degree $s$ if and only if its universal polynomial group $\operatorname{Pol}_s(G)$ is permutation stable. While every finite group is polynomially permutation stable in degree two, we prove that the cyclic group of order six is not stable in degree three. More precisely, we construct a finite-index direct-product subgroup of $\operatorname{Pol}_3(C_6)$ to which an instability theorem of Ioana applies. We also show that polynomial sofic approximations characterize the usual class of sofic groups. In degree two, we obtain a split exact sequence relating $\operatorname{Pol}_2(G)$ to a restricted wreath product, with applications to soficity and property $(T)$. A quotient-transfer principle yields infinite, finitely presented, nonperfect groups that are polynomially permutation stable in every degree. Finally, we obtain nonamenability and largeness results for higher-degree universal polynomial groups of finite groups.

papers.title: Photonic Weyl Points and Fermi Arc Surface States in a Self-Assembling Zinc-Blende Colloidal Crystal
papers.abstract: We characterize the design, photonic band structure, and self-assembly of a colloidal crystal capable of supporting robust topological Weyl points and Fermi arc surface states in 3D. To achieve this, we propose a new zinc-blende structure, built off of recent progress in self-assembling diamond photonic crystals, which lacks inversion symmetry and supports photonic Weyl points. Furthermore, we show that the geometry can be optimized to make the Weyl point and its Fermi arc surface states experimentally observable in the photonic crystal's projected band structure. Finally, we perform molecular dynamics simulations to demonstrate that the geometry we propose for observing Weyl points is capable of being self-assembled with realistic interparticle interactions. Together, these results provide a platform for the assembly of large-scale photonic crystals supporting topological degeneracies and robust Fermi arc surface states in the visible and near-infrared.

papers.title: Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics
papers.abstract: Web studies often measure what happens after a user action, such as a search after a chatbot answer. To credit an AI answer with later commercial activity, a study must separate what the answer caused from what the user would have done anyway. But people act in the middle of activity already underway, so the activity that drives what follows also chooses when the clock starts. We call this endogenous time zero. Using an opt-in panel that links conversational-AI use, browsing, and search, we insert inert timestamps (moments that match recent activity but mark no event) and rerun the standard analysis. In a pre-registered replication, these timestamps, which by construction cannot cause anything, reproduce 76% of the search increase after AI responses that follow recent browsing. Other users matched on 30-day activity, the usual control, give the same answer, and inert timestamps show a similar search excess across 16 kinds of Web events. Comparing with moments of matching recent history removes most of the increase, but no placebo audit we ran could confirm that this comparison is unbiased, and published studies almost never run one. We give a protocol for choosing comparisons and stress-testing estimators.

papers.title: Fujiki Class $\mathcal C$ Varieties and a K\"ahler Criterion
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that flips and divisorial contractions preserve the K\"ahler condition (for strongly $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial compact K\"ahler generalized klt pairs with $B+\beta_X$ big), and we give a criterion for varieties in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$ to be K\"ahler. We also prove the existence of small $\mathbb Q$-factorializations for generalized klt pairs and of dlt modifications for generalized pairs.

papers.title: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
papers.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-K\"ahler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

papers.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
papers.abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, leading to incorrect model selection in settings such as deep learning. The Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion (WBIC) relies on local learning coefficients $\lambda$, which in the analytic case coincides with local Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the model, to capture correct marginal likelihood asymptotics. Exact computation of the learning coefficients has been limited to special cases, and only sampling-based estimation methods are generally applicable. We present the first deterministic algorithm that computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose Kullback-Leibler distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, derive a bound on its complexity, and demonstrate its effectiveness for a broad class of models, with applications including polynomial neural networks. Beyond providing ground truth to calibrate sampling-based estimators, exact computation reveals algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot and out-speeds it in the shallow regime.

papers.title: Geometry-Encoded Multireceiver Fluorometry Affords Full-Range Nonlinear Quantification under the Primary Inner Filter Effect
papers.abstract: The inner filter effect (IFE) transforms the nominally linear fluorescence-concentration relationship into a geometry-dependent and often nonmonotonic response, resulting in reduced sensitivity, concentration ambiguity, and inaccurate underestimation at high optical densities. Here, we introduce a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that does not eliminate or correct the IFE, but instead harnesses the spatial fluorescence attenuation induced by IFE as an additional quantitative encoding dimension. Fluorescence generated along the excitation axis is integrated over independently positioned receiver windows, and concentration is recovered by nonlinear optimization of the joint fluorescent intensity vector. Tryptophan was selected as a biomedically relevant model fluorophore to validate the proposed strategy. Single-window calibration exhibited vanishing-gradient boundary and two-valued concentration inversions, whereas two spatially separated receiver windows restored global identifiability across the full concentration range. Screening of 35 two-receiver geometries identified the minimum-uncertainty configuration, achieving an average 95% error half-width of mean E_95= 0.884 mg/L, and the maximum-sensitivity configuration, reaching a noise-normalized response sensitivity of mean S_N=3.832 a.u./(mg/L). By converting spatial attenuation into a multidimensional concentration coordinate, this approach extends quantitative fluorescence analysis without dilution, a separate absorbance measurement, or piecewise calibration and provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence metrology even under strong IFE conditions.

papers.title: 3D trapping of a meta-atom in an intensity minimum
papers.abstract: High-refractive-index particles have recently attracted a growing interest in optical manipulation, enabling to engineer optical forces through electromagnetic Mie resonances. Unlike standard silica particles, which exhibit trap frequencies mainly determined by material density, resonant meta-atoms formed by high-index particles enable qualitatively new trapping behaviors. In this work, we experimentally investigate the trapping of resonant silicon particles in an optical standing wave. A direct comparison of silicon and silica highlights the fundamental differences in their optical force scaling and trapping dynamics. Beyond conventional trapping at intensity-maxima, we demonstrate deterministic and stable three-dimensional trapping of silicon nanoparticles in optical intensity minima, a regime that remains inaccessible for silica particles. Drawing a mesoscopic analogy with blue-detuned atom trapping, our results establish meta-atoms as a versatile approach to further extend the optical manipulation tool box towards accessing novel trapping regimes e.g. in close proximity to a surface.

papers.title: Three-body forces in the quark model
papers.abstract: We review the connection between constituent-quark Hamiltonians and QCD and investigate the long-standing difficulty of describing meson and baryon spectra with one common two-body interaction. A Hamiltonian calibrated to ground-state mesons leaves systematic baryon mass residuals, largest in the light-quark sector and decreasing toward heavier flavors. We show that a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction substantially reduces this incompatibility. Mass-scaled finite-range profiles yield high-accuracy baryon spectra, whereas flavor-independent common-range profiles do not remove the residual flavor pattern. The result is tested on additional ground-state baryons outside the calibration set and through meson--baryon compatibility analyses across several alternative quark-model Hamiltonians. We also benchmark radial and orbital excitations to identify the regime in which a static compact valence Hamiltonian remains reliable, and provide explicit color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark configurations. Within the tested valence-space representations, the results indicate that a mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction provides the missing contribution required for a consistent simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra.

papers.title: Entrywise Positivity Preservers on Green Matrices
papers.abstract: We classify entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness on Green matrices with positive parameters. For each fixed \(n\ge2\), PSD preservation is equivalent to \(f\) being nondecreasing and \((f(tr^{i+j}))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) being PSD for all \(t>0,r>1\). For \(f\in C^{2n-2}\), this is equivalent to \(f'\ge0\) and positive semidefiniteness of \(((t\,d/dt)^{i+j}f(t))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) at every positive \(t\). These fixed-order classes strictly decrease with \(n\); their intersection consists exactly of \(f(t)=\int_{[0,\infty)}t^\alpha\,d\mu(\alpha)\), where \(\mu\) is a finite positive measure and the integral is finite for every \(t>0\). At each fixed order, entrywise Loewner monotonicity is equivalent to \(f\in C^1\) and \(f'\) belonging to the corresponding PSD preserver class. In all orders, monotonicity itself implies smoothness. Nonnegative minors of orders one and two on every strict three-by-three Green input already force \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(t)=ct^\alpha\), with \(c>0\) and \(\alpha\ge0\). They give TN output in every order; the nonzero members also preserve PSD Green structure. We also classify PSD, TN, and Loewner-monotone extensions to the closure allowing zero entries. No regularity is assumed except in the differential criterion.

papers.title: High-Harmonicity Planar Penning Traps for Single-Electron Qubits
papers.abstract: We present a detailed account of the design choices required for planar Penning traps that feature a highly harmonic confining potential. High harmonicity is indispensable for a number of applications, particularly for confinement of single electrons as qubits in quantum-information processing. The present work extends previous studies [J. Goldman and G. Gabrielse, Phys. Rev. A 81, 052335 (2010)] by a fully analytic treatment of finite electrode gaps and their relevance for small traps on the millimeter size scale and below, when relative gap sizes are non-negligible. We derive the overall trap potential with a particular focus on different models of finite-gap potentials and show how to find the optimum trap geometry and electrode voltages to minimize anharmonicities. The analytic calculations are compared with detailed finite-element simulations.

papers.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate how the one-loop running of local couplings in weakly nonlocal, super-renormalizable completions of $R+R^{2}$ gravity affects the predictions of the Starobinsky model. Our study is motivated by the larger scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by recent data. For a canonical inflaton at first order in slow roll, we derive the response of the observables to an arbitrary fractional deformation $\Delta$ of the Einstein-frame potential $V$. We find that it is governed by $\mathcal{R}[\Delta]=(V/V')\Delta'$, and that the shift of the logarithm of the slow-roll parameter is twice the logarithmic derivative of the trajectory average of $\mathcal{R}$. This provides a test which requires one differentiation only. Deformations with constant $\mathcal{R}$, which we call removable, change the E-model exponent and shift $n_s$ at $O(\ln N/N^{2})$ only, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds, while $\mathcal{R}\propto N^{k}$ gives $\Delta n_s=[2k^{2}/(k+1)]\mathcal{R}/N$. When the running is improved at the Einstein-frame Hubble rate, the renormalization-group time is half the logarithm of the tree-level potential and the gravitational flow is removable. Under a naturalness condition, a matching to the nonlocality scale yields $|\Delta n_s|\lesssim3\times10^{-4}$, a factor of about $30$ below the shift preferred by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). However, for a scale tied to the Jordan-frame curvature, the same flow is not removable and $\Delta n_s\simeq K/3$, where $K$ is a linear combination of the running parameters. Removability is a property of the flow together with the scale prescription. None of the deformations proposed since ACT DR6 that raise $n_s$ to the preferred value is removable. These results hold within a projected truncation of the local couplings and a first-order improvement of the potential.

papers.title: Boundary Layers and Finite-Section Asymptotics for Small Polygons
papers.abstract: In large even polygons of unit diameter, computed angle profiles oscillate near the vertex carrying the pendant diameter. We study the half-line variational problem behind this observation of Bingane and Mossinghoff. Its unique positive equilibrium approaches the regular state with alternating multiplier $(-3+\sqrt5)/2$. We determine the sharp energy errors for two ways of closing a finite section and enclose the limiting cubic coefficient in a rational interval of width below $9.4\times10^{-29}$. An explicit scaling identifies these energies with the cubic coefficients of the finite polygon constructions. Transferring the profile to unrestricted area maximizers is a further, conditional result: under the stated geometric hypothesis, the profile gives the $n^{-3}$ term of their maximal area. The recurrence, its finite-section estimates and the enclosure can be checked independently of that hypothesis.

papers.title: Social Learning with Selective Sampling
papers.abstract: This paper studies social learning when some types of actions are more likely to be sampled by successors than others. We show that Bayesian agents can achieve learning even without expanding observations, because the endogenous observation network itself carries information and agents can correct for selection bias. For nonanonymous sampling, we establish sufficient and pairwise necessary conditions of the sampling procedure for learning, which coincide in the binary state-matching model to yield an exact characterization. We also show that stationary anonymous sampling permits asymptotic learning, as agents can correct for selection bias using inverse-probability weighting. Finally, we demonstrate that asymptotic learning can fail under arbitrarily small misspecification of the sampling procedure.

papers.title: Reference-free logged energy-oracle recovery for neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems: conforming Riesz reconstruction and archive-level selection
papers.abstract: Neural PDE training yields a finite checkpoint archive, yet its logged energy errors are inaccessible without the exact solution, while loss-based selection does not necessarily recover the logged energy oracle. For admissible neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems, we introduce a reference-free selection rule based on minimizing a computable conforming Riesz monitor. The exact residual-energy identity and conforming projection make the monitor an unconditional lower bound converging monotonically to each logged energy error under nested conforming refinement; under saturation, hierarchical enrichment yields a computable upper estimate and hence a lower-upper bracket. A key finding is that archive selection is order-sensitive: unresolved checkpoint-dependent components can reverse the oracle-non-oracle ranking at finite resolution, so checkpointwise recovery alone is insufficient. For finite archives, we prove uniform recovery, yielding convergence to the logged-oracle error and, without saturation, logged-oracle selection at sufficiently fine auxiliary resolution. Under saturation, the bracket gives a computable near-oracle bound and certifies unique logged-oracle selection upon interval separation. We also bound logging-resolution loss and certify oracle inclusion over prescribed comparison trajectories. Experiments on diffusion and elasticity, including a non-manufactured perforated plate, demonstrate energy-scale calibration, oracle-level selection, and modest post-processing cost. This work frames neural checkpoint selection as an ordering problem, establishes projection-based reliability guarantees beyond checkpointwise error estimation and loss-error equivalence, and opens directions for variational loss design and more general selection theory.

papers.title: Second-Order Response Laws for LLM Judges:From Prompt Stability to Decision Quality
papers.abstract: LLM judges are used to compare models and select responses, yet a judge can change its verdict when a prompt is reworded. The change may come from the wording or from the randomness of another call. Confusing the two can distort model comparisons and response selection, but they are hard to separate with few repeated calls, and plug-in prompt-dispersion scores mix them. We develop a framework that connects measurements of judge variability to decision quality. It rests on second-order response laws, which describe how verdict distributions vary across prompts. Crossing prompts with candidate orders separates prompt, position, interaction, and call variation, and agreement between distinct calls removes the finite-call bias. We derive the corrected estimator's exact variance and matching bounds for detecting weak prompt effects under a fixed, balanced design. In over one million judgments from six judges on three benchmarks, the correction changes conclusions. On a matched panel, it reverses the estimated Qwen--Gemma-3 ranking by prompt sensitivity. Lowering the sampling temperature (cooling) makes Qwen's calls more consistent while its corrected prompt estimate rises nearly fivefold (call-level interval 3.3 to 8.5), a rise the plug-in estimate misses. Pre-specified studies on 320 unseen items and 24 unseen prompts confirm the increase. In votes balanced across candidate orders, cooling produces more ties in Qwen, and changing only the tie rule shifts the estimated accuracy effect of cooling by 9.84 percentage points. An analytical model shows how position dependence can push such votes toward ties and lower accuracy under abstention even when the judge favors the correct answer. The value of consistency therefore depends on alignment with correct answers, the voting rule, and the cost of abstention.

papers.title: A Two Stage Quasi-Likelihood Estimation Method for High Dimensional Generalized Structural Equation Models
papers.abstract: Estimating high dimensional Generalized Structural Equation Models presents severe computational challenges. Traditional simultaneous estimators frequently suffer from numerical instability and prohibitive computational costs. Moreover, there are no tractable algorithms for families such as Poisson, negative binomial, and gamma. To overcome these limitations, this article introduces a Two Stage Quasi-Likelihood Expectation-Maximization framework. The proposed method isolates the structural model from the measurement model. First, it approximates the conditional distribution of the latent variables given the observed indicators. Second, it employs marginal quasi-likelihood estimating equations to evaluate the structural parameters, deriving the necessary conditional moments either exactly or through Monte Carlo integration. This approach completely avoids the need to evaluate the full joint likelihood. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our method drastically reduces computational runtime, providing a numerically stable framework that minimizes the mean squared error and structural bias to yield a scalable and flexible solution for analyzing complex latent variable models.

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.

papers.title: History-Dependent Mode Selection in a Driven Holographic Superfluid
papers.abstract: We study finite-rate mode selection among competing Landau-unstable modes in a holographic superfluid. The first mode to reach a prescribed amplitude need not be the instantaneously fastest-growing one. Time-dependent linear evolution on the driven homogeneous background closely reproduces the modal amplitudes obtained from full bulk evolution. Protocols with identical present driving conditions can reverse the relative ordering of two modes. For the controlled histories studied here, the change in their logarithmic amplitude ratio is well approximated by the excess accumulated differential QNM gain.

papers.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
papers.abstract: The quantum geometry of Floquet-Bloch states in periodically driven crystals evolves throughout each drive cycle. We show that Floquet topology and micromotion constrain this evolution. Using a projector formulation that separates stroboscopic and micromotion contributions, we bound the deviation of the integrated quantum metric of any Floquet-band subspace from its stroboscopic value and derive a geometric speed limit on its evolution. In chiral Floquet systems, these bounds extend the topological lower bounds set by the $0$- and $\pi$-gap invariants at two symmetry-selected times into finite intervals of the drive, a dynamical topological obstruction. When both invariants are nonzero, it can force a minimum intra-period change in the metric, driven by micromotion. Because the integrated metric is a periodic lower bound on the total spread of time-evolved Wannier functions, such a change can make this spread breathe. An exactly solvable driven spin chain realizes this obstruction and further hosts a flat-band point where each band's metric equals the breathing of its compact localized state. This equality provides a direct geometric characterization of local micromotion, accessible through local spin correlators.

papers.title: Comeager hereditary families of compact sets are big
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Polish space and let $\mathcal K(X)$ be its Vietoris hyperspace. A family $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal K(X)$ is hereditary if it is downward closed under inclusion. Matheron and Zelen\'y asked whether every comeager hereditary family in $\mathcal K(X)$ contains a dense hereditary $G_\delta$ subfamily. We give an affirmative answer in ZFC.

papers.title: Equivariant learning of a transferable three-dimensional classical density functional
papers.abstract: Liquids exhibit collective behavior that depends sensitively on thermodynamic conditions, interfaces and confinement, yet predicting each new state commonly requires a separate atomistic simulation. Classical density functional theory offers a reusable variational description, but its central excess free-energy functional is generally unknown, and learned approximations for fluids have largely been developed in reduced-dimensional geometries. Here we show that this functional can be learned directly from fully three-dimensional canonical equilibrium density fields while preserving spatial symmetry and variational consistency, without free-energy or chemical-potential training labels. A functional learned from coarse three-dimensional density fields remains predictive at finer resolution, separating the sampling demands of training from the spatial resolution of subsequent predictions. A single learned functional transfers across temperatures, system sizes and statistical ensembles, and recovers the equation of state, liquid--vapor coexistence and interfacial broadening, none of which are used as training targets. Applied to complex three-dimensional geometries, it predicts the potential of mean force between colloids due to solvent mediation, and adsorption isotherms in an interconnected gyroid pore. These results demonstrate that molecular dynamics equilibrium density data can be converted into a transferable thermodynamic generator connecting microscopic liquid structure to response, phase behavior and collective phenomena.

papers.title: Online Inference for Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In this work, we initiate a systematic study of online statistical inference for quantile-based distributional policy evaluation, which aims to characterize the distribution of discounted cumulative rewards under a given policy. To obtain a finite-dimensional representation of the return distribution, we consider the fixed point $\bm\eta_m$ of the quantile-projected distributional Bellman equation, parameterized by the quantile vector $\bm\theta_m$. We develop two online inference procedures for $\bm\theta_m$, covering synchronous and asynchronous sampling from a generative model as well as Markovian data. The first method uses the trajectory of quantile temporal-difference learning (QTD). We establish functional central limit theorems for the partial sums of QTD iterates and construct a recursively computable random-scaling statistic. The resulting confidence intervals have asymptotically exact coverage at deterministic times, with length of order $T^{-1/2}$ in probability. The second method constructs anytime-valid confidence intervals directly from samples. We invert multiscale tests of the Bellman estimating equation and use dyadic reward histograms to evaluate conservative evidence bounds online. The resulting intervals have finite-sample simultaneous coverage, and the histogram contribution to their length bound is of order $T^{-\zeta}$ for $\zeta\in[1/2,1)$. Under positive limiting state-visit frequencies, the resulting confidence intervals have lengths of order $\sqrt{\log\log T/T}$, which we establish as classwise optimal through a matching lower bound. Together, these results provide complementary guarantees for online inference in quantile distributional reinforcement learning, combining asymptotically exact fixed-time inference with finite-sample anytime validity.

papers.title: Portfolio Choice of Spouses with Heterogeneous Risk Preferences over Shared Household Consumption
papers.abstract: A number of recent empirical papers rely on a collective model to analyze the portfolio choice of spouses, their heterogeneous risk preferences, and intra-household bargaining. I show that although Pareto-Efficient, this approach generates a counterintuitive result with constant Pareto weights: an increase in the risk aversion of a household member can lead to an increase in household risk-taking. Moreover, household wealth affects the preferred risky portfolio share even under CRRA preferences and can make the household insensitive to preferences of a spouse. I offer an alternative approach based on the concept of risk premia and show that it always generates a Pareto-efficient and monotonic household level solution. I derive an intuitive normalization to the Pareto weights in the collective model which generates an approximately equivalent solution. Finally, I discuss multiplicative aggregation of utilities previously used in this literature and show that it is also approximately equivalent to the suggested approach.

papers.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.

papers.title: Random close packing at extreme size ratios with an Adam-based inflation protocol
papers.abstract: We present \texttt{rcpgenerator}, an openly available code for generating $d$-dimensional dense, disordered, non-overlapping close packings from an arbitrary prescribed list of particle diameters. The method adapts the Clarke--Wiley inflation protocol, but instead uses the Adam optimizer to relax the particle configuration. Typically, particle coordinates are advanced with a single, global step size, which must shrink as the size ratio $S\equiv D_{\max}/D_{\min}$ grows, generally stalling the optimization. Adam instead gives each coordinate its own adaptive step size, stabilizing the optimization time across a broader range of $S$. We demonstrate this in three-dimensional periodic tests that reach $S\sim5\times10^{5}$ for a continuous lognormal distribution ($N\sim10^{6}$ diameters) and particle numbers up to $N\approx5.6\times10^{6}$ for power-law distributions, with the densest packings reaching $\phi\simeq0.87$, each completed in minutes to hours on a multicore machine. Across truncated-lognormal, truncated-power-law, and Weibull distributions, the resulting $\phi$ reproduces trends such as the locations of peaks and knees with distribution shape and $S$ found in prior numerical results and in the parameter-free Farr--Groot prediction, with a remaining offset typically $0.005$--$0.01$. Additionally, results are commensurate with multimodal packing densities measured in vibrated-bed experiments. The code and the complete per-case census behind every figure are released with the paper.

papers.title: Algebraic versus physical uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators
papers.abstract: We give explicit determinant counterexamples to the uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators from their degrees and simultaneous pair zeros. At seven points the solution space has dimension seven; Bose symmetry removes six directions and leaves the Hodges line. At eight points a two-dimensional Bose-symmetric space remains. Regular integer-spinor configurations distinguish these deformations from the Hodges numerator. On the eight-point plane, collinear factorization, the leading positive-helicity soft coefficient and ordinary BCFW decay each select the Hodges line. For $n\ge5$, we prove two results on the full fixed-degree, common-denominator ansatz, without pair-zero conditions. Complete collinear residue functions on all pairs determine at most one numerator; Bose symmetry makes one channel sufficient. The splitting law and a normalized lower-point amplitude supply the boundary function, starting from an explicit five-point seed. With Bose symmetry, $O(Z^{-1})$ decay under one fixed same-helicity shift at generic conserving kinematics also selects the Hodges line. Normalized collinear and soft data fix the eight-point scale; the homogeneous shift condition leaves one constant per multiplicity.

papers.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.

papers.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
papers.abstract: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.

papers.title: Who is who: injury rates between players and within each player in professional team sports
papers.abstract: Objective: Per-hour injury rates inform rest and match calendars. We measured how injury rates differ between players and with recent load. Methods: Observational study of public match records in nine team sports. Injury records covered 22,573 players in six sports (748 women, in one league). In football, injuries were injury-coded substitutions. A heavy week had a full match or more within seven days; a longer-gap week followed an 8-to-13-day gap. We compared heavy weeks across players and within each player. Results: As expected, players' usual injury rates differed: between two players picked at random, the higher was typically 1.83 times the lower. As known, two or more injuries of 28 days or more in three years went with 1.3 to 1.7 times the rate in five sports. As expected, within the same player, playing time rose less after a heavy week than across players, whether or not a replaced player may return. As expected, simulations with no effect of load read heavy weeks as riskier within each player's season in the usual comparisons, because injuries lower later load. Over whole seasons, they read them as 1.05 to 2.19 times as risky in all six sports. Conclusion: Researchers and injury surveillance programmes who compare each player's heavy weeks with the same player's longer-gap weeks should check that comparison by simulation. Per-hour rates that compare players mix recent load with who carries it. So club medical staff can read lower injury rates among their most-used players as a sign of who plays.

papers.title: Quantum Theory of Third-harmonic Generation in Epsilon-Near-Zero Materials
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical framework, based on the Green's tensor quantisation method, to describe third-harmonic generation in epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials and derive analytical, closed-form solutions for the generation efficiency. We validate our model against experimental measurements of wavelength- and angle-resolved third-harmonic generation efficiency from 30 nm-thin ITO nano layers at low pump intensity, described under the undeleted pump approximation. Our results provide a local and scalar model for quantum nonlinear processes in dispersive and lossy ENZ media, and establishes a simple and reliable framework for investigating a variety of nonlinear optical phenomena with applications to quantum sensing, quantum information, and quantum non demolition measurements.

papers.title: Sheaf-Based Federated Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous federated systems require agents to learn and exchange informative representations despite differences in data distributions, model architectures, and latent dimensionalities. We propose Sheaf-based Federated Representation Learning (SFRL), a framework that jointly learns and aligns heterogeneous latent representations without sharing parameters, labels, or a single latent space. SFRL relates agent-specific latent spaces through learnable orthogonal transformations and isometric embeddings, promoting consistency via a sheaf-Laplacian gluing regularizer evaluated on a shared set of pilot samples. We develop Sheaf-FRL, a decentralized alternating algorithm combining local gradient updates with closed-form Procrustes updates of the alignment maps, and establish convergence guarantees in deterministic and stochastic settings. On collaborative classification with semantic communication across four datasets, under model and data heterogeneity, Sheaf-FRL improves communication accuracy over federated baselines at no cost in private accuracy, and is more robust to latent-space compression.

papers.title: Matrix Multiverses Meet Multiple Mythologies
papers.abstract: We present a model in which asymptotically de Sitter universes of various types, and de Sitter (dS) radii $R_n$, live in the interiors of black holes in a maximally entropic flat $p = \rho$ Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe. These dS universes clearly have many quantum states. We argue that they decay and equilibrate with the maximal entropy universe on time scales of order $\alpha_n R_n {\rm ln} (R_n /\delta_n)$, where $\alpha_n$ are model-dependent dimensionless constants and $\delta_n$ are the initial distances between the shell, satisfying the Israel junction conditions, and the dS horizon. These are time-scales as viewed by a detector following a trajectory far from the would-be cosmological horizon. These times are all exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times, which have no meaning in this model. It is impossible for a detector inside one of the dS universes to determine whether it is actually part of such a structure. This model could be used as the basis for claiming that certain constants of nature or cosmological initial conditions were chosen to have mathematically unnatural values because other values could not lead to any form of intelligent life.

papers.title: An asymptotic Liouville-type theorem for systems of Lane-Emden equations on RCD*(-K,N) spaces via gradient estimates
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish elliptic gradient estimates for positive solutions of the Lane-Emden system on metric measure spaces satisfying the synthetic Ricci curvature-dimension condition $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$. Our approach combines the weak differential calculus and the Bochner inequality available in the $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$ setting with suitable auxiliary function arguments, extending classical gradient estimate techniques to nonsmooth spaces. The resulting estimate is valid for all exponents $\alpha,\beta>0$ and all $N\in[1,\infty)$, with no dimensional case distinction and with explicit constants. As an application, we prove a quantitative, asymptotic Liouville-type theorem on $\mathrm{RCD}^*(0,N)$ spaces: for positive solutions that are bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, the normalized gradients $|\nabla f|/f$ and $|\nabla h|/h$ are bounded by a quantity that is of order $\max\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and hence tends to zero as the exponents tend to zero (with comparable size). We also explain why the method gives no rigidity for large exponents, which is consistent with, but does not prove, the existence of nonconstant solutions there. These results generalize corresponding results from the smooth Riemannian setting and contribute to the study of nonlinear elliptic systems on spaces with synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds.

papers.title: Resolving the Gibbs Paradox through Local Free Space and Collision Potential
papers.abstract: The Gibbs paradox is conventionally resolved by invoking the indistinguishability of identical particles and the associated $N!$ correction, while the standard entropy of mixing remains independent of molecular properties. Here, we develop a classical framework that does not rely on quantum indistinguishability. We treat molecules initially occupying different spatial regions as distinguishable and describe the accessible volume of each molecule by its instantaneous local free space. We further account for the non-negligible time-averaged potential energy associated with molecular collisions and rederive the entropy increment of gas mixing within the canonical ensemble. The resulting expression depends explicitly on molecular properties, including molecular mass, effective radius, and characteristic collision time, and therefore varies among different gases while yielding zero entropy increment for identical gases naturally. This framework provides a novel classical resolution of the Gibbs paradox by connecting the entropy of mixing to molecular properties rather than to an additional quantum assumption or some new conceptual explanation.

papers.title: Autonomous Optimization of Complex Oxides for Thermochemical Fuel Production
papers.abstract: Two-step thermochemical cycles for H2O and CO2 splitting offer a promising route to sustainable fuel production. Their performance depends on redox-active oxides that undergo cyclic reduction and oxidation reactions. Achieving high thermal-to-fuel conversion efficiency requires both favorable redox thermodynamics and sufficiently rapid reaction kinetics. These requirements have shifted materials design toward complex multication oxides, including mixed-cation fluorites, perovskites, and high-entropy oxides. Developing such materials requires the simultaneous optimization of their composition, defect chemistry, phase stability, and morphology. The resulting design space is difficult to explore through sequential trial and error. Thermochemical fuel production therefore provides a compelling testbed for autonomous materials design and optimization. In this study, we first examine why redox-active complex oxides are challenging to develop owing to their multidimensional phase spaces, harsh operating conditions, and competing functional targets. We then discuss how high-throughput computation, automated synthesis, characterization, and testing, together with machine learning, can be integrated into closed-loop workflows to address these challenges. Drawing on advances from broader oxide materials research, we define a capability roadmap encompassing complex-oxide synthesis, operando characterization, robotic testing, condition-aware computation, and multi-objective optimization. Finally, we identify the key experimental, computational, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities required to build self-improving optimization platforms for materials development in thermochemical fuel production

papers.title: Bayesian Distilled Clustering for High-Dimensional Mixture Models
papers.abstract: Latent subgroup analysis is central to fields such as genomics, precision medicine, and social science, where the goal is to identify heterogeneous populations with distinct covariate structures or response behaviors. Mixture models provide a natural probabilistic framework for this task, representing the data-generating distribution as a weighted combination of subgroup-specific laws with unobserved labels. In high-dimensional regimes, these analyses face significant challenges. Often, only a small subset of covariates drives meaningful subgroup separation; the remaining variables may introduce noise or redundancy. Standard clustering methods typically treat all dimensions as equal, but in high-dimensional spaces, irrelevant coordinates can distort distances and obscure the low-dimensional structures defining latent classes. This paper introduces a Bayesian distilled clustering framework for high-dimensional mixture models. We propose that clustering should occur within a statistically justified subspace rather than the full ambient space. Our method utilizes a Bayesian variable selection model to estimate posterior inclusion probabilities, quantifying the evidence that each covariate contributes to subgroup separation or response behavior. A "distilled" covariate set is then identified by controlling the expected false-discovery proportion. Clustering is performed on this reduced subspace, followed by conditional independence diagnostics to examine subgroup-specific dependencies among selected variables. Critically, this framework is model-based: the distillation step is tied directly to the mixture structure and response model rather than a generic dimension-reduction criterion. This ensures the resulting subspace remains aligned with the scientific objective: identifying latent subgroups that differ in both distributional structure and behavior.

papers.title: Newton's Second Law: A Structural Necessity of Mechanics Constrained by Excluded Perpetual Motion and Universal Free Fall
papers.abstract: For over three centuries, Newton's second law (F = ma) has governed mechanics with extraordinary success, while its epistemic warrant has remained empirical. That merely empirical contingency vanishes once mechanics is constrained by two principles: the principle of excluded perpetual motion (PEPM) with its pre-Newtonian phenomenological content and the weak equivalence principle (WEP) with universal free fall as its primitive content. The PEPM secures the applicability of Suppes' measurement-theoretic framework to gravitational mass and force, exposing the formal structure latent in their empirical manifestations and establishing both as independent primitives. Gravity bridges statics and kinematics in Stevin's and Galileo's inclined-plane arguments, where the common sine factor in force and acceleration cancels in F/a. Cycle arguments under the PEPM extend this result to arbitrary force mechanisms, establishing F/a as object-intrinsic and securing inertial mass as a well-defined physical quantity. Further constrained by universal free fall, the resulting quantitative structure compels the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass, with Newton's second law as the operational expression of that equivalence. Direct implications include constraints on modified-inertia MOND that follow from the PEPM alone. The PEPM also places free-fall and torsion-balance experiments on equal footing as tests of the WEP. Together with the WEP, the derivation further grounds both the dimensional reduction of mechanics and the location-invariance of the Kibble-balance realization of the SI kilogram. Deeper still, Newton's second law derives its necessity from exclusion and invariance principles whose scope extends beyond mechanics itself.

papers.title: Hypothesis Testing with Conditional Queries: Learnability and the Value of Interaction
papers.abstract: Model evaluations may fix all tests before observing any responses or select later tests using earlier responses. We study this choice in a conditional-query model on a finite outcome space $\mathcal{X}$ with $|\mathcal{X}|=N$. We first ask which pairs of distribution classes can be reliably distinguished. We then ask how many additional queries are required to match an adaptive tester when all queried events must be fixed in advance. We show that learnability holds if and only if the two classes have positive separation in their pairwise conditional probabilities. When this separation is zero, the optimal worst-case error is exactly $1/2$ at every finite query budget. For any $T$-query adaptive policy and any $\rho \in (0,1)$, we construct a randomized non-adaptive procedure using $O(N^2(T + \log(1/\rho)))$ pair queries chosen before any response is observed. Its simulated transcript is within $\rho$ in total variation of the adaptive transcript, uniformly over all distributions in the model. We also construct a matching family with constant adaptive query complexity and $\Omega_\varepsilon(N^2)$ non-adaptive query complexity. Consequently, the worst-case fixed-error adaptivity gap is $\Theta_\varepsilon(N^2)$. Thus interaction can reduce the required number of tests by a quadratic factor, but the apparent exponential branching of an interactive evaluation does not yield an exponential query advantage.

papers.title: Handling Missing Data in Probabilistic Regression Trees
papers.abstract: Probabilistic regression trees are a smooth alternative to classical regression trees, consistent in the complete-data case, producing continuous predictions through probabilistic split assignments. This paper extends this framework by proposing three approaches to accommodate missing predictor values directly during tree construction, without a separate imputation step. These modifications are defined to preserve the fundamental probabilistic properties of the original methodology, including probability conservation and marginal compatibility, under arbitrary patterns of missing covariate values. The proposed methods are evaluated on several real-world datasets exhibiting different levels of missingness and are compared with classical regression trees. In addition, a semi-synthetic study, in which missing values are injected completely at random, at random and not at random, compares the proposed strategies with impute-then-fit pipelines based on commonly applied imputation methods.

papers.title: Rotational spectra and de-perturbation analysis for ground state ytterbium oxide, YbO
papers.abstract: A combination difference analysis of Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (FTMW) measurements of $^{174}$YbO combined with earlier near-infrared chemiluminescence data have resulted in much improved YbO rotational and centrifugal distortion constants. These have been confirmed in a multi-isotopologue analysis of further FTMW measurements of $^{172}$YbO and $^{176}$YbO and an analysis of nuclear-size-dependent Born-Oppenheimer breakdown effects in the molecule. Multiple excited electronic states overlap with low-lying excited vibrational levels of the electronic ground state leading to irregularities in its vibrational spacings and other previously observed electronic manifolds. This has been modeled with a matrix of the vibrational levels of the ground and multiple interacting states assuming Morse potentials and including electronic Hamiltonian matrix elements mixing the states. Vibrational level overlaps were calculated numerically assuming Morse vibrational wavefunctions. The resulting de-perturbed potentials for the states inform continuing experimental and theoretical work on this and other ytterbium-containing molecules.

papers.title: Topological Charge-Transfer Excitons
papers.abstract: Excitons possess internal structure absent from single-particle Bloch particles, allowing their band topology to emerge from the bound-state structure rather than being inherited from their constituents. This raises the question of how the internal structure of a bound state can provide a microscopic origin of exciton topology. Here we show that the real-space embedding of charge-transfer excitons can generate an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals whose coupling supports topological exciton bands. Lateral electron-hole separation embeds the localized exciton on the bond connecting its constituent sites rather than on either site. We demonstrate this mechanism in a honeycomb lattice, where three bond-centered charge-transfer exciton orbitals form a Kagome lattice. By solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation, we show that this emergent multi-orbital manifold supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when the electron and hole bands are topologically trivial. The resulting band exhibits nearly uniformly distributed quantum geometry, favorable for interaction-driven bosonic states. Our results establish a general route toward topological bands of localized composite bound states and unconventional strongly correlated bosonic phases.

papers.title: Equivalence of mapping gravitational wave background anisotropy across bases at equal information content
papers.abstract: Mapping anisotropies in the gravitational-wave background (GWB) requires choosing a basis to represent the sky intensity, such as pixel and spherical harmonic bases. Each introduces a truncation---e.g., a number of pixels or a maximum multipole l_max---often set by a naive counting argument that relate the number of measurable modes to the number of independent cross-correlations, N_pair, in a pulsar timing array (PTA). However, such truncations can lead to reconstruction artifacts, as they do not reflect the true information content of the PTA response. Increasing the value of truncation parameters spans the observable space better but reveals poorly constrained modes, making the inverse problem ill conditioned and requiring regularization. A natural approach is to restrict the reconstruction to a well-measured subspace via principal maps, defined by the dominant eigenmodes of the detector response (or Fisher) matrix. However, these maps are not a fundamental parametrization of the sky but, rather, are derived from an underlying representation---such as a pixelization or a spherical harmonic expansion. While their explicit form depends on basis choice, they can span the \textit{same subspace} when the underlying representation is sufficiently complete. Here, we show that reconstructed anisotropy maps via different bases are equivalent, provided they retain the same information content, i.e., span the same principal subspace. As illustrative cases, we consider a toy model for PTA configuration and several GWB anisotropy shapes: point source, an extended source with deterministic anisotropy, and a statistical isotropic background, along with its summary statistic---the angular power spectrum. Although the reconstructions are equivalent, their computational costs can differ. We conclude with brief comments on the construction of principal maps for ground-based interferometers.

papers.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does
papers.abstract: Different optimization algorithms can find very different solutions to the same problem. Gradient descent (GD) exhibits a low-rank bias in overparameterized problems when initialized near zero, while Adam does not. GD is rotationally equivariant: rotating both factors of a factored model $W = UV^\top$ by an orthogonal matrix leaves the loss unchanged, and GD's solution rotates accordingly. In contrast, Adam is not. We show that any algorithm using only the current gradient and respecting rotational symmetry amounts to a left-preconditioner depending only on the gradient's Gram matrix.
