papers.abstract: We present a high-order implicit-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (IMEX-DG) solver for the compressible Euler equations that accounts for rotational effects within an atmospheric framework. Time integration follows a second-order additive Runge-Kutta scheme, treating stiff acoustic modes implicitly and advective terms explicitly. The solver is built on the deal.II finite element library, combining matrix-free operator evaluation, adaptive non-conforming mesh capabilities, and distributed-memory parallelism. The inclusion of rotation extends the framework to large-scale atmospheric dynamics, where the Coriolis force plays a central role in geostrophic balance. Its incorporation into a high-order matrix-free DG discretisation is, however, non-trivial, as it requires a careful formulation of the discrete rotational operator. Two alternative treatments of the rotational and gravitational source terms within the solution strategy, based on nonlinear fixed-point iterations, are therefore introduced and compared in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. A discrete analysis of the rotational operator is also carried out in order to derive a formulation suitable for efficient matrix-free implementation. The proposed formulation is verified through convergence studies on rotating inertia-gravity wave benchmarks and further assessed in fully three-dimensional simulations of stratified flow over orography on both uniform and adaptive meshes. The numerical results show that the rotating IMEX-DG framework has the expected accuracy and stability properties while correctly capturing the asymmetry and wave structures induced by rotation in large-scale atmospheric flows.

papers.title: Comparison of Proton, Helium-Ion, and Carbon-Ion CT Imaging for Hadron Radiotherapy Using Monte Carlo Simulations
papers.abstract: Objective: To perform a comprehensive comparative analysis of proton, helium-ion, and carbon-ion computed tomography (CT) as direct imaging modalities for hadron therapy treatment planning, focusing on Relative Stopping Power (RSP) reconstruction accuracy and patient radiation dose. Approach: High-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations were conducted using the GATE/Geant4 platform to model a standard CTP404 phantom. RSP maps were reconstructed using two iterative algorithms: the Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique (SART) and the Richardson-Lucy (RL) deconvolution. Imaging performance was evaluated by comparing reconstructed RSP values against ground truth data for various tissue-equivalent inserts, while integral doses were estimated for a human head geometry using a Shepp-Logan-like phantom. Main results: All investigated particle modalities demonstrated a significant dose reduction compared to conventional X-ray CT protocols (which are approximately 40 mGy). The estimated imaging doses were 0.5 mGy for protons, 1.3 mGy for helium ions, and 7.5 mGy for carbon ions. In terms of accuracy, carbon-ion imaging achieved promising accuracy for soft-tissue materials (mean absolute error <0.5%). Helium ions offered a balanced performance with sub-1% errors for most materials and a dose burden significantly lower than carbon ions. Protons exhibited the widest range of RSP deviations. Significance: Direct particle imaging eliminates the systematic uncertainties inherent in photon-to-hadron conversion, which typically introduce RSP deviations of 1.6%-3.5% in standard single-energy X-ray CT. While carbon ions provide better RSP reconstruction precision essential for complex treatment plans in heterogeneous anatomy, helium and proton imaging offer exceptional dose sparing, making them particularly advantageous for pediatric patients and frequent adaptive replanning scenarios.

papers.title: Development and ground demonstration of a Modular Astrobiological Experiments (MAEx) payload for autonomous biological monitoring in Low Earth Orbit (LEO)
papers.abstract: The spaceflight environment presents unique challenges for biological systems, including microgravity, ionizing radiation, altered fluid transport, and confined habitats. Understanding and harnessing biological processes under these conditions are essential for future space biomanufacturing, including biological production and bioregenerative life-support technologies. Such applications require compact, autonomous experimental platforms capable of monitoring biological responses to spaceflight stressors. Here, we present the ground-based validation of the Modular Astrobiological Experiments (MAEx) payload, a compact 3U platform designed to support future autonomous biological investigations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). MAEx integrates three analytical modules: camera-based imaging, optical spectroscopy, and microbial electrochemistry. Its versatility was evaluated using three biological systems: the electroactive bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1, the radiation-resistant fungus Ustilago maydis FB1, and the human eye-lens protein {\gamma}D-crystallin. The imaging module was validated by monitoring microbial growth over time, while the spectroscopy module was evaluated for its ability to detect changes associated with microbial growth and protein aggregation. The electrochemical module was functionally validated by monitoring anodic current production during S. oneidensis MR-1 cultivation. Together, these results demonstrate the functionality of the three analytical modules and establish MAEx as a ground-validated TRL-4 platform. The MAEx architecture provides a foundation for future investigations relevant to space biomanufacturing, bioregenerative life-support, and in situ resource utilization. Environmental qualification for spaceflight remains ongoing, and further development is required before the payload can be integrated into existing or planned orbital laboratories.

papers.title: From Augmentation to Reconstruction: Guiding the AI Disruption to the Good Place
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence feels omnipresent, yet the disruption many expect has not fully arrived. The main reason is not model capability, nor even the tools built to harness those models. Rather, most organizations are still using AI to accelerate workflows designed for a pre-AI world. We offer a three-stage lens: Augmentation, Automation, and Reconstruction, and argue that the most consequential disruption resides in the third stage where workflows and markets are rebuilt around delegation, machine-to-machine interaction, continuous monitoring, and auditable constraints. Achieving this system-level transformation takes time: it requires trust and accountability infrastructure, machine-legible and interoperable data and interfaces, the design and adoption of these new workflows, and economic incentives that favor reconstruction rather than local optimization: the complementary investments that produce the familiar "productivity J-curve" of general-purpose technologies. We illustrate this transition through examples in consumer markets, education, news, and coding. Finally, we emphasize a normative point: the agentic future is not predetermined. Leaders must both skate to where the puck is going and actively steer it toward a good place, ensuring innovation delivers welfare gains felt by businesses and consumers around the world.

papers.title: Do VLMs Align Better with Humans than LLMs Do during Natural Reading?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly useful computational models of human language processing, yet it remains open whether vision--language learning is associated with more human-like text representations during natural reading. We address this question by comparing matched LLM and vision--language model (VLM) pairs under strictly text-only input and evaluating alignment with human brain activity (whole-cortex fMRI) and reading behavior (synchronized regressive saccades). Across evaluated pairs, we identify a selective, rather than global, pattern in human--model alignment. In first-party continued-pretraining pairs (Qwen2 and DeepSeek), VLMs more accurately predicted human regressive saccades while exhibiting practical equivalence with matched LLMs in whole-cortex fMRI alignment, whereas a LoRA-adapted pair (Mistral/Idefics2) showed no divergence. However, sentence-level fMRI analyses revealed a growing VLM advantage for more visually evocative sentences. Together, these findings provide a controlled comparison of matched LLMs and VLMs, showing selective human-alignment advantages in reading behavior and visually grounded content.

papers.title: Admissibility of Adaptive Monotone Step-Down Multiple Testing Procedures Under Arbitrary Covariance Dependence
papers.abstract: We study finite-sample admissibility for simultaneous testing of multivariate normal means under a vector loss whose components are the usual individual $0$--$1$ losses, with an arbitrary known positive-definite covariance matrix. For the two-sided problem, we establish admissibility for a broad class of procedures that rank active hypotheses using locally adaptive, strictly increasing transformations of suitably standardized conditional residuals. The result also covers residual-based sequential procedures with positive stage-specific cutoffs common to all active hypotheses at each stage, without requiring the cutoffs to be nonincreasing. The proof derives the interval structure of the acceptance sections from two properties: the previously rejected indices remain invariant while the hypothesis under study is active, and the stopping rule ensures that a perturbation leading to its rejection cannot defer that rejection beyond the stage at which the procedure at the unperturbed observation stops while accepting it. We also establish the corresponding one-sided result for locally adaptive, strictly increasing transformations of signed residuals, under both point-null and composite-null formulations and their respective vector losses. Together, these results extend vector-loss admissibility beyond the original Maximum Residual Down (MRD) procedure and identify a broader monotone ordering structure induced by covariance-adjusted residuals. We also show that the two-sided and one-sided classes are almost-everywhere limits of finite-support Bayes rules under their corresponding additive total losses; this representation, however, does not assert admissibility under those losses.

papers.title: Propagation of Regularity for Schroedinger Equations with Time Dependent Potentials
papers.abstract: The dynamics of Schr\"odinger equation with time dependent potentials of general time dependence is considered. It is shown that for localized in space potentials, there is propagation of regularity which is uniformly bounded in higher Sobolev norms. Unlike the cases where the solution scatter, and then propagation is proved via a standard bootstrap argument, the solutions considered here have a part that does not scatter, as expected in general. For this we introduce propagation estimates that work directly in (e.g.) $H^2(\mathcal{R}^3).$

papers.title: EEG-FM-Audit: A Systematic Evaluation and Analysis Pipeline for EEG Foundation Models
papers.abstract: EEG foundation models (EEG-FMs) show potential for learning generalized representations from heterogeneous EEG signals. However, existing studies exhibit three critical limitations: opaque model tuning, unverified contributions of complex learning paradigms to EEG-FMs, and a limited understanding of the neurophysiological features that FMs rely on to make decisions. To address these challenges, we propose EEG-FM-Audit, a systematic evaluation and diagnostic pipeline comprising three modules: (1) a fairness-calibrated benchmarking protocol ensuring fair comparisons through model-tailored hyperparameter optimization for EEG-FMs and supervised baselines; (2) three paradigm-level ablation workflows isolating contributions of heterogeneous data scale, self-supervised pretraining, and pretrained linguistic priors; and (3) a neurophysiological probing (NPP) framework exploring whether FMs leverage valid EEG features. Extensive experiments across four leading EEG-FMs and five supervised models on four datasets reveal that well-tuned supervised baselines can match or outperform tuned FMs in some cases, despite requiring significantly fewer parameters. Furthermore, ablation analysis indicates that FM pre-training is indispensable for data-scarce downstream tasks, whereas the contribution of pre-trained linguistic components depends heavily on model architecture. Finally, NPP analysis shows that FMs generally extract the established temporal, spatial, and spectral characteristics of the evaluated datasets, establishing a systematic diagnostic benchmark for assessing EEG-FMs.

papers.title: Symmetry-Protected Bipartite Entanglement in Hopf-Linked Quantum Rings
papers.abstract: We study two interacting electrons in Hopf-linked quantum rings, one electron on each ring. In the absence of the inter-ring interaction, the two lowest orbital states on each ring have the same energy. For the ideal geometry, the Fourier coefficients of the three-dimensional Coulomb kernel satisfy $V_{1,0}=-V_{0,1}$, making the positive-parity block of the four-state Hamiltonian diagonal in the Bell basis. Unitary symmetries of the full orbital Hamiltonian preserve the parity sectors under virtual transitions. For pure states odd under ring exchange followed by a half-turn on each ring ($\mathcal Y=-1$), the Schmidt weights occur in equal pairs, giving at least one bit of entanglement between the rings. An elliptic deformation changes the Coulomb selection rule to first order while preserving the link. Finite-basis diagonalization shows that higher orbitals can reduce the probability of obtaining the encoded Bell pair by projection onto the two lowest orbitals of each ring even when the entanglement between the rings remains close to one bit.

papers.title: Pseudo-Likelihood Regression for the Marginal Rate of Recurrent Events with a Competing Terminal Event
papers.abstract: Regression modeling of recurrent and terminal events continues to present methodological challenges in survival analysis. Existing approaches either make unverifiable assumptions about the dependence between the two event types, rely on a proportional mean rate assumption, or use ad hoc estimating equations. We propose a semiparametric regression model based on a novel weighted pseudo-likelihood function that directly targets the marginal rate of the recurrent event and extends the Ghosh--Lin model to a large class of transformation models. Our framework accommodates external time-dependent covariate effects on the marginal rate and enables flexible prediction of the marginal mean. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimators and propose a robust sandwich estimator for the variance. In simulation studies, we demonstrate a strong performance of the proposed estimator under independent right-censoring. We apply the method to data from the interim analysis of a randomized clinical trial on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease to predict the expected number of severe exacerbations, and illustrate how the choice of regression model affects the estimated covariate effects and predictions.

papers.title: Bayesian Rational Search Engine User
papers.abstract: A user faces a list ordered by a noisy proxy for relevance and decides whether to pay to inspect another item or stop with the best she has found. Because she does not know the page's quality, each inspection both produces a candidate and updates her beliefs about the remaining items. We show that the optimal policy is a standout rule: the user stops when her best find is sufficiently good relative to what she expects from the page, with the required margin changing with depth. The browsing dynamics collapse to a one-dimensional Markov chain, yielding the full distribution of inspection depth through a closed-form recursion. The model uncovers three reasons for stopping: trust, commit, and cut-losses, and yields testable implications. It also turns inspection depth into a learning-to-rank likelihood. Observed depth restricts the latent relevance path to a polyhedron of survival inequalities, while conversion identifies the terminal winner. Simulations show that the estimator recovers relevance under correct specification and improves ranking using only the incumbent ranker's features. Applied to public Baidu search logs, the inspection depth likelihood produces rankings that align more closely with expert relevance judgments than click-trained alternatives.

papers.title: Deformed seminorms, anisotropic sectors and Phragm\'en Lindel\"of principles for $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$\allowbreak difference operators
papers.abstract: We study the deformed derivative of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba on spaces of holomorphic functions, with the induced geometry and growth principles. The deformed derivative maps the holomorphic functions on a disc of radius $\rho$ into those on the disc of radius $\rho/\beta$, $\beta$ being the upper limit of the $n-$th roots of the deformed numbers, and this loss of radius is optimal. For two root structure functions the deformed gauge equals $\max\{|z|,1/\phi_{1}\}$, so that deformed discs are Euclidean above a minimal radius; Borel Carath\'eodory and vector valued Cauchy Hadamard theorems follow. On factorial weighted Banach spaces the deformed derivative has norm $1/r$ and spectrum the closed disc of radius $1/r$. A deformed Borel transform identifies these spaces with weighted Wiener algebras, yields the Gelfand theory, and shows that the associated Fr\'echet space is nuclear. We establish logarithmic convexity and subharmonicity results, Phragm\'en Lindel\"of and Lindel\"of principles in the anisotropic sectors of half aperture $\theta\sup_{k}k^{-1}\log[k]$ and in their curved variants, with sharp critical orders, and a rigidity theorem: under Gaussian growth of the deformed factorials, functions of finite deformed exponential type are entire of order zero and cannot be bounded on a ray unless constant. A dominant term principle shows that, for a large dominant root, the deformed exponential and trigonometric functions have only real simple zeros, localized between explicit geometric means of deformed numbers, whereas the deformed exponential series has nonreal zeros when the two roots have sum at most two.

papers.title: Two Operational Principles Single Out Quantum Theory
papers.abstract: Within a finite-dimensional causal operational-probabilistic theory (OPT), we show that adding just two postulates, local equivalence and purification, suffices to derive the mathematical structure of quantum theory as a whole, without separately assuming quantum rules for states, measurements, composites, or transformations. This resolves the question raised by Chiribella, D'Ariano, and Perinotti (CDP) [Phys. Rev. A 81, 062348 (2010)]. The key step is to establish homogeneity of state cones by combining infinitesimal cone-preserving deformations obtained from these postulates with geometric optimization. CDP purification requires every normalized state to be purifiable and purifications of the same state on any common ancilla to be related by a reversible channel on that ancilla. Our alternative assigns each system one operationally equivalent ancilla that purifies all its normalized states, requiring such reversible equivalence only there. Together with local equivalence, this condition also yields quantum theory.

papers.title: Proxy-Based Approximation of Shapley and Banzhaf Interactions
papers.abstract: Shapley and Banzhaf interactions capture the complex dynamics inherent in modern machine learning applications. However, current estimators for these higher-order interactions trade off between speed and accuracy. To overcome this limitation, we introduce ProxySHAP. ProxySHAP reconciles the high sample efficiency of tree-based proxy models with a situational residual correction recovering consistency. On a theoretical level, we derive a polynomial-time generalization of interventional TreeSHAP that computes exact interaction indices for tree ensembles, thereby bypassing exponential tree-depth dependencies in prior methods. Furthermore, we formally analyze the residual adjustment strategy, characterizing the specific conditions under which Maximum Sample Reuse (MSR) corrects proxy bias without its variance scaling exponentially with interaction size. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates that ProxySHAP sets a new state-of-the-art standard for approximation quality, including in large-scale applications with thousands of features. By achieving the lowest error in both small- and large-budget regimes, ProxySHAP significantly outperforms the prior best estimators ProxySPEX and KernelSHAP-IQ, while also delivering superior performance on downstream explainability tasks.

papers.title: Mechanisms and Pathways of Extreme Events in Partially Observed Stochastic Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Extreme events occur across the natural, engineering, and socioeconomic sciences, where rare but high-impact episodes can lead to disproportionate consequences and pose challenges for prediction and risk management. Existing studies have mainly focused on the statistics, sampling, forecasting, and attribution of extremes from observable variables. We develop a mathematical framework for studying the mechanisms and pathways of extreme events in partially observed stochastic dynamical systems with hidden variables. By integrating data assimilation with information-theoretic and trajectory-based diagnostics, we infer latent precursor dynamics, quantify their uncertainty, and determine how their influence propagates toward an observed extreme event. Conditional Gaussian models provide a tractable analytical setting for closed-form diagnostics, while the framework extends more broadly through numerical methods. From a trajectory-wise viewpoint, we compare filtering and smoothing distributions to identify the onset of hidden precursors and quantify their temporal influence range. From a statistical viewpoint, we construct event-conditioned hidden-state distributions to identify sensitive triggering directions, representative latent pathways, and distinct candidate pathway classes through clustering. Three case studies illustrate the methodology. In an intermittent stochastic model, hidden damping dynamics emerge before observed bursts, and filter-smoother discrepancies provide an onset diagnostic. In a stochastic model with damping and forcing, separate damping-induced, forcing-driven, and mixed pathways to extremes are identified. In a nonlinear topographic-flow model, distinct mechanisms and pathways for blocking and unblocking patterns associated with observed extreme events are revealed.

papers.title: Optimal work extraction in measurement-based quantum Otto engines: Non-adiabaticity and generalized measurements can be beneficial
papers.abstract: Measurement-based quantum heat engines have attracted significant interest as alternatives to conventional thermal engines, as they replace the hot thermal reservoir with quantum measurements, thereby offering greater controllability and simpler implementation. Motivated by these advantages, we investigate a measurement-driven quantum Otto engine with a qubit working substance and study the optimal work extractable from such engines along with the corresponding efficiency, including whether their performance can surpass that of conventional quantum Otto cycles. We analyze the engine in both the infinite-time (adiabatic) and finite-time (non-adiabatic) regimes, considering two distinct implementations obtained through optimization over all projection-valued measurements (PVMs) and over all two-outcome positive operator-valued measurements (POVMs). We show that measurement-based engines can outperform conventional quantum Otto engines within specific parameter regimes and that POVM-based engines can yield higher optimal work extraction than PVM-based ones. Furthermore, by incorporating the thermodynamic cost associated with resetting the auxiliary system required for POVM implementation, we demonstrate that the resulting net work output can still exceed that of PVM-based engines under suitable conditions on the spectral gaps and cold bath temperature. We also identify regimes in which non-adiabatic implementations can yield higher work output and efficiency than their adiabatic counterparts. Our study provides operational guidelines for designing improved measurement-driven quantum Otto engines.

papers.title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: Efficiently realizing logical operations on general stabilizer codes remains a long-standing challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing. While code surgery provides a general framework with provable guarantees through joint logical measurements, existing constructions are largely theoretical and incur substantial ancilla overhead in practice. We present GeneCS, a resource-efficient synthesizer of code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes, designed for the backend of fault-tolerant quantum compilers. Our approach leverages structure-aware optimizations to eliminate redundancy in graph construction, dynamically balance expansion and congestion, and incorporate code degree constraints. Experimental results show that GeneCS reduces ancillary qubits and checks by over 85\% on average for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, while the optimized constructions exhibit logical-error-rate behavior comparable to the baseline under BP-OSD (belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding). On surface-code stress tests with more than $10^4$ physical qubits, one independent synthesis run takes about one second on average. These results enable practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication for modern QLDPC (quantum low-density parity-check) codes and heterogeneous code systems.

papers.title: Carbon-Aware Age of Information Scheduling in IoT Networks
papers.abstract: Ensuring timely information delivery while reducing environmental impact is a fundamental challenge in future large-scale 6G and beyond Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. Information timeliness is typically measured using the Age of Information (AoI) metric, whereas environmental impact is often characterized by the Carbon Footprint (CF), which depends on both energy consumption and the Carbon Intensity (CI), defined as the amount of CO$_2$-equivalent emissions produced per unit of consumed energy. Because CI varies over time, minimizing energy consumption alone does not necessarily minimize CF: transmitting the same status update at different times may result in different carbon costs. To address this challenge, we propose Sustainable Age-of-Information Scheduling for IoT Hardware-Constrained Edge Networks (SAOITHE), a scalable scheduling heuristic inspired by Whittle-index decomposition. A closed-form index is derived for a relaxed infinite-horizon single-source model with immediate transmission and unit AoI reset; this index is subsequently used as a priority rule for the original finite-horizon, multi-source system with buffered gateway and server dynamics. Using real-world CI traces across low-, medium-, and high-CI regions, the proposed heuristic operates within the allocated CF and duty-cycle budgets in all evaluated configurations and achieves lower average AoI than baseline policies. The AoI reduction relative to Round Robin is approximately 25% and 20% in low- and medium-CI regions, respectively, and up to 75% in high-CI settings, while maintaining quasilinear per-slot computational complexity.

papers.title: Properties of the skyrmion crystal in the Heisenberg triangular lattice with scalar chirality
papers.abstract: Skyrmion crystals have been primarily discovered under a magnetic field for materials with noncentrosymmetric interactions. More recent developments have investigated the stability of skyrmion crystals in itinerant magnets without a magnetic field. In this study, we find that a type of skyrmion crystal with two topological charges per unit cell and no magnetization at the ferromagnetic point in reciprocal space, SkX-2, is naturally stabilized in an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric model with short-range interactions realized by the Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice with scalar chirality. We complement our numerical results with a theoretical analysis that quantitatively describes the transition from the ferromagnetic to the SkX-2 ground state and the evolution of the topological charge density. Despite the constraints given by the Mermin-Wagner theorem at finite temperature, the SkX-2 can either exhibit a first-order phase transition with translation symmetry breaking, or a continuous transition to a floating solid depending on the charge density, which is given by the strength of the scalar chirality interaction. Finally, the numerical results indicate the presence of $\mathbb{Z}_2$-vortices at finite temperature above the tetrahedral ground state in the antiferromagnetic region of our model, suggesting the existence of a vortex topological transition similar to that reported in the ordering of the pure antiferromagnetic model.

papers.title: Adaptive Slater Koster Parameters: Crossing Oxidation States with Density Functional Tight Binding
papers.abstract: We propose to adapt the confined pseudo-atomic orbitals underpinning the Slater-Koster (SK) tables in density functional tight binding (DFTB) to local atomic environments. Assigning optimal SK parameters to metal atoms in different oxidation states improves the electronic structure of a partially oxidized Ni surface and, with adapted repulsion, Li insertion energetics in graphite. Their smooth, interpretable response to chemical and spatial environment, independently observed for Ni and Co oxides, enables a simple, physically informed machine-learning scheme, here applied to Ni-O binaries.

papers.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a normed space
papers.abstract: We prove that the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of every real or complex normed space $X$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $X$.

papers.title: Rate-Optimal Randomised Kernel Quadrature
papers.abstract: Kernel quadrature is used to approximate integrals of smooth functions, with the worst-case error typically decaying at the minimax rate $n^{-\alpha/d}$ for smoothness $\alpha$ in dimension $d$. Existing rate-optimal methods often depend on deterministic point sets, sometimes tailored to a specific kernel. Here, we study randomised designs for kernel quadrature on compact and unbounded domains for kernels whose reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces are norm-equivalent to Sobolev spaces of integer order $\alpha>d/2$. We bound the worst-case error of prescribed designs adapted to a sampling density $p$ by $n^{-\alpha/d}$ times an explicit functional of the sampling and integration densities. Minimising this factor gives $p^\star\propto\pi^\gamma$ with $\gamma=2d/(2\alpha+d)$, where $\pi$ is the integration density. The proposal depends on the kernel only through its Sobolev order $\alpha$. Under local mass and cell-average conditions, together with a tail condition on $\mathbb{R}^d$, independent samples from $p^\star$ attain the same minimax rate with high probability, up to a logarithmic factor. The same bound also controls posterior contraction. We verify these conditions for Beta-type densities on the cube and, for integrands in $\mathcal{H}^\alpha(\mathbb{R}^d)$, for Gaussian and Student-$t$ measures. The deterministic minimax exponent for Student targets is $\min(\alpha,\nu+d/2)/d$, with a logarithmic gap between the bounds at $\alpha=\nu+d/2$.

papers.title: Conformal tubular parameterization and toroidal bending of tube-like surfaces
papers.abstract: Tube-like surfaces are widely encountered in geometry processing, engineering structures, and medical anatomy, yet their intrinsic longitudinal and circumferential information is not well preserved by conventional planar annular or rectangular parameterization domains. In this work, we propose a new conformal parameterization framework for open tube-like surfaces with two boundary components. The proposed method first constructs a fixed-boundary tubular parameterization by cutting the input mesh, computing a disk-to-parallelogram quasi-conformal map, and lifting the result to a cylindrical surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. To reduce residual distortion introduced near the cut seam, we further introduce a localized quasi-conformal correction scheme formulated on an annular domain, which improves conformality while leaving regions away from the seam unchanged. To handle noisy or irregular input boundaries, we also develop a free-boundary variant based on boundary extension and cycle-Laplacian smoothing, allowing the prescribed boundary constraints to be imposed on artificial outer rings rather than directly on the original surface. Finally, as an optional post-processing step, we derive two conformal toroidal bending maps that embed the tubular parameterization into toroidal geometries without altering its conformal structure. Experiments on synthetic tube meshes and real vascular surfaces demonstrate that the proposed framework produces low-distortion parameterizations, effectively mitigates seam-induced artifacts, improves robustness for boundary-noisy inputs, and provides flexible tubular and toroidal target domains for downstream surface processing tasks.

papers.title: Temporal evolution of the periodic GeV signal from 4FGL J1913.2+0512 and analysis of the SS 433/W50 lobes
papers.abstract: SS 433 is a microquasar whose relativistic jets precess every ~162 days, providing a laboratory for jet-interstellar medium interactions. We present a comprehensive analysis of 16 years of Fermi Large Area Telescope data (August 2008-September 2024) of the SS 433/W50 field, using events in the 0.3-300 GeV range and employing pulsar gating to mitigate contamination from the bright nearby pulsar PSR J1907+0602. We detect the GeV source 4FGL J1913.2+0512 (TS = 45, where TS denotes the likelihood-ratio Test Statistic) with a power-law spectrum (photon index 2.61 +- 0.08) and confirm a GeV excess at the western lobe (TS = 17). The eastern lobe of SS 433 is hinted at with lower significance. One additional GeV excess, Fermi J1909.6+0552 (TS = 20; TS = 28 over 0.1-300 GeV), located outside the SS 433/W50 system, is revealed after gating. Exposure-corrected Lomb-Scargle periodograms and precessional phase-folded light curves show a ~162-day modulation in 4FGL J1913.2+0512. The phase-folded emission is mainly confined to the first half of the precessional cycle, while the source is not significantly detected in the second half. This periodic signal is mainly concentrated in the 5-10 yr interval, remains visible in the cumulative 0-10 yr data set, and is not recovered in the subsequent 10-16 yr interval. Over the full 16-year data set, the modulation remains detectable but with reduced significance, consistent with dilution by the later non-modulated epoch. These results indicate that the efficiency and/or geometry of gamma-ray production in the SS 433 environment evolves on multi-year timescales.

papers.title: Anomalous Transport from Effective Field Theory
papers.abstract: A systematic study of chiral effects is presented using an Effective Field Theory framework. By integrating out a massive Dirac fermion at finite temperature in presence of vector and axial background fields, the currents and their anomalies are computed from the path-integral. Chiral effects previously considered separately naturally arise in a unified computation, including new mass corrections. The link between each anomalous transport effect and the anomalies is clearly established, beyond the identification of their coefficients. In particular, we can appreciate how these effects are sourced by the anomalous nature of the theory even in configurations where the anomaly itself vanishes. The consistent and covariant anomalies are both encapsulated in master formulae for the currents which result from a careful treatment of the regularisation. It is finally found that, at finite temperature, the physical currents cannot be inferred simply from the Chern-Simons terms whose divergence reproduce the chiral anomalies.

papers.title: Forward hadron production in pp collisions at LHC energies from an event generator based on the color glass condensate framework
papers.abstract: We investigate inclusive forward single-hadron production in high-energy proton--proton collisions using a CGC-inspired Monte Carlo event generator, MC-CGC. We carried out a systematic study of the sensitivity of the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov (rcBK) evolution equation to its initial conditions by comparing three parameterizations: the McLerran-Venugopalan (MV) model and its two HERA DIS-constrained variants, MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$. Our results indicate that the current LHCb data favor the MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$ models, while the differences from the original MV model become more pronounced at higher transverse momentum and at mid-rapidity. As a complementary analysis, we also compared the dilute-dense (DHJ factorization) and dense-dense ($k_T$ factorization) frameworks. We found that the $k_T$ factorization framework provides a better description of the particle production spectra at mid-rapidity than the DHJ framework, where both the projectile and target are in the dense regime at LHC energies. Predictions for the FoCal measurements at ALICE, including the production of identified neutral mesons and jets, are also presented.

papers.title: A tree-like fractal Dirichlet space lying between strong and weak elliptic Harnack inequalities
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a self-similar fractal configured as an infinitely branched tree and equip it with a regular self-similar Dirichlet form. Fixing a typical metric ball, we compute accurately the effective resistance between an inner point and the boundary of this ball. Based on this result, anomalous behaviour of the mean exit time from such balls is shown -- the ratio between whose supremum and infimum can be arbitrarily large. Under properly selected self-similar measure, we further show the weak elliptic Harnack inequality holds but the strong analogue fails.

papers.title: Fair outputs, Biased Internals: Causal Potency and Asymmetry of Latent Bias in LLMs for High-Stakes Decisions
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuned language models exhibit behavioural fairness in high-stakes decisions while retaining biased associations in their internal representations. However, whether these suppressed representations can affect model outputs - and whether such causal potency is symmetric across demographic groups - remains unknown. We investigate the use of open-weight models for mortgage underwriting using matched applications that differ only in racially-associated names and reveal a critical disconnect: models show no output-level bias, yet retain and amplify demographic representations across model layers. Through activation steering and novel cross-layer interventions, we demonstrate that this suppressed information is decision-relevant: when reinjected at critical layers, it produces near-complete decision reversals. Critically, this latent bias is asymmetric - steering interventions affect decisions in one demographic direction, while producing minimal effects in reverse - and susceptible to adversarial prompt engineering and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. These findings demonstrate that behavioural audits focused on outputs are insufficient: fair outputs can mask exploitable internal biases. They also motivate dual-layer testing frameworks combining output evaluation with representational analysis for AI governance in high-stakes decisions.

papers.title: Worst-Case Sample Complexity Bounds for Distributed Inner Product Estimation with Local Randomized Measurements
papers.abstract: We study distributed inner product estimation for $n$-qubit states using local randomized measurements, for which rigorous worst-case guarantees are less understood. We first reduce the minimax kernel optimization to Hamming-distance kernels. Within this class, unbiasedness fixes a unique kernel. For this kernel under local Clifford sampling, we prove a fourth-moment bound for arbitrary inputs. This yields a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{5.25^n})$ copies per party at fixed additive error and failure probability. For the same kernel under local Haar sampling, we prove a local twirling identity that compares its fourth moment with the Clifford fourth moment. A direct bound on the Haar fourth moment shows that $\mathcal(\sqrt{4^n})$ copies per party suffice. We also show that independent single-qubit Pauli shadows have a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{7.5^n})$ for large $n$.

papers.title: C-Phase-Aware Compilation for Efficient Fault-Tolerant Quantum Execution
papers.abstract: Achieving practical quantum advantage on fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQC) is fundamentally constrained by significant spatial and temporal overheads required to execute logical operations on physical hardware. Existing compilers fail to exploit the connection between algorithmic structure and fault-tolerant execution primitives, leaving substantial optimization opportunities unrealized. Additionally, they often rely on coarse-grained, slice-based abstractions that ignore microarchitectural overheads, leading to poor resource utilization. We present a microarchitecture-aware compilation approach that integrates algorithmic structure directly with lattice surgery (LS) execution. By leveraging the commutativity of C-Phase operations, the method transforms inherently sequential gate sequences into concurrent multi-target interactions, effectively removing artificial dependencies and exposing significant instruction-level parallelism. To enable this, we design a dynamic, event-driven scheduling strategy that accurately models spatial layout and routing constraints, allowing operations to overlap in time while minimizing contention. Compared to the state-of-the-art compiler, our work achieves up to 24.5$\times$~(geomean~3.7$\times$) reduction in execution time, up to 20.8$\times$~(geomean 2.9$\times$) reduction in space-time volume, and up to 2.7$\times$~(geomean 2.4$\times$) reduction in program-failure probability across three regimes of magic-state production. By co-optimizing the circuit reordering and LS primitives, we make executing fault-tolerant programs faster, cheaper, and more reliable on the same hardware.

papers.title: From Organization to Viability: A Multi-Level Analysis of Gait Dynamics Under Occlusal Constraint
papers.abstract: Clinical interpretation often assumes that observable performance sufficiently reflects the organization of an adaptive system. The preceding Level 3 study showed that neither an aggregated scalar score nor a static exploratory UMAP embedding uniquely resolved the occlusal observational probes. This study introduces Level 4, centered on observed longitudinal viability. Using an exploratory single-case design in a participant with Parkinson's disease, gait was recorded with instrumented insoles under three probes: neutral natural occlusion (ONL), a nominal 2.5-degree increase in vertical dimension of occlusion (OC2.5), and a nominal 3-degree increase (OC3). Two sessions were conducted eleven weeks apart. A common PCA representation was used to compare M1-M2 centroid displacement. In the selected PC1-PC2 plane, OC3 showed the smallest Euclidean displacement, ONL an intermediate displacement, and OC2.5 the largest. This ordering was preserved in most bootstrap iterations but was not preserved after Mahalanobis covariance normalization, showing that within-condition dispersion contributes to the result. Level 4 therefore provides a retrospective, representation-dependent proxy for longitudinal reorganization when static representations remain non-identifying. The findings are exploratory and non-causal. They do not establish distinct physiological states, a causal occlusal effect, a validated viability threshold, a therapeutic optimum, or a covariance-independent ranking.

papers.title: Characterization of stability radii for robustly asymptotically stable dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems
papers.abstract: We study linear time-invariant dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems. We characterize when the systems are robustly asymptotically stable and derive exact conditions and bounds when this property is lost under structure-preserving perturbations.

papers.title: Assessing the imprint of eccentricity in GW signatures using two independent waveform models
papers.abstract: The gravitational-wave signal from merging compact binaries encodes information about their orbital and intrinsic properties. Over the last few years, state-of-the-art waveform models have begun to incorporate the effects of orbital eccentricity into their estimated signal. Over a similar period, many groups have applied these waveforms to characterize whether the imprint of eccentricity is present and, if so, measure this time-evolving property (at a suitably-defined reference point). In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of 162 confident sources identified in the O3 and O4a observing runs of the International Gravitational Wave Network (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA). Using the RIFT parameter inference engine, we employ two independently implemented waveform models (SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dali) which account for orbital eccentricity and the effects of aligned compact object spins. Using these two waveforms, we find consistent conclusions that disfavor the eccentric hypothesis. Unlike previous work, among binary black hole candidates, we find potential evidence for eccentricity in three events: GW200129, GW231001, and GW231123. For the latter two events, the evidence for eccentricity is ambiguous, with different degrees of support from different waveforms. Consistent with previous work, we find conclusions obtained about GW200129 can be sensitive to analysis settings, as expected, given the nonstationary noise present.

papers.title: Classifying double copies and multicopies in AdS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we draw a parallel between solutions of pure three-dimensional gravity with a negative cosmological constant and classical double copies in four dimensions. In the former case, topological solutions, such as the BTZ black hole, deficit angles, and naked singularities, emerge from identifying points in AdS using elements from its isometry algebra $so(2,2)$. The type of solution corresponds one-to-one with the orbits of $so(2,2)$. We demonstrate how various double copies of four-dimensional AdS gravity similarly arise from the $so(2,3)$ isometry elements, which also correspond one-to-one with their orbits through a Penrose-type transform. We classify all such elements and generate the corresponding double copies, which include AdS black holes, black branes, and many others. The double-copy isometries originate from the centralizer of a given AdS isometry, allowing us to define canonical coordinates associated with its Abelian part. Additionally, the two Casimir invariants of $so(2,3)$ feature in the metrics via the characteristic polynomial of the AdS symmetry parameter. Our classification naturally extends to higher spins, providing nonequivalent multicopies at the linearized level.

papers.title: Two Results on Outer-String Graphs
papers.abstract: An \emph{outer-string representation} of a graph $G$ is an intersection representation of $G$ where vertices are represented by curves (strings) inside the unit disk and each curve has exactly one endpoint on the boundary of the unit disk (the anchor of the curve). Additionally, if each two curves are allowed to cross at most once, we call this an \emph{outer-$1$-string representation} of $G$. If we impose a cyclic ordering on the vertices of $G$ and require the cyclic order of the anchors to respect this cyclic order, such a representation is called a \emph{constrained outer-string representation}. In this paper, we present two results about graphs admitting outer-string representations. Firstly, we show that for a bipartite graph $G$ (and, more generally, for any $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free graph $G$) with a given cyclic order of vertices, we can decide in polynomial time whether $G$ admits a constrained outer-string representation. Our algorithm follows from a characterization by a single forbidden configuration, similar to that of Biedl et al. [GD 2024] for chordal graphs. Secondly, we answer an open question from the same authors and show that determining whether a given graph admits an outer-1-string representation is NP-hard. More generally, we show that it is NP-hard to determine if a given graph $G$ admits an outer-$k$-string representation for any fixed $k\ge1$.

papers.title: From Clever Hans to Hypotheses: Interpreting EEG Foundational Transformers with LRP
papers.abstract: Emerging foundation models (FMs) in electroencephalography (EEG) promise a path to scale deep learning in diagnostics and brain-computer interfaces despite data scarcity, yet their opaque nature remains a barrier to wider adoption. We investigate attention-aware Layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) as a post-hoc attribution method for EEG-FMs, extending LRP's use on convolutional neural network (CNN)-based EEG models to the Transformer architectures that current FMs are based on. We find that LRP can both verify EEG-FM decisions and surface novel, biologically plausible hypotheses from them. In motor imagery, it unmasks 'Clever Hans' behavior where models prioritize task correlated ocular signals over the intended motor correlates. In a naturalistic paradigm for affect prediction, it reveals a recurring reliance on a central electrode cluster, suggesting a candidate sensorimotor signature of arousal. Though heatmap interpretation remains ambiguous in this complex domain, the results position LRP as a tool for both verification and exploration of EEG-FMs, a role that will grow in both importance and discovery potential as the underlying models mature.

papers.title: Self-similar dendrites with finite boundary and P-sprouts
papers.abstract: Each self-similar dendrite K with a finite self-similar boundary defines a finite acyclic edge-labeled bipartite graph G, called the sprout of K. The paper shows that the sprout G determines the combinatorial properties of the dendrite K and its topological structure.

papers.title: An energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of ferronematic equilibrium states and its numerical realization
papers.abstract: We develop an energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of two-dimensional ferronematic equilibrium states. The problem is formulated as the minimization of the harmonic energy of two two-dimensional vector fields, both with prescribed length, together with an additional nonlinear relation on the orientation of the two vectors. The finite element setting is based on piecewise continuous finite elements on a weakly acute triangulation. The numerical realization of the energy-decreasing algorithm employs a decomposition-coordination framework and a Uzawa-like iteration. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the computational performances of the algorithm.

papers.title: Mitigating residual foregrounds and systematic errors in SKA1-Low AA* EoR observations via Bayesian Gaussian Process Regression
papers.abstract: The redshifted 21-cm line is an emerging tool in observational cosmology that can serve as a direct probe of the intergalactic medium throughout the cosmic timeline. However, the observation of the cosmological 21-cm signal is extremely challenging in practice, regardless of the scale of interest and redshift, due to the presence of astrophysical foregrounds and residual systematic errors. Machine-learning-based Gaussian process regression (ML-GPR) has proven to be the most effective strategy for signal separation in LOFAR and NenuFAR observations to measure the 21-cm signal power spectrum from the Cosmic Dawn (CD) and Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we extend this framework to synthetic CD/EoR SKA1-Low observations to assess its robustness in mitigating residual foregrounds against instrumental and environmental systematic effects. We use our developed end-to-end realistic simulation pipeline (21cmE2E) for SKA-Low observations. Our 4-hour tracking simulation includes extragalactic point sources, the AA* telescope configuration, primary beam response, and residual systematics. The modelled errors incorporate antenna-based gain calibration errors, ionospheric phase errors, partial de-mixing of the out-of-field sources, and instrumental noise for 1000 hours of deep integration time. This work is one of the first demonstrations of the efficacy of the ML-GPR method in a realistic observing scenario. We compare different Bayesian GPR frameworks to assess their ability to suppress residual foreground contamination while minimising signal loss and providing reliable uncertainty estimates. Our results demonstrate that even in a realistic scenario where observations have a combination of residual systematics, ML-GPR can recover the 21-cm signal robustly within the $2\sigma$ confidence interval across almost the entire range of k-modes sampled.

papers.title: On the global convergence of gradient flow for wide shallow models beyond homogeneous nonlinearities
papers.abstract: A surprising phenomenon in the training of neural networks is the ability of gradient descent to find global minimizers of the training loss despite its non-convexity. Following earlier work, we investigate this behavior for wide shallow models. Existing global convergence results primarily concern models with positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities, such as ReLU activations, and models with scalar output weights and bounded nonlinearities, such as sigmoid activations. We study a broader class of models, including multi-head attention layers and two-layer fully connected networks with bounded or asymptotically positively one-homogeneous activations and vector output weights. Building upon (Chizat and Bach, 2018), we prove that, in the limit of infinitely many hidden neurons or attention heads, non-minimizers of the training loss are unstable under the mean-field gradient flow dynamics by constructing "escape regions" in the parameter space. Our global convergence statements are conditional in the following sense: if the mean-field gradient flow converges for the Wasserstein 2-distance, then its limit must be a global minimizer. We revisit the bounded nonlinearity, scalar-output setting of (Chizat and Bach, 2018), giving an escape region construction adapted to unbounded nonlinear parameter domains. We also propose new constructions for nonlinearities with at most linear growth under a non-degeneracy assumption and for asymptotically positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities. Finally, we show the well-posedness and stability estimates for the mean-field training dynamics under sub-Gaussian initializations.

papers.title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Optical Skyrmions Enabled by a Silicon Microring Optical Phased Array for Robust Free-Space Communication
papers.abstract: Optical skyrmions can encode information in the skyrmion number for free-space communication through atmospheric turbulence. However, programming both the skyrmion number and type on a compact chip remains challenging. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate a skyrmion generator based on a silicon optical phased array with optimized inner- and outer-grating microring emitters. The two emitter types provide orthogonal circularly polarized components and generate optical skyrmions through coherent superposition. The on-chip phase shifters configure the azimuthal phase distribution, enabling the $4\times4$ array to generate states with target skyrmion numbers of $-2$, $-1$, 1, and 2. Adjustment of the relative phase bias continuously switches states with target skyrmion numbers of $\pm1$ between the N\'eel and Bloch types. Increasing the array size to $12\times12$ extends the target range from $-8$ to 8. Laser wavelength tuning and calibration of the microring input phases and amplitudes recover target states within a range of simulated fabrication errors, which shows the robustness of the generator. Furthermore, we evaluate four-symbol communication using skyrmion-number decoding over a simulated 100 m turbulent link and observe no symbol errors in $10^4$ trials at Rytov variances up to 0.12. These results demonstrate the potential of this generator as a compact, programmable transmitter for turbulence-tolerant free-space optical communication.

papers.title: The Geometric Wall: Manifold Structure Predicts Layerwise Sparse Autoencoder Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: SAEs operationalise the linear representation hypothesis: they reconstruct model activations as sparse linear combinations of dictionary atoms hypothesised to represent meaningful linear directions. Their reconstruction error varies sharply across layers in ways that existing scaling laws, fitted at a single layer, do not explain. We contend that this variation is the empirical trace of the changing geometric structure of activation manifolds across depth: as their intrinsic dimension and curvature vary from layer to layer, so does the difficulty of approximating them with sparse linear dictionaries, and SAE width-sparsity scaling becomes a layer-dependent function of manifold structure rather than a single universal law. We conduct the first cross-layer SAE scaling study, fitting per-layer scaling-law surfaces to 844 residual-stream Gemma Scope SAE checkpoints spanning all 68 layers of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, and relating the fitted scaling parameters to four geometric summaries of the activation manifold. We find that manifold geometry predicts the per-layer width-scaling exponent in both models, explaining variation that cannot be reliably captured by layer depth alone. A controlled experiment on 150 synthetic manifolds, where intrinsic dimension and curvature vary independently, further reveals two distinct geometric contributions: intrinsic dimension governs the rate at which reconstruction improves with dictionary width, while curvature governs the residual error at the largest trained width. At the six Gemma showcase layers where richer width grids permit identification of an asymptotic floor, the fitted floors follow the same geometric ordering, consistent with the second-order residual that sparse linear approximations of curved manifolds can leave behind. SAEs thus encounter not merely a finite-resource ceiling but a geometric wall set by the manifold they are trying to reconstruct.

papers.title: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
papers.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $\Sigma A_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

papers.title: Embodied Communication: Sensing-Induced Reliability Fields and Capacity Bounds
papers.abstract: This paper introduces embodied communication, a new wireless communication modality in which information is imprinted onto environmental states and recovered by the receiver through sensing. No dedicated communication transmitter is activated, and no additional communication spectrum is occupied; instead, the sensed environment itself becomes the carrier of information. The key insight is that sensing must be reinterpreted for communication. Rather than asking how accurately an unknown physical state can be estimated, embodied communication asks how reliably two states can be distinguished. We formalize this idea through a multi-snapshot radio frequency (RF) sensing model and derive a sensing-induced reliability field that quantifies the distinguishability between physical states. This field turns embodied symbol design into a geometric packing problem shaped by the sensing resolution of the infrastructure. For this embodied channel, we characterize the finite-snapshot $\epsilon$-capacity through achievable designs and converses. We develop lattice-based codebooks, obtain a closed-form hexagonal design under a main-lobe approximation, and establish information-theoretic and geometric upper bounds. We further investigate the sensing-duration tradeoff: more sensing snapshots improve reliability, but also lengthen each embodied symbol, leading to a finite optimal sensing time. These results expose a latent communication pathway in sensing-enabled infrastructure and show how the environment can be transformed from a passive backdrop into an active information carrier.

papers.title: Structural and Lagrangian properties of analogue ensembles to characterize multifractality of stochastic processes
papers.abstract: We present a framework for the scale-invariance characterization of stochastic processes in reconstructed finite-dimensional spaces. This framework analyses the structural and dynamical properties of the reconstructed space and is based on a Takens embedding reconstruction followed by the definition of ensembles of analogue states. First, we specify a collection of target states densely sampling the full embedding space. For each target state, we search for the ensemble of its k-nearest neighbors, its k-best analogues, and we analyze its volume and dynamics. On the one hand, we study the probability distribution of the volumes and relate its mean and variance to the scale-invariance properties of the stochastic process. On the second hand, we study the Lagrangian properties of the analogues by characterizing how they disperse in time. More particularly, we study the volume occupied by the analogue's successors in function of time and of their initial volume. The main contribution of this paper is to highlight the link between these dynamical properties and the scale-invariance features of the process. We analyze two types of stationary and dissipative 1-dimensional scale-invariant processes: regularized fractional Brownian motion and regularized multifractal random walk. For both processes, the structure and dynamics of the embedding space are determined by their scale-invariant properties.

papers.title: Advance warning of $\gamma$-ray blazar flares from Fermi-LAT light curves: a strictly causal machine-learning backtest
papers.abstract: Long-term Fermi-LAT monitoring makes it possible to ask whether a blazar light curve shows signs of an upcoming flare before it becomes obvious in the $\gamma$-ray emission. We present a strictly causal machine-learning framework for forecasting $\gamma$-ray blazar flares from 3-d binned LAT light curves. Flare intervals are identified with Bayesian Blocks, and 42 variability features are measured from 365-d trailing windows. We train separate WATCH and TRIGGER models: WATCH predicts whether flare activity will appear within the next 90 d, while TRIGGER predicts whether a new flare onset will occur within the next 45 d. To avoid temporal leakage, all scaling, calibration, threshold selection, and validation use only pre-cutoff data (before MJD 60000). We apply the method to the FSRQ 4FGL J1048.4+7143, using 13 bright blazars as auxiliary training sources. Among logistic regression, polynomial logistic regression, and random forest classifiers, polynomial logistic regression gives the strongest held-out WATCH performance, with ROC AUC = 0.884, average precision = 0.392, and a block-permutation probability $p_{\rm perm}$ = 0.009. At the selected threshold it recovers 21 of the 21 positive WATCH windows. For TRIGGER, the same model gives AUC = 0.751, but with just nine positive test windows its AP = 0.121 is only about twice the random baseline (0.052), and no reliable pre-onset TRIGGER alert is obtained. The WATCH state appears before both held-out flares, with alerts 4.5 and 2.5 d before onset. These results suggest that the Fermi-LAT light curve of this source contains useful predictive information about its flare build-up during the period considered.

papers.title: Bootstrapping ground state properties of classical frustrated magnets
papers.abstract: We introduce a method based on semidefinite programming that produces rigorous two-sided bounds on ground state energy densities and correlation functions of translation-invariant classical spin models on infinite lattices. In this method, the challenge of non-convex optimization on an infinite lattice is replaced with a hierarchy of finite-size convex optimizations arising from positivity conditions that any probability distribution over spin configurations must satisfy. This adapts the Lasserre hierarchy in the theory of polynomial optimization to the context of frustrated magnetism, and we prove convergence of this hierarchy in the thermodynamic limit. Our method subsumes the Luttinger--Tisza method and further applies to non-quadratic Hamiltonians and non-Bravais lattices, thus addressing limitations of prior analytical methods. We apply the method to various two-dimensional frustrated spin models, where it brackets the energy densities and observables accurately across large parameter ranges with typical run times of seconds per parameter point.

papers.title: A High-Precision Statistical Analysis of the SN1987A Neutrino Temporal Distribution
papers.abstract: The interpretation of the SN1987A neutrino data remains limited by significant absolute timing uncertainties across independent detectors and a long-standing tension in the angular distributions. This work presents a high-precision statistical framework that resolves these issues by formalizing the mathematical distinction between intrinsic and relative timing offsets (ITOs and RTOs). By performing a simultaneous $\chi^2$-alignment of the Kamiokande-II and Baksan data with the IMB clock, we systematically incorporate non-Gaussian statistical correlations, reducing the temporal uncertainty by two orders of magnitude to the sub-second level. The $\chi^2$-analysis shows that Baksan's absolute timestamps require an advancement of $30.4\,\rm s$, while those of Kamiokande-II require a delay of about $6.4\,\rm s$. Establishing this unified, high-precision timeline is critical to test the physical nature of the first Kamiokande-II event (K1), specifically whether its distinct angular features signal the onset of the prompt neutronization burst. Previous literature often assumes that K1 originated from inverse beta decay (IBD) on qualitative grounds. By contrast, our multidimensional likelihood analysis incorporates energy, direction, and MSW flavor-conversion effects to provide the first quantitative constraint on its origin. We find a likelihood ratio of 3-6 in favor of an accretion-phase $\bar{\nu}_e$ origin over a neutronization-burst origin, thereby turning a traditional assumption into a statistically bounded physical inference. This framework provides the most stringent constraints to date on the chronology of SN1987A and establishes a precise methodology for future multimessenger observations of Galactic supernovae.

papers.title: Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calder\'on problem
papers.abstract: We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calder\'on problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.

papers.title: An extensive theory of nonlinearly intercoupled pseudomodes for noise model reduction in circuit QED
papers.abstract: Superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamical (cQED) platforms present a persistent modeling challenge: the intrinsic nonlinearity of the Josephson potential couples to a dissipative electromagnetic environment in ways that resist both perturbative treatment and naive Markovian reduction. Standard approaches either scale poorly with system size or absorb undeclared approximations about the noise structure into their master equations. In this work, we generalize Garraway's pseudomode construction to accommodate nonlinearly intercoupled auxiliary modes, providing a nonperturbative and systematically reducible framework for open-system cQED dynamics. The key observation is that pseudomode elimination is not fundamentally tied to linearity but to representability: any eliminated sector whose influence on the retained subsystem admits a rational self-energy can be replaced by a finite set of damped auxiliary modes, independent of the internal nonlinear structure of the retained Hamiltonian. We develop the general theory in the Heisenberg picture via a Dyson equation for the retained-mode Green's function, then demonstrate closed-form elimination for two-, three-, and four-mode Kerr-coupled systems with bilinear exchange and three-wave mixing interactions. The resulting framework substantially reduces the computational overhead of open-system cQED modeling while remaining faithful to the underlying physics, provided the spectral description of the eliminated sector is chosen to match the experimentally measured response functions of the hardware.

papers.title: Molecular Attoscope: Pulse Shape Spectroscopy of Electronic Coherence
papers.abstract: Tracking the coupled motion of electrons and nuclei on their intrinsic timescales is essential to understanding and controlling photochemical transformations. While attosecond techniques have provided unprecedented insight into electronic dynamics, they have largely been restricted to ionic systems, with nuclear motion often neglected or indirectly inferred. Here, we demonstrate a ``molecular attoscope", which uses shaped laser pulses in the deep ultraviolet to perform a coherent measurement of electronic and nuclear dynamics in an entangled wave packet in neutral benzene. This enables us to trace both the 856-attosecond-period electronic motion and the 36-femtosecond-period nuclear motion. We observe electronic coherence persisting over hundreds of optical cycles, modulated by nuclear dynamics. Our holographic approach is general, and lays the groundwork for coherent measurements capable of visualizing the evolution of the coupled electronic-nuclear wave function in real time.

papers.title: Characterizing electronic scattering rates with transport in multiterminal devices
papers.abstract: Strongly interacting electrons in clean two-dimensional devices are theorized to exhibit many distinct transport regimes, such as ballistic, hydrodynamic, or diffusive. Realistic samples often lie in crossover regimes between these idealized limits. We show how a single experiment on a multiterminal device can distinguish these regimes and constrain the relevant scattering rates without space-resolved imaging. Using a linearized Boltzmann model in a five-terminal geometry, we find that current partition among the drain contacts diagnoses the ballistic-hydrodynamic-Ohmic crossover and allows extraction of momentum-relaxing and momentum-conserving scattering rates in the crossover regime. The same geometry also exhibits clear signatures of the tomographic regime, potentially allowing for a quantitative discrimination between viscous and tomographic flow in experiments. Our results demonstrate that multiterminal devices are a simpler experimental route to characterize transport regimes in electron liquids, relative to space-resolved imaging experiments.

papers.title: A CV-TMLE global test approach to improve power in rare disease clinical studies with multiple-component endpoints
papers.abstract: Rare disease trials face unique statistical challenges due to limited patient populations and heterogeneous clinical manifestations among patients. Multiple endpoints are often necessary to comprehensively capture treatment benefits. A global test is an approach for evaluating whether a treatment has any beneficial effect across multiple endpoints. We propose a new global test based on a weighted composite endpoint. The proposed global test employs shrinkage-based cross-validated targeted maximum likelihood estimation (CV-TMLE) to learn data-adaptive weights that maximize power while maintaining Type I error control. Shrinkage can be tailored to incorporate existing domain knowledge, such as anticipated relative effect sizes. In simulation studies designed to reflect real rare disease trial settings, the proposed procedure demonstrated improved power over standard multiplicity adjustments and classical global tests (such as the O'Brien test), while maintaining nominal Type I error, when effects are heterogeneous across endpoints. The proposed method simultaneously learns an optimal weighted composite outcome and provides an unbiased and efficient targeted maximum likelihood estimator (TMLE) for the average treatment effect (ATE) on that weighted outcome, with valid inference taking into account that the ATE is data dependent.

papers.title: Factorization and monotonicity methods for reconstructing an impenetrable obstacle in inverse biharmonic scattering
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an impenetrable obstacle with a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition from far-field measurements. The associated data-to-pattern operators are noninjective, because the biharmonic scattered fields can be decomposed into propagative and evanescent components. We derive new symmetric factorizations of the far-field operator and analyzie the middle operators on the closures of the ranges of the adjoint data-to-pattern operators to establish range identities. These identities yield factorization criteria for the support of the obstacle when the wavenumber is not an associated transmission eigenvalue. Furthermore, we derive monotonicity criteria without excluding transmission eigenvalues. Numerical experiments for Dirichlet obstacles illustrate the reconstruction methods and show their performance with noisy data and for wavenumbers near a clamped transmission eigenvalue.

papers.title: Temporal State Tomography via Quantum Snapshotting the Temporal Quasiprobabilities
papers.abstract: Quantum tomography is a cornerstone of quantum information science, enabling the reconstruction of states and channels from experimental data. Here we introduce a new paradigm, temporal state tomography (TST), for reconstructing quantum processes across multiple times. Our approach is based on temporal quasiprobability distributions (TQDs), which, in the informationally complete setting, provide a complete description of multi-time quantum processes and uniquely determine temporal states. We formulate TST as a unified framework for reconstructing both density operators and quantum channels within a single scheme. We show that any TQD can be obtained via classical post-processing of measurement outcomes generated by a fixed set of quantum instruments, thereby establishing a direct operational route to accessing TQDs experimentally. For informationally complete TQDs, the associated temporal state can be reconstructed via a temporal Bloch-type representation. Leveraging this correspondence, we derive the sample complexity of TST, thereby quantifying its statistical efficiency.

papers.title: Estimation and Inference for the $\tau$-Quantile of Heterogeneous Individual-Specific Coefficient
papers.abstract: We study quantiles of heterogeneous coefficients across the $n$ observed units of a panel. Treating the coefficients as deterministic, we estimate each from $T$ observations, then use the estimates and their standard errors to construct a smoothed quantile estimator and estimate its variance. When $T^{1/2}\ll n\ll T^{3/2}$, the estimator is asymptotically normal around a deterministic center. A feasible bias correction relaxes the sample growth restriction to $n/T^{3/2}\to c\in[0,\infty)$, accommodating panels with large $n$. Normal inference extends to the target quantile when the difference between the deterministic center and the target is negligible relative to the standard error. Without this restriction, we establish an impossibility result that the distribution of the studentized error relative to the target cannot be estimated uniformly consistently. For practical inference in this case, we construct a conservative interval whose coverage tends uniformly to one and whose length attains the optimal worst-case rate in probability. We give primitive conditions for smooth GMM. Mortgage data show widespread but uneven declines in delinquency across credit scores.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Optimal Group Selection via the Double-Commutator Eigenvalue Problem
papers.abstract: The algebraic diversity framework generalizes temporal averaging over multiple observations to algebraic group action on a single observation for second-order statistical estimation. The central open problem in this framework is $\textit{group selection}$: given an $M$-dimensional observation with unknown covariance structure, find the finite group whose spectral decomposition best matches the covariance. Naive enumeration of all subgroups of the symmetric group $S_M$ requires exponential time in $M$. We prove that this combinatorial problem, restricted to a basis of $d$ candidate generators, reduces to a generalized eigenvalue problem derived from the double commutator of the covariance matrix, with complexity $O(d^2M^2 + d^3)$ for sparse (permutation-type) generators and $O(d^2M^3 + d^3)$ in general. The minimum eigenvector gives the optimal generator in the span of the basis in closed form, with no iterative optimization. The minimum eigenvalue is zero if and only if a generator in the span commutes exactly with the covariance, and its magnitude is a certifiable optimality gap otherwise. The problem does not appear in the standard catalog of Garey and Johnson (1979) and links group theory, matrix analysis, and statistical estimation.
