Empirical evaluations on the TACRED, TACRED-Revisited (TACREV), and Re-TACRED datasets reveal substantial performance improvements with fine-tuned LLMs, such as Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, and Flan-T5 Large and surpass previous methods on these datasets.

papers.title: Reduced Basis method for finite volume simulations of parabolic PDEs applied to porous media flows
papers.abstract: In the context of underground gas storage (of CO2 typically) in saline aquifers, numerical simulation is a highly valuable tool to evaluate the impact of the uncertainties of various model parameters and to optimize, e.g., injection-production scenarios. For this purpose, finite volume approximations of Darcy's parabolic model for flows in porous media are usually run many times, for many values of parameters like permeability and porosity, at costly computational efforts. We study the relevance of reduced basis methods as a way to lower the overall simulation cost of multi-point finite volume approximations to Darcy's parabolic model for flows in porous media for different values of the parameters such as permeability. We aim to quickly evaluate any linear form (or quantity of interest) of the pressure for many parameter values. To this end, we construct reduced bases by a standard POD-Greedy algorithm. Our POD-Greedy algorithm uses two new goal-oriented error estimators designed from a discrete space-time energy norm independent of the parameter. We provide some numerical experiments that validate the efficiency of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
papers.abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.

papers.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by F\'elix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.

papers.title: Operator dependent para-controlled calculus, periodic homogenisation and singular PDEs
papers.abstract: We develop a variant of the para-controlled distributions framework based on operator dependent (generalised) Besov spaces. This in particular covers the class of oscillatory operators from periodic homogenisation. We then apply the framework to study periodic homogenisation problems for a class of singular stochastic PDEs. One novel viewpoint is to measure regularity via the geometry induced by the operators at hand rather than classical Fourier basis. The generalised Besov spaces were introduced by Kerkyacharian-Petrushev. In contrast to the Fourier decomposition in the classical setting, they are built from spectral decomposition of general self-adjoint elliptic operators. A major difference is that products of two spectrally localised functions in general have ``frequencies" spread over the whole spectrum. We obtain a decay estimate on ``high frequency" component of the product of two spectrally-localised functions. This enables us to obtain uniform bounds for the naturally associated para-product and commutator operations over a class of operators. This in particular includes the family of periodic homogenisation operators uniform in the oscillation parameter. Next, we show convergence properties of these operations in the periodic homogenisation setting. A key ingredient is a sharp quantitative convergence of the generalised Littlewood-Paley block operators. The proof utilises the Helffer-Sj\"ostrand's formula for self-adjoint operators. Finally, we apply this framework to periodic homogenisation problems for dynamical $\phi^4_3$, $2$D gPAM, and $1$D KPZ. Assuming the convergence of stochastic objects to their homogenised limits, we show that the solutions and fluxes also converge to the corresponding limits. The convergence of the explicit stochastic terms with suitable renormalisations will be treated in a separate note.

papers.title: Resolving Gilbert's Conjecture: Dimensional Dependencies in Hardy Spaces Valued in Clifford Modules
papers.abstract: This article provides a thorough investigation into Gilbert's Conjecture, pertaining to Hardy spaces in the upper half-space valued in Clifford modules. We explore the conjecture proposed by Gilbert in 1991, which seeks to extend the classical principle of representing real $L^p$ functions on the real line as boundary values of Hardy holomorphic functions to higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces valued in any Clifford module. We present a complete resolution to this conjecture, demonstrating that its validity is contingent upon the dimension $n$, specifically holding true when \(n \not\equiv 6, 7 \mod 8\) and failing otherwise. The pivotal discovery that Gilbert's conjecture can be reformulated as a set of algebraic conditions is underscored in this work. To navigate these conditions, we employ a novel strategy that leverages the octonions, revealing their instrumental role in addressing issues related to Clifford modules and spinors. This innovative approach not only provides explicit realization through the generalization of the Hilbert transform to the Riesz transform but also establishes a significant advancement in the understanding of Hardy spaces within higher dimensions.

papers.title: Token Noise and the Illusion of Preference: A Shapley Value Framework for Auditing LLM-Simulated Choice Experiments
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate human respondents in choice experiments, yet their answers depend on the exact tokens of a prompt rather than on the offered products alone. I show that invisible characters, blank lines, or minor wording changes shift or reverse simulated choice probabilities. This sensitivity, which I term token noise, creates an illusion of preference and exposes studies to prompt hacking. I introduce a Shapley value audit that divides a model's choice response among the pieces of its prompt and reads each share beside the effect of removing that piece. The edit game divides the effect of several wording and formatting changes beside an actual price change. The word game divides a prompt's response across its words or tokens and summarizes the credit earned by the product attributes as the attribute share. Across four open-weight models and three product categories, wording and formatting edits could rival a substantive price change, while product attributes consistently received a minority of the word-level credit, sometimes less than the answer instruction. Framing cues could take credit from the very price they emphasized and frequently vanished or reversed across equivalent wordings of the question. A persona (even a bare statement that the respondent is a consumer) also shifted choice probabilities and the attributes' credit. Declared with its "players," reference, scale, and uncertainty, my audit separates what a simulated respondent prefers from how the question was asked, the distinction a study must draw before it reads a simulated choice as a preference.

papers.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite holes
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 3$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $n$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with ${\rm Ric}_h > \lambda $. In this paper, we construct, for each given $\epsilon >0$, a sequence of $(n+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(M_{i} ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_\epsilon ,d_\epsilon ) $ with ${\rm Ric}_{g_i} > \lambda $, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_\epsilon ) \leq \epsilon $, and $X_\epsilon $ is homeomorphic to the space obtained by removing an infinite number of balls from $X$. Hence $X_\epsilon $ has dense boundary with an infinite number of connected components. Moreover, $X_\epsilon $ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. This generalizes Hupp-Naber-Wang's result (arxiv: 2308.03909) from $4$-dimensional case to the general case of dimension $n\geq 3$. Our construction differs from that of Hupp-Naber-Wang. In their approach, Hupp-Naber-Wang considered doing an infinite number of blow-ups on the local complex surface structure of $X$, thus relying on the $4$-dimensional condition. However, our method involves removing an infinite number of balls from $X$, allowing us to construct in the general case of dimensions greater than or equal to $3$. As a corollary, we provide a solution to an open problem posed by Naber in the $3$-dimensional case.

papers.title: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomass\'e. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

papers.title: Combatting Fraud in Artificial Currency Based Government Benefits Programs
papers.abstract: Benefits programs are policy tools for providing targeted aid, such as food assistance or transit subsidies. However, these programs are often susceptible to misreporting fraud, wherein users misreport private attributes to obtain excess aid. To address this problem, we introduce a two-stage audit game between an administrator and users in which the administrator can audit users at a cost and levy fines on misreporting users, with player payoff structures designed to reflect real-world benefits programs. We show that the administrator's least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibria can be computed tractably via linear programming and derive prescriptive bounds on the administrator's excess payments and users' misreporting probability as functions of audit costs and fines. We further establish that, with an appropriately chosen budget level, the reduction in excess payments in any least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibrium offsets the audit budget required to sustain the mechanism, yielding total costs no greater than those of a baseline without an auditing authority, which we corroborate through a case study of Washington D.C.'s federal transit benefits program.

papers.title: The Vienna Architecture Description Language
papers.abstract: The Vienna Architecture Description Language (VADL) is a powerful processor description language (PDL) that enables the concise specification of processor architectures. From a single VADL processor specification, the VADL compiler can automatically generate a wide range of artifacts required for rapid design space exploration. These include assemblers, compilers, linkers, functional and cycle-accurate instruction set simulators, synthesizable hardware description language (HDL) specifications, as well as test cases and documentation. A distinctive feature of VADL is the separation of the instruction set architecture (ISA) specification from the microarchitecture (MiA) specification. This decoupling gives users the flexibility to combine various ISAs with different MiAs, offering a versatile approach to processor design. In contrast to existing PDLs, VADL's MiA specification operates at a higher level of abstraction, enhancing the clarity and simplicity of the design process. Notably, using a single ISA specification, VADL streamlines compiler generation and maintenance by eliminating the need for intricate compiler-specific knowledge. Because the original VADL implementation is subject to restrictive licensing, the open-source implementation OpenVADL was initiated. This article introduces VADL, compares the original implementation with the ongoing OpenVADL development, describes the generator techniques in detail, and demonstrates both the expressiveness of the language and the performance of the generators in an empirical evaluation. The evaluation highlights the conciseness of VADL and the efficiency of the generated artifacts. Finally, the viability of OpenVADL for design space exploration is demonstrated in a case study on CRC32 checksum computation for the RISC-V ISA.

papers.title: Functional weak convergence of stochastic integrals for moving averages and continuous-time random walks
papers.abstract: There is an extensive theory of weak convergence for moving averages and continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) with respect to Skorokhod's M1 and J1 topologies. Here we address the fundamental question of how this translates into functional limit theorems in the M1 or J1 topology for stochastic integrals driven by these processes. As an important application, we provide weak approximation results for general SDEs driven by time-changed L\'evy processes. Such SDEs and their associated fractional Fokker--Planck--Kolmogorov equations are central to models of anomalous diffusion in statistical physics. Our results yield a rigorous functional characterisation of these as continuum limits of the underlying models driven by CTRWs. With regard to strictly M1 convergent moving averages and correlated CTRWs, it turns out that the convergence of stochastic integrals can fail decidedly and fundamental new challenges arise compared to the J1 setting. Nevertheless, we identify natural classes of integrand processes for which there is M1 convergence of the stochastic integrals. We also show that these results are flexible enough to yield functional limit theorems in the M1 topology for certain stochastic delay differential equations driven by moving averages.

papers.title: A convergence result for a local planning problem for mean field games and rigorous proof of a Freidlin-Ventchel-type Large Deviations Principle for the $1+1$ KPZ equation
papers.abstract: We study an innovative connection between a very singular optimal transport variational problem with a congestion term connecting two Dirac measures, which is related to the planing problem in mean field games or gases with negative pressure, and a large deviation principle for the KPZ equation. The main result proves a limit of a singular approixmate problem with vanishing diffusive flux and a relaxed initial condition. The paper also provides a rigorous justification for the informal analysis of the ad hoc large deviation principle for the KPZ equation appearing in the physics literature.

papers.title: Ruin Theory Problems in Simple SDE Models with Large Deviation Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We examine hitting probability problems for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes and Geometric Brownian motions (GBM) with respect to exponential boundaries related to problems arising in risk theory and asset and liability models in pension funds. In Section 2 we consider the OU process described by the Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) $dX_t = \mu X_t dt + \sigma dW_t$ with $X_0=x_0$ evolving between a lower and an upper deterministic exponential boundary. Both the finite horizon ``ruin probability'' problem and the corresponding infinite horizon problem is examined in the low noise case, using the Wentzell-Freidlin approach in order to obtain logarithmic asymptotics for the probability of hitting either the lower or the upper boundary. The resulting variational problems are studied in detail. The exponential rate characterizing the ruin probability and the ``path to ruin'' are obtained by their solution. Logarithmic asymptotics for the meeting probability in a pair of OU processes with different positive drift coefficients, driven by independent Brownian motions is also obtained using Wentzell-Freidlin techniques. The optimal paths followed by the two processes and the meeting time $T$ are determined by solving a variational problem with transversality conditions. In Section 3 a corresponding problem involving a Geometric Brownian motion is considered. Since in this case, an exact, closed form solution is also available and we take advantage of this situation in order to explore numerically the quality of the Large Deviations results obtained using the Wentzell-Freidlin approach.

papers.title: Depth-multiplexing spectral domain OCT for full eye length imaging with a single modulation unit
papers.abstract: Clinical measurement of a patient's axial eye length is emerging as a crucial approach to track progression and monitor management of myopia. However, the preferred method for such measurements is swept-source OCT, whose cost prohibits broad use, especially in lower-income communities. Spectral domain (SD) OCT is a more affordable option, but it has limited imaging depth range, so is not suitable for full eye length measurement. Depth-multiplexing (DM) techniques for SD-OCT provide a workaround by capturing images at multiple depths within the eye. However, these methods typically require multiple light modulation units or detectors for simultaneous imaging across depths, adding complexity and cost. In response, we propose a novel DM-SD-OCT approach that utilizes a single light modulation unit for depth encoding. We capture images at multiple depths within the eye simultaneously with a single line scan camera, then computationally demix the contributions from different depths. Here, we demonstrate acquisition and demixing of signals from three distinct depths within the eye and validate experimentally in human subjects. Our method thus offers a cost-effective solution for comprehensive eye length measurement in clinical myopia research.

papers.title: RQFormer: Rotated Query Transformer for End-to-End Oriented Object Detection
papers.abstract: Oriented object detection presents a challenging task due to the presence of object instances with multiple orientations, varying scales, and dense distributions. Recently, end-to-end detectors have made significant strides by employing attention mechanisms and refining a fixed number of queries through consecutive decoder layers. However, existing end-to-end oriented object detectors still face two primary challenges: 1) misalignment between positional queries and keys, leading to inconsistency between classification and localization; and 2) the presence of a large number of similar queries, which complicates one-to-one label assignments and optimization. To address these limitations, we propose an end-to-end oriented detector called the Rotated Query Transformer, which integrates two key technologies: Rotated RoI Attention (RRoI Attention) and Selective Distinct Queries (SDQ). First, RRoI Attention aligns positional queries and keys from oriented regions of interest through cross-attention. Second, SDQ collects queries from intermediate decoder layers and filters out similar ones to generate distinct queries, thereby facilitating the optimization of one-to-one label assignments. Finally, extensive experiments conducted on four remote sensing datasets and one scene text dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. To further validate its generalization capability, we also extend our approach to horizontal object detection The code is available at https://github.com/wokaikaixinxin/RQFormer

papers.title: The Chiral Lagrangian of CP-Violating Axion-Like Particles
papers.abstract: We discuss the construction of the most general CP-violating chiral Lagrangian for an axion-like particle (ALP). Starting with an effective Lagrangian containing light quarks and gluons, we provide its matching onto a chiral effective Lagrangian at $\mathcal{O}(p^2)$ described in terms of mesons and baryons, identifying the correspondence between the Jarlskog invariants of the two theories. After deriving the ALP interactions with mesons and baryons, we analyse a few relevant phenomenological implications such as the permanent electric dipole moments of nucleons and the CP-violating ALP and kaon decays.This work provides the necessary tools for further phenomenological analyses connecting low-energy observables with the couplings of the underlying ultraviolet complete theory.

papers.title: Robust Brain MRI Image Classification with SIBOW-SVM
papers.abstract: Primary Central Nervous System tumors in the brain are among the most aggressive diseases affecting humans. Early detection and classification of brain tumor types, whether benign or malignant, glial or non-glial, is critical for cancer prevention and treatment, ultimately improving human life expectancy. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the most effective technique for brain tumor detection, generating comprehensive brain scans. However, human examination can be error-prone and inefficient due to the complexity, size, and location variability of brain tumors. Recently, automated classification techniques using machine learning methods, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have demonstrated significantly higher accuracy than manual screening. However, deep learning-based image classification methods, including CNNs, face challenges in estimating class probabilities without proper model calibration. In this paper, we propose a novel brain tumor image classification method called SIBOW-SVM, which integrates the Bag-of-Features model with SIFT feature extraction and weighted Support Vector Machines. This new approach can effectively extract hidden image features, enabling differentiation of various tumor types, provide accurate label predictions, and estimate probabilities of images belonging to each class, offering high-confidence classification decisions. We have also developed scalable and parallelable algorithms to facilitate the practical implementation of SIBOW-SVM for massive image datasets. To benchmark our method, we apply SIBOW-SVM to a public dataset of brain tumor MRI images containing four classes: glioma, meningioma, pituitary, and normal. Our results demonstrate that the new method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, including CNNs, in terms of uncertainty quantification, classification accuracy, computational efficiency, and data robustness.

papers.title: The universal Euler characteristic and Burnside group for definable groupoids
papers.abstract: We introduce the universal Euler characteristic of orbit space definable groupoids, a class of groupoids containing cocompact proper Lie groupoids as well as translation groupoids associated to proper definable group actions. We show that every additive and multiplicative invariant of orbit space definable groupoids with an additional local triviality hypothesis arises as a ring homomorphism applied to the universal Euler characteristic. This in particular includes the $\Gamma$-orbifold Euler characteristic introduced by the first and third authors when $\Gamma$ is a finitely presented group. For definable groupoids, where the object and arrow spaces as well as the structure maps are definable, we also introduce a Burnside group which is an analog of the classical Burnside ring associated to compact Lie groups and, for a transitive groupoid with compact isotropy, admits a partial multiplication.

papers.title: Optimal Rate of Kernel Regression in Large Dimensions
papers.abstract: We perform a study on kernel regression for large-dimensional data (where the sample size $n$ is polynomially depending on the dimension $d$ of the samples, i.e., $n\asymp d^{\gamma}$ for some $\gamma >0$ ). We first build a general tool to characterize the upper bound and the minimax lower bound of kernel regression for large dimensional data through the Mendelson complexity $\varepsilon_{n}^{2}$ and the metric entropy $\bar{\varepsilon}_{n}^{2}$ respectively. When the target function falls into the RKHS associated with a (general) inner product model defined on $\mathbb{S}^{d}$, we utilize the new tool to show that the minimax rate of the excess risk of kernel regression is $n^{-1/2}$ when $n\asymp d^{\gamma}$ for $\gamma =2, 4, 6, 8, \cdots$. We then further determine the optimal rate of the excess risk of kernel regression for all the $\gamma>0$ and find that the curve of optimal rate varying along $\gamma$ exhibits several new phenomena including the multiple descent behavior and the periodic plateau behavior. As an application, For the neural tangent kernel (NTK), we also provide a similar explicit description of the curve of optimal rate. As a direct corollary, we know these claims hold for wide neural networks as well.

papers.title: Embedding Capabilities of Neural ODEs
papers.abstract: Neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs) are a class of neural networks that have gained particular interest in recent years. We study input-output relations of neural ODEs using dynamical systems theory and prove several results about the exact embedding of maps in different neural ODE architectures in low and high dimensions. The embedding capability of a neural ODE architecture can be increased by adding, for example, affine linear layers or augmenting the phase space. However, there is currently no systematic theory available, and our work contributes towards this goal by developing various embedding results as well as identifying situations where no embedding is possible. Our core mathematical techniques include iterative functional equations, Morse functions, and suspension flows, as well as several further ideas from analysis. Although in practice mostly universal approximation theorems are used, our geometric dynamical systems viewpoint on universal embedding provides a fundamental understanding of why certain neural ODE architectures perform better than others.

papers.title: Metric-Measure Concentration and Strong Cosmic Censorship in Vacuum Gowdy Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy maximal globally hyperbolic development is $C^2$-inextendible if its asymptotic velocity differs from one on a dense subset of the singular circle. This is the implication posed in Section~14.2 of Ringstr\"om's 2010 review. The proof compares the spacetime volume of a timelike boundary collar with that of a shrinking angular cone, using Killing transport and the Einstein constraint. We connect this criterion to Gromov's observable distance: the physical spatial mm-spaces satisfy the lower bound $d_{\rm conc}(X_\tau,*)\ge L(\tau)/(4+L(\tau))$, where $L(\tau)$ is the length of the orbit circle. If $L(\tau)\to0$, then $v_\infty\ge1$ everywhere, the critical set $\{v_\infty=1\}$ has Lebesgue measure zero, and the development is $C^2$-inextendible. Thus physical point concentration is sufficient for inextendibility, but is not necessary. We also give explicit, non-perturbative subcritical characteristic conditions on vacuum Cauchy data ensuring quantitative Kretschmann blow-up without using Gowdy asymptotic theorems in the curvature estimate. The exact volume-transfer identity yields predictive monotonicity criteria and distinguishes coordinate localization from intrinsic metric collapse. In the transversely expanding regime, observable rescalings with an extended transverse-length limit are classified as a point, a measured circle, or the maximal pyramid; a uniform spectral estimate eliminates all nontrivial toroidal Fourier sectors, including in the presence of spikes. The geometric framework is completed by quantitative tube estimates, a local CMC redistribution theorem, and constrained variational descriptions of the reduced energy current and normalized-volume flow.

papers.title: Soft photon corrections in $B \to K^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ decays
papers.abstract: We calculate QED corrections to the semileptonic decays $H_1\to H_2\ell^+\ell^-$ where $\ell=e, \mu$ and $H_{1,2}$ are hadrons. The soft and/or collinear divergences are regulated in a gauge-invariant manner and demonstrably cancel, leaving behind a finite residue that depends on the (infrared) momentum cutoff below which a photon is considered to be indistinguishable. On resumming, the said sensitivity reduces drastically, {\em i.e.}, for the NLL result as compared to the NLO one. The overall correction is negative and its magnitude is larger for a lighter lepton. The corrections are presented for $B\to K^{(*)}$ and, for the first time, for $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda^{(*)}$ decays. Given that QED final-state radiation is routinely incorporated in experimental Monte Carlo simulations, for example through PHOTOS, our results provide an important theoretical framework for assessing the accuracy and limitations of these simulations and their impact on LFU observables such as $R_{K^{(*)}}$.

papers.title: The complete dynamics description of positively curved metrics in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$
papers.abstract: The family of invariant Riemannian manifolds in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$ is described by three parameters $(x,y,z)$ of positive real numbers. By restricting such a family of metrics in the \emph{tetrahedron} $\cal{T}:= x+y+z = 1$, in this paper, we describe all regions $\cal R \subset \cal T$ admitting metrics with curvature properties varying from positive sectional curvature to positive scalar curvature, including positive intermediate curvature notion's. We study the dynamics of such regions under the \emph{projected Ricci flow} in the plane $(x,y)$, concluding sign curvature maintenance and escaping. In addition, we obtain some results for positive intermediate Ricci curvature for a path of metrics on fiber bundles over $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$, further studying its evolution under the Ricci flow on the base.

papers.title: PartSLAM: Unsupervised Part-based Scene Modeling for Fast Succinct Map Matching
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore the challenging 1-to-N map matching problem, which exploits a compact description of map data, to improve the scalability of map matching techniques used by various robot vision tasks. We propose a first method explicitly aimed at fast succinct map matching, which consists only of map-matching subtasks. These tasks include offline map matching attempts to find a compact part-based scene model that effectively explains each map using fewer larger parts. The tasks also include an online map matching attempt to efficiently find correspondence between the part-based maps. Our part-based scene modeling approach is unsupervised and uses common pattern discovery (CPD) between the input and known reference maps. This enables a robot to learn a compact map model without human intervention. We also present a practical implementation that uses the state-of-the-art CPD technique of randomized visual phrases (RVP) with a compact bounding box (BB) based part descriptor, which consists of keypoint and descriptor BBs. The results of our challenging map-matching experiments, which use a publicly available radish dataset, show that the proposed approach achieves successful map matching with significant speedup and a compact description of map data that is tens of times more compact. Although this paper focuses on the standard 2D point-set map and the BB-based part representation, we believe our approach is sufficiently general to be applicable to a broad range of map formats, such as the 3D point cloud map, as well as to general bounding volumes and other compact part representations.

papers.title: Inference in clustered IV models with many and weak instruments
papers.abstract: This paper studies inference in instrumental variable models with many, weak instruments and clustered data. It first examines how clustering affects identification strength, showing how to adapt the concentration parameter to account for within-cluster dependence. The adapted concentration parameter may be smaller and may grow more slowly asymptotically than the concentration parameter that ignores the dependence, thereby weakening identification. Next, the paper extends the identification-robust jackknife Anderson--Rubin and jackknife score statistics for independent data to clustered data by removing clusters rather than individual observations from the statistics. These statistics converge jointly to a normal distribution under many-instrument asymptotics, such that scaling with cluster cross-fit variance estimators yields identification-robust tests. Simulations show that the cluster jackknife tests achieve close to nominal size and have good power. A reanalysis of a study on the effect of queenly reign on war shows the empirical relevance of the new tests.

papers.title: Sensitivity Analysis in Unconditional Quantile Effects
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework to analyze the effects of counterfactual policies on the unconditional quantiles of an outcome variable. For a given counterfactual policy, we obtain identified sets for the effect of both marginal and global changes in the proportion of treated individuals. To conduct a sensitivity analysis, we introduce the quantile breakdown frontier, a curve that $(i)$ indicates whether a sensitivity analysis is possible or not, and $(ii)$ when a sensitivity analysis is possible, quantifies the amount of selection bias consistent with a given conclusion of interest across different quantiles. To illustrate our method, we perform a sensitivity analysis on the effect of unionizing low income workers on the quantiles of the distribution of (log) wages.

papers.title: The pro-$\mathcal{C}$ anabelian geometry of number fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathcal{C}$ a nontrivial full class of finite groups. Write $K^{\mathcal{C}}/K$ for the maximal pro-$\mathcal{C}$ Galois extension of $K$ and $G_K^{\mathcal{C}}$ for its Galois group. Write $\Sigma(\mathcal{C})$ for the set of prime numbers $p$ such that $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{C}$. We prove that, for two such pairs $(K_i,\mathcal{C}_i)$, every isomorphism $G_{K_1}^{\mathcal{C}_1}\simeq G_{K_2}^{\mathcal{C}_2}$ is induced by a unique isomorphism between $K_2^{\mathcal{C}_2}/K_2$ and $K_1^{\mathcal{C}_1}/K_1$, provided that $\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_i)$ has positive upper Dirichlet density for at least one $i$. As a consequence, we generalize reconstruction results of Uchida and Sueyoshi to Galois extensions $\Omega_i/K_i$ such that $\Omega_i$ has no nontrivial abelian pro-$\Sigma$ extension, where $\Sigma$ has positive upper Dirichlet density. We also prove a relative version of the first result without a density assumption: the same conclusion holds if the group isomorphism is compatible with the canonical restriction maps to the maximal abelian pro-$\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_1)$ quotient of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}$, and if $2\in\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_1)$ or at least one of $K_1,K_2$ has a complex prime. This relative result applies, in particular, to maximal pro-$p$ quotients under these conditions.

papers.title: Isoparametric functions on Finsler space forms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that each connected regular level hypersurface of a transnormal function on a Finsler space form $(N(c),F)$ has constant principal curvatures under suitable conditions. This result extends Miyaoka's refinement of Q. M. Wang's classical theorem on transnormal functions in Riemannian space forms to the Finsler setting. On forward Finsler space forms $(\overrightarrow{N}(c),F)$, we discuss the relationship between umbilic hypersurfaces and isoparametric hypersurfaces, and construct global and local isoparametric functions using the distance function.

papers.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
papers.abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

papers.title: Uniformly Expanding Coupled Maps: Self-Consistent Transfer Operators and Propagation of Chaos
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation, uniformly in time, for systems of $N$ deterministic uniformly expanding heterogeneously coupled maps. The local dynamics and interactions may vary between coordinates, so exchangeability is not required. Under assumptions (independent of the dimension) on expansion, regularity, and weak-coupling, we construct self-consistent transfer operators whose product evolutions approximate every fixed finite marginal. For a class of weakly dependent initial laws (containing products), the error is $O(N^{-1})$ on fixed time intervals and $O(\log N/N)$ uniformly in time. The finite-time rate is optimal within this class. An explicit family exhibits error of order $\sqrt{\log N}/N$ at times of order $\log N$, proving that a uniform $O(N^{-1})$ bound is impossible in general; the optimal correction remains open. The proof is based on ergodic theory: expansion preserves classes of regular, weakly dependent densities, while transfer-operator contraction controls error accumulation. These classes yield concentration estimates and allow direct comparison of densities, giving strong propagation of chaos without external noise. Under additional assumptions, we also obtain Gaussian approximation for empirical observables on fixed time intervals and invariant neighbourhoods of stable fixed points of the self-consistent operator.

papers.title: Backtesting Trading Strategies with GAN To Avoid Overfitting
papers.abstract: Many works have shown the overfitting hazard of selecting a trading strategy based only on good IS (in sample) performance. But most of them have merely shown such phenomena exist without offering ways to avoid them. We propose an approach to avoid overfitting: A good (meaning non-overfitting) trading strategy should still work well on paths generated in accordance with the distribution of the historical data. We use GAN with LSTM to learn or fit the distribution of the historical time series . Then trading strategies are backtested by the paths generated by GAN to avoid overfitting.(This paper is an tanslated English version of a thesis (10.6342/NTU201801645) which was originally written in Chinese in 2018, where some statements and claims are outdated in 2022)

papers.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
papers.abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.

papers.title: Functional equation, upper bounds and analogue of Lindel\"of hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta function
papers.abstract: The functional equations of the Riemann zeta function, the Hurwitz zeta function, and the Lerch zeta function have been well known for a long time, and there is great importance in studying these zeta functions. For example, fundamental properties such as the upper bounds, the distribution of zeros, and the zero-free regions in the Riemann zeta function derive from functional equations. In this paper, we consider the functional equations for the Barnes double zeta-function $ \zeta_2 (s, \alpha ; v, w ) = \sum_{m=0}^\infty \sum_{n=0}^\infty (\alpha+vm+wn)^{-s} $. Additionally, by applying this functional equation and the Phragm\'en-Lindel\"of convexity principle, we obtain some upper bounds for $ \zeta_2(\sigma + it, \alpha ; v, w) $ with respect to $ t $ as $ t \rightarrow \infty $. Furthermore, we prove that an analogue of the Lindel"of hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta-function is equivalent to suitable upper bounds for its positive even moments on vertical lines in the critical strip.

papers.title: A note on split extension classifiers of perfect objects
papers.abstract: It is well known that the automorphism group of a perfect group has trivial center. This is a consequence of the fact that for a perfect group the centralizer of the normal subgroup of inner automorphisms of its automorphism group is trivial. We find a categorical explanation for this fact by showing that for a semi-abelian category $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying (WNH), if $X$ is a perfect object in $\mathbb{C}$ such that the split extension classifier $[X]$ exists, then the centralizer of the \emph{conjugation} morphism $c_X : X\to [X]$ is trivial and hence the center of $[X]$ is trivial. Our proof depends on the following fact, which we show holds in an arbitrary semi-abelian category satisfying (WNH). If $f:X\to Y$ is a central extension and $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ and $\phi$ are internal object actions of $B$ on $X$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, such that $f:(X,\theta_i)\to (Y,\phi)$ is an internal $B$-action morphism, then $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ restrict to the same action on $[X,X]$. Using this latter fact we also prove that (UCE) is a consequence of (WNH) alone (rather than of (WNH) together with (SH) as previously known).

papers.title: Direct electron cooling at millikelvin temperatures with quantum-well heat pump
papers.abstract: Unconventional solid-state cooling is proposed whereby the electron subband degeneracy of a semiconductor quantum well is cycled at cryogenic temperatures. By "expanding" electrons to higher subband degeneracy and "compressing" to lower degeneracy in an Otto cycle, a stack of ultra-wide 150 nm GaAs quantum wells filling a 1 cm3 volume could be operated as a heat pump to pump 26 uW at 100 mK. Operated as a refrigerator, it can piggy-back onto dilution refrigerators to cool from T_base to T_base/4. Possible cooling applications include quantum computers and infrared detectors.

papers.title: Constant solutions of the SU(2) Yang-Mills-Dirac equations: classification and explicit form
papers.abstract:
We present a complete classification of all constant solutions of the ${m SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Dirac equations in Minkowski space ${\mathbb R}^{1,3}$. The method combines the hyperbolic singular value decomposition of the real matrix of the gauge potential with the two-sheeted covering of ${m SO}(3)$ by ${m SU}(2)$. In the degenerate case of zero potential, we classify the solutions by the causal structure of the current. For nondegenerate solutions with $\Psi
eq 0$ and $A
eq 0$, the equations force a sharp dichotomy: a nonzero constant current requires a nonzero mass, and massless solutions necessarily have zero current. The massive branch gives a constant non-Abelian field configuration with nonvanishing invariant $F^2=F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}$. The remaining (degenerate) solutions are classified for completeness. For each case we give explicit formulas for the spinor $\Psi$, the potential $A$, the current $J$, and the invariant $F^2$, and we summarize the classification in a table. Nonconstant solutions can be sought as perturbation-theory series around constant solutions. We write the linear equations for the first-order correction, which reduce to linear partial differential equations with constant coefficients, and find explicit plane-wave solutions of these equations in the massless case.

papers.title: Cohomology of SL(3,Z) with coefficients in the standard representation
papers.abstract: This paper is a natural continuation of a joint paper with Bajpai, Harder and Moya Giusti \cite{BHHM}, even though it began as an answer to Goncharov's question. It that paper, we had complete description for all representations except for odd symmetric powers and their dual ones. For those representations we were left with two options: certain one dimensional module is a ghost space or not. Here we find the $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3)$ has ghost classes. It means that it is generated by a class from the cohomology of the Borel subgroup. With the techniques developed here, we show that the $d_2$ map of the spectral sequence for the boundary cohomology of $GL_4(\Z)$ is non-trivial if and only if there is a ghost class in $GL_3(\Z)$ (see Propositions 11 and 12.) We use a result of Elbaz-Vincent, Gangl and Soule to show that a spectral sequence related to $GL_4(\Z)$ does not degenerate at $E_2$-level. Then $d_2$ is non-trivial. Therefore, we obtain that $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3))$ is a ghost space, where $V_3$ is the standard representation.

papers.title: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
papers.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

papers.title: Twisted light affects ultrafast demagnetization
papers.abstract: Irradiation with an ultrashort laser pulse can completely destroy the magnetic order of ferromagnetic thin films on the femtosecond timescale. This phenomenon holds great potential for ultrafast spintronics and information processing and is an active field of research. It is still an open question if the angular momentum of light can support this effect. While it has been shown that the spin of light only has a negligible influence, we experimentally demonstrate the influence of photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) on the magnetization dynamics of a thin nickel film. Our results reveal that the photonic OAM affects the demagnetization behavior by a non-coherent, secondary process within the first hundreds of femtoseconds depending on the handedness of the OAM with respect to the direction of the sample magnetization.

papers.title: Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
papers.abstract: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $\alpha\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $\Gamma=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $\gamma\in\Gamma$, a $\gamma$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $\gamma$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $\Gamma\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $\gamma$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows. We first consider $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$, the expected number of fixed points in a $\gamma$-random permutation in $S_{N}$. We show that unless $\gamma$ has finite order, the limit of $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ as $N\to\infty$ is an integer, and is equal to the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ such that $H\cong\mathbb{Z}$ or $H\cong C_{2}*C_{2}$. Equivalently, this is the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ and having (rational) Euler characteristic zero. We also prove there is an asymptotic expansion for $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ and determine the limit distribution of the number of fixed points as $N\to\infty$. These results are then generalized to all statistics of cycles of fixed lengths.

papers.title: Personalized Execution Time Optimization for Billion-Scale Scheduled Jobs
papers.abstract: Scheduled batch jobs are widely used on asynchronous computing platforms to execute enterprise applications such as promotional notifications and candidate pre-computation for recommender systems. Delivering or updating information at the right time is important for user experience and execution impact, yet providing a versatile, personalized execution time optimization solution across diverse product scenarios while maintaining reasonable infrastructure costs remains challenging. In this paper, we present a deployed system that serves billions of users daily, combining learning-to-rank with a "best time policy" for execution time selection. We describe the four-stage evolution of our approach: from heuristic peak-hour rules, to pointwise ML-based activity pattern predictions, to a linear signal assembler with globally fixed weights, and finally to a contextual ensemble learner that produces per-user adaptive fusion weights via a neural policy network trained with listwise learning-to-rank objectives. We further report the discovery of cross-use-case cannibalization effects and introduce a coordination system to mitigate the problem. Our production experiments demonstrate measurable improvements in both execution efficiency and downstream product impact. We share deployment lessons including failure analyses and design decisions accumulated over four years of operating this system at scale. To our knowledge, this represents the first ML-based multi-tenant execution time optimization system deployed across different product domains at industrial scale.

papers.title: Wavescan: Multiresolution Time-Frequency Transform of Gravitational-Wave Data
papers.abstract: Identifying transient signals embedded in non-stationary noise requires analyzing the time-dependent spectral components of the observed time series. The time-frequency distribution of the signal power can be estimated with Gabor atoms, or wavelets, localized in time and frequency by a window function. Such analysis is constrained by the Heisenberg-Gabor uncertainty principle, which limits the simultaneous time and frequency localization achievable with individual wavelets. Moreover, the resulting time-frequency distribution is subject to temporal and spectral leakage, limiting the identification of sharp or rapidly varying features in the power spectrum. This paper introduces a time-frequency transform that uses a stack of wavelets to scan local power across multiple scales. At each time-frequency location, a wavelet least affected by the leakage is selected from the stack to obtain high-resolution localization of power. The resulting wavelet scan ("wavescan") extends conventional multiresolution analysis by enhancing time-frequency localization and mitigating local power distortions caused by temporal and spectral leakage. The paper describes the principal components of the wavescan framework, including the estimation of the time-varying spectrum, identification of transient signals in the time-frequency data, and reconstruction of the corresponding time-domain waveforms. To demonstrate the performance of the method, the wavescan transform is applied to gravitational-wave data from the LIGO detectors.

papers.title: Approximating TSP walks in subcubic graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every simple 2-connected subcubic graph on $n$ vertices with $n_2$ vertices of degree 2 has a TSP walk of length at most $\frac{5n+n_2}{4}-1$, confirming a conjecture of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Kr\'al', and Mohar. This bound is best possible; there are infinitely many subcubic and cubic graphs whose minimum TSP walks have lengths $\frac{5n+n_2}{4}-1$ and $\frac{5n}{4} - 2$ respectively. We characterize the extremal subcubic examples meeting this bound. We also give a quadratic-time combinatorial algorithm for finding such a TSP walk. In particular, we obtain a $\frac{5}{4}$-approximation algorithm for the graphic TSP on simple cubic graphs, improving on the previously best known approximation ratio of $\frac{9}{7}$.

papers.title: Can Satellite Mega-Constellations Justify Their Impact on Astronomy?
papers.abstract: Private space companies are increasingly commercializing near-earth space. Some estimates show that more than 100,000 satellites may orbit the Earth by 2030. This increase in the number of satellites has many consequences for science, particularly astronomy. Satellite mega-constellations for satellite Internet connectivity are one of the main drivers behind the explosion in the number of satellites. Here, we briefly note whether such satellite mega-constellations can justify their impact on astronomy.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Embeddings in Toric Geometry: Effectivity and Deformation Stability
papers.abstract: We study the deformation behavior of Kobayashi hyperbolic embeddings for complements of divisors in projective toric varieties. In the toric setting, the Zariski closure of an entire curve in a torus complement is a translate of an algebraic subtorus contained in that complement. This translates hyperbolicity questions into combinatorial conditions on lattice-point configurations of Newton polytopes. Building on a theorem of Tiba, which guarantees hyperbolic embedding for a general divisor under suitable facewise lattice conditions, we develop an effective refinement of his argument. We construct an explicit constructible bad locus in the coefficient parameter space, characterized by the presence of translated subtori in the divisor or its complement on a torus stratum, and use its proper Zariski closure as an exceptional locus. This description makes the exceptional set amenable to computation. Using this effectivity, we prove a deformation stability result: along any algebraic one-parameter family of divisors whose initial member avoids the exceptional locus, hyperbolic embedding fails for at most finitely many parameters. Under strengthened lattice-point hypotheses, we further exhibit distinguished one-parameter families for which hyperbolic embedding persists without any exceptional parameters. We also analyze deformations arising from diagonal torus reparametrizations. If the initial divisor lies outside $\mathcal Y$, the inverse image of $\mathcal Y$ under the similarity family is empty on the nondegenerate parameter domain, while the smallest possible degeneracy set of a rational similarity presentation is controlled by a multiplicative rank invariant of the scaling vector. Finally, we illustrate the theory through examples in projective spaces and Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: On a Conjecture About the Sombor Index of Graphs
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. A graph invariant for $G$ is a number related to the structure of $G$ which is invariant under the symmetry of $G$}. The Sombor and reduced Sombor indices of $G$ are two new graph invariants defined as $SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2}$ and $SO_{red}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{ ig(d_G(u)-1 ig)^2 +  ig(d_G(v)-1 ig)^2}$, respectively, where $d_G(v)$ is the degree of the vertex $v$ in $G$. We denote by $H_{n,
u}$ the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $
u$ edge(s), $0\leq 
u\leq n-2$, between a fixed pendent vertex and $
u$ other pendent vertices. R'eti et al. [T. R'eti, T Do\v{s}li'c and A. Ali, On the Sombor index of graphs, 	extit{Contrib. Math.} 	extbf{3} (2021) 11--18] proposed a conjecture that the graph $H_{n,
u}$ has the maximum Sombor index among all connected $
u$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, where $0\leq\,
u\leq n-2$. In some earlier works the validity of this conjecture was proved for $
u\leq 5$. In this paper we confirm that this conjecture is true, when $
u = 6$. The Sombor index in the case that the number of pendent vertices is less than or equal to $n - 
u - 2$ is investigated and the same results are obtained for the reduced Sombor index. Some relationships between Sombor, reduced Sombor and first Zagreb indices of graphs are also obtained.

papers.title: Precise predictions for double-Higgs production via vector-boson fusion
papers.abstract: Theoretical predictions with next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD accuracy combined with the next-to-leading order (NLO) electroweak (EW) corrections are presented for differential observables of the double-Higgs production process via vector-boson fusion. While the QCD corrections were previously known, the EW ones are computed here for the first time. The numerical results are obtained for a realistic experimental set-up at the LHC and are presented in the form of fiducial cross sections and differential distributions. Within this setup we find that the VBF approximation employed in the NNLO QCD correction is accurate at the sub-percent level. We find that the NLO EW corrections within the fiducial volume are $-4.8\%$, making them of almost the same order as the NLO QCD corrections. In some kinematic regions they can grow as large as $-30\%$ making them the dominant radiative corrections. When the EW corrections are combined with the NNLO QCD corrections we find a total correction of $-14.8\%$. The results presented here thus comprise the state-of-the-art theoretical predicition for the double-Higgs production via vector-boson fusion, which will be of value to the high-luminosity programme at the LHC.

papers.title: Topological conjugacy and its relations for symbolic matrices
papers.abstract: In 1988 Boyle and Krieger defined sub-matrices for representation matrices of sofic shift. This paper presents some details of relations between integral sub-matrices and representation matrices. Besides, we express a new version of the Decomposition Theorem by sub-matrices. Generally, strong shift equivalence (conjugacy) of sub-matrices does not apply to representation matrices, but we show that this result can be achieved by the fixed diagonal integral sub-matrix.

papers.title: Learning Delicate Local Representations for Multi-Person Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method called Residual Steps Network (RSN). RSN aggregates features with the same spatial size (Intra-level features) efficiently to obtain delicate local representations, which retain rich low-level spatial information and result in precise keypoint localization. Additionally, we observe the output features contribute differently to final performance. To tackle this problem, we propose an efficient attention mechanism - Pose Refine Machine (PRM) to make a trade-off between local and global representations in output features and further refine the keypoint locations. Our approach won the 1st place of COCO Keypoint Challenge 2019 and achieves state-of-the-art results on both COCO and MPII benchmarks, without using extra training data and pretrained model. Our single model achieves 78.6 on COCO test-dev, 93.0 on MPII test dataset. Ensembled models achieve 79.2 on COCO test-dev, 77.1 on COCO test-challenge dataset. Code and model are publicly available for further research at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/RSN/ . Our project page at https://caiyuanhao1998.github.io/RSN-Project/ shows more video results. An online Gradio demo is available on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/RSN

papers.title: Gene ologs: a categorical framework for Gene Ontology
papers.abstract: The Gene Ontology (GO) is the most widely used resource for the functional annotation of genes and gene products. It unifies biological knowledge across species through a dynamic, controlled vocabulary, and it is now primarily represented in the Web Ontology Language (OWL), a logic-based language that supports automated reasoning. Ologs (ontology logs), introduced by Spivak and Kent, offer a different language for knowledge representation, grounded in category theory: concepts are types, functional relationships are aspects, and declared equalities between paths are facts. Ologs come with features that are not part of the standard use of GO: path equations, universal constructions (products, coproducts, pullbacks and pushouts), a database reading in which instance data are set-valued functors, and functors with which ontologies can be compared and merged. In this work we take an initial step towards Gene ologs, i.e. ologs for GO. We fix conventions for reading GO terms as olog types, examine which GO relations can be represented as aspects and which must instead be represented as spans, illustrate each olog construction with GO examples, show that standard GO annotations and GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAM) can be represented as olog instance data subject to checkable constraints, and describe how functors and pushouts can be used to compare and merge Gene ologs. We also discuss what ologs do not provide relative to OWL. We regard Gene ologs as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the OWL representation of GO.

papers.title: Chiral QCD phase in equilibrium with Hadron Gas and the location of the critical point
papers.abstract: We develop a description of the equation of state of QCD matter with restored chiral symmetry, which is in thermal and chemical equilibrium with the hadronic phase. The hadron gas is described with thermodynamically consistent volume corrections. The chiral phase is composed of a set of few quark condensates, each of which corresponds to a family of hadrons with specific quark content. On the boundary between the two phases we apply the requirement of conservation of particle numbers per family. We use lattice calculations for temperatures below the transition curve to determine hadronic volumes. We find that the pion system plays decisive role in the shift of the transition from higher order (crossover) to first order. For four volume models and five hadron sets we calculate the location of the critical point as function of critical temperature $T_c$ at vanishing baryon density. Among other acceptable solutions, if we additionally impose the equality between the densities of quarks contained in mesons and baryons, we find a critical point residing in the interval of baryon chemical potential $\mu_B \simeq$ 234-279 MeV and of temperature $T \simeq$ 148-156 MeV. We propose as signal of approach to the critical point the determination of the chiral pion mass through experimentally measured pion multiplicities in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: General Slit Stochastic L\"owner Evolution and Conformal Field Theory
papers.abstract: This monograph is dedicated to a generalization of the L\"owner equation in its stochastic form, known as SLE, and to its coupling with the Gaussian free field, with the ultimate aim of constructing a boundary conformal field theory with one free scalar bosonic field. The exposition aims to be a systematic, and hopefully concise, account and generalization of known elements of the theory of L\"owner evolution. We also study the relation to singular representations of the Virasoro algebra, as well as methods of numerical simulation. The main results are proofs of the basic properties of the generalized SLE and general necessary and sufficient conditions for its coupling with the Gaussian free field. We also introduce a framework that allows one to treat all L"owner equations and known types of coupling as different manifestations of the same phenomenon.

papers.title: Dirichlet heat kernel estimates for fractional Laplacian under non-local perturbation
papers.abstract: For $d\geq 1$ and $0 \varepsilon\}}(f(x+z)-f(x))\frac{b(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\beta}}\,{\mathrm{d}z},$$ and $b(x,z)$ is a bounded measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with $b(x,z)=b(x,-z)$ for every $x,z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Here ${\mathcal{A}}(d, -\beta)$ is the normalizing constant for which $\mathcal{S}^b=-(-\Delta)^{\beta/2}$ when $b(x, z)\equiv 1$. It is known that if $b(x, z) \geq -\frac{{\mathcal{A}}(d, -\alpha)} {{\mathcal{A}}(d, -\beta)}\, |z|^{\beta -\alpha}$ for a.e. $z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, then $\mathcal{L}^b$ admits a unique fundamental solution $p^{b}(t,x,y)$, which determines a conservative Feller process $X^{b}$ with the strong Feller property. In this paper, we study the subprocess $X^{b,D}$ of $X^{b}$ killed upon leaving a $C^{1,1}$ open set $D\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. We establish explicit small-time upper and lower bounds for its transition density function $p^{b}_{D}(t,x,y)$. These estimates are uniform in $b$: all constants depend on $b$ only through an upper bound of $\|b\|_{\infty}$. Moreover, $b$ enters the form of the upper bound only through the size of its large positive part, $\mathrm{ess\,sup}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d},\,|z|>\lambda}b(x,z)^{+}$ for a fixed $\lambda>0$. When the jump kernel of $\mathcal{L}^b$ satisfies matching upper and lower bounds, either of $\alpha$-stable type or of mixed $\alpha$- and $\beta$-stable type, the small-time estimates for $p^{b}_{D}(t,x,y)$ are sharp. For bounded $D$, we also obtain large-time estimates governed by the principal eigenvalue of the generator of $X^{b,D}$. Under a non-degeneracy condition on the jump kernel, we further establish sharp two-sided estimates on the Green function of $X^{b, D}$ in bounded $C^{1,1}$ open sets.

papers.title: Newton's second law: not so elementary (as it may seem)
papers.abstract: Introductory courses present Newton's second law either as a definition of force or as a law of nature, and in both cases leave unexplained why it holds only in a special class of reference frames. We give an operational reading of the law built on a single instrument, the spring balance. Its reading is a local fact on which all observers agree; in a given laboratory it defines the masses of bodies and a vector {\gamma} characterising the laboratory. Laboratories with $\gamma$ = 0 are, by definition, inertial. The empirical content of the second law is then the statement {\gamma} = -KA, where A is the acceleration of the laboratory measured kinematically from any inertial laboratory, and K is a universal constant that the choice of the newton as unit of force makes invisible. In this reading a spring balance is an accelerometer and an accelerometer is a dynamometer: both measure the specific force a-g familiar from inertial navigation. We discuss the hypotheses involved (universality of free fall, absence of rotation, locality) and the relation with Newton's own formulation.

papers.title: Alain Badiou's Mistake: Two Postulates of Dialectical Materialism
papers.abstract: Originally published in 2013, this revised article constitutes the first stage of a two-part intervention that revisits Alain Badiou's deployment of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. It interrogates the structural and philosophical consequences of taking the category-theoretic foundations of mathematics seriously, extending the formal boundaries of mathematical discourse. This part focuses on Logics of Worlds, which emerged as Badiou's response to his own theory of subjectivity. While revisiting structures implicit in his reading of Cohen's proof of the independence of the continuum hypothesis, I demonstrate how his concept of 'dialectical materialism' remains constrained by set-theoretic ontology and localic topos theory - essentially a theory of intuitionistic logic. In particular, Badiou's claim that categorical thinking does not substantially change mathematics overlooks the true geometric momentum driving topos theory. While the primary contents of this article are technical, I further explore how Badiou's formal omissions critically impact his philosophical project. This is especially visible in regard to his 'postulate of materialism' - a device he utilizes to promote dialectical materialism as a credible alternative to science. Through its category-theoretic reframing, I show that the postulate actually encapsulates two structurally different conditions, one of which directly constrains his own project while the other part captures a type of atomism juxtaposed with Badiou's condescending assessment of democracy. By leveraging such claims indebted to his pre-committed, logicist comprehension of mathematics, Badiou reinstitutes an absolutist Truth-doctrine and an ultimately despotic political program against a genuine concept of multiplicity. His errors thus hardly constitute merely an inadvertent formal slip, but indicate a deeper, political intent.

papers.title: Transverse deflecting cavities
papers.abstract: Transverse deflecting cavities are used for a number of applications in modern accelerators. In this paper we discuss the fields of these cavities, some of their applications, and some important aspects of their design.

papers.title: A bordism theory related to matrix Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Matrix Grassmannians give finite-dimensional representatives for virtual bundles of rank one and vanishing first Chern class. We use them to study two groups of labelled manifolds. A choice of stable normal framing gives framed bordism of $\BSU_{\otimes}$ and an integral Pontryagin--Thom description. Forgetting the framing gives a quotient defined by the boundary relations for labelled, stably parallelizable manifolds. The forgetful map is surjective with torsion kernel. Both rational bordism rings are polynomial on explicitly labelled spheres, one generator in each even dimension at least four. We compute the characteristic numbers of their products and show that each sphere generator spans an integral direct summand in its own degree.

papers.title: Theories of bundles with additional homotopy conditions
papers.abstract: A homotopy between two amplified special unitary bundles and a trivialization of a tensor product give two different finite-dimensional classifying spaces. For coprime ranks $k,l>1$ the first space is a biquotient of $\SU(kl)$ and the second is a homogeneous matrix Grassmannian. We distinguish the two manifolds for every such pair by their first Pontryagin classes. For $(k,l)=(2,3)$ their eighth integral cohomology groups have orders $3$ and $21$, respectively. The same amplification maps define a dimension-drop algebra on a labelled simplex. Its skeletal filtration gives a weighted cellular complex and computes $K_0$, $K_1$ and the unit when the vertex labels have greatest common divisor one. We also compute both groups for triangles with arbitrary vertex labels.

papers.title: On Some Diophantine Parameters of the Cyclic Torsion Subgroups of Odd Order of Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: For elliptic curves $ E $ over the rational number field $ \Q, $ based on Mazur's classical result, we give in this paper some explicit Diophantine parameters for their cyclic torsion subgroups $ E(\Q)_{\text{tors}} $ of odd order. This work is a continuation of the ones in ([Q1], [QZ1$\sim $2]). Such explicit form of parameters might be useful in calculating torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over higher degree number fields.
